text: Potio omnis Arabica quam biberat nullum effectum habuit.

text: Si aliquid facere non vis, noli id facere.
translation: If you don't want to do something, don't do it.

text: Ostende mihi alium, quaeso.

text: Quo pacto res se tibi habent?

text: Il tronco del pero è più grande di quello del susino.
translation: The trunk of the pear tree is bigger than that of the plum tree.

text: Selena dea lunae est.
translation: Selene is the goddess of the moon.

text: Plus pecuniae opus est mihi, sed non multum.
translation: I need more money, but not much.

text: Ille unus homo grandissimus modernarum est litterarum.

translation: If you wish for peace, prepare for war.

text: Mars, filius Jovi Junonisque, deus belli erat.
translation: Mars, son of Jupiter and Juno, was the god of war.

text: Oppidum in bello solo aequatum est.

text: Filii eorum in bello mortui sunt.
translation: Their sons died during the war.

text: Multi iuvenes in bello perierunt.
translation: In the war, many people died young.

text: Scio vitam meam male scriptam esse.
translation: I know, my life is poorly written.

text: Non vitae, sed scholae discimus.
translation: Not for life, but for school do we learn.

text: Non scholae, sed vitae discimus.
translation: Not for school, but for life do we learn.

text: Liberi flores vitarum nostrarum sunt.

text: Ea est amor vitae meae.

text: Homo ille, de quo locutus es, soror mea est.

text: Hic liber a multis hominibus scriptus est.

text: Homo non vivit ut edat, sed edit ut vivat.
translation: People do not live to eat but eat to live.

translation: Spring is the season that Lucy likes best.

text: Iam tempus est me verum dicere.
translation: It is high time you told the truth.

text: Iam tempus est te verum dicere.

text: Lingua Gallica ei magis quam lingua Theodisca placet.
translation: He likes French more than German.

text: Utrum magis tibi placet? Mala an musae?

text: Miho est puella quae magis mihi placet.

text: Magis iste pharmacopola quod dicit audis quam quod medicus.

text: Beatius est magis dare quam accipere.

text: Illa sententia est interpretatio primi versus soneti duodevicesimi Shakespeariani.

text: "Ubi liber eius est?" "Super mensam est."
translation: "Where's his book?" "It's on the table."

translation: Tell me where you were and what you did.

translation: Kids, why are you alone? Where's Mom?

text: Thomas in cubiculo suo non est. Demiror ubi sit.
translation: Tom isn't in his room. I wonder where he is.

text: Thoman a hostibus interfectum esse putabam.
translation: I thought that the enemy had killed Tom.

text: Roma a multis hostibus oppugnata est.
translation: Rome was attacked by many enemies.

text: Jugurtha et Roma acerrimi hostes erant.

text: Elephantibus hostes inspicito etsi formicae erunt.
translation: Even if your enemy is an ant, consider him an elephant.

text: Caesar exspectabat quid consili hostes caperent.

text: Thoman hostem meum puto esse.

text: Pirāta est hostis humāni generis.
translation: A pirate is an enemy to all mankind.

text: "Ipse hostis Teucros insigni laude ferebat, / seque ortum antiqua Teucrorum ab stirpe volebat".
translation: "Himself, a foe, oft lauded Troy's renown, / and claimed the Teucrian sires as kinsmen of his own."

text: Quis globus, o cives, caligine volvitur atra? Ferte citi ferrum, date tela, ascendite muros, hostis adest, heia!
translation: See what a ball of black dust, O citizens, advances towards us! Quickly bring the weapons, distribute the darts, run to the walls, hey, the enemy is coming!

text: "Sic o, sic positum affati discedit corpus. / Ipse manu mortem inveniam; miserebitur hostis / exuviasque petet. Facilis jactura sepulcri."
translation: "Leave me, pray, / and bid me, as a shrouded corpse, farewell. / For death, this hand will find for me the way, / or foes who spoil will pity me and slay. / Light is the loss of sepulchre or pyre."

text: Post mortem Thomae, Maria in magno luctu erat.
translation: After Tom's death, Mary was in deep mourning.

text: Post mortem Mariae, Thomas in magno luctu erat.
translation: After Mary's death, Tom was in deep mourning.

text: Nativitas et mors non eadem sunt.
translation: Birth and death are not the same.

translation: We received word of his death.

translation: The soul survives the death of the body.

translation: This car is as big as that car.

translation: My brother is as tall as me.

translation: Joan is as charming as her sister.

translation: Nothing is so difficult that it cannot be studiously investigated.

text: Thomas non tam fessus est quam Maria.
translation: Tom isn't as tired as Mary.

translation: Nobody is so learned that he is able to know all things.

text: Hac de causa tecum ire non possum.
translation: For this reason, I cannot go with you.

translation: In August, I'm going to Japan with my friends.

text: In Italiam iit ut linguam Italicam disceret.
translation: She went to Italy to learn Italian.

text: Non opus est tibi ire cum ea.
translation: You don't have to go with her.

translation: I'm going to go to Boston to see Tom.

translation: Tom was armed with a kitchen knife.

text: Pacemne huc fertis an arma?
translation: Do you bring peace, or warfare?

translation: Tom was armed with a machete.

text: Consequimur cuncti et densis incurrimus armis.
translation: One and all, / with weapons massed, press on and follow at his call.

translation: Caesar stripped the enemy of their arms.

text: Pictis bellantur Amazones armis.
translation: The Amazons fight with colorful weapons.

translation: Nor lacks my sire his presents; for the rest / steeds, guides and arms he finds, and oarsmen of the best.

text: Quis has fecit picturas, quae supra fenestram sunt?
translation: Who painted these pictures that are above the window?

text: Veruntamen aiunt principem esse supra leges.
translation: Nevertheless they say a prince is above the law.

text: Est fenestra supra lectum.
translation: There is a window above the bed.

text: Nec Caesar suprā grammaticōs.

text: Caesar nōn suprā grammaticōs.
translation: Caesar is not above grammarians.

text: Nōn Caesar suprā grammaticōs.
translation: Caesar is not above grammarians.

text: Thomas se sperare Mariam vincere posse dixit.
translation: Tom said he hopes Mary can win.

text: Thomas quam ob causam non vicisses nescit.
translation: Tom doesn't know why you didn't win.

text: Thomas et Maria mihi dixerunt se vincere non posse.
translation: Tom and Mary have told me they can't win.

text: Puto fore ut Thomas vincere possit.
translation: I think Tom will be able to win.

text: Dīcit sē vincere in animō habēre.
translation: He says that he plans to win.

text: Nemo praeter Mariam Thoman vincere potest.
translation: Nobody can beat Tom except Mary.

text: Attulerunt patellas, et posuerunt in mensa.
translation: They brought the plates and put them on the table.

text: Thomas cultrum super mensam posuit.
translation: Tom put the knife on the table.

text: Nescio ubi telephonum gestabile posuerim.
translation: I don't know where I put my cell phone.

translation: Mary put her clothes in the suitcase.

text: Thomas libum in furno posuit.
translation: Tom put the cake in the oven.

translation: Her grandfather died writing a letter.

translation: I'll stay with you as long as you want me to.

translation: What does Tom eat when he's watching TV?

translation: If only she had been home when I called yesterday!

translation: Why are you happy when someone else suffers?

translation: Don't do anything stupid while I'm gone.

translation: I shouldn't have borrowed so much money from Tom.

translation: Tom and Mary have only two children.

text: Semel tantum inter nos osculati sumus.
translation: We only kissed once.

text: Semel tantum inter nos osculatae sumus.
translation: We only kissed once.

text: Cur unam musam tantum emisti?
translation: Why did you buy only one banana?

translation: I couldn't help but admire Tom's perseverance.

translation: He couldn't help but like her.

text: Quamdiu matrimonium tenetis uterque vestrum?
translation: How long have you two been married?

translation: Hold the baby very carefully.

text: Teneri non potui quin flerem.
translation: I couldn't help but cry.

translation: There is no reason for me to apologize.

translation: He told me why he did that.

translation: I know why you're leaving.

translation: Do you know why that happens?

translation: Tom came to Australia on business.

translation: If what you say is true, it follows that he has an alibi.

translation: Tom followed me night and day.

translation: I couldn't help but follow her.

text: Vir quidam Mariam sequi coepit.
translation: A certain man began to follow Mary.

translation: A man began to follow Tom.

text: Non puto quempiam dicere se Deo non credere.
translation: I don't think anyone says they don't trust God.

translation: I believe you know what Marcus is doing.

translation: I believe I understood your words well.

translation: Tom got more presents than Mary.

text: Qui ait: Venit germanus tuus fraudulenter et accepit benedictionem tuam.
translation: And he said: Thy brother came deceitfully and got thy blessing.

text: Dixitque ad Hemmor patrem suum: Accipe mihi puellam hanc coniugem.

text: Putasne eum invitationem meam accipere?
translation: Do you think he would accept my invitation?

text: Quomodo suam pecuniam accipere volunt?
translation: How do they wish to receive their money?

translation: For it is not in keeping with his valor to ask for peace.

translation: The teacher was speaking about the virtue of the Romans.

translation: Tom has a lot of courage.

text: Passiō virtūs nōn est.
translation: Suffering is not a virtue.

text: Iactat se sua virtute.
translation: He boasted of his courage.

text: Is quaesivit a me utrum aliquis ibi esset.
translation: He asked me whether anybody was there.

text: "Sine te hoc exorare, quaeso." "Quidnam id est?"
translation: “Just do us one favor, will you?” “And what would that be?”

text: Marīa ā Thōmā quaesīvit num satis ēdisset.
translation: Mary asked Tom if he had eaten enough.

text: Thōmās ā Marīā quaesīvit num canem habēret.
translation: Tom asked Mary if she had a dog.

translation: I asked her if she had been to Mexico.

text: Thōmās ā Marīā quaesīvit num Bostoniae fuisset.

translation: A lion was sent to kill Hercules.

text: Gutta cavat lapidem non vi, sed saepe cadendo.

text: gutta cavat lapidem, non vi sed saepe cadendo.
translation: A water drop hollows a stone not by force but by falling often.

translation: This house has six rooms.

text: Thomas viribus male utitur.
translation: Tom makes bad use of his strength.

text: Vim vi repellere licet.
translation: One nail drives out another.

text: Narratio haec est amoris incomparabilis.
translation: It's the story of an unparalleled love.

text: Non puto hoc esse amorem.
translation: I don't think that's love.

text: Thomas magnum amorem patriae habet.
translation: Tom is very patriotic.

text: Ver est tempus amoris.
translation: Spring is the season of love.

text: Amor amorem amare amat.
translation: Love loves to love love.

text: Multas stellas in caelo videre potes.

translation: I see a big star in the sky.

translation: Many stars shine in the sky.

text: Thomas de caelo emissus est.
translation: Tom is extraordinary.

translation: Evil that comes out of your mouth flies in your bosom.

translation: If the sky fell, many larks would be caught.

translation: The sky is clear and the sun is bright.

text: Deus creavit caelum et terram.
translation: God created the heaven and the earth.

text: Caelum habet Ignem et Stellas.
translation: The sky has fire and stars.

text: Dixit se illius noctis non obliturum esse.
translation: He said he won't forget that night.

text: Praeteria nocte inter nos locuti sumus.

text: Praeteria nocte inter nos locutae sumus.
translation: We spoke last night.

text: Ea nocte ad concentum ierat.
translation: She had gone to the concert that evening.

text: Ad urbem ante noctem perveniemus.
translation: We arrived at the city before night.

text: Nocte dieque de ea cogito.
translation: I think of her day and night.

text: Hic liber de vita in Britanniarum Regno est.
translation: This book deals with life in the United Kingdom.

text: Ursa unum acutissimum olfactum in regno animali habet.
translation: A bear has one of the keenest noses in the animal kingdom.

text: Cur Britanniarum Regnum invisas?
translation: Why are you visiting the United Kingdom?

translation: It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.

text: Cum mundus videatur infinite magnus et regnum atomicum infinite parvum, cellula infinite complexa videtur.
translation: Where the cosmos feels infinitely large and the atomic realm infinitely small, the cell feels infinitely complex.

text: Et murmuravit populus contra Moysen dicens: Quid bibemus?
translation: And the people murmured against Moses, saying: What shall we drink?

translation: In recognition of these great services a crown was bestowed upon him by the people.

translation: And the people was scattered through all the land of Egypt to gather straw.

text: Is a populo suo amatur.

translation: The voice of the people is the voice of god.

text: Fessus sum, et caput mihi dolet.

text: Caput meum dolet et ad pharmacopolium eo ut medicinam emam.

text: Caput mihi dolet et ad pharmacopolium eo ut medicinam emam.
translation: I have a headache and I am going to the pharmacy to buy medicine.

text: Caput est pars corporis hominis.

translation: That child has a very large head.

translation: Tom and Mary divided the money between themselves.

translation: At that time, the Romans ruled land and sea.

translation: A woman fell from a ship into the sea.

translation: He rode a horse to the sea.

translation: This reminds me of a girl.

translation: I have to learn a language.

translation: I learned about Greek culture.

translation: We are born of love; love is our mother.

translation: His mother had three sons, of whom he was the youngest.

translation: My father is a native French speaker and my mother is a native English speaker.

text: In patella volante venerunt et Thoman ceperunt.

text: Thomas fratrem tuum in therotrophium duxit.

translation: You're the one Tom wants to take to the dance.

translation: Tom married her anyway.

translation: Your brother didn’t get married, did he?

text: "Quid est tibi nomen?" "Nomen mihi est Carolus."
translation: "What is your name?" "My name is Charles."

translation: I had a teacher named Mr Bakir.

translation: "Yes, I'm cheating on you." "What's his name?"

translation: She has a daughter whose name is Mary.

translation: In his time, he was an anonymous writer.

translation: In which language do you want to see names of animals?

translation: Tom knows the names of all his customers.

translation: We live on a planet called Earth.

translation: In the name of God, the Gracious, the Merciful.

translation: She didn't even let me kiss her.

translation: Tom loves Maria, but not me.

text: O meritò quidem te ex jurisconsulto Grammaticum!
translation: You have done well in leaving off being an Advocate and sticking to grammar.

text: Non video causam, cur ita sit, hoc quidem tempore.
translation: I don't see the reason why it should be so, especially at this time.

text: Ne Mariam exitam quidem observabat Thomas.
translation: Tom didn't even notice that Mary was gone.

text: Ne me quidem rogavisti quid vellem.
translation: You did not even ask me what I wanted.

text: Maria se valde miseram esse dixit.
translation: Mary said that she was very unhappy.

text: Thomas et Maria valde miseri sunt.
translation: Tom and Mary are very unhappy.

text: Quid tibi accidit? Miser videris.
translation: What happened to you? You look miserable.

text: Scisne cur Thomas miser esset?
translation: Do you know why Tom was unhappy?

text: Scisne cur Thomas miser sit?
translation: Do you know why Tom is unhappy?

text: Occidit miseros crambe repetita magistros.
translation: Tedious repetition kills unhappy teachers.

text: Pugnare cum diis cumque fortuna, grave est.
translation: "Tis useless to kick against the pricks.

text: Misera fortuna, qui caret inimico.
translation: If you have no enemies, it is a sign fortune has forgotten you.

text: Si fortuna foveat, vincam.
translation: I may win if I have luck.

text: Modo mihi est fortuna.
translation: I'm just lucky.

text: Rursus in arma feror, mortemque miserrimus opto. / Nam quod consilium aut quæ jam fortuna dabatur?
translation: Then again I fly / to arms – to arms, in frenzy of despair, / and long in utter misery to die. / What other choice was left, what other chance to try?

text: legem nocens veretur, fortunam innocens.
translation: The guilty fear the law, the innocent fortune.

text: Thomas Mariae bonam fortunam optavit.
translation: Tom wished Mary good luck.

text: Quisque parat sibi fortunam.
translation: Everybody is the architect of their own fortune.

text: Ostendistine ei novum illum librum quem emisti?
translation: Did you show him that new book you bought?

text: Num urbs Novum Eboracum in California est?
translation: Surely the city of New York is not in California, is it?

text: Novum Eboracum in America Foederata est.
translation: New York is in the United States.

text: Esne etiam assuefactus domo novo tuo?
translation: Have you gotten settled into your new house yet?

text: Debeo tapetum novum pro camera emere.
translation: I have to buy a new rug for the room.

text: Quid nomen est novo amico tuo?
translation: What is your new friend's name?

text: Thomas et brevior et gravior quam Ioannes est.
translation: Tom is shorter and heavier than John.

text: Maria in cubiculo suo graviter dormit.
translation: Mary is in her bedroom, sound asleep.

text: Thomas multo gravior quam Maria est.
translation: Tom is much heavier than Mary.

text: Ea multo gravior quam is est.
translation: She's much heavier than him.

text: Decies gravior es quam ego.
translation: You're ten times heavier than I am.

text: Hominibus gravis est statisticam percipere.
translation: People are very bad at understanding statistics.

text: Thomas est longissimus in familia sua.
translation: Tom is the tallest in his family.

text: Longo tempore ad pharmacopolium non ivi.
translation: I have not gone to the pharmacy in a long time.

text: Longum iter emensus mendacia longa reportat.
translation: Long ways, long lies.

text: Hoc est longe omnium optimum.
translation: This is by far the best of all.

text: Longum iter a centro sumus.
translation: We are a long way from the center.

text: Luna longe a Terra abest.
translation: The moon is distant from the earth.

text: Thomas Mariaque parvum hortum post domum suam habent.
translation: Tom and Mary have a small garden behind their house.

text: Cubiculum meum parvum est, sed mihi satis est.
translation: My room is small, but it's big enough for me.

text: Hic liber est tam parvus quam ille.
translation: This book is as small as that one.

text: Hic liber est aeque parvus ac ille.
translation: This book is as small as that one.

text: Hic liber est aeque parvus atque ille.
translation: This book is as small as that one.

text: Num parvam pueri mensam vides?
translation: You haven’t seen the boy’s little table, have you?

text: Scisne cur uxor Thomae eum reliquerit?
translation: Do you know why Tom's wife left him?

text: Biennium fuit ex quo me reliquit.
translation: It's been two years since she left me.

text: Terribile spectaculum eum horrore concussum reliquit.
translation: He shuddered with horror at the grisly sight.

text: Hoc post nos relinquamus ac progrediamur.
translation: Let's put this behind us and move on.

text: Thoman hic solum relinquere non possumus.
translation: We can't leave Tom here by himself.

text: Dixit se me numquam relicturus esse.
translation: He said that he'd never leave me.

text: Amicus meus Amastan de amicis Tatoebae saepe scribit.
translation: My friend Amastan often writes about his friends on Tatoeba.

text: Non volo scribere satiram. Tamen satira saepe resultatum est.
translation: I don't want to write satire. However, satire is often the result.

text: Hic liber ab adultis saepe legitur.
translation: This is a book often read by adults.

text: Saepe suo de patre Thomas narratat.
translation: Tom talks a lot about his father.

text: Thomas fratrem suum non saepe videt.
translation: Tom doesn't see his brother often.

text: Saepe litigium Thomae est cum uxore.
translation: Tom often quarrels with his wife.

text: Thomas saepius dicit me uxorem suam esse.
translation: Tom often tells people I'm his wife.

text: "Quid officium præstabas illi?" "Legebam ei sæpius."
translation: "What job did you do for her?" "I often read to her."

text: Aestate saepius quam hieme ambulamus.
translation: In summer, we walk more often than in winter.

text: Laesa saepius repugnat ovis.
translation: Tread on a worm, and it will turn.

text: Optimi natatores saepius submerguntur.
translation: Good swimmers, at last, are drowned.

text: Os magnum est tibi, et multum loqueris.
translation: You have a big mouth, and you talk a lot.

text: Os pueri rubrum est.
translation: The mouth of the child is red.

text: Noli cani os iactare.
translation: Don't throw the dog a bone.

text: Nolite cani os iactare.
translation: Don't throw the dog a bone.

text: Os halat 'ha'h ha'h'.
translation: The mouth breathes 'ha-h ha-h'.

text: Os meum mundum est.
translation: My mouth is clean.

text: Cubiculum meum altero tanto maius est quam eius.
translation: My room is twice as big as his.

text: Duas feles habet: altera nigra, altera alba est.
translation: He keeps two cats: one is black, and the other white.

text: Duas feles habet. Altera alba, altera nigra est.
translation: She has two cats. One is white and one is black.

text: Duas feles habet. Altera alba est, altera nigra.
translation: She has two cats. One is white and the other one is black.

text: Duas raedas habet; altera raeda est Benz, altera Porsche.
translation: He has two cars; one is a Benz and the other is a Porsche.

text: Thomas altero tanto maior est me.
translation: Tom is twice as big as me.

text: Thomas dixit se Mariam semper detestaturus esse.
translation: Tom said that he would always detest Mary.

text: Maria dixit se Thoman semper detestaturam esse.
translation: Mary said that she would always detest Tom.

text: Scio illum ab ea semper amatum fuisse.
translation: I know that he has always been loved by her.

text: Didymus mane Potionem Sinensem semper bibit.
translation: Tom always drinks tea in the morning.

text: Scimus Thoman non semper id facere.
translation: We know Tom doesn't always do that.

text: Semper litigium Thomae est cum uxore.
translation: Tom always quarrels with his wife.

text: Elementa sunt quattuor: ignis, aqua, aer et terra.
translation: The elements are four: fire, water, air and earth.

text: Ignis non potest impediri per medias mensuras.
translation: Fire cannot be prevented by half measures.

text: Urbs ignī dēlēta est.
translation: The city was destroyed by fire.

text: Domus igni deleta est.
translation: The house was destroyed by fire.

text: Ignis sub ponte est.
translation: There is fire under the bridge.

text: Sub ponte ignis est.
translation: There is fire under the bridge.

text: "Cur libros in ignem eiicis?" "Quia algeo."
translation: "Why are you throwing books in the fire?" "Because I'm cold."

text: Maria imagines photographicas in ignem eiecit.
translation: Mary threw the photos in the fire.

text: Thomas Bibliam in ignem eiecit.
translation: Tom threw the Bible in the fire.

text: Maria Bibliam in ignem eiecit.
translation: Mary threw the Bible in the fire.

text: Noli ea in ignem eiicere!
translation: Don't throw those things in the fire!

text: Cur ea in ignem eiicis?
translation: Why are you throwing those things in the fire?

text: Quid est timendum ei, qui mortem non timet?
translation: What should he fear, who doesn't fear death?

text: Nihil spero, nihil timeo; liber sum.
translation: I hope for nothing, I fear for nothing, I am free.

text: Nihil spero, nihil timeo; libera sum.
translation: I hope for nothing, I fear for nothing, I am free.

text: Quid times, ubi nihil est timendum?
translation: What are you afraid of, when there is nothing to fear?

text: Thomas, audiens patris interfectorem in Italia esse, timuit illo ire.
translation: Hearing that his father's killer was in Italy, Tom was afraid to go there.

text: Non mortem, sed mori, timeo.
translation: I do not fear death, but dying.

text: Thomas se scelus commitere non arbitrabatur.
translation: Tom didn't think he was committing a crime.

text: "Sed regna Tyri germanus habebat / Pygmalion, scelere ante alios immanior omnes".
translation: "But soon her brother filled the throne of Tyre, / Pygmalion, swoln with sin."

text: "Tum vero ardemus scitari et quærere causas, / ignari scelerum tantorum artisque Pelasgæ."
translation: "Then, all unknowing of Pelasgian art / and crimes so huge, the story we demand."

text: "Ast illum, ereptæ magno inflammatus amore / conjugis et scelerum Furiis agitatus, Orestes / excipit incautum, patriasque obtruncat ad aras."
translation: "But mad with love's despair, / and stung with Furies for his spouse denied, / at length Orestes caught the wretch unware, / e'en by his father's shrine, and smote him then and there."

text: Et ego et tu debemus dormire, nonne?
translation: You and I both should go to sleep, right?

text: Quamquam mathematicam non amabam, logarithmis studere debui.
translation: Although I did not like math, I had to study logarithms.

text: Idem facere debes quod Thomas et Maria nunc faciunt.
translation: You should do the same thing Tom and Mary are doing.

text: Et ego et tu dormire debemus.
translation: You and I both should go to sleep.

text: Thomas pecuniam vult quam ei debes.
translation: Tom wants the money that you owe him.

text: Pecuniam amicis debere non mihi placet.
translation: I don't like owing money to my friends.

text: In aqua vivere non possum. Ego non sum piscis.
translation: I cannot live in water. I'm not a fish.

text: Nec possum tecum vivere nec sine te.
translation: I can't live with or without you.

text: Feles margarita est animal rarum quod in deserto vivit.
translation: The sand cat is a rare animal that lives in the desert.

text: Quot homines in urbe tua vivunt?
translation: How many people live in your town?

text: Pisces extra aquam vivere non possunt.
translation: Fish cannot live out of water.

text: Duae aquilae ūnā vīvere nōn possunt.
translation: Two eagles cannot live together.

text: Non ut edam vivo, sed ut vivam edo.
translation: I do not live to eat, but eat to live.

text: Caesare vivo res publica salva erat.
translation: While Caesar was alive the state was safe.

text: Vivorum memini nec possum oblivisci mortuorum.
translation: I remember the living and I can't forget the dead.

text: Discite, dum vivo mors inimica venis.
translation: Learn that while I live, you, vile death, come as an enemy.

text: Estne avis viva aut mortua?
translation: Is the bird alive or dead?

text: Quis sum? Poeta sum. Quid facio? Scribo. Quomodo vivo? Tantum vivo.
translation: Who am I? I am a poet. What do I do? I write. How do I live? I just live.

text: Habent sua fata libelli.
translation: Books have a fate of their own.

text: "Nec tu mensarum morsus horresce futuros: / fata viam invenient, aderitque vocatus Apollo."
translation: "Fear not this famine – 'tis an empty scare; / the Fates will find a way, and Phoebus hear thy prayer."

text: arma virumque cano, Troiae qui primus ab oris Italiam, fato profugus, Lavinaque venit litora.
translation: I sing of arms and the man, who first from the mouth of Troy, exiled by fate, came to Italy and the Lavinian shore.

text: Arma virumque cano, Trojæ qui primus ab oris / Italiam, fato profugus, Lavinjaque venit / litora.
translation: I sing of arms and the man, made a fugitive by fate, who first came from the coasts of Troy, to Italy and the Lavinian shores.

text: Ex verbis fatuum, ex sonitu cognoscimus ollas.
translation: A bird is known by its note, and a man by his talk.

text: Creisne mundum fatum habere?
translation: Do you think the world has a destiny?

text: Fatum suum nemo fugit.
translation: Nobody escapes their destiny.

text: Non opinor fatum esse quod viris, actionibus neglectis, accidit; opinor autem fatum esse quod illis, nisi agitur, occidit.
translation: I do not believe in a fate that falls on men however they act; but I believe in a fate that falls on them unless they act.

text: Potesne vocare Mariam et dicere ei quod hic sumus?
translation: Can you call Mary and tell her that we are here?

text: Ea mater mea est. Beatrix vocatur.
translation: This is my mother. Her name is Beatrice.

text: Is quem vocavisti frater meus est.
translation: The person you called is my brother.

text: Didymo dic, quaeso, Mariam eum vocavisse.
translation: Please tell Tom that Mary called.

text: Thomas dixit se vocem Mariae audire.
translation: Tom said he heard Mary's voice.

text: Thomas dixit se vocem Mariae audivisse.
translation: Tom said he heard Mary's voice.

text: Turris Khalifa hoc tempore caeliscalpium altissimus mundi est.
translation: Burj Khalifa is currently the tallest skyscraper in the world.

text: Illum montem ascendere non possumus. Altissimus est.
translation: We can't climb that mountain. It's too high.

text: Ille est mons altissimus mundi.
translation: That is the highest mountain in the world.

text: Mons altissimus Sloveniae est Triglavus.
translation: The highest mountain of Slovenia is the Triglav.

text: Qui mons altissimus mundi est?
translation: What's the highest mountain in the world?

text: Recessus etiam inflationem altam attulit.
translation: The recession also brought high inflation.

text: Dominus Ioannes delibat sorbitionem quam femina sua paravit.
translation: Mr. Jones is tasting the soup his wife made.

text: Pater nunc cenam in culina parat.
translation: Father is cooking dinner in the kitchen now.

text: Placuitne tibi cibus, quem Thomas paravit?
translation: How did you like the food Tom made?

text: In culina est, quia cenam parat.
translation: She is in the kitchen because she's making dinner.

text: Thomas paniculos fartos in culina parat.
translation: Tom is in the kitchen making sandwiches.

text: Mater in culina cibum parat.
translation: Mom is preparing a meal in the kitchen.

text: Deus hominem ad suam imaginem creavit; ipse miles est.
translation: God created man in his own image, God is a warrior.

text: Avus meus miles per bellum erat.
translation: My grandfather was a soldier in the war.

text: Pompeius tam fortis miles est ut amici eum "Magnum" vocent.
translation: Pompey is such a brave soldier that his friends call him "The Great".

text: Militem aut monachum facit desperatio.
translation: Desperation makes the soldier or the monk.

text: Miles negavit mortem timendam esse.
translation: The soldier said that death is not to be feared.

text: Non omnes milites fortes sunt.
translation: Not all policemen are brave.

text: Ad mediam urbem ibimus ut placentam Neapolitanam edamus.
translation: We are going downtown to eat pizza.

text: Thomas in Australia ad medium mensem octobrem remanebit.
translation: Tom is going to stay in Australia until the middle of October.

text: Haec via te ad mediam urbem ducet.
translation: This road will lead you to the center of town.

text: Didymus et Maria ad mediam urbem eunt ut placentam Neapolitanam edant.
translation: Tom and Mary are going downtown to eat pizza.

text: Num ad mediam urbem ibimus?
translation: We aren’t going to the city centre, are we?

text: Didymus ad mediam urbem ivit.
translation: Tom went downtown.

text: At ille: Obsecro, inquit, Domine, mitte quem missurus es.
translation: But he said: I beseech thee, Lord, send whom thou wilt send.

text: Dum crucificitur, Spartacus "vae," inquit, "vobis, servi liberum crucificentes".
translation: As he was being crucified, Spartacus said, "Woe to you slaves, for you crucify a free man."

text: Thomas inquit Mariam illud cur fecerit Ioanni dicere non debere.
translation: Tom said Mary shouldn't tell John why she did that.

text: Cum rogarem num post longam deambulationem fessa esset, ''aliquantum'' inquit.
translation: When I asked her if she was tired after the long walk, she said, "Sort of."

text: Rex intellecto fuco, quid, inquit, an tu facies me canem ?
translation: The King, having understood the trick, says what, would you claim that I am a dog?

text: “Sanusne est?”, inquit. “Valet, inquiunt, et ecce Rachel filia eius venit cum grege”.
translation: He said: Is he in health? He is in health, say they: and behold, Rachel, his daughter, cometh with his flock.

text: Thomas audire potuit Mariam in cubiculo suo canentem.
translation: Tom could hear Mary singing in her bedroom.

text: Putabam me audire aliquem in cubiculum introire.
translation: I thought I heard somebody enter the room.

text: Non poteramus audire id quod dicebat Thomas.
translation: We couldn't hear what Tom was saying.

text: Non poteramus audire ea quae dicebat Thomas.
translation: We couldn't hear what Tom was saying.

text: Maria dicit se Thoman audivisse loquentem gallice.
translation: Mary says she heard Tom speaking French.

text: Thomas id quod dicebatur audire non potuit.
translation: Tom couldn't hear what was being said.

text: Thomas putat Mariam etiam nunc in Australia habitare.
translation: Tom thinks Mary is still living in Australia.

text: Thomas putat Mariam etiam nunc Bostoniae habitare.
translation: Tom thinks Mary is still living in Boston.

text: Putabam te in Park Street domicilium habere.
translation: I thought you lived on Park Street.

text: Thomas et Maria se stertere non putant.
translation: Tom and Mary don't think they snore.

text: Qui se satis didicisse putat, nihilum didicit.
translation: He who thinks he has learned enough has learned nothing.

text: Quot animalia in hoc vivario esse putas?
translation: How many animals do you think are in this zoo?

text: Puto Thoman etiam nunc in Park Street habitare.
translation: I think Tom still lives on Park Street.

text: Puto Thoman etiam nunc in Australia habitare.
translation: I think Tom is still living in Australia.

text: Puto istam aquam tibi non potandam fuisse.
translation: I think you shouldn't have drunk that water.

text: Puto eum apud domum parentum suorum esse.
translation: I think he's at his parents place.

text: Non puto me id tibi facere posse.
translation: I don't think that I can do that for you.

text: "Ubi est tuus pater nunc?" "Puto eum esse Lugduni."
translation: "Where is your father now?" "I believe he is in Lyons."

text: "Quot annos natus es?" "XVI annos natus sum."
translation: "How old are you?" "I'm 16 years old."

text: "Quot annos nata es?" "XVI annos nata sum."
translation: "How old are you?" "I'm 16 years old."

text: Constructivismus natus est in Russia circa annum 1920.
translation: Constructivism was born in Russia around 1920.

text: Haec sculptura plus quam ducentos annos habet.
translation: This sculpture is more than two thousand years old.

text: Duobus annis maior natu est, quam ego.
translation: He's three years older than me.

text: Scio Thoman aliquot annis maior natu quam Mariam esse.
translation: I know Tom is a few years older than Mary is.

text: Laborare non possum, cum illic stas.
translation: I can't work with you standing there.

text: Mater eius in ostio stabat.
translation: His mother was standing in the doorway.

text: Puer in terrore immobilis stetit.
translation: The boy stood still in horror.

text: Regina iuxta regem stabat.
translation: The queen stood beside the king.

text: Thomas prope aditum stabat.
translation: Tom was standing near the entrance.

text: Magister prope me stabat.
translation: The teacher was standing near me.

text: Maiore voce loquere ut omnes te audiant.
translation: Speak louder so that everyone may hear you.

text: Clariore voce loquere ut omnes te audiant.
translation: Speak louder so that everyone may hear you.

text: Tunc Iacob osculatus est Rachel et elevata voce flevit.
translation: And having watered the flock, he kissed her: and lifting up his voice wept.

text: Haec vox in dictionario non invenitur.
translation: This term is not found in the dictionary.

text: Thōmās litterās Marīae magnā vōce lēgit.
translation: Tom read Mary's letter aloud.

text: Vir cum vōce suppressā dīxit.
translation: The man spoke in a low voice.

text: Melius est pedibus mori quam genibus vivere.
translation: Better to die on our feet, than to live on our knees.

text: Utrum cibi genus melius esse tibi videtur: Iaponense an Sinense?
translation: Which type of food do you think is better: Japanese or Chinese?

text: Hic flos genus rosae est.
translation: This flower is a kind of rose.

text: Quid genus paniculi farti vis?
translation: What kind of sandwich do you want?

text: Cum pediludio ludebam, genu vulneravi.
translation: I hurt my knee when I was playing soccer.

text: Genu vulveravit, cum cecidit.
translation: He hurt his knee when he fell.

text: Non refert quam multos, sed quam bonos libros habeas.
translation: It doesn't matter how many books you have, but how good they are.

text: "Cur rides solus?" "Quid refert tua?"
translation: "Why are you laughing alone?" "What business is it of yours?"

text: Haec res mihi Thomae memoriam refert.
translation: That reminds me of Tom.

text: Haec res mihi tui memoriam refert.
translation: That reminds me of you.

text: Quidquid autem gravius erat, referebant ad eum, faciliora tantummodo iudicantes.
translation: And whatsoever was of greater difficulty they referred to him, and they judged the easier cases only.

text: Nomen tuum in indicem referetur.
translation: Your name will be added to the list.

text: Thomas Iohannem hic non cessaturum esse scit.
translation: Tom knows John isn't going to stop here.

text: Thōmās scit mē hodiē venīre nōn posse.
translation: Tom knows that I can't come today.

text: Nolo familiam meam scire quid mihi obtigerit.
translation: I don't want my family to know what's become of me.

text: Hoc unum scio, me nihil scire.
translation: I only know this: that I know nothing.

text: Scire velim quot annos nata sit.
translation: I'd like to know how old she is.

text: Velim scire num Thomas opus absolverit.
translation: I wonder whether or not Tom is done.

text: Prō certō sciō Thōman nōbīs subventūrum esse.
translation: I'm sure Tom will help us.

text: Scio Thoman nescire Mariam hoc non fecisse.
translation: I know that Tom doesn't know that Mary didn't do that.

text: Scio Thomam id facere non posse.
translation: I know Tom isn't able to do that.

text: Scio Thoman pulchriorem esse quam ego.
translation: I know that Tom is more handsome than I.

text: Scio Mariam pulchriorem esse quam ego.
translation: I know that Mary is more beautiful than I.

text: Scio Thoman fuisse tuum amicum dilectissimum.
translation: I know Tom was your best friend.

text: Vidi mentes optimas meae generationis dementiā destructas.
translation: I saw the best minds of my generation destroyed by madness.

text: In vestimentis non est sapientia mentis.
translation: It's not the gay coat that makes the gentleman.

text: Spero fore ut istam mentem mutes.
translation: I hope you change your mind.

text: Satanas est inventio mentis humanae.
translation: Satan is an invention of the human mind.

text: Ei dixi me mutavisse mentem.
translation: I told him I'd changed my mind.

text: Non est creator nisi mens.
translation: There's no creator besides the mind.

text: Cur non Mariae pecuniam, quam petivit, modo reddidisti?
translation: Why didn't you just give Mary the money she asked for?

text: "Id est satis mihi." "Sed quando reddes?"
translation: "That is enough for me." "But when will you give it me back?"

text: "Reddam tibi hodie." "Addendum fuit, Deo juvante."
translation: "I will give it back today." "You should have added, 'with God's help'."

text: Nec verbum verbo curabis reddere fidus interpres.
translation: Do not worry too much, O faithful translator, about translating word for word.

text: Redde Caesari quae sunt Caesaris, et quae sunt Dei Deo.
translation: Return to Caesar what belongs to Caesar and to God that which belongs to God.

text: Munus tibi reddere non possumus.
translation: We can't give you your job back.

text: Cur hoc in flumine natare non licet?
translation: Why is swimming not allowed in this river?

text: Tom et Maria dixerunt se sperare licere id facere.
translation: Tom and Mary said they hoped they'd be allowed to do that.

text: Licet illud facere nemini praeter me!
translation: No one but me is allowed to do that!

text: Hoc in flumine natare non licet.
translation: Swimming is not permitted in this river.

text: Dixisti mihi licere cum Thoma loqui.
translation: You said I could talk to Tom.

text: In hoc loco venari non licet.
translation: Hunting is prohibited in this area.

text: Thomas Mariam solam in bibliotheca sedentem vidit.
translation: Tom saw Mary sitting by herself in the library.

text: Mariam censebam solam id facere non posse.
translation: I thought Mary wouldn't be able to do that by herself.

text: Ne me solam relinquas.
translation: Don't leave me alone.

text: Thomas dixit Mariam fugisse priusquam advenisset.
translation: Tom said that Mary had run away before he arrived.

text: Magnum animal e therotrophio fugit.
translation: A large animal fled from the zoo.

text: Puer timéns né capiátur fugit.
translation: The frightened boy flees so he will not be caught.

text: Superbiam fuge, neque eam in animum aut in sermonem sinas obrepere.
translation: Run from arrogance, do not allow it to seep into your mind or into your speech.

text: Canis et feles fugerunt.
translation: The dog and the cat ran away.

text: Senex fugit, sed vix.
translation: The old man escaped, but with difficulty.

text: Quæ respondit: A facie Sarai dominæ meæ ego fugio.
translation: And she answered: I flee from the face of Sarai, my mistress.

text: Thomas a nullo videbatur, ipse autem omnes videbat.
translation: Tom was seen by no one, but he himself saw everyone.

text: Multae sunt sententiae, quibus nulla est traductio.
translation: There are many sentences that have no translation.

text: Qui amant de nulla re aut de omnibus dubitant.
translation: People who love doubt nothing, or doubt everything.

text: Eo tempore nulla erat radiophonia in Iaponia.
translation: There were no radios in Japan in those days.

text: Abire volo, sed mihi pecunia nulla est.
translation: I want to go, but I don't have money.

text: Credunt in hunc calorem nulla crystalla esse.
translation: It is thought that at this temperature there are no crystals.

text: Quidnam in rerum natura prius fuerit, an gallina an ovum?
translation: What came first? The egg or the hen?

text: Rustica natura semper sequitur sua iura.
translation: No fine cloth can hide the clown.

text: Natura mihi numquam naturalis visa est.
translation: Reality has never felt real to me.

text: Homo natura animal sociale est.
translation: Man is by nature a political animal.

text: Natura non facit saltus.
translation: Nature does not make jumps.

text: Nullum facit inutiliter natura.
translation: Nature does nothing uselessly.

text: Mors est remedium Naturae pro omnibus.
translation: Death is Nature's remedy for all things.

text: Quot medicōs nōvistī nātūrae cordis perītōs?
translation: How many cardiologists do you know?

text: Qui naturam sequitur sapiens est.
translation: He who follows Nature is wise.

text: Num homines pars naturae sunt?
translation: Are humans a part of nature?

text: Nonne homines pars naturae sunt?
translation: Are humans a part of nature?

text: Inter linguas transferre multos esse errores sinit atque orationem contra naturam.
translation: Translating from one language to the other makes room for a lot of mistakes and unnatural speech.

text: Bonum est nobis aliarum gentium mores intellegere.
translation: It is good for us to understand other cultures.

text: Bonum est nobis mores alienos intellegere.
translation: It is good for us to understand other cultures.

text: Hic mos usque adhuc est retentus.
translation: This custom is still observed today.

text: Thomae mores mutare opus est.
translation: Tom needs to change his behavior.

text: Mores eius tibi imitandi sunt.
translation: You should imitate his behavior.

text: Alia aetas alios mores postulat.
translation: Other times, other customs.

text: Quam diu vixit eius beneficiorum non oblita est.
translation: She did not forget his kindness as long as she lived.

text: Non est parvum beneficium, quod profectum est ab optima voluntate.
translation: It is not a small kindness, which has come from very good inclinations.

text: Beneficium accipere libertatem est vendere.
translation: Accepting a favor is selling your freedom.

text: Nemo accepta beneficia calendario inscribit.
translation: An injury graves itself in metal, but a benefit writes itself in water.

text: "Consulis bene tibi, qui habeas rationem temporis. Sed valetne pater?" "Recte, Dei beneficio."
translation: "You do well to hear others' opinions, who value your time. But how is your father?" "Well, thanks be to God."

text: "Sed heus, cura ne macules, alioquin ægre commodabo posthac." "Nempe essem indignus beneficio."
translation: "But hey, take care not to blot it, or I won't be likely to lend it you again." "Indeed, I would not deserve any favours."

text: Non capiunt ullos hostilia pectora somnos.
translation: Enemies don't sleep.

text: Vos ambos toto pectore amo.
translation: I love both of you with all my heart.

text: Deus est in pectore nostro.
translation: There is a god within us.

text: Toto pectore te amo.
translation: I love you with all my heart.

text: Obstupui, miroque incensum pectus amore, / compellare virum et casus cognoscere tantos. / Progredior portu, classes et litora linquens.
translation: Straightway / I burn to greet them, and the tale explore, / and from the harbour haste, and leave the ships and shore.

text: "Prima hominis facies et pulchro pectore virgo / pube tenus; postrema immani corpore pistris, / delphinum caudas utero commissa luporum."
translation: "A maiden to the waist, with bosom fair / and human face; below, a monstrous whale, / down from whose wolf-like womb hangs many a dolphin's tail."

text: Bona fide spero te mox ex morbo convalescere.
translation: I sincerely hope that you will soon recover from your illness.

text: Cui magis fidis: mihi an ei?
translation: Who do you trust more: me or him?

text: Hoc fidem amicis eius monstrat.
translation: This shows his loyalty to his friends.

text: Tibi fidem dare non possum.
translation: I can't give you any guarantees.

text: Nullum donum pretiosius fide.
translation: No gift is more precious than trust.

text: Nonne datae fidei reminisceris?
translation: Don't you remember your promise?

text: Fides montes transmovere potest, ego autem dynamitem malo.
translation: Faith can move mountains, but I prefer dynamite.

text: Tum vero manifesta fides, Danaumque patescunt / insidiæ.
translation: Then, then I see that Hector's words were right, / and all the Danaan wiles are naked to the light.

text: Fides eius in Deo inconcussa est.
translation: Her faith in God is unshaken.

text: Nullum donum pretiosius quam fides.
translation: No gift is more precious than trust.

text: Haec fides publica mea est.
translation: This is my passport.

text: An adhuc est fides?
translation: Does loyalty even exist anymore?

text: Quam diu est cum manuum curam non habuisti?
translation: When was the last time you got a manicure?

text: Thomas mihi dixit id Mariae curae esse.
translation: Tom told me Mary was interested.

text: Hic puer magnam curam nobis dat.
translation: This boy gives us a lot of trouble.

text: Mammalia curam catulorum suorum gerunt.
translation: Mammals care for their young.

text: Habes curam cordis tui.
translation: You have to take care of your heart.

text: Age curam valetudinis tuae.
translation: Take care of your health.

text: Thomas plenus irae fratrem suum interfecit.
translation: Filled with anger, Tom killed his own brother.

text: Incensi ira in interfectorem eramus.
translation: We were filled with anger against the murderer.

text: Thomas nullam causam irae habebat.
translation: Tom had no reason to be angry.

text: Iram in eum effudit.
translation: She took her anger out on him.

text: Sine ira et studio.
translation: Without anger and fondness.

text: Exarsere ignes animo, subit ira cadentem / ulcisci patriam et sceleratas sumere pœnas.
translation: Then, fired with passion and revenge, I burn / to quit Troy's downfall and exact the fee / such crimes deserve.

text: Quot verba habet glossarium tuum in lingua Toki Pona?
translation: How many words does your Toki Pona vocabulary have?

text: Suntne verba anōmala in linguā Esperanticā?
translation: Are there any irregular verbs in Esperanto?

text: Hodie verba "ser" et "estar" discemus.
translation: Today we are going to study the verbs “ser” and “estar”.

text: His verbis eum non persuadebis.
translation: You will not persuade him with these words.

text: His verbis eam non persuadebis.
translation: You will not persuade her with these words.

text: Nulla verba eum admonere potuerunt.
translation: No words were able to admonish him.

text: Erant quidam pueri prope flumen ludentes.
translation: There were some boys playing near the river.

text: Thomas Mariaque prope oceanum habitant.
translation: Tom and Mary live close to the ocean.

text: Schola mea prope stationem est.
translation: My school is near to the station.

text: Scio me prope mortem esse.
translation: I know that I am near death.

text: Thomas domum prope lacum habet.
translation: Tom owns a house near the lake.

text: Thomas domum prope flumen aedificavit.
translation: Tom built a house near the river.

text: Thomas etiam nunc in Australia apud parentes habitat.
translation: Tom still lives in Australia with his parents.

text: Thomas etiam nunc Bostoniae apud parentes habitat.
translation: Tom still lives in Boston with his parents.

text: Qua lingua cum parentibus tuis loqueris?
translation: What language do you speak with your parents?

text: Parentes Mariae in magna domo habitant.
translation: Mary's parents live in a big house.

text: Soror etiam nunc apud parentes habitat.
translation: My sister still lives with our parents.

text: Habitatne Thomas etiam nunc apud parentes?
translation: Does Tom still live with his parents?

text: Thomas Roma abiit, qua in urbe a puero habitaverat.
translation: Tom left Rome, the city he had lived in since he was a boy.

text: Thomas Mariaque pueros docunt clavichordo canere.
translation: Tom and Mary give piano lessons to children.

text: Pueri puellaeque in horto ludunt.
translation: The boys and girls play in the garden.

text: Pueri mane in ludum eunt.
translation: The children go to school in the morning.

text: Aliqui pueri in mari natant.
translation: Some children are swimming in the sea.

text: Aliqui pueri in oceano natant.
translation: Some children are swimming in the ocean.

text: Non est puer qui heri hic venit.
translation: He is not the boy who came here yesterday.

text: Is est puer quem heri vidi.
translation: This is the boy whom I saw yesterday.

text: Quis est puer in flumine natans?
translation: Who is the boy swimming in the river?

text: Ioannes est puer qui librum legit.
translation: John is the boy who is reading the book.

text: Cum puer eram, in Australia habitabam.
translation: I lived in Australia when I was a child.

text: Cum puer eram, spinacam non edebam.
translation: I didn't like spinach when I was a child.

text: Eum sine causa ex officio movere non possumus.
translation: We can't just fire him.

text: Fere semper fleo cum motus sum.
translation: I almost always cry when I get emotional.

text: Ne moveant animos frivola verba tuos.
translation: For mad words deaf ears.

text: Thomas ne se movere quidem poterat.
translation: Tom couldn't even move.

text: Malum bene condītum ne movēris.
translation: Don’t open old wounds.

text: Cur movere me non possum?
translation: Why can't I move?

text: Omnes dolores tolerabiles esse debent, etiamsi magni sunt.
translation: All sorrows should be tolerable, even if they are great.

text: Difficile est magno dolori paria verba reperire.
translation: It's hard to find words to describe such pain.

text: Attenderunt populi et commoti sunt, dolores obtinuerunt habitatores Philisthææ.
translation: Nations rose up, and were angry: sorrows took hold on the inhabitants of Philisthiim.

text: Dixit se ei nunquam dolorem fecisse.
translation: He said he never hurt her.

text: Quae est causa cotidiana doloris?
translation: What is the usual cause for the pain?

text: Gaudia principium sunt nostri dolores.
translation: After pleasure comes pain.

text: Intimo amore non est dolor, nec fuit umquam.
translation: There's no suffering in the depths of love, and there never has been.

text: Perfer et obdura, dolor hic tibi proderit olim.
translation: Be patient and tough; someday all this pain will be useful to you.

text: Amor non solum dolor est.
translation: Love isn't just pain.

text: Amor non solum est dolor.
translation: Love isn't just pain.

text: "Nate, quis indomitas tantus dolor excitat iras? / Quid furis, aut quonam nostri tibi cura recessit?"
translation: "O son, what mean / these transports? Say, what bitter grief doth move / thy soul to rage untamed? Where vanished is thy love?"

text: Omnis gens electa est a Deo.
translation: Every people is chosen.

text: Thomas e gentibus est.
translation: Tom is a gentile.

text: Constat quod gentibus periculos opus esse sed crudelitas debet non esse necesse.
translation: That people need to be exposed to dangers is clear, but cruelty should not be necessary.

text: Faciamque te crescere vehementissime et ponam te in gentes; regesque ex te egredientur.
translation: And I will make thee increase exceedingly, and I will make nations of thee, and kings shall come out of thee.

text: Verumtamen et gentem, cui servituri sunt, ego iudicabo, et post hæc egredientur cum magna substantia.
translation: But I will judge the nation which they shall serve, and after this they shall come out with great substance.

text: Ibi experti sumus incredibilem humanitatem gentis, suppeditantis, nobis omnia, mira alacritate; hospitium, ignem, cibum, vestes, viaticum.
translation: There we experienced the incredible humanity of the nation, furnishing us with all things, with wonderful chearfulnes; lodging, fire, meat, cloaths, provisions for our way home.

text: Prae tibi in hoc ludo modo tiro sum.
translation: Compared to you, I'm only a beginner at this game.

text: Prae tibi in hoc ludo modo rudis sum.
translation: Compared to you, I'm only a beginner at this game.

text: "Quid es ita laetus?" "Quia pater meus modo venit."
translation: "Why are you so happy?" "Because my father has just arrived."

text: "Quando advenit?" "Modo; ut dixi tibi jam."
translation: "When did he return?" "Just now, as I just told you."

text: Feles modo oculis torvis eum contemplavit.
translation: The cat just gave him a stern look.

text: Puto illam paulum lassam modo esse.
translation: I think she is just a bit tired.

text: In eius via nec flores nec arbores erant.
translation: There were no flowers or trees on his street.

text: Scisne quae via ad domum meam ducat?
translation: Do you know which road leads to my house?

text: Nemo omnium in via visus est.
translation: Not a soul was to be seen in the street.

text: Linea alba in media via est.
translation: There is a white line in the middle of the road.

text: Nemo alius in via erat.
translation: There was no one else on the road.

text: Multi homines in via sunt.
translation: There are many people in the street.

text: Scisne quam viam Thomas et Maria accolant?
translation: Do you know what street Tom and Mary live on?

text: Suntne multae viae in illō vīcō?
translation: Are there many streets in that village?

text: In Tatoeba omnes viae Bostoniam ducunt.
translation: At Tatoeba, all roads lead to Boston.

text: Scisne quam viam Thomas accolat?
translation: Do you know what street Tom lives on?

text: Viam ad stationem mihi monstravit.
translation: He showed me the way to the station.

text: Vidi puerum ire per viam.
translation: I saw a boy crossing the street.

text: Est mihi amicus, cui nomen est Thomas.
translation: I have a friend whose name is Tom.

text: Sorores meae omnibus amicae et urbanae sunt.
translation: My sisters are friendly and kind to everyone.

text: Non omnis, qui nobis arridet, amicus est.
translation: To smile to one's face and to stab one in the back.

text: Id feci quod amicus Mariae sum.
translation: I did it because I'm Mary's friend.

text: Thomas est solus amicus quem habeo.
translation: Tom is the only friend I have.

text: Amicus meus in hac domo habitat.
translation: My friend lives in that house.

text: Didymus dixit se multos amicos Bostoniae habuisse.
translation: Tom said he had plenty of friends in Boston.

text: Amicum habeo cuius pater est scriptor illustris.
translation: I have a friend whose father is a famous novelist.

text: Amicum habeo cuius pater est histrio illustris.
translation: I have a friend whose father is a famous actor.

text: Habet duos amicos qui sunt peregrini.
translation: He has two friends who are foreigners.

text: Amicum habeo cuius pater medicus est.
translation: I have a friend whose father is a doctor.

text: Num sciebas Thoman amicum Mariae esse?
translation: Did you know Tom was Mary's boyfriend?

text: Hic canis se movere non vult, quia pes ei dolet.
translation: This dog doesn't want to move because his paw hurts.

text: Pes valde mihi dolet.
translation: My foot really hurts.

text: Et si videris sensatum, evigila ad eum, et gradus ostiorum illius exterat pes tuus.
translation: If you see a wise man, seek him early; let your feet wear down the threshold of his door.

text: Roma cecidit. Cur cecidit Imperium Romanum?
translation: Rome fell. Why did the Roman Empire fall?

text: Quare Imperium Romanum Orientale non occidit?
translation: Why didn't the Eastern Roman Empire fall?

text: Quotiens de Imperio Romano cogitas?
translation: How often do you think about the Roman Empire?

text: Imperium orbis terrarum cupit.
translation: He wants to rule over the world.

text: Ubi est imperium Romanum?
translation: Where is the Roman Empire?

text: Sub imperio eius sumus.
translation: We are under his command.

text: Scio laborem tuum facilem non esse.
translation: I know that your work is not easy.

text: Num laborem meum facilem esse putas?
translation: Do you think that my work is easy?

text: Thomas laborem Mariae facilem esse putat.
translation: Tom thinks that Mary's work is easy.

text: Maria laborem Thomae facilem esse putat.
translation: Mary thinks Tom's work is easy.

text: Multo labore dives factus est.
translation: He became rich through hard work.

text: Multo labore dives facta est.
translation: She became rich through hard work.

text: Labor tuus non tam difficilis est quam meus.
translation: Your work is not as difficult as mine.

text: Labor meus non tam facilis est quam tuus.
translation: My work is not as easy as yours.

text: Ecclesiae turris sub annis labare coepit.
translation: The church's steeple is beginning to crumble with age.

text: Deo non dante, nil valet labor.
translation: Whom God teaches not, man cannot.

text: Ecclesiae turris incipit vetustate labare.
translation: The church's steeple is beginning to crumble with age.

text: Labor pars vitae nostrae est.
translation: Work is part of our lives.

text: Pusillum pusillo si addas, fiet ingens acervus.
translation: A heap is made of grains.

text: Pyrrhus cum ingenti exercitu multisque elephantis in Italiam venit.
translation: Pyrrhus came into Italy with a great army and many elephants.

text: Pons ab ingenti roboto deletus est.
translation: The bridge was destroyed by a giant robot.

text: Ingentes serpentes hac in silva sunt.
translation: There are giant snakes in this forest.

text: Ingentes serpentes hac in insula sunt.
translation: There are giant snakes on this island.

text: Graeci equum ligneum ingentis magnitudinis fecerunt.
translation: The Greeks built a giant wooden horse.

text: Mori malo quam rem talem facere.
translation: I would rather die than do such a thing.

text: Talem rem numquam ante videram.
translation: I had never seen anything like that before.

text: Cur talem librum debes legere?
translation: Why do you need to read such a book?

text: Talem vitam agere non possum.
translation: I can't live that kind of life.

text: Ineptum est cum tali disputare.
translation: There's no point in arguing with someone like that.

text: Sunt multae linguae tales.
translation: There are a lot of languages like that.

text: Talis equus tibi erit, qualis curator equorum.
translation: Such captain, such retinue.

text: Talis puer ab omnibus amatur.
translation: Such a boy is loved by everybody.

text: Heus puer, adfer huc talos.
translation: Hey boy, bring us the dice.

text: Talis est haec lingua.
translation: That's how the language is.

text: Qualis pater, talis filius.
translation: Like father, like son.

text: Talis amor est verus.
translation: This is true love.

text: Plerique politici multum loquuntur et parum faciunt.
translation: Most politicians talk a lot and do little.

text: Bene Graece loquitur et parum Anglice.
translation: He speaks Greek well and a little English.

text: Thomas de Bostonia parum scire videtur.
translation: Tom doesn't seem to know much about Boston.

text: Iste mihi parum placet.
translation: I'm not a big fan of his.

text: Verum velle, parum est.
translation: Hell is paved with good intentions.

text: Si tibi magnae opes suppetant, multum tribue; si parvae, parum, sed libenter; quoniam beneficentia hominem ab aeterna morte liberat.
translation: If you have great resources available, grant much; if small, grant little, but willingly; because kindness liberates man from the eternal death.

text: Mea puella illum passerem plus oculis suis amabat.
translation: My girl loved that sparrow more than her own eyes.

text: Ei ego iam linguam praecidam atque oculos effodiam!
translation: I will cut off his tongue and gouge out his eyes!

text: Piscis ille videre non potest quia oculos non habet.
translation: That fish cannot see because he does not have eyes.

text: Averte oculos tuos a me, quia ipsi me avolare fecerunt.
translation: Turn away thine eyes from me, for they have overcome me.

text: Sed Lia lippis erat oculis, Rachel decora et venusto aspectu.
translation: But Lia was blear-eyed: Rachel was well favoured, and of a beautiful countenance.

text: Oculus quo Deum video est idem quo Deus videt me.
translation: The eye with which I see God is the same eye with which God sees me.

text: Interea magnum sol circumvolvitur annum, / et glacialis hiems Aquilonibus asperat undas.
translation: Meanwhile the sun rolls round the mighty year, / and wintry North-winds vex the waves once more.

text: Apparent rari nantes in gurgite vasto, / arma virum tabulæque et Troja gaza per undas.
translation: Strewn here and there behold / arms, planks, lone swimmers in the surges grey, / and treasures snatched from Trojan homes away.

text: Franguntur remi; tum prora avertit et undis / dat latus; insequitur cumulo præruptus aquæ mons.
translation: The shattered oars start forth; / round swings the prow, and lets the waters sweep / the broadside. Onward comes a mountain heap / of billows, gaunt, abrupt.

text: Provehimur pelago vicina Ceraunia juxta, / unde iter Italiam cursusque brevissimus undis. / Sol ruit interea et montes umbrantur opaci.
translation: On fly the barks o'er ocean. Near us frown / Ceraunia's rocks, whence shortest lies the way / to Italy. And now the sun gows down, / and darkness gathers on the mountains grey.

text: Tollimur in cœlum curvato gurgite, et idem / subducta ad Manes imos desidimus unda.
translation: Now curls the wave, and lifts us to the sky, / now sinks and, plunging in the gulf we lie.

text: Hi summo in fluctu pendent, his unda dehiscens / terram inter fluctus aperit; furit æstus arenis.
translation: These, horsed astride / a surge's crest, rock pendent o'er the deep; / to those the wave's huge hollow, yawning wide, / lays bare the ground below; dark swells the sandy tide.

text: Et in spiritu furoris tui congregatæ sunt aquæ; stetit ut agger unda fluens, coagulatæ sunt abyssi in medio mari.
translation: And with the blast of thy anger the waters were gathered together: the flowing water stood, the depths were gathered together in the midst of the sea.

text: Nesciebam te aegrotare, itaque te in nosocomio non invisi.
translation: I didn't know that you were sick, so I didn't visit you in the hospital.

text: Reversus est itaque illo die Esau itinere suo in Seir.
translation: So Esau returned that day, the way that he came, to Seir.

text: Videtur quasi hoc vespere frigescet itaque cura ne gravedine plangaris.
translation: It looks like the temperature is going to drop tonight, so be careful not to catch a cold.

text: Fessus eram, itaque non ivi.
translation: I was tired, so I didn't go.

text: Mansit itaque Isaac in Geraris.
translation: So Isaac abode in Gerara.

text: Præcesserunt itaque munera ante eum, ipse vero mansit nocte illa in castris.
translation: So the presents went before him, but himself lodged that night in the camp.

text: Sic ait atque animum pictura pascit inani, / multa gemens, largoque humectat flumine vultum.
translation: Thus upon the empty show / he feeds his soul, while ever and again / deeply he sighs, and tears run down his cheeks like rain.

text: In quit ridens, ac placido vultu, ne quis remoretur nostrum cursum, certamen est de cupa cerevistae.
translation: He says smiling, and with a pleasant countenance, please nobody stop our running, the race is for a tankard of ale.

text: Ad Cain vero et ad munus illius non respexit. Iratusque est Cain vehementer, et concidit vultus eius.
translation: But to Cain and his offerings he had no respect: and Cain was exceeding angry, and his countenance fell.

text: Mirantur dona Aeneæ, mirantur Iulum, / flagrantesque dei vultus simulataque verba / pallamque et pictum croceo velamen acantho.
translation: They praise the boy, his glowing looks divine, / the words he feigned, the royal gifts he brought, / the robe, the saffron veil with bright acanthus wrought.

text: Ei erat in facie rigido vultus horribilis et mihi odibilis cui antehac tales similes nunquam super imagines humanas vidi.
translation: On his rigid face there stood an expression of horror, and as it seemed to me, of hatred, such as I have never seen upon human features.

text: Spero fore ut in crastina probatione non cadam.
translation: I hope I don't flunk tomorrow's test.

text: Telehorasis integrus est, etiamsi de mensa cecidit.
translation: The TV set is intact even though it fell off the desk.

text: Magna arbor in procella cecidit.
translation: A big tree fell in the storm.

text: Thomas in aquam frigidam cecidit.
translation: Tom fell into the cold water.

text: Tantum in terra Gessen, ubi erant filii Israel, grando non cecidit.
translation: Only in the land of Goshen, where the children of Israel were, the hail fell not.

text: "Cur simia de arbore cecidit?" "Nescio, Thoma. Quare?" "Quia mortua erat."
translation: "Why did the monkey fall out of the tree?" "I don't know, Tom. Why?" "Because it was dead."

text: Natare possum, sed in flumine libenter non nato.
translation: I know how to swim, but I don't like swimming in the river.

translation: But anon new foes / come swarming up, while ever and again / fast fall the showers of stones, and thick the javelins rain.

translation: I've been put in charge of this project.

text: Eadem lex erit indigenæ et colono, qui peregrinatur apud vos.

translation: He made sure the law was enforced.

text: Lex II: Mutationem motus proportionalem esse vi motrici impressae, et fieri secundum lineam rectam qua vis illa imprimitur.
translation: Law II: The alteration of motion is ever proportional to the motive force impressed; and is made in the direction of the right line in which that force is impressed.

text: Praeses dixit terram in periculo esse.

text: Hoc in periculum vocaberis.
translation: That will put you in danger.

translation: Tom exposed himself to danger.

translation: Tom has lived in Boston since he was born.

translation: He was born in England, but was educated in America.

text: Haec arbor non in Aegypto sed in Syria nascitur.
translation: This tree does not grow in Egypt but in Syria.

translation: "How can a man be born when he is old?" Nicodemus asked.

translation: It was in 1950 that he was born.

text: Quot e magnis eis exercitibus patriam rursus spectaturi erant?

translation: Tell me about your fantastic dreams in which you are the emperor of the universe and command an army of billions of robots.

translation: How the mighty have fallen, and the weapons of war have perished!

translation: Things done rightly, good deeds will never perish.

translation: Both of her sons died during the war.

translation: Then, amid the lurid light, / I see Troy sinking in the flames around, / and mighty Neptune's walls laid level with the ground.

text: Si ex pontem caderes, servari non posses.
translation: If you were to fall from that bridge, it would be almost impossible to rescue you.

translation: I will keep these words my whole life.

translation: Cutlery is kept in these drawers.

text: Is sum qui te servavi.
translation: I'm the one who saved you.

translation: So to the palace she escorts her guest, / and calls for festal honours in the shrine.

translation: Still deep in her heart rankled the judgment of Paris and the injustice of her scorned beauty, and the hated race, and the honors of kidnapped Ganymede.

text: Et capita ante aras Phrygio velamur amictu; / præceptisque Heleni, dederat quæ maxima, rite / Junoni Argivæ jussos adolemus honores.
translation: Veiled at her shrines in Phrygian hood we stand, / and chief to Juno, mindful of the seer, / burnt-offerings pay, as pious rites demand.

translation: So spake he and on altars, reared aright, / due victims offered, and libations meet; / a bull to Neptune and Apollo bright, / to tempest a black lamb, to Western winds a white.

text: Non me dignum est hoc dicere.
translation: It's not proper for me to say that.

text: Nemo Thoman laude dignum putat.
translation: No one thinks Tom is worthy of praise.

text: Nemo Mariam laude dignam putat.

translation: Human nature is excusable when it errs.

text: Non dubito quin dignus fueris.
translation: I'm sure you deserved it.

translation: Tom doesn't deserve any praise.

text: Placuit pharaoni consilium et cunctis ministris eius.

translation: And they all agreed, and circumcised all the males.

text: Claude fenestrae portaeque cuncti!
translation: Close all the windows and doors!

text: Si autem circumcidi nolueritis, tollemus filiam nostram et recedemus.

text: Oscula oris ejus me caelo tollunt.
translation: Her kisses take me to heaven.

text: Saepe est ut populus nolit tyrannum tollere, sæpe est ut non possit.
translation: Often the people do not wish to depose a tyrant, often they cannot not.

text: Tollens autem Booz decem viros de senioribus civitatis dixit ad eos: Sedete hic.
translation: And Boaz, taking ten men of the ancients of the city, said to them: Sit ye down here.

text: Surge, tolle puerum et tene illum manu tua, quia in gentem magnam faciam eum.
translation: Arise, take up the boy, and hold him by the hand, for I will make him a great nation.

text: En Rebecca coram te est; tolle eam et proficiscere, et sit uxor filii domini tui, sicut locutus est Dominus.
translation: Behold, Rebecca is before thee, take her and go thy way, and let her be the wife of thy master's son, as the Lord hath spoken.

text: Thomas negavit se facere posse ea quae rogavissem.

text: Equites arbori equos suos alligaverunt.

text: Habuit quoque in comitatu currus et equites; et facta est turba non modica.

text: Persequentesque Aegyptii ingressi sunt post eos, omnis equitatus pharaonis, currus eius et equites per medium maris.
translation: And the Egyptians pursuing went in after them, and all Pharaoh's horses, his chariots and horsemen, through the midst of the sea.

text: Et scient Aegyptii quia ego sum Dominus, cum glorificatus fuero in pharaone, in curribus atque in equitibus eius.
translation: And the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord, when I shall be glorified in Pharaoh, and in his chariots, and in his horsemen.

text: Et ait Dominus ad Moysen: Extende manum tuam super mare, ut revertantur aquæ ad Aegyptios super currus et equites eorum.
translation: And the Lord said to Moses: Stretch forth thy hand over the sea, that the waters may come again upon the Egyptians, upon their chariots and horsemen.

text: Thomas volebat ut Maria tradat eum omnibus amicis suis.

text: Parva scintilla saepe magnam flammam excitat.

text: Hostes veritatis vocem Mariae fortasse silentiare fecerunt, sed flammam quam in cordibus nostris accendit extinguere non possunt.

text: Ac primum silici scintillam excudit Achates, / suscepitque ignem foliis, atque arida circum / nutrimenta dedit rapuitque in fomite flammam.

text: Tum Cererem corruptam undis Cerealiaque arma / expediunt fessi rerum, frugesque receptas / et torrere parant flammis et frangere saxo.

text: Semper flamma fumo est proxima.

text: Clarus es. Gratias tibi ago pro bono opere quod agis.
translation: You're brilliant. Thank you for the good work that you're doing.

text: Imple hebdomadam hanc, et alteram quoque dabo tibi pro opere, quo serviturus es mihi septem annis aliis.
translation: Make up the week of days of this match: and I will give thee her also, for the service that thou shalt render me other seven years.

text: Complevitque Deus die septimo opus suum, quod fecerat, et requievit die septimo ab universo opere, quod patrarat.
translation: And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made: and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had done.

text: Ait ad eos rex Aegypti: Quare, Moyses et Aaron, sollicitatis populum ab operibus suis? Ite ad onera vestra.
translation: The king of Egypt said to them: Why do you Moses and Aaron draw off the people from their works? Get you gone to your burdens.

text: Dixitque pharao: Multus nimis iam est populus terræ; videtis quod turba succreverit; quanto magis si dederitis eis requiem ab operibus?
translation: And Pharaoh said: The people of the land are numerous; you see that the multitude is increased; how much more if you give them rest from their works?

text: Anita mea lycopersica in horto suo colit.
translation: My aunt grows tomatoes in her garden.

text: Huius raedae color mihi placet.
translation: I like the color of this car.

text: Auri color similis est aeris.
translation: Gold is similar in color to brass.

text: Color cutis non est stirps.
translation: A skin color is not a lineage.

text: Amicus meus hanc domum colit.
translation: My friend lives in this house.

text: Elephantes Asiam et Africam colunt.
translation: Elephants live in Asia and Africa.

text: "Hunc tu olim cœlo, spoliis Orientis onustum, / accipies secura; vocabitur hic quoque votis".
translation: "Him, crowned with vows and many an Eastern prize, / thou, freed at length from care, shalt welcome to the skies."

text: Haud mora, continuo perfectis ordine votis, / cornua velatarum obvertimus antennarum, / Grajugenumque domos suspectaque linquimus arva.
translation: This done, the sailyards to the wind we veer, / and leave the Grecians and the land of fear.

text: Omni desiderio desideravi nunc videre faciem tuam, et utinam aliquando impleret Deus votum meum, antequam moriar.
translation: I have always wanted to see your face and now pray that God grant my desire before I die.

text: De gladio tuo vives et fratri tuo servies. Tempusque veniet, cum excutias et solvas iugum eius de cervicibus tuis.
translation: Thou shalt live by the sword, and shalt serve thy brother: and the time shall come, when thou shalt shake off and loose his yoke from thy neck.

text: Puella, de qua tibi locutus sum, hic habitat.
translation: The girl I told you about lives here.

text: Puella, de qua tibi locutus sum, Kiotii habitat.
translation: The girl I told you about lives in Kyoto.

text: Puella, de qua tibi locutus sum, Tokii habitat.
translation: The girl I spoke to you about lives in Tokyo.

text: Urbs in qua natus sum valde pulchra est.
translation: My hometown is very pretty.

text: Urbs in qua nata sum valde pulchra est.
translation: My hometown is very pretty.

text: Urbs in qua natus es valde pulchra est.
translation: Your hometown is very pretty.

text: Num homo unquam in alia tellure pedem figet?
translation: Will a human ever set foot on a different planet?

text: Mercurium de Tellure aspectare difficile est.
translation: From Earth, Mercury is difficult to observe.

text: Mercurius sicut Tellus Marsque saxosus est.
translation: Mercury has a rocky body like the Earth and Mars.

text: Mercurius ter Soli propior est Tellure.
translation: Mercury is three times closer to the Sun than Earth.

text: Mercurius tam Soli proximus est ut perdifficulter de Tellure aspectetur.
translation: Mercury is so near the Sun that it's very difficult to observe from Earth.

text: Cum tam proximus sit Soli, Mercurius de Tellure difficulter aspectatur.
translation: From Earth, Mercury is difficult to observe because it's so close to the Sun.

text: In hac urbe magnus numerus ludorum est.
translation: There are a great number of schools in this city.

text: Recentioribus temporibus discipulorum numerus peregre proficiscentium crebruit.
translation: The number of students going overseas has been increasing lately.

text: Stellarum in caelo infinitus est numerus.
translation: The number of stars in the sky is infinite.

text: Numerus atomicus pro ferro est XXVI.
translation: The atomic number of iron is 26.

text: Numerus atomicus pro hydrogenio est I.
translation: The atomic number for hydrogen is 1.

text: Numerus atomicus pro cupro est XXIX.
translation: The atomic number for copper is 29.

text: Amata est ab omnibus qui eam cognoverunt.
translation: She was loved by everyone who knew her.

text: Cum exaltaveritis Filium hominis, tunc cognoscetis quia ego sum.
translation: When ye have lifted up the Son of Man, then shall ye know that I am he.

text: Numquam mihi te eam cognovisse dixisti.
translation: You never told me you knew her.

text: Quanto cognosco eam, tanto amo eam.
translation: The more I know her, the more I love her.

text: Et tamen fratres ipse cognoscens non est cognitus ab eis.
translation: And though he knew his brethren, he was not known by them.

text: Nesciebam Thoman Mariam non cognovisse.
translation: I didn't know Tom didn't know Mary.

text: Graecia capta ferum victorem cepit et artes intulit agresti Latio.
translation: Greece, once conquered, in turn conquered its uncivilized conqueror, and brought the arts to rustic Latium.

text: Graecia capta ferum victorem cepit.
translation: Greece, conquered, took captive her savage conqueror.

text: Quisquis repulit amorem, tutus ac victor fuit.
translation: In love's war, he who flies is conqueror.

text: Nonne iam satis linguarum est sine linguis constructis?
translation: Aren't there enough languages without artificial languages?
