text: "Velisne plus potionis Arabicae?" "Nolo, gratias. Satis bibi."
translation: "Will you have some more coffee?" "No, thanks. I've had enough."

text: Si satis pecuniae haberem, id emere potuerim.
translation: If I had enough money, I could buy it.

text: Si satis pecuniae haberem, illam raedam emerem.
translation: If I had enough money, I'd buy that car.

text: Cibus mihi emendus est, sed satis pecuniae non habeo.
translation: I need to buy food, but I don't have enough money.

text: Si satis pecuniae haberem, hoc emerem.
translation: If I had enough money, I'd buy this.

text: Satius est aliquando modo nihil dicere.
translation: Sometimes it's better to just not say anything.

text: Satius est aliquando modo tacere.
translation: Sometimes it's better to just not say anything.

text: Satius est aliquando tacere.
translation: Sometimes it's better not to say anything.

text: In patria natus non est propheta vocatus.
translation: Never was a prophet valued in his native country.

text: In patria mea non multi sunt qui Germanice loquantur.
translation: There are not many people who speak German in my country.

text: Qua lingua in patria tua loqueris?
translation: What language do you speak in your country?

text: Non licet ei discedere e patria.
translation: He's not allowed to leave the country.

text: Nulla patria in terra tuta est, in hac aetate nucleari.
translation: No country on earth is safe in this nuclear age.

text: Pulchrum est pro patria mori.
translation: It's beautiful to die for your country.

text: In Lusitania habito et patriam meam amo.
translation: I live in Portugal, and I love my homeland.

text: Thomas populi scito in patriam restitutus est.
translation: Tom was brought back to his country by order of the people.

text: Nos parati sumus ad defendendam patriam.
translation: We are ready to defend the country.

text: Thomas in patriam suam redire vult.
translation: Tom wants to return to his country.

text: Maria in patriam suam redire vult.
translation: Mary wants to return to her country.

text: Aliquando in patriam meam redibo.
translation: Some day I will return to my country.

text: Indiligentiae sunt casuum causa.
translation: Carelessness is the cause of accidents.

text: Qui e nuce nucleum esse vult, frangit nucem.
translation: He that will eat the kernel, must crack the nut.

text: Frater meus de arbore cecidit, sed nihil fregit.
translation: My brother fell out of the tree but didn't break anything.

text: Frater meus de arbore cecidit sed nihil fregit.
translation: My brother fell out of the tree but did not break anything.

text: Thomas Mariam fenestram frangere vidit.
translation: Tom saw Mary break the window.

text: Hic aquae deiectus fractus est.
translation: This shower is broken.

text: Malum vas non frangitur.
translation: A creaking door hangs long on its hinges.

text: Lingua Malabarica praecipue in civitate Kerala loquitur.
translation: Malayalam is mainly spoken in Kerala.

text: Romulus civitatem ex nomine suo Romam vocavit.
translation: Romulus named the city Rome, in accordance with his own name.

text: Mercatoria confrictio inter duas civitates quolibet tempore oriri potest.
translation: Trade friction might arise between the two nations at any moment.

text: Civitates Foederatae Americae sunt barba Canadae.
translation: America is Canada's beard.

text: Caeliscalpium in media civitatis est.
translation: The skyscraper is in the center of the city.

text: Invadentne Civitates Foederatae Groenlandiam?
translation: Is America going to invade Greenland?

text: Esther Novi Eboraci cum uxoribus suis habitat.
translation: Esther lives in New York with her wives.

text: Novi hominem qui Ruthenice optime loquitur.
translation: I know a person who speaks Russian very well.

text: Maria mihi se te novisse dixit.
translation: Mary told me that she knew you.

text: Didymus et Mariam et Ioannem novit.
translation: Tom knows both Mary and John.

text: Novi aliquem qui Lingua Francogallice loquatur.
translation: I know someone who speaks French.

text: Omnium rerum invidiosa est. Est mulier invidiosissima quam umquam novi.
translation: She is jealous of everything. She is the most jealous woman I have ever known.

text: Nemo Graecorum in proeliis melior quam Achilles erat.
translation: No one of the Greeks was better in battles than Achilles.

text: proelium ad flūmen pugnātum est.
translation: The battle was fought by the river.

text: Ego multis in proeliis pugnavi.
translation: I have fought in many battles.

text: Non levabit gens contra gentem gladium, nec exercebuntur ultra ad praelium.
translation: Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.

text: Nihil eripit fortuna, nisi quod dedit.
translation: Fortune takes away nothing except what she has given.

text: Scio Thoman me ex periculo eripuisse.
translation: I know that Tom rescued me.

text: Eum ex periculo eripuerunt.
translation: They rescued him from danger.

text: Me ex periculo eripuit.
translation: He saved me from danger.

text: Scio Thoman me eripuisse.
translation: I know Tom rescued me.

text: Tum sic reginam alloquitur, cunctisque repente / improvisus ait: "Coram, quem quaeritis, adsum, / Troius Aeneas, Libycis ereptus ab undis".
translation: Then to the queen, all wondering, he exclaimed, / "Behold me, Troy's AEneas; I am here, / the man ye seek, from Libyan waves reclaimed."

text: Absolute insensata fiunt in hoc mundo.
translation: Absolutely nonsensical things happen in this world.

text: Mundum sine electricitate imaginari non possum.
translation: I couldn't imagine the world without electricity.

text: Ego sum deus novi mundi.
translation: I am the god of the new world.

text: Mundus periculosior est quam putabam.
translation: The world is more dangerous than I thought.

text: Mundus ad novum bivium pervenit.
translation: The world has come to a new crossroads.

text: Deus mundum creavit sex diebus.
translation: God created the earth in six days.

text: Illud adduci vix possum, ut ei hoc dixeris.
translation: I can't believe you told him that.

text: Ita fessus sum, ut ambulare vix possim.
translation: I am so tired that I can hardly walk.

text: Ita fessa sum, ut ambulare vix possim.
translation: I am so tired that I can hardly walk.

text: Ita fessus erat, ut ambulare vix posset.
translation: He was so tired that he could hardly walk.

text: Ita fessus erat, ut stare vix posset.
translation: He was so tired that he could hardly stand.

text: In Iaponia, omnes Iaponica loquuntur et vix aliquis anglice loquitur.
translation: In Japan, everyone speaks Japanese and hardly anyone speaks English.

text: Quot homines in illa erant navi?
translation: How many people were aboard that ship?

text: Ad Japoniam per navem traiectoriam ivimus.
translation: We rode a ferry to Japan.

text: In nave manere iussus sum.
translation: I was told to stay on the ship.

text: Gubernator navem ad portum gubernat.
translation: A pilot guides the ship toward the port.

text: Multas naves in portu vidimus.
translation: We saw many ships in the harbor.

text: Multae naves in portu sunt.
translation: There are many ships in the harbor.

text: Haec navis spatialis a trudatore iontis propellitur.
translation: This spacecraft is powered by ion thrusters.

text: Pirata, gladium in manu tenens, in pontem navis insiluit.
translation: The pirate, sword in hand, leapt onto the deck.

text: Navis iam in portu est.
translation: The ship is now in the harbor.

text: Quid est nomen navis tuae?
translation: What's the name of your ship?

text: Navis classis KRI Nanggala ex Indonesia declaratur submersa in oceano Bali.
translation: The navy ship KRI Nanggala from Indonesia is declared sunk in the Bali Ocean.

text: Quota hora navis proficiscitur?
translation: What time does the ship leave?

text: "His lacrimis vitam damus, et miserescimus ultro."
translation: "So, moved at length to pity by his tears, / we spare him."

text: De oculis meis lacrimae lapsae sunt.
translation: Tears ran down my face.

text: De oculis eius lacrimae lapsae sunt.
translation: Tears rolled down her face.

text: Oculi Didymi humidi lacrimis erant.
translation: Tom's eyes were wet with tears.

text: Thomas lacrimas tenere non potuit.
translation: Tom couldn't hold back his tears.

text: Sermo eius lacrimis eos commovebat.
translation: His speech moved them to tears.

text: Nihil enim lacrima citius arescit.
translation: Nothing dries more quickly than a tear.

text: Ille ridebat dum illa lacrimabat.
translation: He was laughing while she was crying.

text: Lacrima mihi, ut flumen fiat.
translation: Cry me a river.

text: Constitit et lacrimans: "Quis jam locus", inquit, "Achate, / quæ regio in terris nostri non plena laboris?"
translation: Pensive he stood, and with a rising tear, / "What lands, Achates, on the earth, but know / our labours?"

text: Errare humanum est, sed in errare perseverare diabolicum.
translation: To err is human, but to persist in error is diabolical.

text: Errare humanum est, ergo Thomas et Maria homines sunt.
translation: To err is human; therefore Tom and Mary are humans.

text: Humanum lingua quam cognovimus figmentum est.
translation: Language, as we know it, is a human invention.

text: Errare humanum est, ignoscere divinum.
translation: To err is human, to forgive divine.

text: Diabolus est inventio cerebri humani.
translation: The devil is an invention of the human brain.

text: Corpus humanum duos pulmones habet.
translation: The human body has two lungs.

text: Cultrum durum est, cocta solana tuberosa mollis est.
translation: The knife is hard, the boiled potato is soft.

text: Molli paulatim flavescit campus arista.
translation: Slow and sure wins the race.

text: Non iacet in molli veneranda scientia lecto, ipsa sed assiduo parta labore venit.
translation: No one acquires knowledge worthy of respect by lying on a soft bed, but by hard and constant work.

text: Maria dixit Thomam mollem esse.
translation: Mary said that Tom was a sissy.

text: Plumbum est molle et grave. Ferrum est durum et durior calybs.
translation: Lead is soft and heavy. Iron is hard and steel harder.

text: Castori pilus est mollissimus.
translation: A beaver's fur is very soft.

text: Liber, quem emi, hodie mane mihi allatus est.
translation: The book that I bought was delivered to me this morning.

text: Raeda, quam emi, hodie mane mihi allata est.
translation: The car that I bought was delivered to me this morning.

text: Hodie mane Didymus Mariam per telephonum adivit.
translation: Tom called Mary this morning.

text: Opus est me in perendinum Bostoniae manere.
translation: I need to stay in Boston until the day after tomorrow.

text: Robertum et Mariam vidi cum Katharinam manerem.
translation: I saw Bob and Mary while I was waiting for Kate.

text: Vesperi est Crespuculum, manē Aurora et Diluculum.
translation: In the evening is twilight; in the morning the breaking and dawning of the day.

text: Volucri curru medium secat agmen.
translation: In a swift chariot he crosses the ranks.

text: Ea lapsa repente ruinam / cum sonitu trahit et Danaum super agmina late / incidit.
translation: Down it goes / with sudden crash upon the Danaan train, / dealing wide ruin.

text: Non tulit hanc speciem furiata mente Corœbus, / et sese medium injecit periturus in agmen.
translation: That sight Coroebus brooked not. Stung with gall / and mad with rage, nor fearing to be slain, / he plunged amid their columns.

text: "Hic Juno Scæas sævissima portas / prima tenet, sociumque furens a navibus agmen / ferro accincta vocat. "
translation: "Here, girt with steel, the foremost in the fight, / fierce Juno stands, the Scaean gates before, / and, mad with fury and malignant spite, / calls up her federate forces from the shore."

text: Invadunt urbem somno vinoque sepultam; / cæduntur vigiles, portisque patentibus omnes / accipiunt socios atque agmina conscia jungunt.
translation: Now, stealing forward, on the town they fall, / buried in wine and sleep, the guards o'erbear, / and ope the gates; their comrades at the call / pour in and, joining bands, all muster by the wall.

text: Sol est rex caeli, luna est regina siderum.
translation: The sun is the king of the sky, the moon is the queen of the stars.

text: "Siderum Bella" bis vidi.
translation: I have seen "Star Wars" twice.

text: Ille simul manibus tendit divellere nodos, / perfusus sanie vittas atroque veneno; / clamores simul horrendos ad sidera tollit.
translation: The hands trying to untie the knots / the ribbons speckled on the forehead / of poisonous spit, horrendous cries / he goes vibrating, making the air pulsate.

text: Semper appetentes gloriae Romani fuerunt.
translation: The Romans were always thirsty for glory.

text: Gloria virtutem tanquam umbra sequitur.
translation: Glory follows virtue as if it were its shadow.

text: Sic transit gloria mundi.
translation: Thus passes the glory of the world.

text: Gloria nostra aeterna erit.
translation: Our glory will be eternal.

text: Et in multitudine gloriæ tuæ deposuisti adversarios tuos; misisti iram tuam, quæ devoravit eos sicut stipulam.
translation: And in the multitude of thy glory thou hast put down thy adversaries: thou hast sent thy wrath, which hath devoured them like stubble.

text: Cumque loqueretur Aaron ad omnem cœtum filiorum Israel, respexerunt ad solitudinem, et ecce gloria Domini apparuit in nube.
translation: And when Aaron spoke to all the assembly of the children of Israel, they looked towards the wilderness; and behold the glory of the Lord appeared in a cloud.

text: Thoman iam diu mortuum esse perspicuum est.
translation: Tom has obviously been dead for a while.

text: Quam diu hodie in schola fuisti?
translation: How long were you at school today?

text: Quam diu solus apud Thoman fuisti?
translation: How long were you alone with Tom?

text: Tempus effluxit. Diutius exspectare non possum.
translation: Time's up. I can't wait any longer.

text: Didymus et Maria diu amici fuerunt.
translation: Tom and Mary have been friends for a long time.

text: Eum invenissemus iam diu, si viveret.
translation: We’d have found him long ago, if he were alive.

text: Amo Paulum, tamquam si sit pater meus.
translation: I love Paul as if he were my father.

text: Lingua Russica est difficilis, tamquam pulchra.
translation: Russian is a difficult as well as a beautiful language.

text: "Eripe, nate, fugam, finemque impone labori. / Nusquam abero, et tutum patrio te limine sistam."
translation: "Haste, son, and fly; the fruitless toil give o'er. / I will not leave thee, but assist thy flight, / and set thee safely at thy father's door."

text: "Vos o, quibus integer ævi / sanguis, ait, solidæque suo stant robore vires, / vos agitate fugam."
translation: "Fly ye, who may, / whom age hath chilled not, nor the years impair."

text: "Prosequitur pavitans, et ficto pectore fatur: / 'Sæpe fugam Danai Troja cupiere relicta / moliri et longo fessi discedere bello.'"
translation: "And falteringly the traitor plays his part. / 'Oft, wearied by the war, the Danaans planned / to leave – and oh! had they but left – the land.'"

text: Hanc aquam bibere tutum non est.
translation: It's not safe to drink this water.

text: Tē absente, quis mē tuēbitur?
translation: Who will protect me while you are away?

text: Thomas modo te tueri conatur.
translation: Tom is just trying to protect you.

text: Tutus es, si tecum sum.
translation: You're safe if I'm with you.

text: Si tute sinis, iam hoc faciam.
translation: If it's OK with you, I'd like to do that now.

text: Volo liberos meos tutos servare.
translation: I want to keep my kids safe.

text: "Seu vos Hesperiam magnam Saturniaque arva, / sive Erycis fines regemque optatis Acesten, / auxilio tutos dimittam opibusque juvabo".
translation: "Whether ye sail to great Hesperia's shore /and Saturn's fields, or seek the realms that own / Acestes' sway, where Eryx reigned of yore, / safe will I send you hence, and speed you with my store."

text: Homines auribus suis minus quam oculis suis credunt.
translation: Men trust their ears less than their eyes.

text: "Sed me magna deum Genetrix his detinet oris."
translation: "Now, by Fate's decree, / here with the mother of the Gods I dwell."

text: Laetitia et verecundia rubebat auribus.
translation: What with joy and shame, she blushed to the ears.

text: Aures ad audiendum factæ sunt.
translation: Ears were made for hearing.

text: Obsecro, ut indumento oris uteris.
translation: Please wear a mask.

text: Oculis video, auribus audio.
translation: I see with my eyes and hear with my ears.

text: Male agitur cum illo, qui alieno nutritur arbitrio.
translation: He that waits upon another's trencher, makes many a little dinner.

text: Homo sum ; humani nihil a me alienum puto.
translation: I'm human; nothing human is foreign to me.

text: Bonum est fugienda aspicere in alieno malo.
translation: Learn from others' mistakes.

text: Homo sum et nihil humani a me alienum puto.
translation: I am human, and I think nothing human is alien to me.

text: Humani nihil a me alienum puto.
translation: I consider nothing human as alien to me.

text: Non habebis deos alienos coram me.
translation: Thou shalt not have strange gods before me.

text: Quo putas tempore huc adventurum esse Thomam?
translation: What time do you think Tom will get here?

text: Non dubito quin Thomas huc venturus sit.
translation: I don't doubt Tom will come here.

text: Credo Thomam iam huc accessurum esse.
translation: I'm sure Tom is on his way.

text: Huc veni ut aliquid tibi darem.
translation: I came here to give you something.

text: Huc veni ut aliquid tibi dicerem.
translation: I came here to tell you something.

text: Huc veni ut cum iis loquerer.
translation: I came here to talk to them.

text: Num licet nobis in tali re tacere?
translation: Can we be silent in such a situation?

text: Stultus quoque, si tacuerit, sapiens reputabitur.
translation: Let a fool hold his tongue, and he will pass for a sage.

text: Homo, qui tacere nescit, legere nescit.
translation: A man who does not know how to be silent does not know how to read.

text: Thomas et Maria tacere debuerunt.
translation: Tom and Mary should've kept their mouths shut.

text: Melius est tacere quam errare.
translation: It's better to stay silent than make a mistake.

text: Non vos duo iam tacetis?
translation: Won't you two just shut up already?

text: Quintili Vare, legiones redde!
translation: Quinctilius Varus, return my legions!

text: Potesne mihi ostendere quomodo hoc faciam?
translation: Can you show me how to do this?

text: Veni hodie vespere. Tibi quomodo ostendam.
translation: Come over tonight. I will show you how.

text: Experimenta ostenderunt hanc sententiam rectam esse.
translation: Experiments have shown that this statement is correct.

text: Ostende mihi quid in manu habes.
translation: Show me what's in your hand.

text: Vinum hominis animum ostendere solet.
translation: Wine is wont to show the mind of man.

text: Hoc tibi ostendere non possum.
translation: I can't show you this.

text: Sic demum socios, consumpta nocte, reviso.
translation: Back to my friends I haste.

text: Sine sociis nemo regere potest.
translation: No one can rule without allies.

text: Non amici, sed socii sumus.
translation: We're not friends, we're partners.

text: Sodales triginta Socii consociatio habet.
translation: The association has thirty members.

text: Socium in Hispania habemus.
translation: We have a colleague in Spain.

text: Sociam in Hispania habemus.
translation: We have a colleague in Spain.

text: Tam mala res nulla, quin sit quod prosit in illa.
translation: Nothing so bad as not to be good for something.

text: Quid hoc mihi nunc prodest?
translation: What good is that to me now?

text: Omnes doctorum conatus nihil profuerunt.
translation: All the efforts of the doctors were to no avail.

text: Si potes, ignotis etiam prodesse memento; utilius regno est meritis adquirere amicos.
translation: If you can, remember to be good even to strangers; it is more useful than a kingdom to obtain friends well-earned.

text: Dixit ergo Iudas fratribus suis: Quid nobis prodest, si occiderimus fratrem nostrum et celaverimus sanguinem ipsius?
translation: And Juda said to his brethren: What will it profit us to kill our brother, and conceal his blood?

text: Spiritus est qui vivificat: caro non prodest quidquam: verba quæ ego locutus sum vobis, spiritus et vita sunt.
translation: The Spirit gives life; the flesh counts for nothing. The words I have spoken to you are spirit and they are life.

text: Quales mugitus, fugit cum saucius aram / taurus et incertam excussit cervice securim.
translation: As when a wounded bull / shakes from his neck the faltering axe and, fain / to fly the cruel altars, roars in pain.

text: Ilicet obruimur numero; primusque Corœbus / Penelei dextra divæ armipotentis ad aram / procumbit.
translation: O'erwhelmed with odds, we perish; first of all, / struck down by fierce Peneleus by the fane / of warlike Pallas, doth Coroebus fall.

text: Vidi Hecubam centumque nurus, Priamumque per aras / sanguine fœdantem, quos ipse sacraverat, ignes.
translation: Saw where among a hundred daughters, stood / pale Hecuba, saw Priam's life-blood stain / the fires his hands had hallowed in the fane.

text: Sacerdotes in ara sacrificare possunt.
translation: The priests can sacrifice on the altar.

text: Sacerdos in ara sacrificare potest.
translation: The priest can sacrifice on the altar.

text: Hic ager numquam aratus est.
translation: This field has never been plowed.

text: "Huc tandem concede: hæc ara tuebitur omnes, / aut moriere simul."
translation: "Hither to this shrine retire, / and share our safety or our death."

text: Agricolae agros celeriter arabant.
translation: The farmers quickly plowed the fields.

text: Lumen candelae mihi placet.
translation: I like candlelight.

text: Luminibus careat quisquis te pinxit, et istum non pinxit naevum, quem Venus ipsa dedit.
translation: Blind be he whoever portrayed you yet did not paint that birthmark of yours gifted by Venus herself.

text: Ovum tegitur Testa, sub quā Albumen in hoc vitellus.
translation: The egg is covered with shell, under which is the white and within this the egg yolk.

text: Nix domus et arbores texit.
translation: The snow covered the houses and the trees.

text: Sub ovium pellibus lupos tegunt.
translation: They are wolves in sheep's clothing.

text: Magna tapeta texere non possum.
translation: I cannot weave big carpets.

text: Vertex hieme montis nive tegitur.
translation: The peak of the mountain is covered in snow in winter.

text: Avia mea texere amat.
translation: My grandmother likes to weave things.

text: Vita turpis ne morti quidem honestae locum relinquit.
translation: A life of shame leaves not to the dead even an honest place of rest.

text: Turpe est tales commentarios periodicos legere.
translation: It is foolish to read such a magazine.

text: Anas parva turpis est.
translation: The little duck is ugly.

text: Pauper verbum est turpe.
translation: Poor is an ugly word.

text: Litteras tuas magna cum voluptate legi.
translation: I read your letter with great pleasure.

text: Litteras tuas magna voluptate legi.
translation: I read your letter with great pleasure.

text: Summa voluptas ex discendo capitur.
translation: The keenest pleasure is derived from learning.

text: Quæ risit occulte dicens: Postquam consenui, et dominus meus vetulus est, voluptas mihi erit?
translation: And she laughed secretly, saying: After I am grown old, and my lord is an old man, shall I give myself to pleasure?

text: Dubito quod Thomas et Maria adhuc dormiunt.
translation: I doubt that Tom and Mary are still sleeping.

text: Thomas adhuc nescit me gravidam esse.
translation: Tom doesn't know yet that I am pregnant.

text: Puto Thoman adhuc Bostoniae esse.
translation: I think Tom is still in Boston.

text: Thomas adhuc domum Bostoniae habet.
translation: Tom still has a house in Boston.

text: Illa adhuc in culina est.
translation: She is still in the kitchen.

text: Infantem suum adhuc dormientem repperit.
translation: She found her baby still asleep.

text: Mihi pergratum esset, si quis mea gratia id faceret.
translation: I'd like it if someone did that for me.

text: "Visne potionem?" "Nolo, gratias. Nunc guberno."
translation: "Do you want a drink?" "No, thanks. I'm driving."

text: Thoman vocavi ut ei gratias agerem.
translation: I called Tom to thank him.

text: Huc veni ut tibi gratias agerem.
translation: I came here to thank you.

text: "Gratias tibi ago." "Tibi agendae sunt."
translation: "Thank you." "No, thank you."

text: Quod hoc fecisti, gratias tibi ago.
translation: Thank you for doing this.

text: Accipere quam facere praestat iniuriam.
translation: It is better to receive an injury than to cause one.

text: Thomas parvas iniurias accepit.
translation: Tom suffered minor injuries.

text: Et egressus die altero conspexit duos Hebræos rixantes dixitque ei, qui faciebat iniuriam: Quare percutis proximum tuum?
translation: And going out the next day, he saw two Hebrews quarrelling: and he said to him that did the wrong: Why strikest thou thy neighbour?

text: "Imperium Dido Tyria regit urbe profecta, / germanum fugiens. Longa est injuria, longæ / ambages; sed summa sequar fastigia rerum".
translation: "Queen Dido rules the land, who came from Tyre afar, / flying her brother. Dark the tale of crime, / and long, but briefly be the sum supplied."

text: Volenti non fit iniuria.
translation: To a willing person, injury is not done.

text: Non tam latera ecfututa pandas, ni tu quid facias ineptiarum.
translation: You wouldn't look so shagged out unless you were doing something naughty.

text: Tabula egimus circa metrum lata.
translation: We need a table about a meter wide.

text: Viae huius urbis latae sunt.
translation: The streets of this city are wide.

text: Fossa decem pedes lata est.
translation: The ditch is ten feet wide.

text: Quadratum quattuor latera aequalia habet.
translation: A square has four equal sides.

text: Quam lata haec via est?
translation: How wide is this road?

text: Dulce et decorum est pro patria mori.
translation: It is sweet and right to die for your homeland.

text: dulce et decorum est pro patria mori.
translation: Sweet and fitting it is to die for your country.

text: Hoc vinum nimis dulce esse censeo.
translation: I think this wine is too sweet.

text: Bona nox, amor meus. Dulcia somnia.
translation: Goodnight, my love. Sweet dreams.

text: Fructus huius arboris dulces sunt.
translation: The fruit of this tree is sweet.

text: Hoc libum valde dulce est.
translation: This cake is very sweet.

text: Ostende mihi faciem tuam, sonet vox tua in auribus meis; vox enim tua dulcis, et facies tua decora.
translation: Shew me thy face, let thy voice sound in my ears: for thy voice is sweet, and thy face comely.

text: Tum sic affari et curas his demere dictis: / "Quid tantum insano juvat indulgere dolori, / o dulcis conjux?"
translation: Then she addressed me thus, and comforted my care. / "What boots this idle passion? Why so fain / sweet husband, thus to sorrow and repine?"

text: Te usque ad extremum spiritum amabo.
translation: I'll love you until the day I die.

text: Omnium rerum mors est extremum.
translation: Death is the end of all things.

text: Profectique de Succoth castrametati sunt in Etham, in extremis finibus solitudinis.
translation: And marching from Socoth, they encamped in Etham, in the utmost coasts of the wilderness.

text: Ninguit extremis diebus Decembris.
translation: It snows on the last days of December.

text: Extrēmis malis extrēma remedia.
translation: Extreme evil needs an extreme remedy.

text: Extremis malis extrema remedia.
translation: For extreme ills, extreme remedies.

text: Nimerum hic erit extremus actus fabulae.
translation: Well this will be the last act of the play.

text: Qui canem alit exterum, huic praeter lorum nil fit reliquum.
translation: He that keeps another man's dog, shall have nothing left him but the line.

text: Hic erit extremus actus fabulae.
translation: This will be the last act of the play.

text: Habitavistine unquam in extera regione?
translation: Have you ever lived abroad?

text: "Quare agite, o tectis, juvenes, succedite nostris".
translation: "Welcome, then, heroes!"

text: Domus mihi est cum tecto caeruleo.
translation: I've got a house with a blue roof.

text: Domus mihi est cum tecto livido.
translation: I've got a house with a blue roof.

text: "Ubi est cattus?" "Est in tecto."
translation: "Where is the cat?" "It is on the roof."

text: Raptor mansionem de tecto intravit.
translation: The cat burglar must have entered the mansion from the roof.

text: Avem in tecto video.
translation: I see a bird on the roof.

text: Scalae quae ad tectum ducunt angustae, praeruptae obscuraeque sunt.
translation: The staircase leading to the rooftop is narrow, steep, and dark.

text: Si in solo sum, tectum statim video.
translation: If I am on the floor, I see the ceiling immediately.

text: Columba alba super tēctum est.
translation: There is a white dove on the roof.

text: Araneam in tectum ambulantem vidi.
translation: I saw a spider walking on the ceiling.

text: Tectum domus Thomae rubrum est.
translation: The roof of Tom's house is red.

text: Tectum domus rubrum est.
translation: The roof of the house is red.

text: Ut saepe summa ingenia in occulto latent!
translation: As often, the greatest geniuses lie hidden in the shadows!

text: Thomas me virum acerrimo ingenio esse dicit.
translation: Tom says I have charisma.

text: Alit lectio ingenium et studio faticatum reficit.
translation: Reading nourishes the imagination and restores it when tired of working.

text: Nullum magnum ingenium sine mixtura dementiae.
translation: Greatness is close to madness.

text: Studia difficilia ingenio vires dant.
translation: Hard studies make strong brains.

text: Divinum ingenium plena crumena facit.
translation: As long as I am rich and reputed, with solemn voice I am saluted.

text: Pax sine iustitia non pax est, sed indutiae.
translation: Peace without justice is a ceasefire.

text: Pax sine iustitia nihil aliud est quam indutiae.
translation: Peace without justice is a ceasefire.

text: Iam pax est inter vos duos?
translation: Is everything cool between you two?

text: "Pax tibi." "Et tibi quoque."
translation: "Peace be upon you." "Peace be upon you, too."

text: Pax in prospectu est.
translation: Peace is on the horizon.

text: Pax maximi momenti est.
translation: Peace is very important.

text: Puella, quae clavichordo canit, soror mea est.
translation: The girl that plays the piano is my sister.

text: Puella quae cum Thoma canit est Maria.
translation: The girl singing with Tom is Mary.

text: Didymus clavichordo melius quam Maria canit.
translation: Tom plays the piano better than Mary.

text: Didymus clavichordo canit, dum Maria cantavit.
translation: Tom played the piano and Mary sang.

text: Hae puellae non loquuntur, sed canunt.
translation: These girls are not speaking but singing.

text: Minor nata sororum mearum optime canit.
translation: My youngest sister sings very well.

text: Libenter cano dum in acquae deiectu lavor.
translation: I like to sing while taking a shower.

text: Postquam cenam sumpsi, clavichordo cano.
translation: I play the piano after supper.

text: Cithara post scholam cano.
translation: I play the guitar after school.

text: Etiam magna tuba cano.
translation: I also play the trombone.

text: Etiam magna bucina cano.
translation: I also play the trombone.

text: Tibi habeam magnam gratiam si me iuvare possis.
translation: I'd be grateful if you could help me.

text: Non est mihi in manu utrum te iuvem.
translation: It's not in my power to help you.

text: Nec Thomas nec Maria hodie me iuvare debet.
translation: Neither Tom nor Mary has to help me today.

text: Thomas ad nos venit ut eum iuvaremus.
translation: Tom has come to us for help.

text: Te omni re qua possum cupio iuvare.
translation: I want to help you in every way I can.

text: Non dubito quin me iuturus sit.
translation: I don't doubt that he will help me.

text: Terra habet Montes, Sylvas, Campos, Animalia et Homines.
translation: The earth has mountains, woods, fields, animals and people.

text: Terra habet Montes, Sylvas, Campos, Animalia, Homines.
translation: Land has hill, woods, fields, animals and men.

text: Ego flos campi, et lilium convallium.
translation: I am the daffodil of Saron, the lily of the valley.

text: Oves in campo herbam edunt.
translation: The sheep in the field are eating grass.

text: Oppidum in campo situm est.
translation: The city is built on lowlands.

text: Cumque proficiscerentur de oriente, invenerunt campum in terra Sennaar et habitaverunt in eo.
translation: And when they removed from the east, they found a plain in the land of Sennaar, and dwelt in it.

text: "Te amo", murmuravit et oculos suos clausit.
translation: "I love you," she murmured and closed her eyes.

text: Mense Iunio theatrum cinematographicum paucis diebus clausum est futurum.
translation: In June, the movie theater is going to be closed for a few days.

text: Nonne claudis fenestram in cubiculo tuo?
translation: Did you close the window in your room?

text: Didymus nesciebat pontem clausum esse.
translation: Tom didn't know that the bridge was closed.

text: Ostium clausum sed habeo clavem.
translation: The door shut but I have the key.

text: Diribitorium cursuale clausum est.
translation: The post office is closed.

text: "Quis docebit me hoc?" "Ego, cum Deo."
translation: "Who will teach this to me?" "I will, with God's help."

text: Linguam Esperanticam in terra mea docebo.
translation: I will teach Esperanto in my land.

text: Omnia, quae scit, ego eum docui.
translation: I taught him everything he knows.

text: Thōmās līberōs suōs linguam Gallicam docuit.
translation: Tom taught French to his children.

text: Thōmās amīcōs suōs linguam Gallicam docuit.
translation: Tom taught French to his friends.

text: Marīa līberōs suōs linguam Gallicam docuit.
translation: Mary taught French to her children.

text: Thomas pilam excipere conatus est.
translation: Tom tried to catch the ball.

text: Pilam excipere non potui.
translation: I wasn't able to catch the ball.

text: Saluit ut pilam exciperet.
translation: He jumped to catch the ball.

text: Thomas pilam non excepit.
translation: Tom didn't catch the ball.

text: Multos et claros homines in illo convivio conveni.
translation: I met lots of famous people at that party.

text: Iustinus Bieber clarior quam Cathia Holmes est.
translation: Justin Bieber is more famous than Katie Holmes.

text: Haec ecclesia locus clarissimus pulcherrimusque est.
translation: This church is a very famous and beautiful place.

text: Cantor est tam clarus quam Madonna.
translation: The singer is as famous as Madonna.

text: Cantor est pariter clarus ac Madonna.
translation: The singer is as famous as Madonna.

text: Cantor est aeque clarus ac Madonna.
translation: The singer is as famous as Madonna.

text: Raeda veximus ut in tempore illuc adveniremus.
translation: We took a taxi so as to reach there on time.

text: Responde mihi, Thomas! Scio te illic esse et me audire.
translation: Tom! Answer me! I know you're in there, and I know you can hear me.

text: Non licet tibi illuc introire.
translation: You are not authorized to enter there.

text: Thomas illic erat nos salutatum.
translation: Tom was there to greet us.

text: Thomas me illuc ire coegit.
translation: Tom forced me to go there.

text: Scisne nomen pueri illic stantis?
translation: Do you know the name of the boy standing over there?

text: Thomas in oppido non procul a Bostonia habitat.
translation: Tom lives in a town not far from Boston.

text: Didymus in oppido non procul a Bostonia habitat.
translation: Tom lives in a town not far from Boston.

text: Estne schola tua procul a domo tua?
translation: Is your school far from your house?

text: Domus mea procul a statione non est.
translation: It is not far from my house to the station.

text: Quantum oculis, animo tum procul ibit amor.
translation: Far from eyes, far from heart.

text: Domus eorum procul a statione est.
translation: Their house is far from the station.

text: Alcoranus est liber sacer religionis Islamicae.
translation: The Qur'an is the Islamic holy book.

text: Hic locus sacer esse dicitur.
translation: This is said to be a sacred place.

text: Thomas inter sacrum saxumque stat.
translation: Tom is caught between a rock and a hard place.

text: Homo, sacra res homini.
translation: Man is something sacred for man.

text: Estne hoc animal sacrum?
translation: Is this animal holy?

text: Hic locus sacer est.
translation: This place is sacred.

text: Noli morari; periculose terminantur morae.
translation: Don't waste time. Procrastinating leads to dangerous results.

text: Tum Nisus et una Euryalus confestim alacres admittier orant: rem magnam pretiumque morae fore.
translation: So Niso and Euryalus ask to be received, insisting that they bring an important message that needs to be conveyed without delay.

text: Vela cadunt, remis insurgimus; haud mora, nautæ / adnixi torquent spumas et cærula verrunt.
translation: No longer tarrying; to our oars we lean. / Down drop the sails; in order ranged, each crew / flings up the foam to heaven, and sweeps the sparkling blue.

text: Ne quo abeas longius ab aedibus.
translation: Don't go too far from the house.

text: Nemo ex hostibus longius manebit.
translation: Not one of the enemy will stay any longer.

text: Haec sanctio multo longius progreditur.
translation: This sanction goes much further.

text: Dixitque pharao: Ego dimittam vos, ut sacrificetis Domino Deo vestro in deserto, verumtamen longius ne abeatis; rogate pro me.
translation: And Pharaoh said: I will let you go to sacrifice to the Lord your God in the wilderness, but go no farther: pray for me.

text: Si tu erras, ego quoque erro.
translation: If you are wrong, I am wrong too.

text: Id erat maximus error vitae meae.
translation: It was the biggest mistake of my life.

text: Errasti, sed non gravis est.
translation: You made a mistake but it's not serious.

text: Placide labora et minus errabis.
translation: Work more calmly to make fewer mistakes.

text: Errare optimus discendi modus est.
translation: The best way to learn is to make mistakes.

text: Ut ego quidem sentio, erras.
translation: In my opinion, you are wrong.

text: Abnegat, inceptoque et sedibus hæret in isdem.
translation: He heeds not – stirs not.

text: "Hanc ex diverso sedem veniemus in unam."
translation: There meet we.

text: Thomas est inquisitor sedis centralis exploratoriae.
translation: Tom is a CIA agent.

text: Aggressi ferro circum, qua summa labantes / juncturas tabulata dabant, convellimus altis / sedibus impulimusque.
translation: Here plying levers, where the flooring shows / weak joists, we heave it over.

text: Cur lingua Esperantica ad traducendum aptissima est?
translation: Why is Esperanto an ideal language for translation?

text: Scisne cur Thomas non amplius Bostoniae habitet?
translation: Do you know why Tom doesn't live in Boston anymore?

text: Scisne cur Thomas linguam Gallicam discat?
translation: Do you know why Tom is studying French?

text: Scisne cur Thomas in Australiam ierit?
translation: Do you know why Tom went to Australia?

text: Cūr mē dē hīs rēbus rogāvistī?
translation: Why have you been asking me these questions?

text: Cūr mē dē hīs rēbus rogāvistis?
translation: Why have you been asking me these questions?

text: Comae color tibi idem est comae color mihi.
translation: You and I have the same hair color.

text: Obstupui, steteruntque comæ et vox faucibus hæsit.
translation: Aghast I stood, tongue-tied, with stiffening hair.

text: Eum diligo, non quod comis sit, sed quia probus est.
translation: I like him not because he is kind but because he is honest.

text: Arrectae erant horore meae comae.
translation: My hair stands on end from fear.

text: Rosam in comis habet.
translation: She has a rose in her hair.

text: Eius comae arrectae sunt.
translation: His hair was standing on end.

text: Hoc est, ait, quod locutus sum: exploratores estis!
translation: He saith, This is it that I said: You are spies.

text: Ait ad eum: “Quod nomen est tibi?” Respondit: “Iacob”.
translation: And he said: What is thy name? He answered: Jacob.

text: Ait: “Tu es filius meus Esau?” Respondit: “Ego sum”.
translation: He said: Art thou my son Esau? He answered: I am.

text: Rursusque ait: Quid vidisti, ut hoc faceres?
translation: And again he expostulated with him, and said: What sawest thou, that thou hast done this?

text: « Qui nescit, scire non potest », ait S. Augustinus.
translation: "He who does not feel cannot know," said St. Augustine.

text: Aiunt se causidico non egere.
translation: They said they didn't need a lawyer.

text: Salve! Ichirou Tanaka sum. Te noscere gaudeo.
translation: Hi! I'm Ichirou Tanaka. Nice to meet you.

text: De male quaesitis non gaudet tertius heres.
translation: Ill-gotten goods thrive not to the third heir.

text: Nomen mihi est Cyril. Te noscere gaudeo.
translation: My name's Cyril. Nice to meet you.

text: Thomas dixit se Lingua Francogallice docere gaudere.
translation: Tom said he enjoys teaching French.

text: Gaudeam, sī Thōmās rem bene gerat.
translation: I'd be happy, if Tom succeeded.

text: Te noscere gaudeo. Ut vales?
translation: Nice to meet you. How are you doing?

text: Scire debes quomodo ignoscere ut beatus sis.
translation: You must know how to forgive to be happy.

text: Num quis sine pecunia beatus esse potest?
translation: Can anyone be happy without money?

text: Quamquam dives est, beatus non est.
translation: Although he is rich, he is not happy.

text: Si amicus meus esses, beatus essem.
translation: If you were my friend, I would be happy.

text: Beatus esse potes, si vis.
translation: You can be happy if you want.

text: Beatus esse posses, si velles.
translation: You could be happy if you wanted.

text: Nihil est ab omni parte beatum.
translation: In this life there is no perfect happiness.

text: Hic nuntius effecit me beatum.
translation: This news made me happy.

text: Laetus in praesens animus quod ultra est oderit curare et amara lento temperet risu. Nihil est ab omni parte beatum.
translation: Joyful let the soul be in the present, let it disdain to trouble about what is beyond and temper bitterness with a laugh. Nothing is blessed forever.

text: Si domo paulo maturius exisses, ad tempus pervenisses.
translation: If you'd left home a bit earlier, you'd have been on time.

text: Thomae pervenire hesterno a die conabamur.
translation: I've been trying to reach Tom since yesterday.

text: Ad domum tuam intra horam pervenero.
translation: I arrive at your house in one hour.

text: Ad caelum pervenire volo, sed nolo mori ut eo perveniam.
translation: I want to go to heaven, but I don't want to die in order to get there.

text: Alii aliis viis Romam perveniunt.
translation: There are many ways to get to Rome.

text: Hoc est cur huc pervenerim.
translation: This is the reason why I came here.

text: Verus amicus nihilo plus se ipsum quam amicum diligit.
translation: A true friend loves their friend more than themselves.

text: Verus amicus dicitur sincerus esse.
translation: They say a true friend is sincere.

text: "Twitter" amicus verus non est.
translation: Twitter is not a real friend.

text: Verus amicus te monuisset.
translation: A true friend would have warned you.

text: "Verane te facies, verus mihi nuntius affers, / nate dea? vivisne? aut, si lux alma recessit, / Hector ubi est?"
translation: "Real, then, real is thy face, and true / thy tidings? Liv'st thou, child of heavenly seed? / If dead, then where is Hector?"

text: Crēdō fābulam vēram esse.
translation: I believe that the story is true.

text: Crēdit fābulam vēram esse.
translation: He believes that the story is true.

text: Verae amicitiae sempiternae sunt.
translation: True friendships are abiding.

text: Aves non sunt verae.
translation: Birds aren't real.

text: "Incipe ubi voles." "Atqui est tuum incipere."
translation: "Begin when you want." "But it's your turn to begin."

text: Incipe tu igitur, qui provocasti me.
translation: You start then, as you challenged me.

text: Mense Aprili scholae in Iaponia incipiunt.
translation: In Japan, school starts in April.

text: Mense Septembri scholae in Europa incipiunt.
translation: School starts in September in Europe.

text: Prima caritas incipit ab egomet.
translation: First kindness begins from my own self.

text: Renascentia litterarum in Italia incepit.
translation: The Renaissance began in Italy.

text: Nullus est tam tutus quaestus, quam, quod habeas, parcere.
translation: There is no gain so secure as to spare what you have.

text: Divitiae grandes homini sunt vivere parce.
translation: The greatest wealth lies in living frugally.

text: Bonis nocet qui malis parcet.
translation: Whoever is lenient with the wicked harms the good.

text: Hic Priamus, quamquam in media jam morte tenetur, / non tamen abstinuit, nec voci iræque pepercit.
translation: Then Priam, though hemmed with death on every side, / spared not his utterance, nor his wrath controlled.

text: identitas pueri amissi confirmata est vestibus suis.
translation: The identity of the lost child was confirmed by its clothes.

text: identitas puellae amissae confirmata est vestibus suis.
translation: The identity of the lost child was confirmed by its clothes.

text: Vestem elige quae tibi placet.
translation: Choose a dress you like.

text: Quaerentes pecuniam, vestem perdiderunt.
translation: Many go out for wool, and come home shorn.

text: Quales vestes referendarii gerunt?
translation: What kind of clothes do referees wear?

text: Didymus novis vestibus eget.
translation: Tom needs some new clothes.

text: Domus eius similis est domibus novis.
translation: Her house is modern.

text: Infans dormiens similis est angelo.
translation: A sleeping child looks like an angel.

text: Thomas similis filio erat Mariae.
translation: Tom was like a son to Mary.

text: Sententia tua est similis meae.
translation: Your idea is similar to mine.

text: Tua birota meae similis est.
translation: Your bicycle is similar to mine.

text: Tua sententia meae similis est.
translation: Your opinion is similar to mine.

text: Veri simile est eos Thoman et Ioannem esse.
translation: That must be either Tom or John.

text: Omnes illae domus inter se similes sunt.
translation: Those houses are all alike.

text: Patri tuo quam matri similior es.
translation: You look more like your father than your mother.

text: Nolo filium meum tui similem esse.
translation: I don't want my son to be like you.

text: Postremo omnes nos valde similes sumus.
translation: In the end, we're all very similar.

text: Me tui similem esse nolo.
translation: I don't want to be like you.

text: Vidi ipse furentem / cæde Neoptolemum geminosque in limine Atridas.
translation: These eyes saw Pyrrhus, rioting in blood, / saw on the threshold the Atridae twain.

text: Thomas reus caedis factus est.
translation: Tom was charged with murder.

text: Thomas reus caedis fit.
translation: Tom is being charged with murder.

text: Thomas suspicionem caedis habebat.
translation: Tom was suspected of murder.

text: Thomas suspicionem caedis habet.
translation: Tom is suspected of murder.

text: Ordo verbi in Toki Pona valde strictus est.
translation: The word order in Toki Pona is very strict.

text: Verba ista sunt in secundo et tertio ordine frequentiae.
translation: Those words are in the second and third tiers of frequency.

text: Saltatio est ordo motus qui peragitur secundum modum musicorum.
translation: Dance is a set of movements that are performed following the rhythm of the music.

text: Anarchia ordo sine potestate est.
translation: Anarchy is order without power.

text: Filius eius advocatus esse optat.
translation: His son wants to be a lawyer.

text: Terra nostra tantum pacem optat.
translation: Our country wants nothing but peace.

text: Fenestram aperire opto. Aere egeo.
translation: I'd like to open the window; I need some air.

text: Aliquid casei emere opto.
translation: I would like to buy some cheese.

text: Patrem meum videre opto.
translation: I would like to see my father.

text: Hunc librum legere optat.
translation: He wants to read this book.

text: Romulus vicinarum nationum virgines rapuit.
translation: Romulus raped virgins of the neighbouring peoples.

text: Thomas librum legit quem Maria ei dedit.
translation: Tom is reading the book that Mary gave him.

text: Ille est liber, quem legere volo.
translation: This is the book I want to read.

text: Pater meus legatus est, non minister.
translation: My father is a deputy, not a minister.

text: Gallice neque legere neque loqui possum.
translation: I can't read French, nor can I speak it.

text: Si librum mihi dederis, eum legam.
translation: If you give me a book, I'll read it.

text: Thomas plures libros legit quam ego.
translation: Tom reads more books than I do.

text: Crebrescunt optatæ auræ, portusque patescit / jam propior, templumque apparet in arce Minervæ.
translation: Fresh blows the breeze, and broader grows the bay, / and on the cliffs is seen Minerva's fane.

text: Jamque dies alterque dies processit, et auræ / vela vocant, tumidoque inflatur carbasus austro.
translation: One day and now another passed; the gale / sings in the shrouds, and calls us to depart.

text: Ilicet ignis edax summa ad fastigia vento / volvitur; exsuperant flammæ, furit æstus ad auras.
translation: Roof-high the fiery glare, / fanned by the wind, mounts up; the loud blast roars in air.

text: Hic vero victus genitor se tollit ad auras, / affaturque deos et sanctum sidus adorat.
translation: Up rose my sire, submissive to the sign, / and briefly to the Gods addressed his prayer, / and bowed adoring to the star divine.

text: Hæc ub dicta dedit, lacrimantem et multa volentem / dicere deseruit, tenuesque recessit in auras.
translation: So spake she, and with weeping eyes I yearned / to answer, wondering at the words she said, / when lo, the shadowy spirit, as I turned, / dissolved in air, and in a moment fled.

text: "Quid puer Ascanius? Superatne et vescitur aura? / Quem tibi jam Troja..."
translation: "And the boy / Ascanius – lives he, or what hap befalls / his parents' darling, and their only joy? / Breathes he the vital air, whom unto thee now Troy..."

text: Ridenti domino et caelo ne crede sereno, nam facili casu dominus mutatur et aura.
translation: Don't trust a boss who laughs or stable weather, because both change easily.

text: Cur impetus hesternus nuntiis non elatus est?
translation: Why weren't last night's attacks mentioned in the news?

text: Tom est forma contracta e nomine Thomas.
translation: Tom is a shortened form of the name Thomas.

text: Pulcherrima forma puella es quam vidi.
translation: You're the most beautiful girl I've ever seen.

text: Eximia forma et prodest et nocet.
translation: Being really beautiful can be a mixed blessing.

text: Gallī aquilās ad tēleplāna intercipienda fōrmant.
translation: France is training eagles to intercept drones.

text: Pluvia in petrarum cavernis stagna formavit.
translation: Rain formed pools in the hollow spaces on the rocks.

text: Res est forma fugax.
translation: Beauty is a blossom.

text: in nova fert animus mutatas dicere formas corpora.
translation: My mind brings me to speak of forms changed into bodies new.

text: Terra, propter formam eius, orbis terrarum appellatur.
translation: The earth, because of its shape, is called the terrestrial globe.

text: In Mercurio aqua est formae glacialis.
translation: Water exists in the form of ice on Mercury.

text: Contignatio novi aedificii lente formam capit.
translation: The framework of the new building is slowly taking form.

text: Mori milies præstitit quam hæc pati.
translation: It would be better to die a thousand times than suffer such infamy.

text: Praestat exorari quam perire funditus.
translation: It is better to plead than to perish.

text: Praestat invidos habere quam misericordiam.
translation: It is better to envy than to pity.

text: Praestat invidiosum esse, quam miserabilem.
translation: Better be envied than pitied.

text: Quemque officium suum praestare oportet.
translation: One should do one's duty.

text: Praestat fugere, quam rogare.
translation: It is better to dismiss than to request.

text: Quo respondente: "Præsto sum”, ait ei.
translation: And when he answered: I am ready:

text: Quis cladem illius noctis, quis funera fando / explicet, aut possit lacrimis æquare labores?
translation: Oh, who hath tears to match our grief withal? / What tongue that night of havoc can make known?

text: "Vobis parta quies: nullum maris æquor arandum, / arva neque Ausoniæ semper cedentia retro / quærenda."
translation: "Your rest is won; no oceans to explore, / no fair Ausonia's ever-fading shore."

text: Multas per gentes et multa per aequora vectus advenio has miseras frater ad inferias.
translation: Carried through many nations and seas, I have come to these miserable funeral rites, brother.

text: Linquere tum portus jubeo et considere transtris. / Certatim socii feriunt mare et æquora verrunt.
translation: Then bid my comrades quit the port and shore, / and man the benches. They with rival strain / and slanting oar-blades sweep the levels of the main.

text: Disjectam Aeneæ toto videt æquore classem, / fluctibus oppressos Troas cœlique ruina; / nec latuere doli fratrem Junonis et iræ.
translation: ... beholds Troy's navy scattered far and nigh, / and by the waves and ruining heaven oppressed / the Trojan crews. Nor failed he to espy / his sister's wiles and hatred.

text: Thomas lac potioni Arabicae miscere solet.
translation: Tom usually adds milk to his coffee.

text: Romani vinum cum aqua miscebant.
translation: The Romans mixed wine with water.

text: Oleum et aqua non miscentur.
translation: Oil and water don't mix.

text: Me mortuo terra misceatur incendio.
translation: He that died half a year ago is as dead as Adam.

text: Sperma longis spatiis ad ovum iter perducere potest.
translation: Sperm can travel long distances to reach an egg.

text: Pulchrum est post tam longum spatium temporis te revidere.
translation: It's beautiful to see you after such a long time

text: Thomas in spatio natus est.
translation: Tom was born in space.

text: Tempus in magna celeritate retardat, et spatium coram campis gravitatis flectitur.
translation: Time slows down at high speed, and space bends in the presence of gravitational fields.

text: Plurima corpora ex spatio constant. Etiam particulae subatomicae apparent similiores spatio quam rebus.
translation: Physical objects are actually made up mostly of space. Even subatomic particles appear more like space than like things.

text: Cum volet, illa dies, quae nil nisi corporis huius ius habet, incerti spatium mihi finiat aevi:
translation: Whenever it will, let the day come, which has absolute power only over this mortal frame, and end for me the uncertain course of life.

text: Quid tandem eum venire vis?
translation: Why do you now finally want him to come?

text: Thomas tandem mihi locutus est aliquid, quod mihi scire opus erat.
translation: Tom did eventually tell me something I needed to know.

text: Tandem Thomas somno se dedit.
translation: Tom finally fell asleep.

text: Tandem somno se dedit.
translation: She finally fell asleep.

text: Prosequitur surgens a puppi ventus euntes, / et tandem antiquis Curetum allabimur oris.
translation: Through the deep we fly; / behind us sings the stern breeze loud and clear. / So to the shores of ancient Crete we steer.

text: Supra lunam sunt omnia aeterna, infra nihil est nisi mortale.
translation: Above the moon, everything is eternal; below, there is nothing save mortality.

text: "Unde venis?" "Venio inferne." "Quod negotium erat tibi infra?" "Ivi redditum urinam."
translation: "Where have you come from?" "I come from below." "What business did you have there?" "I went for a pee."

text: Thomas in hac spelunca commorari metuit.
translation: Tom is scared to stay in the cave.

text: Thomas maluit se diligi quam metui.
translation: Tom preferred to be loved rather than to be feared.

text: Sunt qui araneas metuant.
translation: There are people who are afraid of spiders.

text: Nihil est quod metuas.
translation: There's nothing to be afraid of.

text: Quid a nobis metuit?
translation: What does he fear from us?

text: Qui id, quod vitari non potest, metuit, is vivere animo quieto nullo modo potest.
translation: He who is afraid of the inevitable can in no way live with his soul at peace.

text: Dixit se aliquando id temptavisse.
translation: She said she tried doing that once herself.

text: Utens ad quem hunc nuntium mittere vis non exstat. Quaeso, tempta cum alio utentis nomine.
translation: The user you to want to send this message to does not exist. Please try with another username.

text: A viro ad feminam transitus meus bene fit.
translation: My transition from male to female is going well.

text: Hoc flumen tam vadosum ut vado transiri posse.
translation: This river is shallow enough to wade to the other side.

text: Longa est quidem via, sed tamen gradatim transibitur.
translation: The road is long, but it will be covered step by step.

text: Cumque transissent septem dies, aquæ diluvii inundaverunt super terram.
translation: And after the seven days were passed, the waters of the flood overflowed the earth.

text: A viro ad feminam bene transeo.
translation: I am transitioning well from a man to a woman.

text: Necesse est mihi, qui ad opus proficiscar, urbem cotidie transire.
translation: I have to cross the city every day to go to work.

text: Iam dudum factum est cum ultimum eum vidi.
translation: It's been a long time since I last saw him.

text: Thomas nomen ultimum suum in Jackson mutavit.
translation: Tom changed his last name to Jackson.

text: Ad stationem festinabo ferriviariam hamaxostichum ultimum attentum.
translation: I have to hurry to the station to take the last train.

text: Hunc ultimum diem suum esse putabat.
translation: He thought it was his last day.

text: Spero nos ultimos futuros esse.
translation: I hope we are the last.

text: Hae sunt eius litterae ultimae.
translation: This is his last letter.

text: Maria ad Tatoeba decem fere milia sententiarum addidit.
translation: Mary added almost 10,000 sentences to Tatoeba.

text: Non est vitae annos addere necesse sed annis vitam.
translation: It is not important to give life more years, but to give years more life.

text: Thomas milia sententiarum ad Tatoeba in multiplicibus linguis iam addidit.
translation: Tom has already added thousands of sentences to Tatoeba in multiple languages.

text: Adde paululum sacchari, quaeso.
translation: Add a bit of sugar, please.

text: Saccharum potioni Sinensi adde.
translation: Add sugar to the tea.

text: Sal et piper addes.
translation: Season with salt and pepper.

text: Flava rosa erat flos matri meae gratissimus.
translation: The yellow rose was my mother's favorite flower.

text: Dixit Laban: Gratum habeo, quod petis!
translation: And Laban said: I like well what thou demandest.

text: Gratum mihi fecisti, cum haec dixisti.
translation: You did a favor for me when you said this.

text: Puto Thoma valde hoc gratum esse.
translation: I think that's very sweet, Tom.

text: Pater liberis fabulam gratam narravit.
translation: The father told the children a nice story.

text: Grāta esse vult in lūdō.
translation: She wants to be popular at school.

text: Verbum laudatur, si factum tale sequatur.
translation: Words and no deeds are rushes and reeds.

text: Laudamus veteres, sed nostris utimur annis.
translation: We praise the good old times, but live today.

text: Ante sermonem non laudes virum; haec enim tentatio est hominum.
translation: Do not praise anyone before you hear him speak, for that is the touchstone of human beings.

text: Maccus laudabat ocreas, laudabat calceos.
translation: Maccus praised the stockings, praised the shoes.

text: Laudes pretiosiores sunt quam blasphemia.
translation: Praise is more valuable than blasphemy.

text: Nemo patriam meam laudare vult.
translation: Nobody wants to praise my country.

text: Pater tuus nondum respondit mihi ad meam epistulam.
translation: Your father hasn't answered my letter yet.

text: Liber, quem emi, nondum mihi allatus est.
translation: The book that I bought hasn't been delivered to me yet.

text: Raeda, quam emi, nondum mihi allata est.
translation: The car that I bought hasn't been delivered to me yet.

text: Libri, quos emi, nondum mihi allati sunt.
translation: The books that I bought haven't been delivered to me yet.

text: Glossarium, quod emi, nondum mihi allatum est.
translation: The dictionary that I bought hasn't been delivered to me yet.

text: Ea, quae emi, nondum mihi allata sunt.
translation: The things that I bought haven't been delivered to me yet.

text: Romani victis populis inter alia linguam suam imposuerunt.
translation: The Romans forced onto the people they defeated, among other things, their language.

text: Surrexit itaque Iacob et imposuit liberos suos ac coniuges suas super camelos.
translation: Then Jacob rose up, and having set his children and wives upon camels, went his way.

text: Quod si pretium ei fuerit impositum, dabit pro anima sua, quidquid fuerit postulatus.
translation: And if they set a price upon him, he shall give for his life whatsoever is laid upon him.

text: "Ergo age, care pater, cervici imponere nostræ; / ipse subibo humeris, nec me labor iste gravabit."
translation: "Quick, father, mount my shoulders, let us go. / That toil shall never tire me."

text: Unde appellavit eum Sabee (quod significat Abundantiam); et nomen urbi impositum est Bersabee usque in præsentem diem.
translation: Whereupon he called it Abundance: and the name of the city was called Bersabee, even to this day.

text: Tulit quoque ligna holocausti et imposuit super Isaac filium suum; ipse vero portabat in manibus ignem et cultrum.
translation: And he took the wood for the holocaust, and laid it upon Isaac his son; and he himself carried in his hands fire and a sword.

text: Quamquam fessus sum, somnum capere non possum.
translation: I'm tired, but I can't fall asleep.

text: Thomas e somno mihi excitandum est.
translation: I have to wake Tom up.

text: Somnum capere etiam nunc non possum.
translation: I still can't fall asleep.

text: Thoman e somno excitaturus sum.
translation: I have to wake Tom up.

text: Thoman e somno excitatura sum.
translation: I have to wake Tom up.

text: Puerum gravi somno dormientem invenimus.
translation: We found the boy sound asleep.

text: Nonaginta cum acie mentis attigit annos.
translation: He reached ninety years of age with a sharp mind.

text: Acies oculi mihi mala est.
translation: I have poor eyesight.

text: Se quoque principibus permixtum agnovit Achivis, / Eoasque acies et nigri Memnonis arma.
translation: Himself he knows among the Greeks again, / black Memnon's arms, and all his Eastern clan.

text: "Hic Dolopum manus, hic sævus tendebat Achilles; / classibus hic locus, hic acie certare solebant."
translation: "Here camped the brave Dolopians, there was set / the tent of fierce Achilles; yonder lay / the fleet, and here the rival armies met / and mingled."

text: Expergefactus pharao rursum dormivit et vidit alterum somnium.
translation: So Pharaoh awoke. He slept again, and dreamed another dream.

text: Quae recte data sunt, non licet rursus erigi.
translation: Give a thing and take a thing is the devil's gold ring.

text: Thomas rogari vult ut hoc rursus faciat.
translation: Tom wants to be asked to do that again.

text: Rursus inter se osculati sunt.
translation: They kissed again.

text: Rursus inter se osculatae sunt.
translation: They kissed again.

text: Thomas debuit rursus incipere.
translation: Tom had to start over again.

text: "Emori cupio." "Prius, quaeso, disce quid sit vivere."
translation: "I want to die." "First, I pray you, learn what it is to live."

text: Quo plus habent, eo plus cupiunt.
translation: The more they have, the more they want.

text: Thomas mihi dixit se canem cupere.
translation: Tom told me that he wanted a dog.

text: Cupio ut feles mea loqui possit.
translation: I wish my cat could talk.

text: Eius nomen hercle cupio scire.
translation: I really want to know her name.

text: Scīre cupiō quid sit amor.
translation: I want to know what love is.

text: Robertum et Mariam vidi cum Katharinam exspectarem.
translation: I saw Bob and Mary while I was waiting for Kate.

text: Domum redire volo, ubi pater me exspectat.
translation: I want to go back home, where my father is waiting for me.

text: Veni Aemilia! Pater tuus te exspectat.
translation: Come, Emilia! Your father is waiting for you.

text: Te heri exspectabam. Cur non venisti?
translation: I waited for you yesterday. Why didn't you come?

text: Ea exspectavit eum domum redire.
translation: She waited for him to come home.

text: Thomas Mariam in statione exspectavit.
translation: Tom waited for Mary at the station.

text: Aqua est compositum hydrogenio et oxygenio.
translation: Water is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen.

text: Hic currum automobilem componere non licet.
translation: Parking prohibited!

text: Hic currum automatarium componere non licet.
translation: Parking prohibited!

text: Hic raedam componere non licet.
translation: Parking prohibited!

text: Hic autocinetum componere non licet.
translation: Parking prohibited!

text: Hic autoraedam componere non licet.
translation: Parking prohibited!

text: Estne puer dignus laude?
translation: Is the boy worthy of praise?

text: Benefacta laude digna sunt.
translation: Good deeds are worthy of praise.

text: "En Priamus! Sunt hic etiam sua præmia laudi; / sunt lacrimæ rerum et mentem mortalia tangunt".
translation: "See our Priam! Even here / worth wins her due, and there are tears to flow, / and human hearts to feel for human woe."

text: Thomae domus non longe a mea abest.
translation: Tom's house isn't very far from mine.

text: Pater meus ad Sinas ivit. Nunc abest.
translation: My father has gone to China. He isn't here now.

text: Thomas saepe insciis parentibus a schola abest.
translation: Tom often skips school.

text: Malum per diem ut medicus absit.
translation: An apple a day keeps the doctor away.

text: Frater meus cras a domo aberit.
translation: My brother won't be at home tomorrow.

text: Semper insciis parentibus a schola absunt.
translation: They always skip school.

text: Manus digiti conaequales non sunt, omnes tamen usui sunt.
translation: All fingers are not similar.

text: Usu fortiter edisco tristia posse pati.
translation: I learn through experience to bear evils with courage.

text: Ferrum ad construendas naves usui est.
translation: Iron is used in building ships.

text: Quali veneno usi estis?
translation: What kind of poison did you use?

text: Quali veneno usae estis?
translation: What kind of poison did you use?

text: "Vis dare mutuo mihi?" "Est mihi opus." "In quem usum?" "Ad emendam chartam."
translation: "Will you lend it to me?" "I need it?" "For what?" "To buy paper."

text: O fortuna velut luna statu variabilis semper crescis aut decrescis.
translation: Oh luck! Like the moon, you steadily change, you always grow and then wither again.

text: Senectus est velut altera pueritia.
translation: Old age is like a second childhood.

text: Pisces pinnis veluti remis utuntur.
translation: Fish use their fins as oars.

text: Thomas oluit velut fabrica cervisiae.
translation: Tom smelled like a distillery.

text: Thomas oluit velut braxatorium.
translation: Tom smelled like a distillery.

text: In quibusdam linguis, velut Francogallica aut Persica, solanum tuberosum "pomum terrae" vocatur.
translation: In some languages like French or Persian, a potato is called an 'apple of the earth'.

text: Comites sententias nostras sciunt.
translation: The comrades know our opinions.

text: "Illi me comitem et consanguinitate propinquum / pauper in arma pater primis huc misit ab annis. "
translation: "His kinsman, by a needy father sent, / with him in boyhood to the war I came."

text: Valeas Pinocule! Comites isti mali amorem tuum studio tandem efficient perdendum. Causa erunt propiore die tibi errandi.
translation: Take care, Pinocchio! Those bad companions will sooner or later make you lose your love for study. Some day they will lead you astray.

text: Universitas studiorum prope stationem hamaxostichi sbterranei est.
translation: The college is close to the metro.

text: Hic liber studium meum valde excitat.
translation: I find this book very interesting.

text: Grieg in Conservatorio Lipsiensi studium tulit.
translation: Grieg studied at the Leipzig Conservatory.

text: Hic liber studium valde excitat.
translation: This is a very interesting book.

text: Librum legere studium nostrum excitat.
translation: Reading a book is interesting.

text: Liber eius studium valde excitat.
translation: His book is very interesting.

text: Vita pulchra est. Nemo eam facilem esse dixit.
translation: Life is beautiful. No one said it was simple.

text: Opus gubernatoris non tam facile est quam videtur.
translation: The job of a driver is not as easy as it looks.

text: Non facile est loqui lingua nimis facili.
translation: Speaking too simple a language is not easy.

text: Est facile quodvis, quando fert opem Deus.
translation: Anything is easy when God brings help.

text: Manu scriptae litterae facile legi non potuerunt.
translation: Written by hand, the letter was not very easy to read.

text: Thomas inter taedium et esuriem facile internosse non potest.
translation: Tom is not able to easily distinguish between boredom and hunger.

text: Apparent diræ facies inimicaque Trojæ / numina magna deum.
translation: Dread shapes and forms terrific loomed in sight, / and hostile deities, whose faces frowned / destruction.

text: Ducendum ad sedes simulacrum, orandaque divæ / numina conclamant.
translation: 'On with the image to its home', they cried, / 'and pray the Goddess to avert our woe'.

text: Tum numina sancta precamur / Palladis armisonæ, quæ prima accepit ovantes.
translation: So our vows we pay / to Pallas, famed in arms, whose welcome cheered the way.

text: Vadimus immixti Danais haud numine nostro, / multaque per cæcam congressi prœlia noctem / conserimus, multos Danaum demittimus Orco.
translation: Thus we, elate, but not with Heaven our friend, / march on and mingle with the Greeks in fight, / and many a Danaan to the shades we send. / And many a battle in the blinding night / we join with those that meet us.

text: Thōmās nōn tam sapiēns esse vidētur quam Marīa.
translation: Tom doesn't seem to be as wise as Mary.

text: Thōmās nōn tam sapiēns esse vidēbātur quam Marīa.
translation: Tom didn't seem to be as wise as Mary seemed to be.

text: Nemo nascitur sapiens, sed multi moriuntur stulti.
translation: No one is born wise, but many die stupid.

text: Nunquam sapiunt stulti, nisi in angustiis.
translation: Wise men learn by others' harm, fools by their own.

text: Unusquisque in arte sua sapiens.
translation: Each one is knowledgeable in his own art.

text: Si quisquam, Cato sapiens fuit.
translation: If anybody was ever wise, Cato was.

text: An nescis, mi fili, quantilla sapientia mundus regatur?
translation: Don't you know then, my son, how little wisdom rules the world?

text: Mihi satis apparent propter se ipsam appetenda sapientia.
translation: It is quite apparent to me that knowledge should be sought for its own sake.

text: Puer ille in dies sapientior fit.
translation: That boy gets smarter every day.

text: Fragum non est Musa sapientior.
translation: A strawberry is not tastier than a banana.

text: Didymus est sapientior quam intelligentior.
translation: Tom is more wise than clever.

text: Non omnes homines sapientes sunt.
translation: Not all men are wise.

text: Tom mane librum sumpsit et iam legit.
translation: Tom took the book in the morning and has already read it.

text: Locus est ubi pueri ludunt. Filium tuum ibi sumere potes.
translation: There is a room where children play. You can take your child there.

text: Nox est. Familia cenam sumit.
translation: It is night. The family is eating dinner.

text: Nunc in triclinio cenam sumunt.
translation: They're eating dinner now in the dining room.

text: Cenam apud amicum nostrum sumimus.
translation: We're eating dinner at our friends' place.

text: Quotiēns in diē cibum sūmis?
translation: How many times do you eat in a day?

text: Amicus meus, Thomas, est scholasticus et vir nobilis.
translation: My friend, Tom, is a scholar and a fine gentleman.

text: Nobilis est ille, quem nobilitant bene villae.
translation: A lord without riches is a soldier without arms.

text: Helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon, radon gasa nobilia sunt.
translation: Helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon and radon are noble gases.

text: Non dubito quin Thomas linguam Gallicam discere nolit.
translation: I'm sure Tom doesn't want to study French.

text: Non dubito quin Thomas solus esse nolit.
translation: I'm sure Tom doesn't want to be alone.

text: Non dubito quin Thomas hoc facturus sit.
translation: I don't doubt Tom will do that.

text: Non dubito quin Thomas nos per telephonum aditurus sit.
translation: I'm sure Tom will call.

text: Non dubito quin Thomas hoc fecerit.
translation: I don't doubt Tom has done that.

text: Non dubito quin hoc facturus sit.
translation: I don't doubt but that he will do it.

text: si vis me flere, dolendum est primum ipsi tibi.
translation: If you wish me to weep, you yourself must first feel grief.

text: Risus habet fletum, nectarque molestat acetum.
translation: Pleasure has a sting in its tail.

text: Scin quid est quod Thomas flebat?
translation: Do you know the reason why Tom was crying?

text: Scin quid est quod Thomas flet?
translation: Do you know the reason why Tom is crying?

text: Lentissime coniuges flentur, saepe vero laetissime.
translation: Sorrow for a husband is like a pain in the elbow, sharp and short.

text: Is ridet qui cras flebit.
translation: He that laughs in the morning weeps at night.

text: Noli etiam me rogare de hac re.
translation: Don't ask me about that anymore.

text: Nolo dicere Thoma me in Australia fuisse.
translation: I don't want to tell Tom that I was in Australia.

text: Noli facere mentionem, quaeso, me esse qui hoc fecerim.
translation: Please don't mention that I was the one who did this.

text: Noli facere mentionem, quaeso, Thoman esse qui hoc fecerit.
translation: Please don't mention that Tom was the one who did this.

text: Thomas in eo particeps esse nolebat.
translation: Tom didn't want to be part of it.

text: Tom dixit se Francogallice loqui nolle.
translation: Tom said he didn't want to speak in French.

text: Plenum est mihi temporis non satis autem pecuniae.
translation: I have plenty of time, but not enough money.

text: Hodie dies gaudii plenus est.
translation: Today is a day full of joy.

text: Poculum plenum aquae est.
translation: The glass is full of water.

text: Poculum vini plenum est.
translation: The glass is full of wine.

text: Poculum plenum lactis est.
translation: The glass is full of milk.

text: Lacus plenus piscium est.
translation: The lake is full of fish.

text: Cur cameli odium adversus equos gerunt?
translation: Why do camels hate horses?

text: Considerate lilia agri quo modo crescunt: non laborant neque nent.
translation: Look at the lilies of the field: they grow, and yet they neither work nor spin.

text: Nemus erat calidus et tacitus.
translation: It was warm and quiet in the park.

text: Abrahm vero plantavit nemus in Bersabee et invocavit ibi nomem Domini, Dei æterni.
translation: But Abraham planted a grove in Bersabee, and there called upon the name of the Lord God eternal.

text: "Hinc mater cultrix Cybelæ, Corybantiaque aera, / Idæumque nemus; hinc fida silentia sacris, / et juncti currum dominæ subiere leones."
translation: "Thence Corybantian cymbals clashed and brayed / in praise of Cybele. In Ida's wood / her mystic rites in secrecy were paid, / and lions, yoked in pomp, their sovereign's car conveyed."

text: Diem in nemore agamus.
translation: Let's spend the day in the park.

text: Hunc librum emere non possum. Nimis carus est.
translation: I cannot buy this book. It's too expensive.

text: Illud bisellium minus carum est quam haec mensa.
translation: That sofa is less expensive than this table.

text: Illud horologium minus carum est quam hoc.
translation: That watch is less expensive than this one.

text: Hoc horologium minus carum est quam illud.
translation: This watch is less expensive than that one.

text: Illud bisellium minus carum est hac mensa.
translation: That sofa is less expensive than this table.

text: Haec raeda est tam cara quam illa.
translation: This car is as expensive as that one.

text: Tam desunt avido sua quam quod non habet.
translation: A covetous man is good to none and worst to himself.

text: Dives est qui sibi nihil deesse putat.
translation: He is rich who thinks he lacks nothing.

text: Dominus pascit me, et nihil mihi deerit.
translation: The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.

text: Tempus mihi deest ad hoc faciendum.
translation: I have no time to do that.

text: Semper volumus quod nobis deest.
translation: We always want what we don't have.

text: tempus mihi deest ad explicandum.
translation: I don't have time to explain.

text: Hannibal legatos ad senatum Romanum misit.
translation: Hannibal sends ambassadors to the Roman senate.

text: Legatos sui purgandi causa mittunt.
translation: They send ambassadors to apologize.

text: Et Didymus et Maria linguam Gallicam discunt.
translation: Tom and Mary both study French.

text: Lingua Gallica valde difficilis est, sed eam discere volo.
translation: The Gaulish language is very difficult, but I want to learn it.

text: Thomas linguam Gallicam tres annos didicit.
translation: Tom has been studying French for three years.

text: Linguam Ruthenicam discere valde difficile est.
translation: Learning the Russian language is very difficult.

text: Ad scholam eo, quia discere volo.
translation: I go to school because I want to learn.

text: Ad scholam imus, qua discere volumus.
translation: We go to school because we want to learn.

text: Linguam Latinam disco, quia linguarum maxime mihi placet.
translation: I study Latin because it's my favorite language.

text: Linguam anglicam disco, quia Civitates Foederatas ire volo.
translation: I'm studying English because I plan to go to the United States.

text: Linguam Anglicam disco, quia in mentem habeo Americam visitare.
translation: I am learning English with the idea of going to America.

text: Arabice loquor, sed linguam Anglicam disco.
translation: I speak Arabic but I study English.

text: Et linguam Anglicam et Iaponicam disco.
translation: I study English and Japanese.

text: "Laborasne?" "Non laboro, tantum disco."
translation: "You're working?" "No, I'm just studying."

text: Utrique sunt fures, et qui accipit et qui furatur.
translation: The heeler is as bad as the steeler.

text: Quae furatur non est mus sed apertura.
translation: It is not the mouse that steals; it is the hole in the wall that steals.

text: Pecuniam a me furatus est.
translation: He stole money from me.

text: Quanti Thomas furatus est?
translation: How much money has Tom stolen?
