text: Thomas furore inflammatus est.
translation: Tom became furious.

text: Qui furatus fuerit hominem sive vendiderit eum sive inventus fuerit in manu eius, morte moriatur.
translation: He that shall steal a man, and sell him, being convicted of the guilt, shall be put to death.

text: Arbores hae ab iis satae sunt.
translation: These trees were planted by them.

text: Sub arbore malo suscitavi te.
translation: I raised thee up under the apple tree.

text: Birota sub arbore mea est.
translation: The bicycle under the tree is mine.

text: Fructus huius arboris boni sunt.
translation: The fruit of this tree is good.

text: Haec arbor valde magna est.
translation: This is a very tall tree.

text: Haec arbor fructus nunquam edet.
translation: This tree will never bear fruit.

text: Haec raeda patris mei est, mox autem mea erit.
translation: This car is my father's, but soon it will be mine.

text: Haec domus aviae meae est, mox autem mea erit.
translation: This house is my grandmother's, but soon it will be mine.

text: Mox, ut spero, te iterum videbo.
translation: I hope to see you again before long.

text: Thomas dixit se mox discessurum esse.
translation: Tom said that he would depart soon.

text: Spero te Romam mox adventurum esse.
translation: I hope that you will arrive in Rome soon.

text: Maria dixit se mox discessuram esse.
translation: Mary said that she would depart soon.

text: Arma civīs non occidunt. Civēs civīs occidunt.
translation: Guns don't kill people. People kill people.

text: Cives statim omnia ad urbem defendendam parant.
translation: The citizens immediately prepared everything to defend the city.

text: Iudaea sum, civis autem Civitatum Foederatarum Americae.
translation: I'm an American Jew.

text: Iudaeus sum, civis autem Civitatum Foederatarum Americae.
translation: I'm an American Jew.

text: Patria civibus amanda est.
translation: A country ought to be loved by the citizens.

text: Cives orbis terrarum sumus.
translation: We're all citizens of the world.

text: Hoc facere non potui quia occupatus eram.
translation: I couldn't do that because I was busy.

text: Te adiuvare non possum, quod occupatus sum.
translation: I can't help you because I'm busy.

text: Tam occupatus sum ut legere non possim.
translation: I'm so busy I have no time to read.

text: Pater eius non veniet, valde occupatus est.
translation: His dad will not come, he is very busy.

text: Dubito quin Thomas occupatus sit.
translation: I doubt that Tom is busy.

text: Tam occupatus sum quam Thomas.
translation: I'm as busy as Tom.

text: Poeni miseri erant ubi hoc spectabant.
translation: The Carthaginians were distressed when they saw this.

text: Tota aula nostra hanc pelliculam spectavit.
translation: Our whole class watched this movie.

text: Hanc pelliculam spectans, medicum fieri statuit.
translation: Having watched this movie, he decided to become a doctor.

text: Pelliculam spectavi francogallicam subtitulis anglicis.
translation: I watched a French movie with English subtitles.

text: Fabulam semel in mense spectant.
translation: They go to watch a play once every month.

text: Ne me spectes hoc modo.
translation: Don't look at me that way.

text: Omni nocte series Turcicas cum subtitulis specto.
translation: I am watching Turkish series with subtitles every night.

text: Mílités víctí terga nón vertérunt.
translation: The soldiers, though they were conquered, did not retreat.

text: Egressus ad eos Lot post tergum occludens ostium ait: Nolite, quæso, fratres mei, nolite malum hoc facere.
translation: Lot went out to them, and shut the door after him, and said: Do not so, I beseech you, my brethren, do not commit this evil.

text: Pectora quorum inter fluctus arrecta jubæque / sanguinæ superant undas, pars cetera pontum / ponet legit sinuatque immensa volumine terga.
translation: Their breasts erect they rear amid the deep, / their blood-red crests above the surface shine, / their hinder parts along the waters sweep, / trailed in huge coils and many a tortuous twine.

text: Quibus rebus ipse gloriaris, aliis crimini dare non debes!
translation: The things in which you glory you must not consider a crime in others!

text: Sacrilegium crimen est sine nocito.
translation: Blasphemy is a victimless crime.

text: "Accipe nunc Danaum insidias, et crimine ab uno / disce omnes."
translation: "Mark now the Danaans' cunning; from one wrong / learn all."

text: Fatendum est crimen meum.
translation: I must confess my crime.

text: Hoc est crimen tam bene collocatum, mea sententia, ut non possum inducere animum confiteri.
translation: This is a crime so well placed, in my opinion, that I cannot bring my mind to confess it.

text: Hoc est optimum donum quod semper acquisivi!
translation: This is the best gift I've ever gotten!

text: Quid est donum optimum quod unquam dedisti?
translation: What's the best gift you've ever given?

text: Spero fore ut hoc donum tibi placeat.
translation: I hope you like this gift.

text: Spero fore ut hoc donum vobis placeat.
translation: I hope you like this gift.

text: Ipse canis est quem tibi dono dedi.
translation: It's the dog I gave to you as a gift.

text: Ille est canis quem tibi dono dedi.
translation: It's the dog I gave to you as a gift.

text: Secundum omnes leges notos aviationis, nullo modo est ut apis volare possit.
translation: According to all known laws of aviation, there is no way that a bee should be able to fly.

text: Flumen Mississippiense in Sinum Mexicanum influit.
translation: The Mississippi River flows into the Gulf of Mexico.

text: Effer manus tuas e sinibus.
translation: Take your hands out of your pockets.

text: Susceptumque Noemi puerum posuit in sinu suo et gerulæ officio fungebatur.
translation: And Noemi taking the child, laid it in her bosom, and she carried it, and was a nurse unto it.

text: In sinū mātris sedēbat.
translation: He was sitting on her mother's lap.

text: In sinu meo habitas.
translation: You live in my heart.

text: Deum nemo vidit unquam: Unigenitus Filius, qui est in sinu Patris, Ipse enarravit.
translation: No man hath seen God at any time; the only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him.

text: In expuentis recidit faciem, quod in caelum expuit.
translation: Who spits against heaven, it falls in his face.

text: Erat autem Ioseph pulchra facie et decorus aspectu.
translation: And Joseph was of a beautiful countenance, and comely to behold.

text: Ioseph ruit super faciem patris flens et deosculans eum.
translation: And when Joseph saw this, he fell upon his father's face, weeping and kissing him.

text: Rursumque, lota facie, egressus continuit se et ait: Ponite panes.
translation: And when he had washed his face, coming out again, he refrained himself, and said: Set bread on the table.

text: Livorem in facie habuit Thomas.
translation: Tom had a bruise on his face.

text: Faciem eius intuita est.
translation: She looked him in the face.

text: Cito rumpes arcum, semper si tensum habueris.
translation: A bow that is always extended does not resist, it breaks soon.

text: "Vix tandem magnis Ithaci clamoribus actus, / composito rumpit vocem et me destinat aræ."
translation: "Then, forced by false Ulysses' clamorous cry, / spake the concerted word, and sentenced me to die."

text: Fit via vi: rumpunt aditus, primosque trucidant / immissi Danai, et late loca milite complent.
translation: Force wins a footing, and, the foremost slain, / in, like a deluge, pours the Danaan train.

text: Nónne enim lingua est membrum quo hominés dícunt?
translation: After all, isn’t the tongue the organ that people speak with?

text: Si caput dolet, omnia membra languent.
translation: If the head hurts, all the limbs become weak.

text: Mihi frigidus horror / membra quatit, gelidusque coit formidine sanguis.
translation: Cold horror shook me, in my veins the blood / was chilled, and curdled with affright.

text: membrum gregis esse electus est.
translation: He was chosen to be a member of the team.

text: Quot membra habet polypus?
translation: How many arms does an octopus have?

text: Quot membra sunt polypo?
translation: How many arms does an octopus have?

text: Habitaveruntne unquam Thomas et Maria Bostoniae?
translation: Have Tom and Mary ever lived in Boston?

text: Hoc pulcherrimum est quod umquam vidi.
translation: This is the most beautiful thing I have ever seen.

text: Mariam non amo neque unquam amabo.
translation: I do not like Mary, nor will I ever like her.

text: Librum scribo quem nemo umquam leget.
translation: I'm writing a book that no one's ever going to read.

text: Maria dixit se Thoman nunquam amavisse neque unquam amaturam esse.
translation: Mary said that she had never loved Tom, nor would she ever love him.

text: Thomas dixit se Mariam nunquam amavisse neque unquam amaturum esse.
translation: Tom said that he had never loved Mary, nor would he ever love her.

text: Vult Thomas in domo manere et telehorasim aspicere.
translation: Tom wants to stay at home to watch television.

text: Thomas aspicere nolebat, sed non potuit quin aspiceret.
translation: Tom didn't want to look, but he couldn't help himself.

text: Libros legere quam telehorasim aspicere malo.
translation: I prefer reading books to watching television.

text: Nunc Thomas telehorasim non aspicit. Dormit.
translation: Tom isn't watching TV now. He's sleeping.

text: Illam pelliculam cinematographicam cum Thoma aspexi.
translation: I saw that movie with Tom.

text: Aspice flores in hortis publicis.
translation: Look at the flowers in the park.

text: Ruben primogenitus meus, tu fortitudo mea et principium roboris mei; prior in dignitate, maior in robore!
translation: Ruben, my firstborn, thou art my strength, and the beginning of my sorrow; excelling in gifts, greater in command.

text: In litore lacus magni stat templum pulchrum.
translation: On the shore of a large lake stands a beautiful temple.

text: Aliquid horrendum in templo deserto vivit.
translation: Something frightening lives in the abandoned temple.

text: Nos quoque ad templum ivimus.
translation: We also went to the temple.

text: Templum rubrum et viride est.
translation: The temple is red and green.

text: Quando hoc templum aedificatum est?
translation: When was this temple built?

text: Etiam in templum ibamus.
translation: We also went to the temple.

text: "Quid si amiseris?" "Ferendum erit æquo animo."
translation: "What if you lose it?" "I will put up with it patiently."

text: Thomas septem abhinc annos uxorem amisit.
translation: Tom lost his wife seven years ago.

text: Thomas tres abhinc annos uxorem amisit.
translation: Tom lost his wife three years ago.

text: Maria tres abhinc annos maritum amisit.
translation: Mary lost her husband three years ago.

text: Tres habeo animas; duas amittere possum.
translation: I have three lives; I can lose up to two.

text: Tantum temporis amittere nolebam.
translation: I didn't want to waste so much time.

text: Posco ut respondeas ad rogatum meum!
translation: I demand an answer to my question!

text: Filiam tuam mihi uxorem posco.
translation: I demand your daughter's hand in marriage.

text: ''Quanti poscit?'' ''Mille euruum.''
translation: "How much is he asking for?" "A thousand euros."

text: Opem a te posco.
translation: I ask for help from you.

text: Nihil a te posco.
translation: I ask you for nothing.

text: Hic regina gravem gemmis auroque poposcit / implevitque mero pateram, quam Belus et omnes / a Belo soliti.
translation: Now for the ponderous goblet called the Queen, / of jewelled gold, which Belus used and they / of Belus' line, and poured the wine straightway.

text: Ŝi perdis la malmultan monon, kiun ŝi havis.
translation: She lost what little money she had.

text: Thomas et Maria omnia perdiderunt, quae habebant.
translation: Tom and Mary lost everything they owned.

text: Maria exposuit quo modo pecuniam suam perdidisset.
translation: Mary explained how she lost her money.

text: Thomas dixit se nolle contendendo tempus perdere.
translation: Tom said he didn't want to waste time arguing.

text: Thomas dixit se nolle disputando tempus perdere.
translation: Tom said he didn't want to waste time arguing.

text: Thomas dixit se nolle litigando tempus perdere.
translation: Tom said he didn't want to waste time arguing.

text: Varietas semper est translationum pro quovis loco in quavis lingua.
translation: There is always a variety of translations for any passage in any language.

text: Hamaxostichone adveniet an curru publico?
translation: Is he coming by train or by bus?

text: Vehiturne ad scholam curru publico?
translation: Does he go to school by bus?

text: Currus non egeo. Currus sum.
translation: I don't need a car. I am the car.

text: Quota hora currus publicus proficiscitur?
translation: What time does the bus leave?

text: Anus e curru publico exivit.
translation: The old woman exited the bus.

text: Pater meus currum publicum gubernat.
translation: My father is a bus driver.

text: Precor ut hic dies tibi candidus illuxerit.
translation: Have a wonderful day.

text: "Deus reducat illum." "Ita precor."
translation: "God speed his return." "So I pray."

text: Precor ut bonis avibus adeas.
translation: I wish you a good journey.

text: Precamur omnia laeta vobis omnibus.
translation: We wish you much happiness!

text: Precor tibi noctem placidam.
translation: Good night.

text: Senescere potest solum corpus, animae autem aetas non est.
translation: Only the body can age; the soul has no age.

text: Aperi librum et animam tuam aperiet.
translation: Open a book and it will open your soul.

text: Ars musica animae est mira.
translation: Music is wonderful for the soul.

text: tantaene animis caelestibus irae?
translation: Can there be so much anger in celestial hearts?

text: Musica lingua animae est.
translation: Music is the language of the soul.

text: Religiones carmina animae sunt.
translation: Religions are the poems of the soul.

text: Corpus meum vetus, sed anima iuvenis est.
translation: My body is old, but my soul is young.

text: Anima singularis coniunctionem intimam cum anima universi quaerere debet.
translation: The individual soul should seek for an intimate union with the soul of the universe.

text: Anima singularis unionem arctam cum anima universi quaerere debet.
translation: The individual soul should seek for an intimate union with the soul of the universe.

text: Vacca anima utile est.
translation: A cow is a useful animal.

text: Lingua est anima litterarum.
translation: Language is the soul of literature.

text: Et conglutinata est anima eius cum ea, et amavit puellam et locutus est ad cor eius.
translation: And his soul was fast knit unto her; and whereas she was sad, he comforted her with sweet words.

text: Quid mihi contigisse putas?
translation: What do you think happened to me?

text: Licet sponsam osculo contingere.
translation: You may kiss the bride.

text: Eius contingebat manus sua.
translation: Her hand met his.

text: Deus qui nobis vitam dedit, simul nobis libertatem dedit.
translation: The God who gave us life, gave us liberty at the same time.

text: Feminae huius terrae pro libertate pugnant.
translation: Women in that country are fighting for their freedom.

text: Libertatem habes ut commees ubicumque.
translation: You have the freedom to travel wherever you like.

text: Angli libertatis heredes sunt.
translation: The English are the heirs of freedom.

text: Danis symbolum est libertatis.
translation: Dan is a symbol of freedom.

text: O dulce nomen libertatis!
translation: Oh, sweet name of freedom!

text: Bellum pax est. Libertas servitus est. Ignorantia est vis.
translation: War is peace. Freedom is slavery. Ignorance is strength.

text: Ubi dubium, ibi libertas.
translation: Where there is doubt there is freedom.

text: Libertas bonum pretiosissimum est.
translation: The most precious good is freedom.

text: Libertas res pretiosissima est.
translation: The most precious good is freedom.

text: Præcepitque servis suis medicis, ut aromatibus condirent patrem.
translation: And he commanded his servants, the physicians, to embalm his father.

text: Servus erit, qui ducet pravam uxorem.
translation: A wicked woman and an evil is three halfpence worse than the devil.

text: Me tractat ut servam.
translation: He treats me like his slave.

text: Nōn sum servus tuus.
translation: I'm not your slave.

text: Dixistique servis tuis: Adducite eum ad me, et ponam oculos meos super illum.
translation: And thou saidst to thy servants: Bring him hither to me, and I will set my eyes on him.

text: Qui responderunt: “Sospes est servus tuus pater noster, adhuc vivit”. Et incurvati adoraverunt eum.
translation: And they answered: Thy servant our father is in health; he is yet living. And bowing themselves, they made obeisance to him.

text: Dominus meus interrogavit prius servos suos: Habetis patrem aut fratrem?
translation: My lord. Thou didst ask thy servants the first time: Have you a father or a brother.

text: Me tractat ut servum.
translation: He treats me like his slave.

text: Marcus servos suos vocat.
translation: Marcus calls upon his servants.

text: Nam est nullum discrimen inter pauperem et divitem, inter herum et servum.
translation: For there is no difference betwixt a poor man and a rich, betwixt a master and a servant.

text: Si emeris servum Hebræum, sex annis serviet tibi; in septimo egredietur liber gratis.
translation: If thou buy a Hebrew servant, six years shall he serve thee; in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing.

text: Iulius in villa est apud servos suos - neque is iam meus dominus est!
translation: Julius is at home with his slaves - and is now not my master!

text: Ain' vero? Nesciebam eam sororem tuam esse.
translation: Really? I didn't know she was your sister.

text: Ego raedam non habeo, sed soror habet.
translation: I don't have a car, but my sister does.

text: Feles mihi placent et sorori canes.
translation: I like dogs and my sister likes cats.

text: "Cuius pedulia sunt?" "Sororis meae sunt."
translation: "Whose socks are these?" "They are my sister's."

text: Duos fratres et unam sororem habeo.
translation: I have two brothers and one sister.

text: Duos fratres et tres sorores habeo.
translation: I have two brothers and three sisters.

text: Aliquando fluctus altiores sunt quam naves.
translation: Sometimes the waves are higher than the ships.

text: Navis magno fluctu pulsata est.
translation: The ship was hit by a big wave.

text: Hodie fluctus alti sunt.
translation: The waves are high today.

text: Jam medio apparet fluctu nemorosa Zacynthos, / Dulichiumque, Sameque, et Neritos ardua saxis.
translation: Soon, crowned with woods, Zacynthos we espy, / Dulichium, Same and the rock-bound steep / of Neritos.

text: "Quos ego... sed motos præstat componere fluctus. / Post mihi non simili pœna commissa luetis."
translation: "Beware... / Yet first 'twere best these billows to allay. / Far other coin hereafter ye shall pay / for crimes like these."

text: exegi monumentum aere perennius.

translation: And now I have completed a great work, which not Jove's anger, and not fire nor steel nor devouring time can sweep away.

translation: "I think, therefore I am," said René Descartes.

translation: I'm thinking about traveling to Europe with a friend.

translation: We see the War-God glorying in his might; / up to the roof we see the Danaos pour; / their shielded penthouse drives against the door.

text: Vestibulum ante ipsum primoque in limine Pyrrhus / exsultat, telis et luce coruscus ahena.
translation: Just on the threshold of the porch, behold / fierce Pyrrhus stands, in glittering brass bedight.

text: "Quod tibi delato Ortygiam dicturus Apollo est, / hic canit et tua nos en ultro ad limina mittit."
translation: "Lo! what Apollo from Ortygia's shrine / would sing, unasked he sends us to proclaim."

text: Haec via te ad hortos publicos ducet.
translation: This road will lead you to the park.

translation: We went to the park, and we played there.

translation: "Tatoeba" means "for example" in Japanese.

translation: This story tells us that youth is instructed by nothing so much as an example.

translation: Hatred stirreth up strifes: but love covereth all sins.

translation: Hatreds, dissensions, discords, seditions, and wars are born from desires.

translation: The lion and the wolf are strong animals.

translation: No animal can exist without plants.

text: Aquilae columbaeque pulcherrima animalia sunt.
translation: Eagles and doves are very beautiful animals.

text: Multa in itinere vidit animalia.
translation: She saw many animals on the way.

text: Animal vivens tibi capiendum est.
translation: You must catch the animal alive.

text: Hoc animal corpus elongatum habet.
translation: This animal has an elongated body.

text: Tulipa florum decus est sed odoris expers.
translation: The Tulip is a graceful flower but has no scent.

text: Dicito, quaeso, salutem uxori tuae meo nomine.
translation: Please say hello to your wife for me.

text: Cum ei salutem dico, nunquam respondit; solum caput inclinat.
translation: When I say hello to him, he never replies; he only inclines his head.

text: "Una salus victis nullam sperare salutem."
translation: "Sole hope to vanquished men of safety is despair."

text: Dicito salutem uxori tuae meo nomine.
translation: Send my greetings to your wife.

text: Salus extra ecclesiam non est.
translation: Outside the Church there is no salvation.

text: Thomae meis verbis salutem adscribe.
translation: Give Tom my regards.

text: Patere legem, quam ipse tulisti.
translation: Those who make laws must not break them.

text: "Ea de te rogavit." "Quid dixit?"
translation: "She asked about you." "What did she say?"

text: Thomas rogavit me quid facere voluerim.
translation: Tom asked me what I wanted to do.

text: Thomas Mariam rogavit ne id faceret.
translation: Tom has asked Mary not to do that.

text: Rogavit quid patri eius nomen esset.
translation: He asked her what her father's name was.

text: Ea me rogavit num suere scirem.
translation: She asked me if I knew how to sew.

text: Thomas rogavit num aliquis Mariam vidisset.
translation: Tom asked if anyone had seen Mary.

text: Rogo me num sit gradus humilior quam "utens"?
translation: I wonder if there exists a level that's lower than "user"?

text: "Estne uxor tua Britannica?" "Britannica non est, Scotica est."
translation: "Is your wife British?" "She isn't British, she's Scottish."

text: Non soror, sed uxor mea est.
translation: She's not my sister. She's my wife.

text: Uxor sum, et duos liberos habeo.
translation: I am married and have two children.

text: Thomas domi est apud uxorem suam.
translation: Tom is at home with his wife.

text: Thomas non amplius apud uxorem habitat.
translation: Tom doesn't live with his wife anymore.

text: Nomen uxori meae Maria est. Quid est nomen tuae uxori?
translation: My wife's name is Mary. What's your wife's name?

text: Nec Thomas nec Maria tot libros habent quot habeo.
translation: Neither Tom nor Mary has as many books as I have.

text: Tot libros quot Thomas non habeo.
translation: I don't have as many books as Tom.

text: Hodie commodius me habeo quam heri.
translation: Today I feel better than I did yesterday.

text: In animo habeo in urbe manere.
translation: I plan to stay in the city.

text: Satis pecūniae habeō ut id emam.
translation: I have money enough to buy it.

text: Nihil habuit quod diceret, ergo abiit.
translation: He had nothing to say, so he went away.

text: Sumus in nomine Iesu Christi et Caroli regis.
translation: We are here in the name of Jesus Christ and King Charles.

text: In Italiam ieratis ut regis filium videretis.
translation: You had gone to Italy to see the king's son.

text: Tam pro papa quam pro rege bibunt omnes sine lege.
translation: From a Pope to a King, everyone drinks without restraint.

text: Omnes huius mundi pecunia reguntur.
translation: In this world everyone is ruled by money.

text: Ille rēx sapienter rēxit.
translation: That king ruled wisely.

text: Per me reges regnant.
translation: Through me kings reign.

text: Si mecum loqui vis, adi me per telephonum.
translation: If you want to speak to me, please call me up.

text: Quod per telephonum me adivisti, gratias tibi ago.
translation: Thank you for calling.

text: Quando me te per telephonum adire vis?
translation: When do you want me to call you?

text: Num me heri nocte per telephonum adivisti?
translation: Did you call me up last night?

text: Volo te eos nunc per telephonum adire.
translation: I want you to call them now.

text: Volo te eum nunc per telephonum adire.
translation: I want you to call him now.

text: Ne te auferant aliorum consilia.
translation: Don't be led astray by other people's advice.

text: Aufer me hinc, quaeso!
translation: Please take me away from here!

text: Auferre, trucidare, rapere, falsis nominibus imperium; atque, ubi solitudinem faciunt, pacem appellant.
translation: They plunder, they slaughter, and they steal: this they falsely name Empire, and where they make a wasteland, they call it peace.

text: Respondit Iacob: Quia timui. Dixi enim, ne forte violenter auferres filias tuas a me.
translation: Jacob answered: That I departed unknown to thee, it was for fear lest thou wouldst take away thy daughters by force.

text: Didymus est tam senex quam pater meus.
translation: Tom is as old as my father.

text: Didymus est pariter senex ac pater meus.
translation: Tom is as old as my father.

text: Didymus est aeque senex ac pater meus.
translation: Tom is as old as my father.

text: Didymus est aeque senex atque pater meus.
translation: Tom is as old as my father.

text: Senex, quem nuper vidisti, avus meus est.
translation: The old man you just saw is my grandfather.

text: Senex barbam hirsutam et oculos defessos habebat.
translation: The old man had a shaggy beard and tired eyes.

text: Polyphemus, Neptuni filius, unum oculum in fronte habebat.
translation: Polyphemus, the son of Neptune, had one eye in his forehead.

text: “Quid facié vester Saurea est?” “Macilentís málís, rúfulus aliquantum, ventriósus, truculentís oculís, commoda statúra, trístí fronte.”
translation: “What does your Saurea look like?” “Thin cheeks, rather ruddy, pot-bellied, savage eyes, average height and a scowl.”

text: Puer propter infirmitatem heri a schola aberat.
translation: The boy was absent from school yesterday because of illness.

text: Non loquor tibi propter uxorem tuam.
translation: I don't speak to you because of your wife.

text: Thomas propter incredulitatem oculos angustiavit suos.
translation: Tom narrowed his eyes in disbelief.

text: Puer osculatur propter matrem.
translation: Many kiss the child for the nurse's sake.

text: Propter valitudinem fumare desiit.
translation: He stopped smoking for the sake of his health.

text: Sero fuimus propter te.
translation: We were late because of you.

text: Hasmonaei fuerunt stirps regia Iudaica, quae terram Israel gubernavit et seditionem Maccabaicam duxit.
translation: The Hasmoneans were a Jewish royal dynasty that ruled the Land of Israel and led the Maccabee revolt.

text: Jamque ibat, dicto parens, et dona Cupido / regia portabat Tyriis, duce laetus Achate.
translation: Forth Cupid, at his mother's word, repairs, / and merrily, for brave Achates led, / the royal presents to the Tyrians bears.

text: "Illic res lætæ regnumque et regia conjux / parta tibi: lacrimas dilectæ pelle Creusæ."
translation: "Wide rule and happy days await thee there, / and royal marriage shall thy portion be. / Weep not for lov'd Creusa, weep not."

text: Thomas et Maria in aquam cucurrerunt.
translation: Tom and Mary ran into the water.

text: Audito sonitu, Thomas ad culinam cucurrit.
translation: When he heard the noise, Tom ran to the kitchen.

text: Canes eius circa domum currebant.
translation: Her dogs were running around the house.

text: Thomas Mariaque in aquam cucurrerunt.
translation: Tom and Mary ran into the water.

text: Didymus ter in hebdomade currit.
translation: Tom jogs three times a week.

text: Nimis fessus sum ut curram.
translation: I am too tired to run.

text: Cur e convivio pulsus es?
translation: Why were you thrown out of the party?

text: Fames pellit lupum e silvis.
translation: Hunger fetches the wolf out of the woods.

text: Thomas ex ecclesia pulsus est.
translation: Tom was driven out of the church.

text: Thomas e templo pulsus est.
translation: Tom was driven out of the temple.

text: Thomas e synagoga pulsus est.
translation: Tom was driven out of the synagogue.

text: Tarquinius ex urbe pulsus est.
translation: Tarquin was driven out of the city.

text: Cur putatis omnes Americanos esse divites?
translation: Why do you think that all Americans are rich?

text: Repente dives nemo factus est bonus.
translation: No good man suddenly gets rich.

text: Si dives essem, id emerem.
translation: If I were rich, I would buy it.

text: Si dives essem, iter facerem.
translation: If I were rich, I would travel.

text: Fecit filium suum esse divitem.
translation: He made his son a wealthy man.

text: Thōmās dīves clārusque fierī vult.
translation: Tom wants to become rich and famous.

text: Dan iudicabit populum suum sicut una tribuum Israel.
translation: Dan shall judge his people like another tribe in Israel.

text: Esse sibi similes alios fur iudicat omnes.
translation: Who is guilty suspects everybody.

text: Promptius est omnibus iudicare, quam facere.
translation: It is easier for everyone to judge than to act.

text: Ex photo iudicans, vetustissima domus est.
translation: Judging by the photo, it is a very old house.

text: Gratias ago tibi, quia non iudicas.
translation: Thank you for not judging.

text: Nolite iudicare, ut non iudicemini.
translation: Do not judge, or you too will be judged.

text: Abram autem erat dives valde in pecoribus, argento et auro.
translation: And he was very rich in possession of gold and silver.

text: Quibus ille respondit: Adducite pecora vestra, et dabo vobis pro eis cibos, si pretium non habetis.
translation: And he answered them: Bring me your cattle, and for them I will give you food, if you have no money.

text: Qui responderunt: Non possumus, donec omnia pecora congregentur et amoveamus lapidem de ore putei, ut adaquemus greges.
translation: They answered: We cannot, till all the cattle be gathered together, and we remove the stone from the well's mouth, that we may water the flocks.

text: Aedificavit autem Noe altare Domino; et tollens de cunctis pecoribus mundis et volucribus mundis obtulit holocausta super altare.
translation: And Noah built an altar unto the Lord: and taking of all cattle and fowls that were clean, offered holocausts upon the altar.

text: Cum audisset Iacob quod violasset Dinam filiam suam, absentibus filiis et in pastu pecorum occupatis, siluit, donec redirent.
translation: But when Jacob had heard this, his sons being absent, and employed in feeding the cattle, he held his peace till they came back.

text: Quotiescumque igitur calefiebant pecora robusta, ponebat Iacob virgas in canalibus aquarum ante oculos pecorum, ut in earum contemplatione conciperent.
translation: So when the ewes went first to ram, Jacob put the rods in the troughs of water before the eyes of the rams, and of the ewes, that they might conceive while they were looking upon them.

text: Et equus et leo et canis et pecus animalia sunt.
translation: The horse, the lion, the dog and the sheep are animals.

text: Huc ubi delati portus intravimus; ecce / læta boum passim campis armenta videmus / caprigenumque pecus, nullo custode, per herbas.
translation: The harbour gained, lo! herds of oxen bright / and goats untended browse the pastures fair.

text: Calamus potentior est quam gladius.
translation: The pen is mightier than the sword.

text: Amor potentior est quam mors.
translation: Love is more powerful than death.

text: Adhaerens potenti adversitatem non timet.
translation: Honour the tree that shelters you.

text: Rex insipiens perdet populum suum; et civitates inhabitabuntur per sensum potentium.
translation: An uneducated king ruins his people; prudent rulers make the city prosper.

text: Calamus potentior est gladio.
translation: The pen is mightier than the sword.

text: Amor potentior est morte.
translation: Love is more powerful than death.

text: "Quis libros scripsit?" - "Ego eos scripsi."
translation: "Who wrote the books?" "I wrote them."

text: Spero me nomen tuum non perperam scripsisse.
translation: I hope I haven't misspelled your name.

text: Consentisne de eis, quae in libro scripsit?
translation: Do you agree with what he wrote in the book?

text: Thomas librum de patre suo scribit.
translation: Tom is writing a book about his father.

text: Robertus mihi semel in mense scribit.
translation: Bob writes to me once a month.

text: Ea mihi semel in mense scribit.
translation: She writes to me once a month.

text: Ioannes multo pulchrior est quam Didymus.
translation: Jon is far more attractive than Tom.

text: Maria est tam pulchra quam soror.
translation: Mary is as pretty as her sister.

text: Maria est pariter pulchra ac soror.
translation: Mary is as pretty as her sister.

text: Maria est aeque pulchra ac soror.
translation: Mary is as pretty as her sister.

text: Maria est aeque pulchra atque soror.
translation: Mary is as pretty as her sister.

text: Thomas Mariae dixit eam videri pulchram.
translation: Tom told Mary that she looked beautiful.

text: Qui cum canibus concumbunt cum pulicibus surgent.
translation: If you lie down with dogs, you'll get up with fleas.

text: Thomas surgere conatus est, neque potuit.
translation: Tom tried to stand up, but he couldn't.

text: Oceanum interea surgens Aurora reliquit.
translation: From the ocean meanwhile is emerging Aurora.

text: Thomas surgebat ut nos salutaret.
translation: Tom got up to greet us.

text: Thomas surgebat ut eos salutaret.
translation: Tom got up to greet them.

text: Thomas surrexit ut me salutaret.
translation: Tom got up to greet me.

text: In sylvis proveniunt fungi, fraga, myrtilli et cetera.
translation: Mushrooms, strawberries, myrtle trees and so on come from the woods.

text: Inter reliquas, potissime sunt: Grus pervigil, Turtur gemens, Cuculus, Palumbes, Picus, Garrulus, Cornix et cetera.
translation: Among the rest, the most able are: the ever watchful Crane, the mournful turtle dove, the cuckoo, the stock dove, the woodpecker, the jay, the crow and so on.

text: Gemmae, sunt lapilli pellucidi, ut: adamas candidus, ribinus rubeus, sapphirim caeruleus, smaragdus viridis, hyacinthus luteus, et cetera; et micant angulati.
translation: Jewels are clear stones, as: the white diamond, blue sapphire, green emerald, yellow Jacinth and so on; and glitter when cut.

text: Inter flores notissimi, primo Vere, Viola, Hyachinthus, Narcissus, tum Lilia, alba et lutea, et carulea; tandem Rosa, Caryophyllum et cetera.
translation: Among the most notable flowers, at the start of Spring, are the Violet, the Crow-tree, the Daffodil, then the Lilies, white and yellow, and blue; and Clove-gillow flowers, and so on.

text: Osse caret lingua, secat os tamen ipsa maligna.
translation: The tongue has no bones, however, being malicious, it is capable of hurting its own mouth.

text: Qui caret asino, clitellas ne quaerat.
translation: He that has no head needs no hat.

text: Ista pupa caret crure et oculo.
translation: That doll is missing a leg and an eye.

text: Vīcus noster aquā nōn caret.
translation: Our village is not short of water.

text: Stilus confusus intellectu caret.
translation: A confusing style cannot be understood.

text: Id, quod amo, careo.
translation: I miss what I love.

text: Homines optiones venerantur. Alpha non eligit. Inevitationem efficit.
translation: Humans worship choices. Alpha doesn't choose. It executes inevitability.

text: Nihil est, quod deus efficere non possit.
translation: There is nothing God cannot do.

text: Nihil est, quod Deus efficere non possit.
translation: There is nothing God cannot do.

text: quod ā mē rogāvit illa effēcī.
translation: I did that which she asked me to do.

text: Omnibus rebus sunt causa et effectus.
translation: Everything has a cause and effect.

text: Nihil fit, nisi tu efficias.
translation: Nothing happens unless you make it happen.

text: Non, si male nunc est, olim sic erit.
translation: There is no evil that always lasts.

text: Olim erat in eo loco magna cedrus.
translation: There used to be a large cedar tree there.

text: Olim mulier vetus in parva insula vixit.
translation: Once there lived an old woman on a small island.

text: Erat olim rex cui tres filiae erant.
translation: Once upon a time lived a king who had three daughters.

text: Forsan et hæc olim meminisse iuvabit.
translation: This too sometime we shall haply remember with delight.

text: In silvis atque in aquis olim erant multæ nymphæ atque deæ.
translation: There once were many nymphs and goddesses in the forests and waters.

text: Erat autem terra labii unius, et sermonum eorumdem.
translation: And the whole earth was of one language, and of one speech.

text: Epistulam e Gallico in Anglicum sermonem converti.
translation: I translated the letter from French into English.

text: Librum e Gallico in Anglicum sermonem converti.
translation: I translated the book from French into English.

text: Liber Thomae in Gallicum sermonem conversus est.
translation: Tom's book was translated into French.

text: Thomas epistulam in Gallicum sermonem convertit.
translation: Tom translated the letter into French.

text: Converte hanc sententiam in Anglicum sermonem.
translation: Translate this sentence into English.

text: Quam quisque novit artem, in hac se exerceat.
translation: Let each one practice the branch which he knows.

text: Cogitabasne de uxore tua cum in exercitu esses?
translation: Did you think about your wife when you were in the army?

text: Scribebasne ad uxorem tuam cum in exercitu esses?
translation: Did you write to your wife when you were in the army?

text: Eis diebus, Germania exercitum fortem habebat.
translation: In those days, Germany had a strong army.

text: Lingua dialectus cum exercitu navibusque est.
translation: A language is a dialect with an army and navy.

text: Num exercitus Romanorum unquam victus est?
translation: Was the Roman army ever defeated?

text: Praeteriens dies omnis est alius gradus ad supremum somnum.
translation: Every passing day is another step towards the final sleep.

text: Investigatio ne unum quidem gradum profecit.
translation: The investigation hasn't progressed even one step.

text: Habesne gradum superiorem vel incipientis?
translation: Do you have an advanced or beginner level?

text: Non ascendes per gradus ad altare meum, ne reveletur turpitudo tua.
translation: Thou shalt not go up by steps unto my altar, lest thy nakedness be discovered.

text: Hærent parietibus scalæ, postesque sub ipsos / nituntur gradibus, clipeosque ad tela sinistris / protecti objiciunt, prensant fastigia dextris.
translation: Close cling their ladders to the walls; these, fain / to clutch the doorposts, climb from floor to floor, / their right hands strive the battlements to gain, / their left with lifted shield the arrowy storm sustain.

text: Canis caudam agitans dominum secutus est.
translation: The dog followed its master, wagging its tail.

text: Catellus caudam agitans me secutus est.
translation: A puppy followed me wagging its tail.

text: Cum canis laetatur, cauda agitatur.
translation: When the dog is happy it wags its tail.

text: Quae te res tantopere agitat?
translation: What is bothering you so much?

text: Dic quae res te agitet.
translation: Tell me what's bothering you.

text: Quae res te agitat hodie?
translation: What's bothering you today?

text: Didymus est magis intelligens quam honestus.
translation: Tom is more clever than honest.

text: Didymus est intelligentior quam honestior.
translation: Tom is more clever than honest.

text: Dubito an honestus sit.
translation: I doubt whether he is honest.

text: Thomas vir honestus est.
translation: Tom is a man of honor.

text: Puer valde honestus est.
translation: The boy is very honest.

text: Thomas est vir honestus.
translation: Thomas is an honourable man.

text: Ea domi avunculi sui nunc moratur.
translation: She is now staying at her uncle's house.

text: Ubi morārī in animō habēs?
translation: Where are you planning to stay?

text: Non bene conveniunt, nec in una sede morantur maiestas et amor.
translation: They don't understand each other well, nor do majesty and love live together.

text: Si fecissemus id quod a nobis optavit Thomas, iam fortasse moraremur.
translation: If we'd done what Tom asked us to do, we'd probably be dead now.

text: Thomas Bostoniae moratus est.
translation: Tom stayed in Boston.

text: Et fuit Deus cum eo; qui crevit et moratus est in solitudine factusque est iuvenis sagittarius.
translation: And God was with him: and he grew, and dwelt in the wilderness, and became a young man, an archer.

text: Sonitus pluviae musica mihi est.
translation: The sound of rain is music to me.

text: Telephonum tunc maxime sonuit.
translation: Just then, the telephone rang.

text: Et sonitus bucinæ paulatim crescebat in maius; Moyses loquebatur, et Deus respondebat ei cum voce.
translation: And the sound of the trumpet grew by degrees louder and louder, and was drawn out to a greater length: Moses spoke, and God answered him.

text: Aser, pinguis panis eius, et præbebit delicias regales.
translation: Aser, his bread shall be fat, and he shall yield dainties to kings.

text: Cum vita laetitiam praebet, vita sensum habet.
translation: When life is a joy, then life has meaning.

text: Praebet candoris lac nigri vacca coloris.
translation: A black hen lays a white egg.

text: Hic liber maximum usum mihi praebuit.
translation: This book was very useful to me.

text: Raro lupi lenti praebentur fercula denti.
translation: Sleeping foxes catch no poultry.

text: Occurritque ei servus et ait: Pauxillum mihi ad sorbendum præbe aquæ de hydria tua.
translation: And the servant ran to meet her, and said: Give me a little water to drink of thy pitcher.

text: Volo ire ad regionem ubi Oceanus est.
translation: I want to go to a region where the ocean is.

text: Diaetae huius regionis valde carae sunt.
translation: Apartments here are really expensive.

text: Eram natura sitiens cognoscendi novas res, varias regiones, urbes, linguas, ac mores hominum.
translation: I was by nature greedy of knowing new things, divers countries, cities, languages, and manners of men.

text: Misit autem nuntios ante se ad Esau fratrem suum in terram Seir, in regionem Edom.
translation: And he sent messengers before him to Esau, his brother, to the land of Seir, to the country of Edom.

text: Quibus sedentibus, locutus est ad propinquum: Partem agri fratris nostri Elimelech vendit Noemi, quæ reversa est de regione Moabitide.
translation: They sat down, and he spoke to the kinsman: Noemi, who is returned from the country of Moab will sell a parcel of land that belonged to our brother Elimelech.

text: Si apprehendisti tu linguam huius sententiae, traduce hanc linguae aliae.
translation: If you have learnt the language of this sentence, translate it to another language.

text: Mea sententia, habes familiam admirabilem.
translation: In my opinion, you have a wonderful family.

text: Nēmō sententiam meam audīre vult.
translation: No one wants to listen to my opinions.

text: Ego hanc sententiam non scripsi.
translation: It wasn't me who wrote this sentence.

text: Tantum sententias mihi placentes converto.
translation: I only translate those sentences I like.

text: Haec sententia tibi ediscenda est.
translation: You have to memorize this sentence.

text: Hic culter valde acer est.
translation: This knife is very sharp.

text: Hic culter acerrimus est.
translation: This knife is very sharp.

text: Thomas acri cultro eget.
translation: Tom needs a sharp knife.

text: Tum Danai gemitu atque ereptæ virginis ira / undique collecti invadunt, acerrimus Ajax / et gemini Atridæ, Dolopumque exercitus omnis.
translation: Now too, with shouts of fury and disdain / to see the maiden rescued, here and there / the Danaans gathering round us, charge amain; / fierce-hearted Ajax, the Atridan pair, / and all Thessalia's host our scanty band o'erbear.

text: Vita brevis est, qua de causa Python utor.
translation: Life is short, so I use Python.

text: Duo plumba habet. Alterum longum, alterum breve est.
translation: He has two pencils. One is long and the other one is short.

text: Vobis breviter exponam quid factum sit.
translation: I will explain to you briefly what happened.

text: Tibi breviter exponam quid factum sit.
translation: I will explain to you briefly what happened.

text: Credo illam brevi adventuram esse.
translation: I believe she'll arrive in a short time.

text: Vita brevis esse saepe dicitur.
translation: They often say that life is short.

text: Volat ille per aëra magnum / remigio alarum ac Libyæ citus adstitit oris.
translation: With feathered oars he cleaves the skies, and straight / on Libya's shores alighting, speeds his hest.

text: Equus cornua non habet; bos ovisque cornua habent.
translation: The horse doesn't have horns; the ox and the sheep have horns.

text: Nephthali cerva emissa, dans cornua pulchra.
translation: Nephthali, a hart let loose, and giving words of beauty.

text: Camelus desiderans cornua, perdidit aures.
translation: Desiring to have horns, the camel lost its ears.

text: Antehac putābam te habere cornua.
translation: I thought you had balls, it seems I was wrong.

text: Porcus (Scrofa) cum Porcellis habent Setas, at non Cornua, sed etiam Ungulas bisulcas ut illa.
translation: The pig, the sow and the piglets have bristles, but not horns, but also cloven feet, as others do.

text: Cornu bos capitur, voce ligatur homo.
translation: An ox is captured by the horns, a person is bound by his word.

text: Filium quoque vel filiam si cornu percusserit, simili sententiæ subiacebit.
translation: If he have gored a son, or a daughter, he shall fall under the like sentence.

text: Me paenitet sed tuae excusationes ingratae sunt.
translation: I'm sorry but your excuses are unacceptable.

text: Amicitae videtur Thomam ingratum esse.
translation: Tom doesn't seem to have a lot of friends.

text: Talibus incusat gressumque ad mœnia tendit.
translation: Thus he, reproaching. Towards the town they fare / in haste.

text: Dixerat ille, et jam per mœnia clarior ignis / auditur, propiusque æstus incendia volvunt.
translation: He spake, and nearer through the city came / the roar, the crackle and the fiery glow / of conflagration, rolling floods of flame.

text: Feror huc, et litore curvo / mœnia prima loco, fatis ingressus iniquis, / Aeneadas meo nomen de nomine fingo.
translation: Hither, with fates malign, / I steer, and landing for our purposed town / the walls along the winding shore design, / and coin for them a name "AEneadae" from mine.

text: Filia quinta eius multo pulchrior est quam ceterae.
translation: His fifth daughter is much more beautiful than the others.

text: Una ex raedis eius caerulea est, ceterae rubrae.
translation: One of her cars is blue and the others are red.

text: Ceterum censeo Carthaginem esse delendam.
translation: Moreover, I judge that Carthage must be annihilated.

text: Ceterum censeo Australiam esse delendam.
translation: Furthermore, I think that Australia must be destroyed.

text: Ubi sunt ceterae puellae?
translation: Where are the other girls?

text: E domo exivi et Thoman vidi cum canicula Fido.
translation: I went out of the house and saw Tom with his little dog Fido.

text: Volo te e domo mea exire.
translation: I want you to leave my house.

text: Nemo scire potest, quod erit exitus.
translation: No one can know what the outcome will be.

text: Vir procerus e domo exiit.
translation: The tall man came out of the house.

text: Parentes mei ex ecclesia exierunt.
translation: My parents came out of the church.

text: Thoman prope exitum stantem vidi.
translation: I saw Tom standing near the exit.

text: Pedibus iter facere malim quam curru publico vehi.
translation: I'd rather walk than take a bus.

text: Pedibus ire malim, quam curru publico vehi.
translation: I'd rather walk than take a bus.

text: Mori me malim quam te flentem videam.
translation: I'd rather die than see you cry.

text: Domi manere malim, quam solus ire.
translation: I'd rather stay home than go alone.

text: Mori me malim quam hoc facere.
translation: I'd rather die than do that.

text: Mori me malim quam hoc faciam.
translation: I'd rather die than do that.

text: Mons Fusius ob pulchram speciem notus est.
translation: Mt. Fuji is noted for its beautiful shape.

text: Res per speciem parva ad magnum eventum perducere potest.
translation: An apparently small event may lead to a great result.

text: Sciliciet illius speciei memini.
translation: Of course I remember that scene.

text: Fingit sponsa se noctu a sponso visitari eiusque pulchritudinem, sodalibus alloquens, extollit itemque sponsus dilectae speciem.
translation: The bride imagines that she is visited by the groom at night, and praises his beauty, addressing his companions, and the groom, in turn, also praises the beauty of his beloved.

text: Haec est species aliena invadens.
translation: This is an invasive species.

text: Ea est species aliena invadens.
translation: That's an invasive species.

text: Fallaces sunt rerum species.
translation: You can't judge a book by its cover.

text: Septem Romanorum reges fuerunt, quorum ultimus Tarquinius Superbus fuit.
translation: There were seven kings of the Romans, of whom Tarquinius Superbus was the last.

text: Hodie ultimus dies vitae meae est.
translation: Today is the last day of my life.

text: Tarquinius ultimus rex Romanorum fuit.
translation: Tarquinius was the last king of the Romans.

text: Saturni dies hebdomadis ultimus est.
translation: Saturday is the last day of week.

text: Ultro flens ipse videbar / compellare virum et mæstas expromere voces:
translation: Then, weeping too, I seem in sorrowing strain / to hail the hero, with a voice of pain.

text: Hic ludus ultimus est.
translation: This is the last game.

text: Thomas certissime non tot sapiens est quot putat.
translation: Tom certainly isn't as smart as he thinks he is.

text: Morte nihil certius est, nihil vero incertius quam eius hora.
translation: Nothing is more certain than death, and nothing more uncertain than its hour.

text: Non est arbor solida nec fortis nisi in quam frequens ventus ineversat: ipsa enim uexatione constringitur et radices certius figit.
translation: No tree is solid or strong except one that the frequent wind bends; for it is tightened by the strain and its roots made more secure.

text: Non potest bene imperare, qui male ante serviit.
translation: Through obedience, learn to command.

text: Oppugnatores venditori imperaverunt ut pecuniam sibi daret.
translation: The attackers ordered the vendor to give them the money.

text: Imperaverunt mihi ut in autocineto manerem.
translation: They told me to stay in the car.

text: Thomas Mariae imperavit ut tardius ederet.
translation: Tom told Mary to eat more slowly.

text: Thomas Mariae imperavit ut lentius ederet.
translation: Tom told Mary to eat more slowly.

text: Descenditque in aream et fecit omnia, quæ sibi imperaverat socrus.
translation: And she went down to the barnfloor, and did all that her mother in law had bid her.

text: Cur quod ego tibi impero nunquam facis?
translation: Why do you never do what I tell you?

text: Tibi ut ad dextram flectas impero.
translation: I order you to turn right.

text: A malo ad peius imus.
translation: We are going from bad to worse.

text: Maria Gallice pessime scribit.
translation: Mary writes Greek very poorly.

text: Res peius se habent.
translation: Matters are becoming worse.

text: Puto me non posse prohibere Thoman id facere.
translation: I don't think I can keep Tom from doing that.

text: Isti stulti eam legem perfregerunt quae prohibet leges perfringi.
translation: These fools broke the law that forbade breaking the law.

text: Ius habemus ad prohibere laborem.
translation: We have the right to strike.

text: Noli prohibere benefacere eum qui potest; si vales, et ipse benefac.
translation: If you are capable of doing good for someone then do not hold back.

text: Si potuissem, hoc prohibuissem.
translation: If I could've prevented this, I would have.

text: Nullo modo prohiberi potest.
translation: There's no way to prevent that.

text: Alcmena autem, mater puerorum, clamorem audiverat, et maritum suum e somno excitaverat.
translation: But Alcmena, the boys' mother, heard the scream and woke her husband.

text: Cui ait Dominus: Vidi afflictionem populi mei in Aegypto et clamorem eius audivi propter duritiam exactorum eorum.
translation: And the Lord said to him: I have seen the affliction of my people in Egypt, and I have heard their cry because of the rigour of them that are over the works.

text: Ausus quin etiam voces jactare per umbram, / implevi clamore vias, mæstusque Creusam / nequidquam ingeminans iterumque iterumque vocavi.
translation: I shout, and through the darkness shout again, / rousing the streets, and call and call anew / "Creusa", and "Creusa", but in vain.

text: Auditis Esau sermonibus patris, irrugiit clamore magno et amaro ultra modum et ait patri suo: Benedic etiam mihi, pater mi!
translation: Esau having heard his father's words, roared out with a great cry; and, being in a consternation, said: Bless me also, my father.

text: Quidquid id est, timeo Danaos et dona ferentes.
translation: Whatever it is, I fear the Greeks even when they offer gifts.

text: Thomas uxori suae dona rare dat.
translation: Tom seldom gives his wife presents.

text: Sanguinem donavit ut fratrem salvaret.
translation: He gave blood in order to save his brother.

text: Sanguinem donavit ut sororem salvaret.
translation: She gave blood in order to save her sister.

text: Utri horum puerorum librum donabis?
translation: To which of these boys will you give the book?

text: Dona e terra tua misisti.
translation: You sent gifts from your country.

text: Nullum enim officium referenda gratia magis necessarium est.
translation: No duty is more imperative than saying thank you.

text: Officium ovale in Domo Alba situm est.
translation: The oval office is in the White House.

text: Didymus et Maria nunc in officio sunt.
translation: Tom and Mary are at work now.

text: Visne unicorne ad officium vehi? Ego volo.
translation: Do you want to ride a unicorn to work? Because I do.

text: Ad officium cras mane non erimus.
translation: We won't come to the office tomorrow morning.

text: Officium eius prope stationem ferriviariam est.
translation: His office is near the train station.

text: Fames scelera committere eum coegit.
translation: It was hunger that impelled him to crime.

text: Caesar, hortatus milites, proelium commisit.
translation: Caesar encouraged the soldiers and committed them to battle.

text: Deo et fortunae me committo.
translation: I commit myself to God and fortune.

text: Qui responderunt: Quare sic loquitur dominus noster? Absit a servis tuis, ut tantum flagitii commiserimus.
translation: And they answered: Why doth our lord speak so, as though thy servants had committed so heinous a fact?

text: Plantas si vis crescere, eas rigare oportet.
translation: If you want the plants to grow, you must water them.

text: Hi flores pulchri in Asia crescunt.
translation: These beautiful flowers grow in Asia.

text: Plantae sine aere crescere non possunt.
translation: Plants can't grow without air.

text: Plantae sine aqua crescere non possunt.
translation: Plants can't grow without water.

text: Pecunia in arboribus non crescit.
translation: Money doesn't grow on trees.

text: Oryza in terris calidis crescit.
translation: Rice grows in warm countries.

text: Haec feles est aeque magna ac illa.
translation: This cat is as big as that one.

text: Haec feles est aeque magna atque illa.
translation: This cat is as big as that one.

text: Haec raeda est aeque magna ac illa.
translation: This car is as big as that car.

text: Haec raeda est aeque magna atque illa.
translation: This car is as big as that car.

text: Haec raeda est aeque cara ac illa.
translation: This car is as expensive as that one.

text: Haec raeda est aeque cara atque illa.
translation: This car is as expensive as that one.

text: In hoc modo Thomas et ego amici facti sumus.
translation: That's how Tom and I became friends.

text: Sibi conciliaverunt et amici iterum facti sunt.
translation: They made up and became friends again.

text: Cometae e glacie lapideque facti sunt.
translation: Comets are made from ice and rock.

text: Hī calceī in Italiā factī sunt.
translation: These shoes are made in Italy.

text: Hi calcei e corio facti sunt.
translation: The shoes are made of leather.

text: Omnes flores e charta facti sunt.
translation: All of the flowers are paper.

text: Caedite eos. Novit enim Dominus qui sunt eius.
translation: Kill them all, for the Lord will know his own.

text: Non caedit semper, durum quicumque minatur.
translation: There are more men threatened than stricken.

text: Cedo manum. Posthac tibi exponam.
translation: Give me your hand. I'll explain later.

text: Paleæ non dantur nobis, et lateres similiter imperantur; en famuli tui flagellis cædimur, et populus tuus est in culpa.
translation: Straw is not given us, and bricks are required of us as before; behold we, thy servants, are beaten with whips, and thy people is unjustly dealt withal.

text: Hic primum ex alto delubri culmine telis / nostrorum obruimur, oriturque miserrima cædes / armorum facie et Graiarum errore jubarum.
translation: Here first with missiles, from a temple's height / hurled by our comrades, we are crushed and slain, / and piteous is the slaughter, at the sight / of Argive helms for Argive foes mista'en.

text: Tēne virum perīculōsum esse exīstimās?
translation: Do you consider yourself as a dangerous guy?

text: Quis enim id facile existimaret?
translation: And who claimed it would be easy?

text: Te id iam fecisse existimavi.
translation: I thought you already did that.

text: Te nimium scire existimo.
translation: I think you know too much.

text: Nōnne mē fōrmōsum exīstimās?
translation: Don't you think I'm attractive?

text: Nōnne mē fōrmōsam exīstimās?
translation: Don't you think I'm attractive?

text: Ad Appii Claudii senectutem accedebat ut cæcus esset.
translation: In his old age, Appius Claudius faced the additional challenge of being blind.

text: Ad consilium ne accesseris, antequam voceris.
translation: Give neither counsel nor salt until you are asked for.

text: Accede huc ad me, Thoma.
translation: Come over here, Tom.

text: Accede huc quam primum.
translation: Get here as soon as possible.

text: Accede huc ad me.
translation: Come over here.

text: Qui cum vidissent eum procul, antequam accederet ad eos, cogitaverunt illum occidere.
translation: And when they saw him afar off, before he came nigh them, they thought to kill him.

text: Me impedit pudor haec exquirere.
translation: Embarrassment prevents me from asking such questions.

text: Et Didymo et Mariae pelliculae antiquae placent.
translation: Tom and Mary both like old movies.

text: Liber tuus non antiquus, sed novus est.
translation: Your book isn't old but new.

text: Ecce duo libri Latini: liber antiquus et liber novus.
translation: Look! Two Latin books: an old book and a new book.

text: Habitavistine unquam in aedificio antiquo?
translation: Have you ever lived in an old building?

text: Murus circumdabat urbis partem antiquam.
translation: A wall surrounded the ancient part of the city.

text: Pelliculam antiquam per telehorasim aspexi.
translation: I watched an old movie on TV.

text: Nam tua res agitur, paries cum proximus ardet.
translation: It is indeed your business when the neighbor's wall is burning.

text: Illa imaginem photographicam meam arsit.
translation: She burned my photo.

text: His animum arrecti dictis, et fortis Achates / et pater Aeneas jamdudum erumpere nubem / ardebant.
translation: Roused by these words, long since the sire of Troy / yearned, like his friend, their comrades to surprise / and burst the cloud.

text: Obstipuit simul ipse simul percussus Achates / laetitiaque metuque; avidi conjungere dextras / ardebant, sed res animos incognita turbat.
translation: At once, 'twixt joy and terror rent in twain, / amazed, AEneas and Achates stand, / and long to greet old friends and clasp a comrade's hand. / Yet wildering wonder at so strange a scene / still holds them mute, while anxious thoughts divide / their doubtful minds.

text: Thomas in Australia non est, sed Maria ibi est.
translation: Tom isn't in Australia, but Mary is.

text: Thoman volebam ibi manere ubi erat.
translation: I wanted Tom to stay where he was.

text: Thomas multos ibi dies commoratus est.
translation: Tom stayed there for several days.

text: Thomas ibi cum amicula sua est.
translation: Tom is there with his girlfriend.

text: Ubi est confessio, ibi est remissio.
translation: A fault confessed is half-redressed.

text: Et ille discedens tentoria fixit ad torrentem Geraræ habitavitque ibi.
translation: So he departed, and came to the torrent of Gerara, to dwell there.

text: Numidia scissa est ā Rōmānīs in prōvinciās trēs.
translation: Numidia was ripped into three provinces by the Romans.

text: Quot prōvinciās habet Canada?
translation: How many provinces does Canada have?

text: Omnesque provinciæ veniebant in Aegyptum, ut emerent escas apud Ioseph, quia inopia invaluerat in universa terra.
translation: And all provinces came into Egypt, to buy food, and to seek some relief of their want.

text: sed quis custodiet ipsos custodes?
translation: But who will guard the guards themselves?

text: Custodes debent gemmas custodire.
translation: The guards must keep watch over the jewels.

text: Quis custodiet ipsos custodes?
translation: Who will guard the guards themselves?

text: Parentes liberorum custodes sunt.
translation: Parents are responsible for their children.

text: Canis custos domus est.
translation: The dog protects the house.

text: Custodes eos non videbant.
translation: The guards didn't see them.

text: Sami autocineto eget ut in hac urbe supersit.
translation: Sami needs a car to survive in this city.

text: Est satis atque superest verbum sapientibus unum.
translation: A word to the wise is enough.

text: Ex eo proelio milia hominum triginta superfuerunt.
translation: Thirty thousand men survived that battle.

text: Omni superfuisti quae adhuc tibi obtigerunt.
translation: You have survived everything that has happened to you so far.

text: Duo tantum ex terraemotu superfuerunt.
translation: Only two people survived the earthquake.

text: Post festum fatuus superest.
translation: Once on shore, we pray no more.

text: Quamquam multa iam dies erat, non tamen laborare desinebat.
translation: Though it was very late, he went on working.

text: Acta diurna legere desiit et me aspexit.
translation: She stopped reading the newspaper and looked at me.

text: Anno millesimo nongentesimo quadragesimo quinto bellum desinit.
translation: The war ended in 1945.

text: Thomas se velle me desinere dixit.
translation: Tom said that he wanted me to stop.

text: Roga Thoman ut desinat hoc facere.
translation: Ask Tom to stop doing that.

text: Cur non desinimus Gallice loqui et ad Anglicam linguam transimus?
translation: Why don't we stop speaking French and switch to English?

text: Fessus sum et domum ire volo.
translation: I am tired and I want to go home.

text: Fessa sum et domum ire volo.
translation: I am tired and I want to go home.

text: Fessus erat, cum domum advenit.
translation: He was exhausted when he got home.

text: Pueri natando fessi esse videbantur.
translation: The little children looked tired from swimming.

text: Thomas se fessum esse dixit.
translation: Tom said that he was tired.

text: Dixit se valde fessum esse.
translation: He said he was extremely tired.

text: Aquila solum dīligenter dēspicit. Praedam quaerit.
translation: An eagle is watching the ground vigilantly from on high. He is looking out for prey.

text: Beniamin lupus rapax; mane comedet prædam et vespere dividet spolia.
translation: Benjamin a ravenous wolf, in the morning shall eat the prey, and in the evening shall divide the spoil.

text: Praedam in tres partes divisimus.
translation: We split the loot three ways.

text: Aquila impetum in praedam fēcit.
translation: The eagle dived at its prey.

text: Et jam porticibus vacuis Junonis asylo / custodes lecti Phœnix et dirus Ulysses / prædam asservabant.
translation: Armed, in the vacant courts, by Juno's fane, / Phoenix and curst Ulysses watched the prey.

text: Rursum ex diverso cœli cæcisque latebris / turba sonans prædam pedibus circumvolat uncis, / polluit ore dapes.
translation: Back, from another quarter of the sky, / dark-ambushed, round the clamorous Harpies fly / with taloned claws, and taste and taint the prey.

text: Non habet eventus sordida praeda bonos.
translation: Ill gotten, ill spent.

text: Catulus leonis Iuda: a præda, fili mi, ascendisti; requiescens accubuit ut leo et quasi leæna; quis suscitabit eum?
translation: Juda is a lion's whelp: to the prey, my son, thou art gone up: resting thou hast couched as a lion, and as a lioness, who shall rouse him?

text: Hic hortus publicus mihi pueritiae meae memoriam affert.
translation: This park reminds me of my childhood.

text: Hoc mihi patris mei memoriam affert.
translation: That reminds me of my father.

text: Thomas mihi sui patris memoriam affert.
translation: Tom reminds me of his father.

text: Hoc mihi meae pueritiae memoriam affert.
translation: It reminds me of my childhood.

text: Thomas mihi patris mei memoriam affert.
translation: Tom reminds me of my father.

text: Ea illi eius matris memoriam affert.
translation: She reminds him of his mother.

text: De libro mentionem fecit cuius titulus mihi e memoria excessit.
translation: He mentioned a book the title of which I can't remember now.

text: Memoria minuitur nisi eam exerceas.
translation: Memory is impaired unless you exercise it.

text: Libri sunt chartacea hominum memoria.
translation: Books are the paper memory of mankind.

text: "Tenesne memoria?" "Sic opinor."
translation: “Have you memorised it?” “I think so yes.”

text: “Tenesne memoriā?” “Sic opinor.”
translation: “Do you remember it?” “I think so.”

text: Memoria hominibus mala est.
translation: People have short memories.

text: Hic liber in quattuor partes divisus est.
translation: This book is divided into four parts.

text: In partēs trēs dīvidere possumus mūnus.
translation: We can divide the work into three parts.

text: Asia ab America oceanus Pacificus dividit.
translation: The Pacific ocean separates Asia from America.

text: Domum meam ab eius fluvius dividit.
translation: My home is separated from his by a river.

text: Consilium in quinque partes divisum est.
translation: The committee divided into five sections.

text: Nomina Latina in quinque declinationes dividuntur.
translation: Nouns in Latin have five declensions.

text: Horologium tuum maiore pretio quam horologium meum constat.
translation: Your watch is more expensive than mine.

text: Raeda tua minore pretio quam raeda mea constat.
translation: Your car is cheaper than mine.

text: Hoc brachiale maiore pretio quam illud constat.
translation: This bracelet is more expensive than that one.

text: Ille calamus maiore pretio quam hic constat.
translation: That pen is more expensive than this one.

text: Raeda tua maiore pretio quam mea constat.
translation: Your car is more expensive than mine.

text: Horologius eius maiore pretio quam meum constat.
translation: His clock is more expensive than mine.

text: Magister noster raeda in ludum vehitur.
translation: Our teacher comes to school by car.

text: Modo curru publico, modo autocineto vehimur.
translation: Sometimes we go by bus, and sometimes by car.

text: Modo curru publico, modo autocineto veheris.
translation: Sometimes you go by bus, and sometimes by car.

text: Modo curru publico, modo autocineto vehitur.
translation: Sometimes she goes by bus, and sometimes by car.

text: Modo curru publico, modo autocineto vehuntur.
translation: Sometimes they go by bus, and sometimes by car.

text: Didymus ad scholam curru publico vehitur.
translation: Tom goes to school by bus.

text: Aqua huius maris nigra est.
translation: The water of this sea is black.

text: Napoleo Bonapars feles nigras timebat.
translation: Napoleon Bonaparte feared black cats.

text: Quid est in arcula nigra?
translation: What's in the black box?

text: Felem et canem habeo. Feles nigra est et canis albus est.
translation: I have a cat and a dog. The cat is black and the dog is white.

text: Femina nigram stolam gerit.
translation: The woman is wearing a black dress.

text: Feles nigra celeriter currit.
translation: The black cat is running fast.

text: Oppidum, in quo habitat, mihi non placet.
translation: I don't like the city in which he lives.

text: Uxorem suam ex oppido excedere puto.
translation: I think his wife is going out of town.

text: Praeterivi hoc oppido, cum rediens essem.
translation: I drove past this town on the way home.

text: Quot oppida in Americā Foederātā sunt?
translation: How many cities are in America?

text: Salamanca oppidum non valde magnum est.
translation: Salamanca isn't a very big city.

text: Habitavistine unquam in magno oppido?
translation: Have you ever lived in a big city?

text: Mochos primus dicitur librae pondus invenisse.
translation: It is said Mocho was the first to discover the scale.

text: Ne subeat pondus iumentum viribus impar.
translation: Let not a beast bear a weight unequal to its strength.

text: "Tum celerare fugam patriaque excedere suadet / auxiliumque viæ veteres tellure recludit / thesauros, ignotum argenti pondus et auri".
translation: "Then bade her fly the country, and revealed, / to aid her flight, an old and unknown weight / of gold and silver, in the ground concealed."

text: Multa movens animo, Nymphas venerabar agrestes / Gradivumque patrem, Geticis qui præsidet arvis, / rite secundarent visus omenque levarent.
translation: Much-musing, to the woodland nymphs I pray, / and Mars, the guardian of the Thracian plain, / with favouring grace the omen to allay, / and bless the dreadful vision.

text: Fit sonitus, spumante salo; jamque arva tenebant; / ardentesque oculos suffecti sanguine et igni, / sibila lambebant linguis vibrantibus ora.
translation: Lashed into foam, behind them roars the brine; / now, gliding onward to the beach, ere long / they gain the fields, and rolling bloodshot eyne / that blaze with fire, the monsters move along, / and lick their hissing jaws, and dart a flickering tongue.

text: Arvum fert fruges et olera.
translation: A field yields corn and vegetables.

text: "Quo res summa loco, Panthu? Quam prendimus arcem?"
translation: "Panthus", I cry, "how fares the fight? what tower / still hold we?"

text: Quid si sors aliter quam voles evenerit?
translation: What if fate turns out differently than you would like?

text: Laocoon, ductus Neptuno sorte sacerdos, / solemnes taurum ingentem mactabat ad aras.
translation: Laocoon, Neptune's priest, by lot ordained, / a stately bull before the altar slew.

text: "Maturate fugam, regique hæc dicite vestro: / non illi imperium pelagi sævumque tridentem, / sed mihi sorte datum."
translation: "Presumptuous winds, begone, / and take your king this message, that the sway / of Ocean and the sceptre and the throne / Fate gave to me, not him; the trident is my own."

text: Num bibisti vinum illud omne, quod emi?
translation: You didn't drink all the wine that I bought, did you?

text: Spero fore ut vinum tibi placeat.
translation: I hope the wine is to your taste.

text: Vinum bonum laetificat cor hominis.
translation: Wine makes glad the heart of man.

text: Lac alibilius est quam vinum.
translation: Milk is more nutritious than wine.

text: Vinum rubrum quam album malo.
translation: I prefer red wine to white.

text: Hoc vīnum bonum esse putō.
translation: I think this wine is good.

text: Macerabant illum argillaceum panem vino vetustissi mae faecis.
translation: They soaked that clay bread in wine of very old dregs.

text: Macerabant fragmenta panis vino, immersa cyathis.
translation: They soaked pieces of bread in wine, dipping them into their ladles.

text: Nigriores sunt oculi eius vino et dentes eius lacte candidiores.
translation: His eyes are more beautiful than wine, and his teeth whiter than milk.

text: Vino gravis et impos sui est.

translation: There are no dogs bigger than this one.

text: Canis tuus est. Ubi est meus?
translation: This dog is yours. Where is mine?

text: Quid interest inter lupum et canem?
translation: What's the difference between a dog and a wolf?

text: Quid est optimum pascendi cani tempus?
translation: When is the best time to feed your dog?

text: Genitores meos et canem eorum amo.
translation: I love my parents and their dog.

text: Parentes meos et canem eorum amo.
translation: I love my parents and their dog.

text: Apri omnia tubera solani nostra ederunt.
translation: Wild boars have eaten all of our potatoes.

text: Thomas nescivit quid Mariae placiturum esset.
translation: Tom didn't know what Mary would like.

text: Placentam Neapolitanam edebam, nunc autem non edo.
translation: I used to eat pizza, but now I don't.

text: Vegetarianus sum, carnes non edo.
translation: I am a vegetarian, I don't eat meat.

text: Vegetariana sum, carnes non edo.
translation: I am a vegetarian, I don't eat meat.

text: Ore gusto, edo, bibo.
translation: I taste, eat and drink with my mouth.

text: Librum lego dum edo.
translation: I read a book while I eat.

text: Sorbitionem in culina edo.
translation: I'm eating soup in the kitchen.

text: Marcus neque fateri audebat neque abnuere poterat.
translation: Marcus was neither heard to confess nor able to deny.

text: Thomas mihi fateor non placere.
translation: I admit I don't like Tom very much.

text: Me mentitum esse fateor.
translation: I admit I lied.

text: "Fateor; sed tamen quid facies ista pecunia?" "Emam chartam, et alia, quæ sunt opus mihi."
translation: "I admit it, but what then will you do with that money?" "I will buy paper and other things I need."

text: Inimici sui amicum nemo in amicitiam sumit.
translation: No one takes into friendship the friend of their enemy.

text: Quae potest esse vitae iucunditas sublatis amicitiis?
translation: What can be the pleasure of life if friendships are taken away?

text: Vera amicitia pretiosior est quam pecunia.
translation: A true friendship is more valuable than money.

text: Amicitia quae desiit, nunquam vera fuit.
translation: A friend who has ceased to be one never was one.

text: Vera amicitia pretiosior est pecunia.
translation: A true friendship is more valuable than money.

text: Nihil tam pretiosum quam amicitia.
translation: Nothing is as precious as friendship.

text: Cum parvus eram, cricetum aureum habebam.
translation: When I was small, I had a golden hamster.

text: Rerum universitas aureum opus Domini est.
translation: The universe is the Lord's golden work.

text: Regis filia curru aureo vehebatur.
translation: The princess rode in a golden carriage.

text: Horologium quod habeo aureum est.
translation: The clock that I have is made of gold.

text: Matercula duos anulos aureos habet.
translation: Mom has two gold rings.

text: Horologium aureum ei dedi.
translation: I gave him a gold watch.

text: Calcei et toga candida in cubiculo sunt.
translation: The shoes and the white toga are in the bedroom.

text: Capilli avi mei candidi sunt ut nix.
translation: My grandfather has snowy white hair.

text: Thomas equum candidum habet.
translation: Tom has a white horse.

text: Dentes eius candidi erant.
translation: Her teeth were white.

text: Interim potabamus multum salsae aquae.
translation: In the mean time we drank much salt water.

text: "Fuit tua negligentia." "Fateor, sed interim indica, si scias quem accepisse."
translation: "That was your fault." "I admit it, but in the meantime tell me if you know who has taken it."

text: Novus annus interim incipiebat.
translation: Meanwhile, a new year began.

text: Jam animus coepit vacillare, utrum redirem ad negotiationem, inter missam, an persequerer religionem fugientem. Interim venit in mentem poste conjungi.
translation: Now my mind began to waver, whether I should return to merchandise which I had given over, or pursue religion flying from me. In the mean time it comes into my mind that they might be joined together.

text: Frustra hunc laborem fecimus.
translation: We did this work in vain.

text: "Interea igitur expectabo sperans; sed quid si nihil superstiterit tibi?" "Dicam tibi statim, ne expectes diutius frustra."
translation: "In the meantime I wait in hope, but what if you have nothing left?" "I can tell you straight away that you will not be waiting in vain."

text: Nec latuere doli fratrem Junonis.
translation: Juno's wiles did not go unnoticed by her brother (Neptune).

text: Sicut fragmen mali punici, ita genae tuae, absque eo quod intrinsecus latet.
translation: Your cheeks, two pomegranate cuts, can be seen behind the veil.

text: Id mihi non latet.
translation: I know that.

text: Quatuor hic, primum omen, equos in gramine vidi / tondentes campum late, candore nivali.
translation: Lo, here, first omen offered to our eyes, / four snow-white steeds are grazing on the plain.

text: Cumque habitaret in illa regione, abiit Ruben et dormivit cum Bilha concubina patris sui; quod illum minime latuit.
translation: And when he dwelt in that country, Ruben went, and slept with Bala the concubine of his father: which he was not ignorant of.

text: Si latet fur, dominus domus applicabitur ad Deum et iurabit quod non extenderit manum in rem proximi sui.
translation: If the thief be not known, the master of the house shall be brought to the gods, and shall swear that he did not lay his hand upon his neighbour's goods.

text: Se ad studium applicavit securo vitae suae quotidianae.
translation: He applied himself to his study, without thought for his normal life.

text: Et Mariam et Ioannem conveni, cum Londinii eram.
translation: I met Mary and John when I was in London.

text: Cum Londinii eram, Mariam et Ioannem conveni.
translation: I met Mary and John when in London.

text: Hic est puer quem ibi heri conveni.
translation: This is the boy I met there yesterday.

text: Multos et bonos homines in Australia conveni.
translation: I met a lot of nice people in Australia.

text: Multos et bonos homines Bostoniae conveni.
translation: I met a lot of nice people in Boston.

text: Uno abhinc anno domus dominum conveni.
translation: I met the owner of the house a year ago.

text: Cum ille me interficere non posset, ipsum interfeci.
translation: Because he couldn't kill me, I killed him.

text: Quae mulier sororem meam interfecit suspenda est.
translation: The woman who killed my sister should be hanged.

text: Si nunc non abis, te interficient.
translation: If you don't leave now, they'll kill you.

text: Thomas fratrem manuballistula patris interfecit.
translation: Tom killed his brother with their father's gun.

text: Cervus a venatoribus interfectus est.
translation: The deer was killed by hunters.

text: Miserunt me ut te interficiam.
