translation: They sent me to kill you.

text: Venite mecum, si vos amicos recte appello.
translation: If you are my friends, come with me.

text: Venite mecum, si vos amicas recte appello.
translation: If you are my friends, come with me.

text: Quot homines novisti qui Thomas appellantur?
translation: How many people do you know who are named Tom?

text: Scisne cur te Thoman appellem?
translation: Do you know why I call you Tom?

text: Aegyptus saepe donum Nili appellatur.
translation: Egypt is often called the "Gift of the Nile".

text: Non "tu" at Ricardus appellor.
translation: My name is not "you"; it's Ricardo.

text: Tuus pater non sum, ne dicam dolo.
translation: To be honest, I'm not your father.

text: "Dixerat. Ille, dolis instructus et arte Pelasga, / sustulit exutas vinclis ad sidera palmas:"
translation: "Then schooled in cunning and Pelasgian sleights, / his hands unshackled to the stars he spread:"

text: "Mutemus clipeos, Danaumque insignia nobis / aptemus. Dolus, an virtus, quis in hoste requirat? / Arma dabunt ipsi."
translation: "Take we the Danaans' bucklers; with a foe / who asks, if craft or courage guide the blow? / Themselves shall arm us."

text: "Primusque Thymœtes / duci intra muros hortatur et arce locari, / sive dolo, seu jam Trojæ sic fata ferebant."
translation: "Then first Thymaetes cries aloud, to go / and through the gates the monstrous horse convey / and lodge it in the citadel. E'en so / his fraud or Troy's dark fates were working for our woe."

text: Oportuisset Thomam permittere mihi loqui quum eo.
translation: Tom should've let me talk to him.

text: Heus, permitte mihi aliquid de te petere.
translation: Hey, let me ask you something.

text: Haec similiaque memorabile nihil vel serium agi Romae permittunt.
translation: These and similar things do not allow anything serious or noteworthy to be done in Rome.

text: Tibi permitto ut loquatur cum eo.
translation: I'll let you speak to him.

text: Thomae iam permisi id facere.
translation: I've already given Tom permission to do that.

text: Tibi id facere numquam permitterem.
translation: I'd never allow you to do that.

text: Deus spiritum vitalem in nares eius inspiravit.
translation: God breathed into his nostrils the breath of life.

text: Vidit per muros euntes spiritus.
translation: She saw spirits going through walls.

text: Lingua est spiritus populi.
translation: A language is the spirit of a people.

text: Credisne in mundum spirituum?
translation: Do you believe in the spirit world?

text: Creditisne in mundum spirituum?
translation: Do you believe in the spirit world?

text: Spiritus est Deus: et eos qui adorant eum, in spiritu et veritate oportet adorare.
translation: God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.

text: Putasne Thoman adhuc esse territum?
translation: Do you think Tom is still afraid?

text: Feles tuus canem meum terruit.
translation: My dog got scared of your cat.

text: Non sum is qui terrear.
translation: I am not such a person as to be frightened.

text: Si multam pecuniam habebis, terrebis.
translation: If you have a lot of money, you will become afraid.

text: Tenebrae multos infantes terrent.
translation: Darkness causes many children to be afraid.

text: Canis magnus infantem terruit.
translation: The big dog frightened the baby.

text: scribendi recte sapere est et principium et fons.
translation: Knowledge is the foundation and source of good writing.

text: Sahara fons pulveris plenissimus est terrae.
translation: The Sahara is the largest source of dust in the world.

text: Arbor fructifera Ioseph, arbor fructifera super fontem: rami transcendunt murum.
translation: Joseph is a growing son, a growing son and comely to behold: the daughters run to and fro upon the wall.

text: Thomas nummum in fontem demisit.
translation: Tom tossed a coin into the fountain.

text: Fons in media urbe est.
translation: In the middle of the city, there is a fountain.

text: Sed fons ascendebat e terra irrigans universam superficiem terræ. ­ ­
translation: But a spring rose out of the earth, watering all the surface of the earth.

text: Invidia unum est ex septem peccatis mortalibus.
translation: Envy is one of the seven deadly sins.

text: Fructus eius aliis cantoribus invidiae factus est.
translation: Her success has been arousing jealousy among the other singers.

text: Invidia una est ex sagiliis.
translation: Envy is one of the seven deadly sins.

text: Haec fabula invidiae indolem declarat.
translation: This story illustrates the nature of envy.

text: Septem peccata sunt: superbia, invidia, avaritia, ira, luxuria, gula atque acedia.
translation: The seven deadly sins are: pride, envy, greed, anger, lust, gluttony and sloth.

text: De invidia id fecit.
translation: He did it out of spite.

text: Venit autem Amalec et pugnabat contra Israel in Raphidim.
translation: And Amalec came, and fought against Israel in Raphidim.

text: Nesciebam dominum Gulielmum in bello Vietnamiensi pugnavisse.
translation: I didn't know that Mr. Williams fought in the Vietnam War.

text: Homines ferro propter aurum pugnant.
translation: Men fight with iron for gold.

text: Thomas in pugna vulneratus est.
translation: Tom was wounded in the fight.

text: Vita contra mortem pugna est.
translation: Life is a fight against death.

text: Gladiatores in amphitheatro Flavio pugnabant.
translation: Gladiators fought in the Colosseum.

text: Tu quidem auxisti meam admirationem, non ademisti.
translation: You have indeed increased my admiration, not removed it.

text: Qui auget scientiam, auget et dolorem.
translation: As wisdom grows, and so does pain.

text: Taberna omnia pretia auxit.
translation: The store raised all the prices.

text: Quaeso, auge magnitudinem radiophoni.
translation: Please turn up the radio.

text: In Italiam iit ut litteris studeret.
translation: She went to Italy to study literature.

text: Scripsitne Thomas ad te litteras Bostoniae?
translation: Did Tom write you letters from Boston?

text: Legistine litteras quas Thomas scripsit?
translation: Did you read the letter that Tom wrote?

text: Quaeso, scribe mihi litteras identidem.
translation: Please write to me once in a while.

text: Frater ad sororem litteras scripsit.
translation: The brother wrote a letter to the sister.

text: Tu velim has litteras mittas.
translation: I would like you to post this letter.

text: Medicus me monebat ut corpus meum plus exerceam.
translation: The doctor advised me to exercise more.

text: Medicus eam monuit se in nosocomio curare.
translation: The doctor advised her to enter the hospital.

text: Tu es is qui me monuisti.
translation: You are the one who warned me.

text: Fuge in Aegyptum, et illic esto, donec ego te moneam.
translation: Flee to Egypt and stay there until I tell you otherwise.

text: Nonne nuntii de periculo monebant?
translation: Didn't the messengers warn about the danger?

text: Ea me monuit eo adire.
translation: She advised me to go there.

text: Sero cum domum advenerat nocte divitiis privatus est.
translation: He was robbed when coming home late at night.

text: Pater dixit filio se nullas divitias ei relinquere posse.
translation: The father told his son that he was unable to rid himself of any of his wealth.

text: Agricola nullas divitias filiis relinquere potuit.
translation: The farmer could leave no wealth to his sons.

text: Egestatem operata est manus remissa; manus autem fortium divitias parat.
translation: He becometh poor that dealeth with a slack hand: but the hand of the diligent maketh rich.

text: Thomas nullas divitias filiis reliquit.
translation: Tom left no wealth to his children.

text: Maria nullas divitias filiis reliquit.
translation: Mary left no wealth to her sons.

text: Experiamur an illa iam opus perfecerit.
translation: Let's check whether she already finished.

text: Ne umquam experiaris quis sis.
translation: Mayst thou never learn who thou art.

text: Tu experiaris velim an Thomas in animo habeat solus huc advenire.
translation: I want you to find out if Tom is planning to come here by himself.

text: Thomas expertus est vitam peregrinando vivere non tam facile esse quam opinatus.
translation: Tom discovered that life on the road wasn't as easy as he thought it would be.

text: flectere si nequeo superos, Acheronta movebo.
translation: If I cannot move heaven, I will raise hell.

text: Tandem satis pecuniae habeo, et omne otium quo egeo.
translation: I finally have enough money, and all the time I need.

text: Non hercle otium est nunc mihi auscultandi.
translation: I really don't have time to listen to you right now.

text: Homo tam magnus est quam vestigium quod in mundo relinquit.
translation: Man is as big as the trail he leaves in the world.

text: "Mihi parvus Iulus / sit comes, et longe servet vestigia conjux."
translation: "Let young Iulus at my side repair; / keep thou, my wife, aloof, and follow as we fare."

text: Non erant vestigia squali.
translation: There was no sign of a shark.

text: Calcearius consecutus est e vestigio, quantum poterat, clamitans, tenete furem, tenete furem.
translation: The shoemaker followed him forthwith, as fast as he could, bawling, stop the thief, stop the thief.

text: Facit quasi a familia bona educata sit.
translation: She behaves as if she had been brought up in a good family.

text: Nihil sit de nobis sine nobis.
translation: There should be nothing about us without us.

text: Bene nos aliquid facere illi decet.
translation: We should do something for him.

text: Nam neutiquam homines rebus irasci decet: nil quippe curant ipsae.
translation: It is not right to vex ourselves at things, for they care nought about it.

text: Non decet nos otiari aut garrire hic dum praeceptor expectatur.
translation: It does not become us to be idle or chat away here while the Master is expected.

text: Apud parentes clamare non decet.
translation: It is not appropriate to shout at your parents.

text: Philosophum non decet ira.
translation: Anger does not befit a philosopher.

text: Dum vīvīs spērāre decēt.
translation: Hope while you live.

text: Quaero aliquid in quod iram effundere possim.
translation: I'm looking for something to vent my anger on.

text: Dixit, lacrimasque effudit et omnem / implevit clamore locum.
translation: Tears ensue, / and wailing, shrill as though her heart would bleed.

text: Quod parcus quaeres, effundit prodigus heres.
translation: After a great getter, comes a great spender.

text: Vide ne aquam in claviaturam effundas.
translation: Make sure not to spill water onto the keyboard.

text: Thomas iram in Mariam effudit.
translation: Tom took his anger out on Mary.

text: Iram in eam effudit.
translation: He took his anger out on her.

text: Thomas promisit se pecuniam mox traditurum esse.
translation: Tom promised that he would hand over the money soon.

text: Maria promisit se pecuniam mox tradituram esse.
translation: Mary promised that she would hand over the money soon.

text: Thomas promisit se per telephonum aditurum esse.
translation: Tom promised that he'd call.

text: Promitto me hunc librum lecturum esse.
translation: I promise that I'll read this book.

text: Thomas promisit se id facturum esse.
translation: Tom promised he'll do that.

text: Praepositus huius tabernae barbam promittit.
translation: The manager of this store is growing a beard.

text: Eum te esse finge qui sum ego.
translation: Imagine that you are who I am.

text: Qui amant, ipsi sibi somnia fingunt.
translation: Those who love create their own dreams.

text: Difficile est tristi fingere mente iocum.
translation: It is difficult for those who are sad to feign joy.

text: Et respexit Dominus filios Israel et apparuit eis.
translation: And the Lord looked upon the children of Israel, and he knew them.

text: Respexit ad me et risit.
translation: He looked at me and smiled.

text: Chirurgus qui operationem Thomae perduxit est tantum peritus atque valde respectus.
translation: The surgeon who did Tom's operation is very experienced and highly regarded.

text: Qui responderunt: Tu salvasti nos! Respiciat nos tantum dominus noster, et læti serviemus regi.
translation: And they answered: our life is in thy hand; only let my lord look favourably upon us, and we will gladly serve the king.

text: Et credidit populus, audieruntque quod visitasset Dominus filios Israel et quod respexisset afflictionem eorum; et proni adoraverunt.
translation: And the people believed. And they heard that the Lord had visited the children of Israel, and that he had looked upon their affliction: and falling down they adored.

text: Abel quoque obtulit de primogenitis gregis sui et de adipibus eorum. Et respexit Dominus ad Abel et ad munus eius.
translation: Abel also offered of the firstlings of his flock, and of their fat: and the Lord had respect to Abel, and to his offerings.

text: "Cur hoc facis?" "Quia possum. Imperator Mundi sum."
translation: "Why are you doing this?" "Because I can. I am the Emperor of the World."

text: Imperator exercitum in fines hostium introduxit.
translation: The commanding officer led his army into enemy territory.

text: Imperator separatistas pervincere iuravit.
translation: The emperor swore to crush the separatists once and for all.

text: Apollinaris, medicus Titi Imperatoris hic cacavit bene.
translation: Apollinaris, doctor of Emperor Titus, took a good crap here.

text: De bello judicium imperatoris est, non militum.
translation: The decision concerning war belongs to the general, not to the soldiers.

text: Armis positis ad imperatorum nostrum fidem confugiunt.
translation: They lay down their weapons and throw themselves upon the mercy of our generals.

text: Vacate et videte quoniam ego sum Deus.
translation: Be still, and know that I am God.

text: Opus meum facile est et valde vaco.
translation: My job is easy and I have a lot of free time.

text: Vivos voco, mortuos plango, fulgura frango.
translation: I call the living, I mourn the dead, I chase the lightning.

text: Abi, aut ego vigiles voco!
translation: Go away, or I'm calling the police!

text: Pater meus Saturni die vacat.
translation: My father is free on Saturday.

text: Nescio an Thomas vacet.
translation: I don't know if Tom is available.

text: Tabulae meae pictae coloribus aquatilibus carae non erant.
translation: My watercolors were not expensive.

text: Domus erat plena artificiorum variis coloribus pictorum.
translation: The house was full of colorful art objects.

text: Cuius coloris parietes cubiculi tui sunt?
translation: What color are the walls of your room?

text: Hi colores non casei sunt.
translation: These are not the colors of the cheese.

text: Putat caeruleum colorem pulcherrimum esse.
translation: He thinks that blue is the most beautiful color.

text: Quo colore capillos tingere vis?
translation: What color do you want to dye your hair?

text: Thomas nihil habuit quod diceret, ergo discessit.
translation: Tom had nothing to say, so he left.

text: Modo discessurus eram cum pyrobulus explosus est.
translation: I was just about to leave when the bomb exploded.

text: Nihil habuit quod diceret, ergo discessit.
translation: He had nothing to say, so he left.

text: Novo Eboraco duabus abhinc hebdomadibus discessi.
translation: I left New York two weeks ago.

text: De eius discessu me certiorem fecit.
translation: She informed me of her departure.

text: Thomas a vita per inediam discessit.
translation: Tom died of hunger.

text: Videntes autem stellam gavisi sunt gaudio magno valde.
translation: When they saw the star, they were overjoyed.

text: Gaudium est ut Chopin dum laboro audire possim.
translation: It's a joy to be able to listen to Chopin while I work.

text: Parentes viso filio maximo gaudio laetati sunt.
translation: The parents were overjoyed to see their son.

text: Thomas visa Maria maximo gaudio laetatus est.
translation: Tom was overjoyed to see Mary.

text: Maria viso Thoma maximo gaudio laetata est.
translation: Mary was overjoyed to see Tom.

text: Annuntio vobis gaudium magnum: Habemus Papam.
translation: I announce to you a great joy: we have a Pope.

text: Si caecus caecum ducit, ambo in foveam cadunt.
translation: If a blind man leads a blind man, both will fall into a pit.

text: Lucidae hic sunt colores; caecae ibi sunt.
translation: Here are the light colors and there are the dark ones.

text: Et Maria et Iulia caecae sunt.
translation: Both Mary and Julia are blind.

text: Caecus non judicat de colore.
translation: The blind man is no judge of color.

text: Traditum est, Homerum caecum fuisse.
translation: According to tradition, Homer was blind.

text: Homo sine libris caecus est.
translation: A person without books is blind.

text: Mihi libet quod non vicisse audivi Thomam.
translation: I'm glad to hear that Tom didn't win.

text: "Quis liba facit?" "Alessandra ea facit."
translation: "Who bakes the cakes?" "Alessandra bakes them."

text: "Cur non scribis?" "Quia non libet."
translation: "Why aren't you writing?" "Because I don't like it."

text: "Quis liba coquit?" "Alessandra ea coquit."
translation: "Who bakes the cakes?" "Alessandra bakes them."

text: Qui libet ludibrio habere me?
translation: Why do you enjoy making fun of me?

text: Liba dulcia mihi valde placent.
translation: I like sweet cakes very much.

text: Quam scit uterque, libens exerceat artem.
translation: Every man to his craft.

text: Ubi lubet ire licet accubitum.
translation: You can go and lie down whenever you please.

text: Augete mihi valde dotem et munera; libens tribuam, quod petieritis. Tantum date mihi puellam hanc uxorem.
translation: Raise the dowry, and ask gifts, and I will gladly give what you shall demand: only give me this damsel to wife.

text: Haec arbor plus quam centum annos habet.
translation: This tree is more than a century old.

text: Plus quam centum homines in exedra sunt.
translation: There're more than 100 people in the room.

text: Ex centum militibus decem incolumes redierunt, reliqui mortui sunt.
translation: Out of a hundred soldiers, ten returned unharmed, the rest died.

text: Fuerunt autem dies vitæ Abrahæ centum septuaginta quinque anni.
translation: And the days of Abraham's life were a hundred and seventy-five years.

text: In ludo meo sunt centum homines.
translation: There are one hundred people in my school.

text: Cum Abraham centum esset annorum, natus est ei Isaac filius eius.
translation: When he was a hundred years old: for at this age of his father, was Isaac born.

text: Satis mihi constat me Thomae non placere.
translation: I'm pretty sure that Tom doesn't like me.

text: Pro aliquibus hominibus "Deus" ex ipsis constat.
translation: For some people, "God" is themselves.

text: Haec sententia constat ex verbis sex.
translation: This sentence consists of six words.

text: Quanti constat haec fascia Croatica?
translation: How much is this tie?

text: Quanti constat sucus aurantiorum?
translation: How much does the orange juice cost?

text: Illud trecentum dollariis constat.
translation: That is worth three hundred dollars.

text: Liber Thomae in multas linguas conversus est.
translation: Tom's book has been translated into many languages.

text: Toki Pona lingua non est, sed aenigma.
translation: Toki Pona is not a language but a riddle.

text: Stellarum tanta multitudo est, ut numerari non possint.
translation: There is such a multitude of stars that they cannot be counted.

text: Pro multitudine hominum eorum fines erant angusti.
translation: Their territory was small for the population.

text: Salvete. Quoniam multitudo hominum advenit, quaeso, sedete et paulisper manete.
translation: Welcome. Now that many people have arrived, please take a seat and wait for a while.

text: Et dixit ei angelus Domini: Multiplicans multiplicabo semen tuum, et non numerabitur præ multitudine.
translation: And again he said: I will multiply thy seed exceedingly, and it shall not be numbered for multitude.

text: Deus autem omnipotens benedicat tibi et crescere te faciat atque multiplicet, ut sis in multitudinem populorum.
translation: And God almighty bless thee, and make thee to increase and multiply thee: that thou mayst be a multitude of people.

text: Tu locutus es quod bene mihi faceres et dilatares semen meum sicut arenam maris, quæ præ multitudine numerari non potest.
translation: Thou didst say that thou wouldst do well by me, and multiply my seed like the sand of the sea, which cannot be numbered for multitude.

text: Et Daniel regi respondens ait: Rex, in aeternum vive!
translation: Then said Daniel unto the king, O king, live for ever.

text: Dominus regnabit in æternum et ultra!
translation: The Lord shall reign for ever and ever.

text: Vincere temporarium est, discere autem aeternum.
translation: Winning is temporary, but learning is forever.

text: Custodite verbum istud legitimum tibi et filiis tuis usque in æternum.
translation: Thou shalt keep this thing as a law for thee and thy children for ever.

text: Malum aeternum non est.
translation: Evil isn't eternal.

text: Circumcidetur vernaculus et empticius, eritque pactum meum in carne vestra in fœdus æternum.
translation: He that is born in the house, as well as the bought servant, shall be circumcised, and my covenant shall be in your flesh for a perpetual covenant.

text: "Quis orationes scripsit?" - "Ego eas non scripsi."
translation: "Who wrote the speeches?" "I didn't write them."

text: Caelos non penetrat oratio, quam canis orat.
translation: Amen is not said after an unacceptable prayer.

text: "Quis orationes scripsit?" - "Ego eas scripsi."
translation: "Who wrote the sentences?" "I wrote them."

text: Ad crudelitatem te acuit oratio illorum.
translation: Their speech incited you to cruelty.

text: Duae orationis partes maxime essentiales sunt verba et nomina substantiva.
translation: The two most essential parts of speech are verbs and nouns.

text: Orationem eius diligentissime audiverunt.
translation: They were most attentive to his speech.

text: Putabam me potestatem habere quemlibet missum facere.
translation: I thought I had the right to fire anyone I wanted to.

text: Putabam me habere potestatem hic manendi.
translation: I thought I had the right to be here.

text: Nam et ipsa scientia potestas est.
translation: Knowledge is power.

text: Ad te tanta potestas venit.
translation: To thee all this power has come.

text: Suae quisque mercedis, nullo discrimine, cum pari opera convenientis potestatem habet.
translation: Everyone, without any discrimination, has the right to equal pay for equal work.

text: Exorcizamus te, omnis immunde spiritus, omnis satanica potestas, omnis incursio infernalis adversarii, omnis legio, omnis congregatio et secta diabolica.
translation: We exorcise you, every unclean spirit, every satanic power, every incursion of the infernal adversary, every legion, every congregation and diabolical sect.

text: Iudex ille sapit, qui tarde censet et audit.
translation: One should hear both sides of a question.

text: Si tarde ambulamus, hamaxostichum non attingemus.
translation: If we go slowly, we miss the train.

text: Nimis fueram tardus ne negarem.
translation: It was too late for me to say no.

text: Prudens in loquendo est tardus.
translation: Being skilled in speaking is being deliberate.

text: Veloces estis, nos tardi sumus.
translation: You are fast, we are slow.

text: Me paenitet ut tardus sim.
translation: Sorry I'm late.

text: Infans noster nondum fari potest.
translation: Our baby can't talk yet.

text: Cur Thomas fari non potest?
translation: Why can't Tom talk?

text: Cur bestiae fari non possunt?
translation: Why can't animals talk?

text: Thomas fari non potest.
translation: Tom can't talk.

text: Ortusque est ei sol, cum transgrederetur Phanuel; ipse vero claudicabat propter femur.
translation: And immediately the sun rose upon him, after he was past Phanuel; but he halted on his foot.

text: Sic fatus, amicum / Ilionea petit dextra, laevaque Serestum, / post alios, fortemque Gyan, fortemque Cloanthum.
translation: So saying AEneas with his left hand pressed / Serestus, and Ilioneus with his right, / Brave Gyas, brave Cloanthus and the rest.

text: Emisit eum Dominus Deus de paradiso Eden, ut operaretur humum, de qua sumptus est.
translation: And the Lord God sent him out of the paradise of pleasure, to till the earth from which he was taken.

text: In taberna quando sumus non curamus quid sit humus, sed ad ludum properamus, cui semper insudamus.
translation: In the tavern we do not think how we will be dust, but rush to gamble at dice, which always makes us sweat.

text: Ob hæc invidentes ei Philisthim omnes puteos, quos foderant servi patris illius in diebus Abraham, obstruxerunt implentes humo.
translation: Wherefore the Palestines envying him, stopped up at that time all the wells, that the servants of his father, Abraham, had digged, filling them up with Earth.

text: Accessi, viridemque ab humo convellere silvam / conatus, ramis tegerem ut frondentibus aras, / horrendum et dictu video mirabile monstrum.
translation: Thither I drew, and strove with eager hold / a green-leaved sapling from the soil to tear, / to shade with boughs the altars, when behold / a portent, weird to see and wondrous to unfold!

text: Pluris est oculatus testis unus, quam auriti decem.
translation: One eyewitness is worth more than ten people who have heard it told.

text: Thomas testis bonus non fuit.
translation: Tom wasn't a good witness.

text: Non enim possum redire ad patrem meum, absente puero, ne calamitatis, quæ oppressura est patrem meum, testis assistam.
translation: For I cannot return to my father without the boy, lest I be a witness of the calamity that will oppress my father.

text: Testem habeo, me alibi fuisse.
translation: I have an alibi.

text: Sit conscientia mille testium.
translation: Let conscience be a thousand witnesses.

text: Non bove mactato caelestia numina gaudent, sed quae prestanda est sine teste fides.
translation: The heavenly gods do not rejoice over the slaughter of an ox, but over faith demonstrated without the need for a witness.

text: Haec canticum tam motivum est quam lacrimas in oculis meis infert.
translation: This song is so moving that it brings tears to my eyes.

text: E quibus omnem pecuniam congregavit pro venditione frumenti et intulit eam in ærarium regis.
translation: And Joseph gathered up all the money that was found in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, for the corn which they bought: and Joseph brought the money into Pharaoh's house.

text: Die autem sexta parabunt quod intulerint, et duplum erit quam colligere solebant per singulos dies.
translation: On the sixth day, however, they must gather and prepare twice as much as they usually gather on other days.

text: "Ecqua tamen puero est amissæ cura parentis?"
translation: "Still grieves he for his mother?"

text: Librum tuum magna cum cura legam.
translation: I will read your book with great care.

text: Generosus equus non curat canem latrantem.
translation: A well-bred horse doesn't care about a barking dog.

text: Putasne aliquem si hoc facimus curare?
translation: Do you think anyone would mind if we did that?

text: Thomas illos duos viros occidendos curavit.
translation: Tom had the two men killed.

text: Nemo de te curat, nisi sis pulcher, dives, aut mortuus.
translation: Nobody cares about you unless you're beautiful, rich, or dead.

text: Si internam habes piscinam, multum forsit habeas aes.
translation: If you have an indoor swimming pool, you're probably pretty rich.

text: Aes non habeo, sed somnia habeo.
translation: I have no money, but I have dreams.

text: Æs cȳprium metallum est.
translation: Copper is a metal.

text: Si et hominum loquar et angelorum linguis, neque caritate sim praeditus, sum aes resonans, aut cymbalum tinniens.
translation: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not mercy, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.

text: Thomas dixit cenationes celeres Mariae non placere.
translation: Tom said Mary doesn't like eating at fast food restaurants.

text: Audito sonitu, Thomas e domo celeriter cucurrit.
translation: When he heard the noise, Tom quickly ran out of the house.

text: Lux multo celerior quam sonus est.
translation: Light is much faster than sound.

text: Thomas me nimis celeriter edere dicit.
translation: Tom says I eat too fast.

text: Num ille discipulus celeriter currit?
translation: That student doesn’t run very fast, does he?

text: Raeda celerior quam birota est.
translation: A car is faster than a bicycle.

text: Equus tuus celer est, meus autem celerior.
translation: Your horse is fast, but mine is faster.

text: Raeda tua celer est, mea autem celerior.
translation: Your car is fast, but mine is faster.

text: Didymus est tam celer quam leopardus.
translation: Tom is as fast as a leopard.

text: Didymus est pariter celer ac leopardus.
translation: Tom is as fast as a leopard.

text: Didymus est aeque celer ac leopardus.
translation: Tom is as fast as a leopard.

text: Didymus est aeque celer atque leopardus.
translation: Tom is as fast as a leopard.

text: Pauper natus sum, sed in opes processi.
translation: I was born poor, but I became rich.

text: Informationes processus omnes vitae rationes permeat.
translation: Information processing permeates all aspects of life.

text: Omni custodia serva cor tuum, quia ex ipso vita procedit.
translation: Guard your heart with all caution, because from it spring the sources of life.

text: Procedo et Priami sedes arcemque reviso.
translation: Again to Priam's palace, and again / up to the citadel I speed my way.

text: Si me adiuvisses, processissem.
translation: If you had helped me, I would have succeeded.

text: Cuius est liber qui super mensam est?
translation: Whose book is that on the table?

text: Liber tuus super mensam scriptoriam est.
translation: Your book is on the desk.

text: Horologium tuum super mensam scriptoriam est.
translation: Your watch is on the desk.

text: Visne poculum? Unum super mensam est.
translation: Do you want a glass? There is one on the table.

text: Ita, hodie undecimus dies mensis est.
translation: Yes, today is the eleventh.

text: Sede nunc ad mensam, et mane in cubiculo donec rediero.
translation: Sit now at the table, and wait in the room until I come back.

text: Parvus fuscusque canis sub hac mensa est.
translation: There's a small brown dog under this table.

text: Extrahe librum tuum ex hac mensa, quaeso.
translation: Please take your book off this table.

text: Parvus canis fuscus sub mensa est.
translation: There's a small brown dog under the table.

text: Canis in capsa sub mensa erat.
translation: The dog was in a box under the table.

text: In capsa sub mensa erat canis.
translation: The dog was in a box under the table.

text: Mensa scriptoria e ligno facta est.
translation: The desk is made of wood.

text: Semper obtemperat pius filius patri.
translation: The good son always obeys his father.

text: Thomas valde pius est.
translation: Tom is very pious.

text: Cives ad iudicium pro iustitia eunt.
translation: The citizens go to court for justice.

text: Hæc sunt iudicia, quæ propones eis:
translation: These are the judgments which thou shalt set before them.

text: Meo iudicio vir fortis es.
translation: You're a hero in my eyes.

text: Meo iudicio heros es.
translation: You're a hero in my eyes.

text: Meo iudicio heroina es.
translation: You're a hero in my eyes.

text: A meridie ad occasum solis dubia victoria fuit.
translation: From noon until sunset, victory was doubtful.

text: Propter victoriam virum fortem factus est.
translation: Because of the victory, he became a hero.

text: Nonne confidunt victoriae suae?
translation: They're confident they'll win, aren't they?

text: Cives propter victoriam exsultabant.
translation: The people hailed the victory.

text: Etiam hoc victoria est.
translation: Even this is a victory.

text: Is capitis damnatus est.
translation: He was condemned to death.

text: Didymus capitis damnatus est.
translation: Tom was sentenced to death.

text: Thomas capitis damnatus est.
translation: Tom was sentenced to death.

text: Non enim misit Deus filium suum in mundum, ut mundum damnet, sed ut servetur per eum mundus.
translation: For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.

text: Hadriano imperante, poena capitalis rarior facta est.
translation: When Hadrian was emperor, capital punishment became rarer.

text: Vix pauca furenti / subjicio et raris turbatus vocibus hisco:
translation: Then I, with stammering accents, intercede, / and, sore perplext, these broken words outthrow / to calm her transport:

text: Struthio est ales maximus; Regulus minimus; Noctua despicatissimus; Upapa sordissimus, rescitur enim stercorinibus); Manucodiata rarissimus.
translation: The Ostrich is the largest bird, the Wren the smallest; the Owl is the most despicable; the Hoopoe the most dirty (as it eats dung); the Bird of Paradise is most rare.

text: Confugimus in specum et mansimus tempestatem dum praeteriret.
translation: We took refuge in a cave and waited for the storm to pass.

text: Domus tua tempestāte dēlēta est.
translation: Your home was destroyed by the storm.

text: Quattuor tempestates in anno sunt.
translation: There are four seasons in a year.

text: Quam spurcissima est tempestas hodie!
translation: What miserable weather we're having today!

text: Habetne Australia quattuor anni tempestates?
translation: Does Australia have four seasons?

text: Heri adversa tempestate adflictati sumus.
translation: We had bad weather yesterday.

text: In hoc loco imagines photographicas facere non licet.
translation: Photography of this area is prohibited.

text: Haec imago photographica sororis meae est.
translation: This is a picture of my sister.

text: Noli hic imagines photographicas facere, quaeso.
translation: Please do not take photos here.

text: Imagines photographicae tuae valde iis placent.
translation: They like your photos a lot.

text: Homo creavit Deum ad imaginem suam.
translation: Man made God in his image.

text: Hic liber XL imagines photographicas continet.
translation: This book contains forty photographs.

text: Illud intellego, omnium ora in me conversa esse.
translation: I understand this, that the faces of all are turned toward me.

text: Domum in ora maritima habet.
translation: He has a house at the beach.

text: Ora pro nobis Deum.
translation: Pray for us to God.

text: "Nos quoque oramus, ut servis Dei patris tui dimittas iniquitatem hanc". Quibus auditis, flevit Ioseph.
translation: We also pray thee, to forgive the servants of the God of thy father this wickedness. And when Joseph heard this, he wept.

text: Oro ut me attente audias.
translation: I beg of you to listen carefully.

text: Oro ut me attente audiatis.
translation: I beg of you to listen carefully.

text: Tē ōrō nē id faciās.
translation: I implore you not to do that.

text: Thomas Mariae suasit ut consuleret iurisconsultum.
translation: Tom advised Mary to consult a lawyer.

text: Thomas suasit Mariam consulere iurisconsultum.
translation: Tom advised Mary to consult a lawyer.

text: Cūr igitur nōn eum cōnsuluistī?
translation: Then, why have you not consulted him?

text: Cūr igitur nōn eum cōnsuluistis?
translation: Then, why have you not consulted him?

text: Sed collidebantur in utero eius parvuli. Quæ ait: “Si sic est, cur mihi?” Perrexitque, ut consuleret Dominum.
translation: But the children struggled in her womb, and she said: If it were to be so with me, what need was there to conceive? And she went to consult the Lord.

text: Scisne Hannibalem esse ante portas?
translation: Did you know Hannibal is at the city gates?

text: Obicibus ferratis portas muniemus.
translation: We will fortify the gates with iron bars.

text: Ante portas germani sunt.
translation: The Germans are at the city gates.

text: Thomas portam Acheruntis invenit.
translation: Tom found a portal to the underworld.

text: Portas et fenestras clauderunt.
translation: They locked the doors and windows.

text: Thomas extra portam exspectavit.
translation: Tom waited outside the gate.

text: Sententias suas inusitatas habeo sed mea intersunt eae.
translation: I find her opinions odd but interesting.

text: Didymus nescit quid intersit inter adiectivum et adverbium.
translation: Tom doesn't know the difference between an adjective and an adverb.

text: Nihil interest quis hoc dicat, id verum non est.
translation: It doesn't matter who says that, it's not true.

text: Nihil mea interest ubi Thomas hoc faciat.
translation: It doesn't matter to me where Tom does that.

text: Mea minimi interest quae futura sint.
translation: I don't care a bit about the future.

text: Spero ut alicuius intersit peritia mea.
translation: I hope my experience will be interesting to somebody.

text: Haud facile libidinibus carebat.
translation: He could hardly do without pleasures.

text: admiror, paries, te non cecidisse ruinis, qui tot scriptorum taedia sustineas.
translation: I'm astonished, wall, that you haven't collapsed into ruins, since you're holding up the weary verse of so many poets.

text: Quis sustinet culpam casus?
translation: Who's to blame for the accident?

text: Is me adhuc sustinet.
translation: He still supports me.

text: Divites enim erant valde et simul habitare non poterant; nec sustinebat eos terra peregrinationis eorum præ multitudine gregum.
translation: For they were exceeding rich, and could not dwell together: neither was the land in which they sojourned able to bear them, for the multitude of their flocks.

text: Ecce iuvenibus admonitio: vos omnes aliquando moriemini.
translation: Here is a reminder for young people: you will all die sometime.

text: Spero te nos aliquando visitaturum esse.
translation: I hope that you'll come visit us sometime.

text: Aliquando curru publico, aliquando raeda vehor.
translation: Sometimes I go by bus and sometimes by car.

text: Aliquando in Americam ire volo.
translation: I want to go to America some day.

text: Aliquando Novum Eboracum ire volo.
translation: Some day I want to go to New York.

text: Aliquando in Africam ire volo.
translation: I want to go to Africa someday.

text: Anno bis millesimo tertio decimo repertum est.
translation: It was discovered in 2013.

text: Pluto anno millesimo nongentesimo tricesimo repertus est.
translation: Pluto was discovered in 1930.

text: Necesse est mihi reperire Thoman hodie.
translation: I need to find Tom today.

text: Quaesivi, non autem reperi eum.
translation: I searched, but I didn't find him.

text: Quaesivi, non autem reperi eam.
translation: I searched, but I didn't find her.

text: Quaesivi, non autem reperi id.
translation: I searched, but I didn't find it.

text: Nemo intrat in caelum nisi per philosophiam.
translation: No one enters heaven except through philosophy.

text: Sine fascia Croatica intrare non licet.
translation: Entry without a tie is not permitted.

text: Antequam domum intres, calceos exuere debes.
translation: Before going inside the house, you have to take off your shoes.

text: Intrare cum hoc cigarello nolo.
translation: I don't want to go in there with this cigarette.

text: "Italiam cursu petitis, ventisque vocatis / ibitis Italiam, portusque intrare licebit."
translation: "Ye seek Italia and, with favouring wind, / shall reach Italia, and her ports attain."

text: Simulatque intraverunt pluere desiit.
translation: The rain stopped as soon as they went inside.

text: "Rex erat Aeneas nobis, quo justior alter / nec pietate fuit nec bello major et armis".
translation: "A king was ours, AEneas; ne'er was born / a man more just, more valiant in the fight, / more famed for piety and deeds of might."

text: Pereunt Hypanisque Dymasque, / confixi a sociis, nec te tua plurima, Panthu, / labentem pietas nec Apollinis infula texit.
translation: Then Dymas brave / and Hypanis by comrades' hands are slain. / Nor, Panthus, thee thy piety can save, / nor e'en Apollo's wreath preserve thee from the grave.

text: Barbari bellum renovare conati sunt.
translation: The barbarians tried to renew the war.

text: Barbari bellum renovare conantur.
translation: The barbarians try to renew the war.

text: Liberi saepe se culpant, cum parentes eorum divortium faciunt.
translation: Children often blame themselves when their parents divorce.

text: Utrum ea vestra an nostra culpa est?
translation: Is it your fault or ours?

text: Utrum ea vestra, an nostra culpa est?
translation: Is it your fault or ours?

text: Num de eo me culpare potes?
translation: Can you blame me for that?

text: In quo est culpa huius casus?
translation: Who's to blame for the accident?

text: Vestrane culpa an nostra est?
translation: Is it your fault or ours?

text: Timeo ut umquam culpam suam confiteatur.
translation: I'm afraid he will never admit his guilt.

text: Thomas conscius de culpis suis est.
translation: Tom is aware of his own faults.

text: Thomas culpam in me transtulit.
translation: Tom shifted the blame to me.

text: Et appropinquans ait: Numquid vere perdes iustum cum impio?
translation: And drawing nigh, he said: Wilt thou destroy the just with the wicked?

text: Cur non facimus, quod est justus?
translation: Why don't we do what is right?

text: Thomas dicit id non esse iustum.
translation: Tom says that's not fair.

text: Credebam Thoman esse vir iustum.
translation: I thought Tom was a decent guy.

text: Non omnes leges iustae sunt.
translation: Not all laws are just.

text: Pacem iustam tantum volebant.
translation: They only wanted a just peace.

text: Tamesis est flumen quod per Londinium fluit.
translation: The Thames is a river that flows through London.

text: Flūmen, quod per Lutetiam fluit, Sēquana appellātur.
translation: The river that flows through Paris is called the Seine.

text: Flumen, quod per Londinium fluit, Tamesis vocatur.
translation: The river which flows through London is called the Thames.

text: Hoc flumen in Oceanum Pacificum fluit.
translation: This river flows into the Pacific Ocean.

text: Sub ponte flumen languide fluit.
translation: The river flows sluggishly under the bridge.

text: Sanguis ei naribus fluit.
translation: He has a nose bleed.

text: Mihi necesse est pecuniam ex automato monetali demere.
translation: I need to withdraw money from the ATM.

text: Faciam quidquid necesse est ut liberos meos protegam.
translation: I'll do whatever it takes to protect my children.

text: Quando aliquis est in amore, necesse est dicere.
translation: When you are in love, you must say it!

text: Thomas dixit Mariae necesse esse ei tardius esse.
translation: Tom told Mary to eat more slowly.

text: Necesse est multos timeat quem multi timent.
translation: He who is feared by many must fear many.

text: Necesse mihi est cum Thoma nunc loqui.
translation: I need to speak to Tom now.

text: Nesciebam id tibi quoque necessum esse.
translation: I didn't know you needed one, too.

text: Reor hoc necesse esse.
translation: I guess this was inevitable.

text: Hoc rebar perspicuum esse.
translation: I thought it was obvious.

text: "Quae te tam laeta tulerunt / saecula? Qui tanti talem genuere parentes?"
translation: "What happy ages did thy birth delight? / What godlike parents bore a child so bright?"

text: Gloria Patri et Filio et Spiritui sancto. Sicut erat in principio et nunc et semper et in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
translation: Glory be to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit. As it was in the beginning, is now and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

text: Pater, dimitte illis, non enim sciunt, quid faciunt.
translation: Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do.

text: Induravit autem Dominus cor pharaonis, et noluit dimittere eos.
translation: And the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he would not let them go.

text: Et induravit Dominus cor pharaonis, nec dimisit filios Israel.
translation: And the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, neither did he let the children of Israel go.

text: Quisquis hoc stultum consilium cepit, dimittatur.
translation: Whoever thought of this stupid plan should be fired.

text: Et dimitte nobis debita nostra sicut et nos dimittimus debitoribus nostris.
translation: And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.

text: Et dimitte nobis debita nostra, sicut et nos dimittimus debitoribus nostris.
translation: And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive them that trespass against us.

text: Domus in cineres incensa est.
translation: The house was burnt to ashes.

text: Deus e cineribus creat formosa.
translation: God creates beauty from ashes.

text: Cineres rivo fluenti jace.
translation: Cast the ashes toward a flowing stream.

text: Hoc horologium septuaginta milibus nummorum Iaponensium constitit.
translation: This watch cost 70,000 yen.

text: Utrum consistere vult an mare transire nescitur.
translation: It is not known whether he wants to stay or cross the sea.

text: Quanti constitit ut eo veneris?
translation: How much did it cost to get there?

text: Raeda in media via constitit.
translation: The car stopped in the middle of the road.

text: Consiste cunctari praeparaque scholae.
translation: Stop messing around and get ready for school.

text: Aeneas constitit multa putans.
translation: Aeneas stopped, thinking about many things.

text: Fac aquam turturis mundam et recentem.
translation: Make sure the turtle's water is clean and fresh.

text: Birota mea recentior est quam tua.
translation: My bicycle is newer than yours.

text: Folia post imbrem recentia sunt.
translation: The leaves are fresh after a rainfall.

text: Hoc Rhipeus, hoc ipse Dymas omnisque juventus / læta facit: spoliis se quisque recentibus armat.
translation: So / doth Rhipeus, so brave Dymas and the rest; / all in the new-won spoils their eager limbs invest.

text: Cum adoleverim, multae mihi res aliter videntur.
translation: As I've gotten older, my opinions on many things have changed.

text: Simul ac unus intrat, alter exit.
translation: As soon as one goes in, the other goes out.

text: Quibus ille respondit: Aliter est; immunita terræ huius considerare venistis!
translation: And he answered them: It is otherwise: you are come to consider the unfenced parts of this land.

text: Alter est altus, alter parvus.
translation: One is tall and the other is short.

text: Alter est ruber, alter albus.
translation: One is red and the other is white.

text: Alter Iapo, alter Italus est.
translation: One is Japanese and the other is Italian.

text: Scīre volō quis Thōman laeserit.
translation: I want to know who has hurt Tom.

text: Thomas equi dente laesus est.
translation: Tom was bitten by a horse.

text: Levius laedit, quicquid praevidimus ante.
translation: Afore warned, afore armed.

text: Parentes amicum meum non probant.
translation: My parents don't approve of my boyfriend.

text: Vita proba grata est Deo.
translation: A good life pleases God.

text: Maria est puella proba.
translation: Mary is a good girl.

text: Quos Deus amat, probat.
translation: God tries those he loves.

text: Maria est discipula proba.
translation: Mary is a model student.

text: Hoc facile probari potest.
translation: This can be easily proven.

text: Doleo, at te bene audire non possum.
translation: Sorry, but I can't hear you very well.

text: Valde doleo, quod pater tuus mortuus est.
translation: I'm very sorry your father died.

text: Manus mihi dolet, cum aliquid teneo.
translation: My hand hurts when I hold something.

text: doleō sed tibi satisfacere nōn possum.
translation: I am sorry, but I cannot meet your requirement.

text: Doleo, sed id facere non possum.
translation: I'm sorry, but I can't do that.

text: Hoc ubi primum dixi, hoc dolui.
translation: I regretted it as soon as I said it.

text: Marīa nescit quārē Thōmās sē abīre velit.
translation: Mary doesn't know why Tom wants her to leave.

text: Thomas Mariam quare ei irasci scit.
translation: Tom knows that Mary is angry with him.

text: Deus, Deus meus, quāre mē dērelīquistī?
translation: God, oh God, why have you forsaken me?

text: Quare heri non ad me venisti?
translation: Why didn't you come to me yesterday?

text: Thomas mihi dixit quare non vicit.
translation: Tom told me why he didn't win.

text: Prō certō sciō tē intellegere quārē id facere nōn possīmus.
translation: I'm sure you understand why we can't do that.

text: Reliquum est, ut videatur qui vincit.
translation: It remains to be seen who wins.

text: Sed audi reliquam fabulam.
translation: But listen to the rest of the story.

text: quae volumus, ea credimus libenter, et quae sentimus ipsi, reliquos sentire speramus.
translation: We willingly believe what we want, and we hope that others will feel what we ourselves feel.

text: Et posuit spatium itineris trium dierum inter se et Iacob, qui pascebat reliquos greges Laban.
translation: And he set the space of three days journey betwixt himself and his son-in-law, who fed the rest of his flock.

text: Reliquos autem, quos genueris post eos, tui erunt et nomine fratrum suorum vocabuntur in possessionibus suis.
translation: But the rest whom thou shalt have after them, shall be thine, and shall be called by the name of their brethren in their possessions.

text: "Quotiēns inter sē ōsculātī sunt?" "Semel tantum."
translation: "How many times did they kiss?" "Just once."

text: Ioannes epistulam semel in mense parentibus scribit.
translation: John writes a letter to his parents once a month.

text: Is parentibus semel in mense scribit.
translation: He writes to his parents once a month.

text: Ioannes parentibus semel in mense scribit.
translation: John writes to his parents once a month.

text: Semel in hebdomade ad bibliopolium it.
translation: She goes to the bookstore once a week.

text: Ea semel in hebdomade parentibus scribit.
translation: She writes to her parents once a week.

text: Non dubito quin Thomas te non oderit.
translation: I'm sure Tom doesn't hate you.

text: Non dubito quin Thomas Mariam non oderit.
translation: I'm sure Tom doesn't hate Mary.

text: Thoman oderant, quia verum ei dicebat.
translation: They hated Tom because he told them the truth.

text: Thomas in odio apud omnes est.
translation: Tom is hated by everyone.

text: Benefacite his qui vos oderunt.
translation: Do good to those who hate you.

text: Quis male agit, odit lucem.
translation: One who does evil hates the light.

text: Odii eas, quae omnes viros similes esse dicunt.
translation: I hate women who say that all men are alike.

text: Mei amici eam odierunt, ego autem amo.
translation: My friends hate her, but I love her.

text: Is me odit et ego eum odi.
translation: He hates me. And I hate him!

text: Me odit et eum odi.
translation: He hates me. And I hate him!

text: Odii eos, qui haec dicunt.
translation: I hate people who say that.

text: Thoman multas ob causas odi.
translation: I hate Tom for many reasons.

text: Loquebantur inter se sicut veteres amici.
translation: They were talking together like old pals.

text: Pulchræ sunt genæ tuæ sicut turturis, collum tuum sicut monilia.
translation: Thy cheeks are beautiful as the turtledove's, thy neck as jewels.

text: Nondum egi sicut mandatus eram.
translation: I haven't yet done what I was told to do.

text: Haec raeda sicut nova est.
translation: This car is like new.

text: Induratumque est cor pharaonis, et non audivit eos, sicut dixerat Dominus.
translation: And Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not hearken to them, as the Lord had commanded.

text: Sicut vetus homo scribis.
translation: You write like an old person.

text: Quamquam humanum sit peccare, diabolicum tamen est perseverare.
translation: Although it may be human to sin, it is, however, devilish to continue to sin.

text: Peccavimus, Domine, dimitte nobis
translation: We have sinned, Lord, forgive us.

text: Qui dormit, non peccat.
translation: He who sleeps, does not sin.

text: Thomas eadem peccat peccata.
translation: Thomas is committing the same sin.

text: Piscator sub arborem persicum piscabatur. Persicum pomum furatus est, factus est peccator.
translation: A fisherman was fishing under a peach tree. He stole a peach, and he became a sinner.

text: His ita gestis, accidit ut peccarent pincerna regis Aegypti et pistor domino suo.
translation: After this, it came to pass, that two eunuchs, the butler and the baker of the king of Egypt, offended their lord.

text: Cum Maria de sensibus meis locutus sum.
translation: I talked to Mary about my feelings.

text: Semper sensi filio meo te esse amicum.
translation: I have always felt that you were a good friend to my son.

text: Visus est unus ex quinque sensibus.
translation: Sight is one of the five senses.

text: Odoratus est unus ex quinque sensibus.
translation: Smell is one of the five senses.

text: Caput omnium sensuum sedes est.
translation: The head is the seat of all the senses.

text: Hoc verbum sensum duplicem habet.
translation: This word has a double meaning.

text: Exsilii causa solum vertit.
translation: He left the country in exile.

text: Thomas exsilio multatus est.
translation: Tom was punished with exile.

text: Atque hic ingentem comitum affluxisse novorum / invenio admirans numerum, matresque virosque, / collectam exsilio pubem, miserabile vulgus.
translation: There, behold, / matrons and men, a miserable band, / gathered for exile.

text: Cum bellum finitum esset, ei opus fuit in exsilium proficisci.
translation: When the war ended, he had to go into exile.

text: Homo nocens in exsilium eiectus est.
translation: The criminal was sent into exile.

text: Beati mundo corde: quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt.
translation: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.

text: Beati mundo corde, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt.
translation: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.

text: Nomen tuum in corde meo scripsi.
translation: I have written your name in my heart.

text: Erit semper in corde meo.
translation: She will be forever in my heart.

text: Ex abundantia cordis os loquitur.
translation: Out of the overflow of the heart, the mouth speaks.

text: Oculī sunt cordis fenestrae.
translation: The eyes are the windows of the heart.

text: Dolet mihi caput, bracchia, crura, denique totum corpus.
translation: My head hurts, and so do my arms, legs... in fact, my whole body.

text: Thomas denique quam rem gereret Maria cognovit.
translation: Tom eventually learned what Mary was up to.

text: Tum denique homines nostra intellegimus bona cum quae in potestate habuimus ea amisimus.
translation: People only understand their blessings when they lose what they once had in their power.

text: Haec urbs est in Unitis Statibus Americae.
translation: This city is in the USA.

text: Hoc dolui statim ut hoc dixi.
translation: I regretted it as soon as I said it.

text: Si quid acciderit, me statim voca.
translation: If anything happens, call me right away.

text: Nobis statim tibi loqui opus est.
translation: We need to talk to you immediately.

text: Iube eum statim huce venire.
translation: Tell him to come here at once.

text: Nosocomium statim ire opus est.
translation: You need to go to hospital immediately.

text: Maior natu est, quam puer qui ibi stat.
translation: He is older than the boy who is over there.

text: Aliquis ante cubiculum eius stat.
translation: Somebody is standing in front of his room.

text: Thomas prope mensam suam stat.
translation: Tom is standing near his desk.

text: Puer in exedra stat.
translation: The boy is standing in the living room.

text: Thomas ante ianuam stat.
translation: Tom is standing in front of the door.

text: Thomas prope ianuam stat.
translation: Tom is standing near the door.

text: Quidquid accidit, ego de hac sententia non demovebor.
translation: Come what may, I won't change my opinion.

text: Hoc est aliquid quod iterum atque iterum accidit.
translation: This is something that has happened repeatedly.

text: Quattuor homines erant en raeda, cum calamitas accidit.
translation: Four people were in the car when the accident happened.

text: Res insperatae accidunt his, qui res sperant.
translation: Unexpected things happen to those who expect things.

text: Insperata accidunt magis saepe, quam quae speres.
translation: Unexpected things happen more often than things you expect.

text: "Scisne de Guillelmo?" "Nescio, quid ei accidit?"
translation: "Do you know anything about Bill?" "No, what happened to him?"

text: Decerne tu ipse quod rectum esse censes.
translation: Decide for yourself what you think is normal.

text: Tu dux es. Tu decernis.
translation: You're the leader. You decide.

text: Scit se decernere debere.
translation: She knows it's her call.

text: Senatus decrevit ut consul novum delectum haberet et patriam ab hostibus liberaret.
translation: The Senate decreed that a new consul be chosen and the country be delivered from the enemies.

text: "Quando emes ea, quæ decrevisti?" "Cras, ut spero, aut ad summum perendie."
translation: "When will you buy those things you've planned on?" "Tomorrow, I hope, or at the latest the day after tomorrow."

text: Thomas ante domum suam sclopeto occisus est.
translation: Tom was shot dead in front of his house.

text: Si nobis non dixeris, te occidemus.
translation: If you don't tell us, we'll kill you.

text: Eduardum occidere nolite timere bonum est.
translation: Do not be afraid to kill Edward; it is good.

text: Thomas scit quis canem suum occiderit.
translation: Tom knows who killed his dog.

text: Qua de causa Thomas se occidit.
translation: That's why Tom killed himself.

text: Anser a vulpe occisus est.
translation: The goose was killed by a fox.

text: "Jamne salutavisti?" "Salutavi quum descenderit ex equo."
translation: "Have you already greeted him?" "I will greet him as soon as he's got off his horse."

text: Thomas Mariam dixit huc descendisse.
translation: Tom said that Mary was down here.

text: Maria de septima area descendit.
translation: Maria came down from the seventh floor.

text: Sol pone montem descendit.
translation: The sun is going down behind the hill.

text: Descendit autem Dominus, ut videret civitatem et turrim, quam ædificaverunt filii hominum.
translation: And the Lord came down to see the city and the tower which the children of Adam were building.

text: Venite igitur, descendamus et confundamus ibi linguam eorum, ut non intellegat unusquisque vocem proximi sui.
translation: Come ye, therefore, let us go down and there confound their tongue, that they may not understand one another's speech.

text: Tempora anni sunt quattuor: ver, aestas, autumnus, hiems.
translation: There are four seasons in a year: spring, summer, fall and winter.

text: Hiems multa bona fert, sed mala quoque.
translation: Winter brings many good things, but also bad things.

text: Hiems est tempus quod magis mihi placet.
translation: Winter is the season I like best.

text: "Quae sunt quattuor tempora?" "Ver, aestas, autumnus et hiems."
translation: "What are the four seasons?" "Spring, summer, fall, and winter."

text: Foras non exiit, quamdiu hiems fuit.
translation: As long as it was winter, he did not go outdoors.

text: Hiems mox ventura est.
translation: Winter is coming soon.

text: Quae terra continet multas feminas pulchras, tu cogitas?
translation: Which country do you think has a lot of beautiful women?

text: Thomas habet domum quae duo cubicula continet.
translation: Tom has a house which has two rooms.

text: Nulla sententia in Tatoeba verbum "anathema" continet.
translation: No sentence on Tatoeba contains the word "anathema".

text: America terra non est, sed continens est.
translation: America isn't a country, it's a continent.

text: Haec aula potest continere quinque milia hominum.
translation: This hall can hold 5,000 people.

text: Hic liber quadraginta imagines photographicas continet.
translation: This book contains forty photographs.

text: Prometheus ignem in terras detulit hominibusque dedit.
translation: Prometheus brought down fire to Earth to the mankind.

text: Thomas vidulos nostros ad cubiculum nostrum detulit.
translation: Tom carried our suitcases to our room.

text: Maria excepta omnes sciebant Mariam id facere non oportere.
translation: Everybody except Mary knew that she didn't need to do that.

text: Cur Latíné loquí oportet, cum Rómání iamdiú mortuí sint?
translation: Why should Latin be spoken, if Romans have been dead for a very long time?

text: Thomas dicit se oportere Mariam manere.
translation: Tom says he has to wait for Mary.

text: Post hoc oportet te diligentius agere.
translation: You must be more careful from now on.

text: Hoc jam pridem factum esse oportuit.
translation: This ought long ago to have been done.

text: Si non intellegis, oportet te dicere.
translation: If you don't understand, you need to say so.

text: In plurali, "bos, bovis" est "boves, boum".
translation: The plural of ox is oxen.

text: Quod licet Jovi, non licet bovi.
translation: Gods may do what cattle may not.

text: A bove maiore discit arare minor.
translation: From the old ox, the young one learns to plow.

text: Quod licet Iovi, non licet bovi.
translation: All that is allowed to Jupiter is not necessarily allowed to an ox.

text: Quinque bovēs in vīcō sunt.
translation: There are 5 cows in the village.

text: Estne Jupiter aut bos?
translation: Is this Jupiter or a bull?

text: Scin quid est quod illa tam irascitur?
translation: Do you know the reason why she is so angry?

text: Nonne Thomas etiam nunc tibi irascitur?
translation: Tom is still angry with you, isn't he?

text: An Thomas etiam nunc tibi irascitur?
translation: Is Tom still angry with you?

text: Num quis sine tumultu irasci potest?
translation: Can anybody be angry without excitement?

text: Potestne quisquam sine perturbatione animi irasci?
translation: Can anybody be angry without excitement?

text: Raro fit ut ille irascatur.
translation: It rarely happens that he gets angry.

text: Hodie in ludum ire non possum. Aeger sum.
translation: I can't go to school today. I'm sick.

text: Hodie in ludum ire non possum. Aegra sum.
translation: I can't go to school today. I'm sick.

text: In ludum ire non possum, quod aeger sum.
translation: I can't go to school today because I'm sick.

text: In ludum ire non possum, quod aegra sum.
translation: I can't go to school today because I'm sick.

text: Una ex sororibus eius aegrorum ministra est.
translation: One of his sisters is a nurse.

text: Is venire non potest, quia aeger est.
translation: He is not able to come, because he is ill.

text: Sumus laeti, et ergo ad forum ibimus.
translation: We are happy, and therefore we will go to the forum.

text: I bagni non sono nel forum.
translation: The baths are not in the forum.

text: Omnes praeter iudicem forum reliquerunt.
translation: Everyone except the judge left the courtroom.

text: Lucrificare forum solet adventus fatuorum.
translation: If fools did not go to market, bad wares would not be sold.

text: "Accipe hos duos igitur. Quando reddes?" "Die Saturni, ut spero, cum pater venerit ad forum." "Esto memor igitur." "Ne timeas."
translation: "Take these two then. When will you repay me?" "Saturday, I hope, when my father comes to the market." "Keep it in mind then." "Don't worry."

text: Thomas salutem suam in discrimen obtulit.
translation: Tom risked his life.

text: Thomas vitam suam in discrimen offert.
translation: Tom's risking his life.

text: Vitam suam in discrimen obtulit.
translation: He risked his life.

text: Vitam meam in discrimen offero.
translation: I'm risking my life.

text: Multis periculis oblatus est.
translation: He was exposed to many dangers.

text: Quid tibi obtulit Thomas?
translation: What did Tom offer you?

text: Nullus homo lacrimis unquam revocatur ab umbris.
translation: Tears never brought someone back from the other world.

text: Tum victu revocant vires, fusique per herbam / implentur veteris Bacchi pinguisque ferinæ.
translation: So wine and venison, to their hearts' desire, / refreshed their strength.

text: Nonne habe res alcumistam pro deo, qui posset adjicere decem annos summae vitae, et revocare provectiorem aetatem ad vigorem adolescentiae?
translation: Would not you reckon the alchymist for a god, that could add ten years to the sum of your life, and call back advanced age to the vigour of youth?

text: Domus eius campis heliotropiorum cingitur.
translation: His house is surrounded by fields of sunflowers.

text: Comitia de integro habenda sunt.
translation: Elections must be held anew.

text: Homo debet esse integer.
translation: A man must be honest.

text: Res etiamnunc integra est.
translation: The jury is still out.

text: Iudaeismus religio integra est.
translation: Judaism is a complete religion.

text: Hercules, Alcmenae filius, omnium hominum validissimus fuisse dicitur.
translation: Hercules, the son of Alcmena, is said to have been the strongest of all men.

text: Puto utramque harum translationum validam in Iaponica esse posse.
translation: I think either of these could possibly be a valid translation into Japanese.

text: Thōmās validior est quam Marīa.
translation: Tom is stronger than Mary.

text: Taurus animal est validum.
translation: The bull is a strong animal.

text: Tuba validam sonum habet.
translation: The trumpet has a strong sound.

text: Sed ego scio quod non dimittet vos rex Aegypti, ut eatis, nisi per manum validam.
translation: But I know that the king of Egypt will not let you go, but by a mighty hand.

text: Marcus minus est altus quam Marius.
translation: Marcus isn't as tall as Marius.

text: Hoc flumen non ita altum est.
translation: This river isn't very deep.

text: Nescio quam altus sit lacus.
translation: I don't know how deep the lake is.

text: Omnia quadrupeda foetus lacte alunt.
translation: All quadrupeds feed their young with milk.

text: Liberos suos alere non possunt.
translation: They are unable to feed their children.

text: Quam altus fraterculus tuus est?
translation: How tall is your little brother?

text: Hic flos pulchrior est quam ille.
translation: This flower is more beautiful than that one.

text: Hic flos est omnium florum pulcherrimus.
translation: This flower is the most beautiful of all flowers.

text: Ex horti floribus hic pulcherrimus est.
translation: This is the most beautiful flower in the garden.

text: Maria florem in capillis suis habet.
translation: Mary has a flower in her hair.

text: Hic flos pulchrior est illo.
translation: This flower is more beautiful than that one.

text: Alicia florem in capillis tenet.
translation: Alice has a flower in her hair.

text: Aeroplanus in quo Thomas erat de caelo ictus est.
translation: The plane that Tom was on was struck by lightning.

text: Venator ictum in ursum misit.
translation: The hunter shot a bear.

text: Thomas ictum in cervum misit.
translation: Tom shot a deer.

text: Thomas sagitta ictus est.
translation: Tom was hit by an arrow.

text: Domus Thomae fulmine icta est.
translation: Tom's house was struck by lightning.

text: Domus Mariae fulmine icta est.
translation: Mary's house was struck by lightning.

text: Maria cultro icta est.
translation: Mary was stabbed with a knife.

text: Feceruntque ita filii Israel; et collegerunt alius plus, alius minus.
translation: And the children of Israel did so: and they gathered, one more, another less.

text: Lapides collegerant ad murum construendum.
translation: They had collected stones to build a wall.

text: Lapides collegerant ut murum aedificarent.
translation: They had collected stones to build a wall.

text: Sellam in decem minutis colligavimus.
translation: We assembled the chair in ten minutes.

text: Illi manus fune colligaverunt..
translation: They tied his hands with a rope.

text: Thomas fomitem igni colligebat.
translation: Tom gathered sticks for the fire.

text: Respondit: “Vade”. Perrexit puella et vocavit matrem infantis.
translation: And Pharaoh's daughter said to her, Go. And the maid went and called the child's mother.

text: Ita fessus sum, ut pergere non possim.
translation: I'm so tired that I can't go on.

text: Ita fessa sum, ut pergere non possim.
translation: I'm so tired that I can't go on.

text: Igitur egressus Iacob de Bersabee pergebat Charran.
translation: But Jacob being departed from Bersabee, went on to Haran.

text: Iter clam pergere debuit.
translation: He had to continue his trip in secret.

text: Thōmās epistulam legere perrēxit.
translation: Tom continued reading the letter.

text: In praesenti nihil agere mihi in animo est.
translation: I don't feel like doing anything right now.

text: Putasne Thoman scire ubi Maria in praesentia habitet?
translation: Do you think Tom knows where Mary lives now?

text: Ubi Thomas et Maria in praesentia habitant?
translation: Where do Tom and Mary live now?

text: "Ubi in praesentia habitas?" "In Algerio habito."
translation: "Where do you live now?" "I live in Algeria."

text: Ubi Thomas in praesentia habitet, nemo scit.
translation: Nobody knows where Tom lives now.

text: Nescio ubi Thomas in praesentia habitet.
translation: I don't know where Tom lives now.

text: Conventum est de pretio, pecunia numeratur praesens.
translation: We agreed about the price, the money is paid down presently.

text: Dixitque Booz iuveni, qui messoribus præerat: Cuius est hæc puella?
translation: Then Boaz said to his servant who was set over the reapers, "Whose young lady is this?"

text: Thomas in culina praeest.
translation: Tom is in charge of the kitchen.

text: Thomas tantis rebus praefuit.
translation: Tom was in charge of such matters.

text: Quis huic rei praeest?
translation: Who's in charge of this matter?

text: Generatione autem quarta revertentur huc; necdum enim completæ sunt iniquitates Amorhæorum usque ad præsens tempus.
translation: But in the fourth generation they shall return hither: for as yet the iniquities of the Amorrhites are not at the full until this present time.

text: Non omnia, quae vera sunt, recte dixeris.
translation: All truth is not to be told.

text: Rectum est id quod Thomas tibi dixit.
translation: What Tom told you is correct.

text: Cum recte vivas, ne cures verba malorum.
translation: As long as you do your duty, you don't need to worry about malicious words.

text: Puto te recte agere, ne eas.
translation: I think you're right not to go.

text: Non dubito quin Thomas recte dicat.
translation: I'm sure Tom is right.

text: "Tenesne?" "Non recte satis fortasse."
translation: "Have you memorised it?" "Not well enough perhaps."

text: Et Deum et proximos amare duo magna sunt praecepta.
translation: To love God and neighbors are the two great commandments.

text: Nihil est, quod agas, nisi praeceptis parere.
translation: There is nothing for you to do but obey the rules.

text: Praecepta salutis sanguine scripta sunt.
translation: Safety regulations are written in blood.

text: Cumque acciderit eis aliqua disceptatio, veniunt ad me, ut iudicem inter eos et ostendam præcepta Dei et leges eius.
translation: And when any controversy falleth out among them, they come to me to judge between them, and to shew the precepts of God, and his laws.

text: Timuerunt autem obstetrices Deum et non fecerunt iuxta præceptum regis Aegypti, sed conservabant mares.
translation: But the midwives feared God, and did not do as the king of Egypt had commanded, but saved the men children.

text: Recede e fenestra et veni ad me.
translation: Back away from the window and come to me.

text: Propter pollutionem omnes organismi e laco recesserunt.
translation: As a result of pollution, the lake is without any form of life.

text: Ab equinis pedibus procul recede.
translation: Keep away from the horse's feet.

text: Recede a ianua, quaeso.
translation: Please move away from the door.

text: Recedite a porta, quaeso.
translation: Please move away from the door.

text: Elegitque sibi Lot regionem circa Iordanem et recessit ab oriente; divisique sunt alterutrum a fratre suo.
translation: And Lot chose to himself the country about the Jordan, and he departed from the east: and they were separated one brother from the other.

text: Utrum esse an non esse: id est decidendum.
translation: To be or not to be, that is the question.

text: Utrum vilius est, hoc an illud?
translation: Which is cheaper, this or that?

text: Utrum melius est, hoc an istud?
translation: Which is better, this or that?

text: Uter nostrum magis tibi placet?
translation: Which one of us do you like best?

text: Utra nostrum magis tibi placet?
translation: Which one of us do you like best?

text: Uter vestrum Didymi medicus est?
translation: Which one of you is Tom's doctor?

text: Multi ex operariis fame mortui sunt.
translation: Many of the workers died of hunger.

text: Senex fame mortuus est.
translation: The old man died from hunger.

text: Animal fame mortuum est.
translation: The animal died from hunger.

text: Fames optima coqua est.
translation: Hunger is the best cook.

text: Fames optimus est coquus.
translation: Hunger is the best cook.

text: Thomas fame mortuus est.
translation: Tom died of hunger.

text: Post quem peperit filiam nomine Dinam.
translation: After whom she bore a daughter, named Dina.

text: Quæ respondit: Filia Bathuelis sum filii Melchæ, quem peperit Nachor.
translation: And she answered: I am the daughter of Bathuel, the son of Melcha, whom she bore to Nachor.

text: Maria in partu mortua est.
translation: Mary died in childbirth.

text: Quot ova aquila parit?
translation: How many eggs does an eagle lay?

text: Ea infantem sanum peperit.
translation: She had a healthy baby.

text: Gallina quinque ova peperit.
translation: The hen hatched five eggs.

text: Domini angelus in somnis apparuit Iosepho.
translation: The angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream.

text: Apparet Terram rotundam esse.
translation: It is evident that the Earth is round.

text: In angustiis apparent amici.
translation: A friend in need is a friend indeed.

text: Miror cur non appareant.
translation: I wonder why they aren't showing up.

text: Apparuit in domo mea.
translation: She appeared in my house.

text: Apparuit autem ei Dominus iuxta Quercus Mambre sedenti in ostio tabernaculi sui in ipso fervore diei.
translation: And the Lord appeared to him in the vale of Mambre as he was sitting at the door of his tent, in the very heat of the day.

text: Volo scire quomodo Thomas hoc faciat.
translation: I want to know how Tom does that.

text: Dixitne Thomas quomodo id facere potuerit?
translation: Did Tom say how he was able to do it?

text: Thomas intellexit quomodo Maria se haberet.
translation: Tom understood how Mary felt.

text: Merdae mea interest quomodo me censeant.
translation: I don't give a shit about what they think about me.

text: "Quomodo?" "Dabo mutuam pecuniam vicissim."
translation: "How?" "I will lend you money in turn."

text: Scisne quomodo linguam Latinam discat?
translation: Do you know how he learns Latin?

text: Quam magnum errorem fecisti in commentario tuo Anglice!
translation: What a big mistake you made in your English composition!

text: Errare humanum est, sed in errore perseverare dementis.
translation: To err is human, but to persevere in error is foolish.

text: Haec sententia aliquos graves errores habet.
translation: The sentence contains some serious mistakes.

text: Stulti est in errore manere.
translation: It is foolish to remain in error.

text: Video quanto in errore versentur.
translation: I see how deeply mistaken they are.

text: Magister errōrem discipulī observāvit.
translation: The teacher took notice of the student's mistake.

text: Forsitan tempus amplius ad hoc faciendum opus erit.
translation: It may take longer than we expected.

text: Forsitan et, Priami fuerint quæ fata, requiras.
translation: Haply the fate of Priam thou would'st know.

text: Nos forsitan Thomae non oportet id narrare.
translation: We should probably not tell Tom.

text: Illud Thomae forsitan non agendum est.
translation: Tom might not have to do that.

text: Hoc hodie forsitan faciam.
translation: Maybe I can do that today.

text: Forsitan diabolus hic loquitur.
translation: Perhaps the devil is speaking here.

text: Opera Homeri e Graeco in Anglicum sermonem convertit.
translation: He translated Homer from the Greek into English.

text: Thomas epistulam e Gallico in Germanicum sermonem convertit.
translation: Tom translated the letter from French into German.

text: Thomas librum e Gallico in Anglicum sermonem convertit.
translation: Tom translated the book from French into English.

text: Thomas librum in Gallicum sermonem convertere conatus est.
translation: Tom tried to translate a book into French.

text: Omnia quae Thomas scripsit in Gallicum sermonem converti.
translation: I translated everything Tom wrote into French.

text: Librum e Gallico in Anglicum sermonem convertit.
translation: He translated the book from French into English.

text: Causa non est cur eo proficiscar.
translation: There is no reason why I should go there.

text: Dixit mihi sibi necesse esse proficisci.
translation: He told me he had to leave.

text: Aeroplanus hora quinta et dimidia proficiscetur.
translation: The plane departs at 5:30 PM.

text: Sibi in animo esse proficisci dicit.
translation: She says she plans to go.

text: Thomas in animo habet solus proficisci.
translation: Tom plans on going by himself.

text: Praeses proximo mense Lutetiam proficiscetur.
translation: The President is leaving for Paris next month.

text: Commendavi eum secundum merita eius.
translation: I commended him according to his merits.

text: Thomas secundum flumen ambulabat.
translation: Tom walked along the river.

text: Benedictus es, Domine, Deus noster, Rex Universi, Qui me secundum voluntatem Suam creavit.
translation: Blessed are You, the Lord our God, King of the Universe, Who has made me according to His will.

text: "Mutationem motus proportionalem esse vi motrici impressæ, et fieri secundum lineam rectam qua vis illa imprimitur."
translation: Newton's Second Law says: "Force is equal to the change in momentum per change in time. For a constant mass, force equals mass times acceleration".

text: Feceruntque filii Israel, ut eis mandatum fuerat. Quibus dedit Ioseph plaustra secundum pharaonis imperium et cibaria in itinere.
translation: And the sons of Israel did as they were bid. And Joseph gave them wagons according to Pharaoh's commandment: and provisions for the way.

text: Sed et omnia animantia, iumenta, volatilia et reptilia, quæ reptant super terram, secundum genus suum egressa sunt de arca.
translation: And all living things, and cattle, and creeping things that creep upon the earth, according to their kinds went out of the ark.

text: Liber est donum quod pluries aperiri potest.
translation: A book is a gift they can open again and again.

text: Liber apertus super mensam scriptoriam est.
translation: There's a book lying open on the desk.

text: Cum solus esset, Thomas litteras aperuit.
translation: The moment Tom was alone he opened the letter.

text: Thomās lagoenam sūmpsit sed difficilius aperuit.
translation: Tom picked up the bottle, but had trouble opening it.

text: Aperi librum tuum ad paginam nonam.
translation: Open your book to page nine.

text: Aperi librum tuum ad paginam decimam.
translation: Open your book to page ten.

text: Nam castum esse decet pium poetam ipsum, versiculos nihil necessest.
translation: A poet's verses do not have to reflect his character.

text: Nam castum esse decet pium poētam ipsum, versiculōs nihil necesse est.
