translation: For it is proper for the devoted poet to be chaste himself, but not necessary at all for his verses to be so.

text: "Hunc socii morem sacrorum, hunc ipse teneto; / hac casti maneant in religione nepotes."
translation: "This pious use keep sacred, thou and thine, / the sons of sons unborn, and all the Trojan line."

text: Grammatici certant, et adhuc sub iudice lis est.
translation: On that point the learned disagree.

text: Petit a iudice ut clementer secum ageret.
translation: He pleaded with the judge for mercy.

text: Iudex parere debet non regi, sed legi.
translation: A judge must obey not the king, but the law.

text: Nemo iudex in causa sua.
translation: No one should be a judge in his own cause.

text: Thomas ab iudice indulgentias petiit.
translation: Tom begged the judge for leniency.

text: Cum te aliquis laudat, iudex tuus esse memento; plus aliis de te, quam tu tibi, credere noli.
translation: When somebody praises you, remember to be your own judge; do not trust others about you more than you about yourself.

text: Haec lapis pulchra est. Ubi eam invēnistī?
translation: This stone is beautiful. Where did you find it?

text: Num uno lapide duas aves capis?
translation: Can you catch two birds with one stone?

text: Lapis Rosettae anno MDCCXCIX reperta est.
translation: The Rosetta Stone was found in 1799.

text: Hoc aedificium e lapide factum est.
translation: This building is made of stone.

text: Lapis in calceo meo est.
translation: There's a rock in my shoe.

text: Lapis est in calceo meo.
translation: There's a stone in my shoe.

text: Nimis multos advocatos Bostoniae esse puto.
translation: I think there are too many lawyers in Boston.

text: Thomas dixit se nimis multum edisse.
translation: Tom said he ate too much.

text: Maria dixit se nimis multum edisse.
translation: Mary said she ate too much.

text: Hoc instrumentum photographicum nimis carum est.
translation: This camera is very expensive.

text: Iuvenis est, fortasse nimis etiam iuvenis.
translation: She's young, maybe too young.

text: Nimis multi in concento erant.
translation: There were too many people at the concert.

text: Longo in itinere, etiam palea oneri est.
translation: Light burdens borne far become heavy.

text: Suum quisque onus portet.
translation: Each one should carry his own load.

text: Multae manus onus levant.
translation: Many hands make quick work.

text: Hæc fatus, latos humeros subjectaque colla / veste super fulvique insternor pelle leonis, / succedoque oneri.
translation: So saying, my neck and shoulders I incline, / and round them fling a lion's tawny hide, / then lift the load.

text: Præposuit itaque eis magistros operum, ut affligerent eos oneribus; ædificaveruntque urbes promptuarias pharaoni, Phithom et Ramesses.
translation: Therefore he set over them masters of the works, to afflict them with burdens: and they built for Pharaoh cities of tabernacles, Phithom, and Ramesses.

text: Cum operaris operaris, cum ludis ludis.
translation: Work while you work, play while you play.

text: Dum tempus habemus, operemur bonum.
translation: As we have opportunity, let us do good.

text: Liberi nostri adhuc scholae operantur.
translation: Our children still go to school.

text: Magia tua hic non operabitur.
translation: Your magic won't work here.

text: Magia vestra hic non operabitur.
translation: Your magic won't work here.

text: Magni opera ejus existimata est.
translation: His assistance was highly esteemed.

text: Nonne secundum illius operis volumen habes?
translation: Don't you have the second volume of that work?

text: Laboriosi nihil tibi quicquam operis imperabo.
translation: I won't assign you any difficult tasks.

text: Operam fumo tabaci dare non licet.
translation: Smoking is prohibited.

text: Veni Bostoniam operis quaerendi causa.
translation: I came to Boston to look for work.

text: Valde multum adhuc restat operis!
translation: There's still so much to do!

text: Thomas linguae Gallicae operam dat.
translation: Tom is studying French.

text: Thomas fuit pauper, cum ditissimus esse posset.
translation: Tom was poor, although he could have been very rich.

text: Maria fuit pauper, cum ditissima esse posset.
translation: Mary was poor, although she could have been very rich.

text: Si fueris pauper, qui tibi amicus?
translation: If you were poor, who would be your friend?

text: Pauper esse malim, quam dives.
translation: I'd rather be poor than rich.

text: Pauper est, sed laeta.
translation: She is poor, but happy.

text: Pauper sed felix sum.
translation: I'm poor, but I'm happy.

text: Beati pauperes spiritu quoniam ipsorum est regnum cælorum.
translation: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

text: Beati pauperes spiritu, quoniam ipsorum est regnum caelorum.
translation: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

text: Paupera femina pecuniam pro cibo non habet.
translation: The poor woman does not have money for food.

text: Mors servat legem: tollit cum paupere regem.
translation: At the end of the game, the king and the pawns go into the same bag.

text: Thomas mihi dixit se pauperem esse.
translation: Tom told me he was poor.

text: Nova stragula pauperibus distributa sunt.
translation: New blankets were distributed to the poor.

text: Instrumentum aeri temperando munere suo non fungitur.
translation: The air conditioner doesn't work.

text: Aqua octingenties gravior est quam aer.
translation: Water is 800 times heavier than air.

text: Nonne Maria in aere tuo est?
translation: Does Maria not owe you?

text: Homines sine aere vivere non possunt.
translation: People can't live without air.

text: Homo sine aere vivere non potest.
translation: Man can't live without air.

text: Aurum colore simile est aeri.
translation: Gold is similar in color to brass.

text: Thomas in Australiam negotii causa praeterito mense ivit.
translation: Tom went to Australia on business last month.

text: Thomas Bostoniam negotii causa praeterito mense ivit.
translation: Tom went to Boston on business last month.

text: Interrete utor ad versandum in negotio.
translation: I use the internet to do business.

text: Negotia nostra ad eorum nihil sunt
translation: Our problems are nothing compared to theirs.

text: Est mihi aliud negotium, idemque pernecessarium.
translation: I have other business, which is very important to me.

text: Thomas in Australiam negotii causam ivit.
translation: Tom went to Australia on business.

text: Bene imperat qui bene paruit aliquando.
translation: He that cannot obey, cannot command.

text: Mater tua sum. Mihi te parere oportet – nec dubitare.
translation: I am your mother. I am to be obeyed - not questioned.

text: Filius meus mihi non paret.
translation: My son doesn't obey me.

text: Uterque parens mortuus est.
translation: Her parents both died.

text: Thomas mihi non paret.
translation: Tom doesn't obey me.

text: Tulit itaque Booz Ruth et accepit uxorem; ingressusque est ad eam, et dedit illi Dominus, ut conciperet et pareret filium.
translation: Boaz therefore took Ruth, and married her: and went in unto her, and the Lord gave her to conceive, and to bear a son.

text: Videam quantum argenti mihi apud trapeziam sit.
translation: I'm going to see how much money I have in the bank.

text: Sapientia praestantior auro atque argento.
translation: Wisdom is better than gold or silver.

text: Aurum multo pretiosius est argento.
translation: Gold is much more expensive than silver.

text: Aurum pretiosior est argento.
translation: Gold is more valuable than silver.

text: E stanno, faciunt cantbaros, e cupro ahena; ex orichalco, Candelabro; ex Argento, Thaleros; ex Aure, Scutates (Ducatos) et Coronatos.
translation: From tin, tankards are made; from copper, kettles; from lattin, candlesticks; from silver, dollars; from gold, Ducats and Crown pieces.

text: Quamquam argentum pretiosum est, aurum pretiosius est.
translation: Although silver is precious, gold is more precious.

text: Aurum multo pretiosius est quam argentum.
translation: Gold is much more expensive than silver.

text: Vivum argentum, semper liquidum, metalla corrodit.
translation: Quicksilver, always liquid, corrodes metals.

text: Argentum minoris pretii est quam aurum.
translation: Silver is cheaper than gold.

text: Primum, argentum non habeo. Secundo, mihi satis otii non est.
translation: First, I don't have any money. Second, I don't have the time.

text: Hydrargyrum etiam vivum argentum appellatur.
translation: Mercury is also known as quicksilver.

text: Hoc glossarium est tam utile quam illud.
translation: This dictionary is as useful as that one.

text: Hoc glossarium est pariter utile ac illud.
translation: This dictionary is as useful as that one.

text: Hoc glossarium est aeque utile ac illud.
translation: This dictionary is as useful as that one.

text: Hoc glossarium est aeque utile atque illud.
translation: This dictionary is as useful as that one.

text: Hic liber multo utilior est quam ille.
translation: This book is much more useful than that one.

text: Hoc glossarium est tam utile quam tuum.
translation: This dictionary is as useful as yours.

text: 'Præcipue, cum jam hic trabibus contextus acernis / staret equus, toto sonuerunt æthere nimbi.'
translation: 'And louder still, when towered the horse on high / with maple timbers, pealed the thunder through the sky.'

text: Vix ea fatus erat, cum circumfusa repente / scindit se nubes et in aethera purgat apertum.
translation: Scarce had he said, when straight the ambient cloud / broke open, melting into day's clear light.

text: "Hæc sunt quæ nostra liceat te voce moneri. / Vade age, et ingentem factis fer ad æthera Trojam."
translation: "Thou hast whate'er 'tis lawful to advise; / go, and with deathless deeds raise Ilion to the skies."

text: Thomas mercedem non meret quam ei tribuunt.
translation: Tom doesn't deserve the salary they're giving him.

text: Nolite dare praemium Thomae. Id non meret.
translation: Don't give the award to Tom. He doesn't deserve it.

text: Omnia quae recepturus es mereris.
translation: You deserve everything you get.

text: Thomas praemium Nobelianum meruit.
translation: Tom won the Nobel prize.

text: Maria praemium Nobelianum meruit.
translation: Mary won a Nobel prize.

text: Primus error veniam meretur.
translation: The first error deserves forgiveness.

text: Hannibal pecuniam Roma ad Africam portavit.
translation: Hannibal brought the money from Rome to Africa.

text: Romam ad Caesarem munera magna portant.
translation: They bring great presents to Caesar in Rome.

text: Crustula ad puellas et pueros porto.
translation: I bring cookies to the girls and the boys.

text: Dominus Fuscus semper librum portat.
translation: Mr Brown always carries a book.

text: Culices istae febrem paludis portant.
translation: Those mosquitoes transmit malaria.

text: Omnia mea mecum porto.
translation: All that is mine I carry with me.

text: In vita singularum cellularum propriae intelligentiae radices videre possumus.
translation: In the lives of single cells, we can perceive the roots of our own intelligence.

text: Meae gratia matri ego proprius sum.
translation: I am who I am thanks to my mother.

text: A Deo es proprium mihi donum.
translation: You're my special gift from God.

text: Age negotium tuum proprium!
translation: Mind your own business!

text: "Hæ nobis propriæ sedes; hinc Dardanus ortus / Iasiusque pater, genus a quo principe nostrum."
translation: "Thence sprang great Dardanus; there lies thy seat; / thence sire Iasius and the Trojans came."

text: Aptenodytes est avis quae volare non potest.
translation: A penguin is a bird that cannot fly.

text: Thomas Lingua Francogallice cum avis suis loquitur.
translation: Tom speaks French to his grandparents.

text: Avis caput suum in aquam lavit.
translation: The bird dipped its head into the water.

text: Vespertilio avis non est, sed mammalis.
translation: A bat is not a bird, but a mammal.

text: Canaria fringilla parva avis lutea est.
translation: The canary is a little yellow bird.

text: Huius avis cantus pulcherrimus est.
translation: The song of this bird is very beautiful.

text: Mare piscibus est, quod caelum avibus est.
translation: The sea is to fish what the sky is to birds.

text: Praeestne homo animalibus et avibus?
translation: Does mankind have dominion over animals and birds?

text: Is mei avi memoriam affert.
translation: He reminds me of my grandfather.

text: Haec domus avi mei est.
translation: This house is my grandfather's.

text: Librum de avi scripsit.
translation: She wrote a book about the bird.

text: Aquila rēgīna avium est.
translation: The eagle is king of birds.

text: Non assumes nomen Domini Dei tui in vanum.
translation: Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain.

text: Absque argento omnia vana.
translation: Without money you can't do anything.

text: Chromosomata in cellulis nostris totam materiam geneticam continent.
translation: The chromosomes in our cells contain the whole of our genetic material.

text: Hae capsae e materia plastica factae sunt.
translation: These boxes are made of plastic.

text: Haec sella e materia plastica facta est.
translation: This chair is made of plastic.

text: Catillus e materia plastica factus est.
translation: The plate is made of plastic.

text: Est magnum praeparare materiam bene.
translation: It is a great idea to prepare your materials well.

text: Materia plastica non facile crematur.
translation: Plastic does not burn easily.

text: Non puto paucas feles in Europa esse.
translation: I don't think there are few cats in Europe.

text: Multi homines et paucae mensae sunt hic.
translation: There are a lot of people and few tables here.

text: In multis familiis Romanis temporibus Augusti pauci liberi erant.
translation: There were few children in many Roman families in Augustus' times.

text: Tot interrogationes et tam pauca responsa.
translation: So many questions and so few answers.

text: vir sapit qui pauca loquitur.
translation: Wise is the man who speaks little.

text: Vir sapit, qui pauca loquitur.
translation: Wise is the man of few words.

text: Non puto paucos feles in Europa esse.
translation: I don't think there are few cats in Europe.

text: Ne quis miretur qui sim, paucis eloquar.
translation: Lest anyone wonder who I am, let me explain briefly.

text: Paucis verbis de Thoma te volo.
translation: I want to talk to you for a minute about Tom.

text: Paucis annis omnes mortui erimus.
translation: In a few years, we'll all be dead.

text: Paucos post annos me suppilaverunt.
translation: They robbed me a few years later.

text: Paucis diebus raedam gubernare poteris.
translation: You'll be able to drive a car in a few days.

text: Fiat voluntas tua sicut in caelo et in terra.
translation: May your will be done on Earth as it is in Heaven.

text: Dixerunt: Vocemus puellam et quæramus ipsius voluntatem.
translation: And they said: Let us call the maid, and ask her will.

text: Cuique voluntati placere non potest pecunia.
translation: Money can't satisfy every desire.

text: Quibus ille respondit: Nolite timere. Num Dei possumus resistere voluntati?
translation: And he answered them: Fear not: can we resist the will of God?

text: Contra voluntatem tuam nihil faciemus.
translation: We will do nothing against your will.

text: Iam illo tempore iuvenes itinera desiderantes sumus voluntate agendi non terminabili.
translation: At that time, we were still young, thirsting for adventure, and our desire for action knew no bounds.

text: Egregia forma et prodest et nocet.
translation: Being really beautiful can be a mixed blessing.

text: Se gerit egregium speculum veteranus amicus.
translation: Our image is always flawless for an old friend.

text: In Asia multae linguae difficiles sunt.
translation: There are many difficult languages in Asia.

text: Vero non est difficile hoc facere.
translation: It really isn't all that difficult to do that.

text: Estne lingua Gallica difficilior quam Anglica?
translation: Is French more difficult than English?

text: Nōnne linguam Iapōnicam difficilem esse putātis?
translation: Japanese is hard, don't you think?

text: Nōnne linguam Gallicam difficilem esse putās?
translation: French is hard, don't you think?

text: Nōnne linguam Gallicam difficilem esse putātis?
translation: French is hard, don't you think?

text: Omnes qui acceperint gladium gladio peribunt.
translation: All those who take up the sword shall perish by the sword.

text: Ei gladium e manibus extorsi.
translation: I wrested the sword from his hands.

text: Lingua mulieris gladius ipsius est.
translation: A woman's tongue is her sword.

text: Gladius meus vita mea est.
translation: My sword is my life.

text: Et conflabunt gladios suos in vomeres, et lanceas suas in falces.
translation: They shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruning hooks.

text: Maria gladium Thomae dedit.
translation: Mary gave Tom the sword.

text: Thomas cibum edit quem ei dedimus.
translation: Tom ate the food we gave him.

text: Puto pomum cibum saluberrimum esse.
translation: I consider fruit to be the healthiest food.

text: Placuitne tibi cibus, quem delibavisti?
translation: How did you like the food you tasted?

text: Cibus in hac popina sumptuosus.
translation: The food in this restaurant is very expensive.

text: Placuitne tibi cibus illius cauponae?
translation: How did you like the food at that restaurant?

text: Esne recordatus cibum caninum emere?
translation: Did you remember to buy dog food?

text: Lingua latina est via certa ad sapientiam.
translation: The Latin language is a sure way to wisdom.

text: Scisne cur Thomas et Maria certarent?
translation: Do you know why Tom and Mary were fighting?

text: Certa sum eas victuras esse.
translation: I'm sure they'll win.

text: Certa sum eos victuros esse.
translation: I'm sure they'll win.

text: Certa amittimus dum incerta petimus.
translation: He who seeks to achieve the doubtful can lose what is certain.

text: Aenean acciri omnes, populusque patresque, exposcunt mittique viros qui certa reportent.
translation: Everyone, the people in general and the elders in particular wanted Aeneas to be called back, to send messengers to inform him of the situation.

text: Quisque turma pediludii undecim lusores initio lusu habere debet.
translation: Each soccer team must have eleven players at the beginning of the match.

text: Id factum initio risum spectantibus concitabat.
translation: At first, this fact was making viewers laugh.

text: Timor Domini initium sapientiae est.
translation: The fear of God is the start of wisdom.

text: Initium mensis Augusti calidus est.
translation: During the first days of August, it is hot.

text: "Quid agit illic?" "Negotiatur." "E quo tempore?" "Ab ipso initio mercatus."
translation: "What is he doing there?" "Trading." "Since when?" "Since the start of the fair."

text: Lege ab initio paginae.
translation: Read from the beginning of the page.

text: Sermo eius brevis erat atque ad rem pertinebat.
translation: His speech was short and to the point.

text: Num illud ad te minime pertinet?
translation: That's none of your business, is it?

text: Hanc regula ad omnes casus pertinet.
translation: This rule applies to all cases.

text: Meae interrogationes ad mundum phaenomenon pertinent.
translation: My questions concern the phenomenal world.

text: Hoc horologium ad avum meum pertinebat.
translation: That watch belonged to my grandfather.

text: Res parvae nihil ad me pertinent.
translation: I'm not concerned with the details.

text: Tria pocula et quattuor patellae in mensa sunt.
translation: There are three cups and four plates on the table.

text: Quadrupeda sunt animalia quae quattuor pedes habent.
translation: Quadrupeds are animals that have four feet.

text: Tres fratres et quattuor sorores habeo.
translation: I have three brothers and four sisters.

text: "Quot sunt quattuor et quinque?" "Quattuor et quinque sunt novem."
translation: "What is four plus five?" "Four plus five is nine."

text: Iulius non solus est, nam quattuor servi apud eum sunt.
translation: Julius is not alone – there are four slaves with him.

text: Linguam Anglicam quattuor annos didici.
translation: I have been studying English for four years.

text: Argumentum pessimi turba est.
translation: The crowd is a bad example of conduct.

text: Domus turbine dēlēta est.
translation: The house was destroyed by a tornado.

text: Quae haec turba est?
translation: What is this commotion all about ?

text: Hic aliud majus miseris multoque tremendum / objicitur magis, atque improvida pectora turbat.
translation: A greater yet and ghastlier sign remained / our heedless hearts to terrify anew.

text: Thomas multum temporis in cubiculo suo consumit.
translation: Tom spends a lot of time in his room.

text: Thomas Mariae non dixit quantam pecuniam consumpsisset.
translation: Tom didn't tell Mary how much money he had spent.

text: Multum temporis consumo in legendis poetis.
translation: I spend a lot of time reading poets.

text: Omne meum tempus tecum consumere volo.
translation: I want to spend all my time with you.

text: Ubi Thomas vacationem aestivam consumpsit?
translation: Where did Tom spend his summer vacation?

text: Ubi vacationem aestivam consumpturus es?
translation: Where are you going to spend your summer vacation?

text: Pomum compunctum cito corrumpit sibi iunctum.
translation: The rotten apple injures its neighbour.

text: Accusatus est Socrates, quod adulescentes corrumperet.
translation: Socrates was arraigned on the ground that he was corrupting the young.

text: Socrates accusatus est quod corrumperet juventutem.
translation: Socrates was arraigned on the ground that he was corrupting the young.

text: A rege corruptus erat.
translation: He had been corrupted by the king.

text: Incidit in foveam, qui primus fecerat illam.
translation: The first to make a hole will fall into it.

text: Mortem non timeo, sed malo abesse cum idem incidit.
translation: I'm not afraid of death, but I prefer not to be here when it occurs.

text: Didymus in aquam frigidam fluminis incidit.
translation: Tom fell into the ice-cold water of the river.

text: Mariam superiore hebdomade in convivio incidi.
translation: I ran into Mary at a party last week.

text: Gutta, incidens in aquam, facit bullam, multae bullae faciunt spuman.
translation: A drop, falling into water, makes a bubble; many bubbles make froth.

text: Fugiens ursum, incidit in leonem.
translation: Fleeing a bear, he runs into a lion.

text: Canes vocati veniunt, hospites autem boni non invitati.
translation: Dogs come when they're called. Good guests come uninvited.

text: Hic munere fungor. Hospes non sum.
translation: I work here. I'm no guest.

text: Veniat hospes quisquis proferturus est.
translation: They are welcome that bring.

text: Librum de hospitibus scripsit.
translation: She wrote a book about the visitors.

text: Hospes ante aedis astat.
translation: A stranger is standing in front of the house.

text: Omnibus idem animus, scelerata excedere terra, / linqui pollutum hospitum et dare classibus austros.
translation: All vote to sail, and quit the shore accurst.

text: Thomas et Maria et Ioannes et Alicia omnes ridebant.
translation: Tom, Mary, John and Alice all smiled.

text: Et Didymus et Maria ridere coeperunt.
translation: Tom and Mary both started to laugh.

text: Thomas risit ubi Maria hoc dixit.
translation: Tom laughed when Mary said that.

text: Dixitque Sara: Risum fecit mihi Deus; quicumque audierit, corridebit mihi.
translation: And Sara said: God hath made a laughter for me: whosoever shall hear of it will laugh with me.

text: Mulier in subsellio sedens risit.
translation: The woman who sat on the bench laughed.

text: Puer qui ridet est Marcus.
translation: The boy who is smiling is Marcus.

text: collige, virgo, rosas, dum flos novus et nova pubes et memor esto aevum sic properare tuum.
translation: Gather, maiden, roses, while the flower is new and new is youth, and be mindful that your time hurries thus.

text: Ille minime audax vir est cui munus mandavi.
translation: He is the least capable man I have ever employed.

text: In foribus propriis canis est audacior omnis.
translation: Every dog is a lion at home.

text: Audacia eius laudanda est.
translation: His bravery should be praised.

text: Non vos pudet, puellae audaces, sic sectari iuvenem in agris? Qui istic mos est?
translation: Are you not ashamed of yourselves, you bold girls, to run after a young man in that way over the fields? Is that good behaviour?

text: Carpe diem quam minimum credula postero.
translation: Seize every day, giving no thought for tomorrow.

text: dum loquimur, fugerit invida aetas: carpe diem, quam minimum credula postero.
translation: Even as we speak, envious time will have fled: seize the day, trusting as little as possible in the hereafter.

text: Quae statio posterior est?
translation: What's the next station?

text: Quae statio postera est?
translation: What's the next station?

text: Edixeritne praetor ut adesses?
translation: Did the praetor order you to appear?

text: In urbe habito, sed parentes mei ruri habitant.
translation: I live in a town, but my parents live in the country.

text: Hieme in urbe sum, commoror autem ruri per aestatem.
translation: In the winter I'm in the city, but I stay in the country for the summer.

text: Herī ivi rus cum meō patruō.
translation: Yesterday I went into the country with my uncle.

text: Tibine mos est aestate rus eundi?
translation: Do you usually go to the country in the summer?

text: – Eo rus! – I!
translation: "I'm off to the country!" "Go!"

text: Parentes mei ruri habitant.
translation: My parents live in the country.

text: Hi omnes lingua, institutis, legibus inter se differunt.
translation: These all differ from each other in language, customs and laws.

text: Spes quae differtur, aggravat animum.
translation: Hope deferred makes the heart sick.

text: Omnes homines inter se differunt.
translation: Everybody is different.

text: Qui distulit diu, noluit.
translation: A long-awaited gift is sold and not given.

text: Hae arbores differunt folio.
translation: These trees have different leaves.

text: Sine dioxydo carbonico non est vita.
translation: There is no life without carbon dioxide.

text: Ubi aqua est, ibi vita est.
translation: Where there's water, there's life.

text: In eo vita erat, et vita illa lux hominum erat.
translation: In him was life, and that life was the light of men.

text: Multa pars mei vitabit Libitinam.
translation: The best part of myself will not die.

text: Vita Thomasae facilis non erat.
translation: Tom has not had an easy life.

text: Vivere tota vita discendum est.
translation: We are to learn as long as we live.

text: Tota erat urbs aqua privata.
translation: The whole city was deprived of water.

text: Mitte mihi nuntium privatum.
translation: Send me a private message.

text: Nēmō potest duōbus dominīs servīre.
translation: No man can serve two masters.

text: Temporibus semper cautus servire memento.
translation: Always make sure to accommodate yourself prudently to the occasion.

text: Multi homines animi perturbationibus serviunt.
translation: Many are slaves to the passions.

text: Gaudeo si licet tibi servire.
translation: I will be glad if I can be of any service to you.

text: Servivit igitur Iacob pro Rachel septem annis, et videbantur illi pauci dies præ amoris magnitudine.
translation: So Jacob served seven years for Rachel: and they seemed but a few days, because of the greatness of his love.

text: Et ingressus etiam ad Rachel amavit eam plus quam Liam serviens apud eum septem annis aliis.
translation: And having at length obtained the marriage he wished for, he preferred the love of the latter before the former, and served with him other seven years.

text: Nauta esse mihi non placeret quod aquam vereor.
translation: I wouldn't like to be a sailor because I'm afraid of water.

text: "Cur non?" "Vereor, ne irascatur mihi."
translation: "Why not?" "I'm afraid he'll be angry with me."

text: Vereor ne tale concilium nihil prosit.
translation: I'm afraid this kind of meeting isn't getting us anywhere.

text: Tuum est maiores natu vereri.
translation: You must respect your elders.

text: Veritas nihil veretur nisi abscondi.
translation: Truth fears nothing but concealment.

text: Vereor ne cras pluat.
translation: I'm afraid it will rain tomorrow.

text: "Vide praeceptorem, qui jam ingreditur scholam." "Eamus auditum prælectionem."
translation: "Look, the master is now arriving at school." "Let's go to hear the lesson."

text: Sol egressus est super terram, et Lot ingressus est Segor.
translation: The sun was risen upon the earth, and Lot entered into Segor.

text: Bene mane tram ingredior ad academiam.
translation: Early in the morning, I get on a tram and go to the university.

text: Navem nisi sarcinas recuperem ingrediar.
translation: I cannot get on this boat if I don't find my luggage.

text: Cum itaque ingressus esset Abram Aegyptum, viderunt Aegyptii mulierem quod esset pulchra nimis.
translation: And when Abram was come into Egypt, the Egyptians saw the woman that she was very beautiful.

text: Avertitque se et ingressus est domum suam nec ad hoc apposuit cor suum.
translation: And he turned himself away, and went into his house, neither did he set his heart to it this time also.

text: Te hoc quidem ei dixisse non adducor.
translation: I can't believe you told him that.

text: Thomas Mariam ad stationem ferriviariam adduxit.
translation: Tom drove Mary to the train station.

text: Hoc te in periculum adducet.
translation: That will put you in danger.

text: Illud vos in periculum adducet.
translation: That will put you in danger.

text: Cūr mē hūc addūxistī?
translation: Why have you brought me here?

text: Cūr mē hūc addūxistis?
translation: Why have you brought me here?

text: Et Didymus et Maria in horto opus faciunt.
translation: Tom and Mary are both working in the garden.

text: In horto meo multae arbores pomiferae sunt.
translation: In my garden many trees are bearing fruit.

text: Et Didymus et Maria in horto laborant.
translation: Tom and Mary are both working in the garden.

text: Aranea telam suam delicatam in horto texuit.
translation: The spider spun her delicate web in the garden.

text: Eos cum pueris in horto laborantes vidi.
translation: I saw them working with the children in the garden.

text: Thomas ut ignoraret Mariam hortatus sum.
translation: I tried to get Tom to ignore Mary.

text: Negavit se reum esse.
translation: He said that he wasn't guilty.

text: Si effringens fur domum sive suffodiens fuerit inventus et, accepto vulnere, mortuus fuerit, percussor non erit reus sanguinis.
translation: If a thief be found breaking open a house or undermining it, and be wounded so as to die: he that slew him shall not be guilty of blood.

text: Servus tuus pro puero patri meo spopondit: Nisi reduxero eum, peccati reus ero in patrem meum omni tempore.
translation: Let me be thy proper servant, who took him into my trust, and promised, saying: If I bring him not again, I will be guilty of sin against my father for ever.

text: Quod si orto sole hoc fecerit, erit reus sanguinis. Fur plene restituet. Si non habuerit, quod reddat, venumdabitur pro furto.
translation: But if he did this when the sun is risen, he hath committed murder, and he shall die. If he have not wherewith to make restitution for the theft, he shall be sold.

text: Hoc scilicet non litteratim legatur.
translation: This, of course, does not have to be taken literally.

text: Vivit, ergo scilicet cacat.
translation: It's a living being, so of course it shits.

text: Erant autem uterque nudi, Adam scilicet et uxor eius, et non erubescebant.
translation: And they were both naked: to wit, Adam and his wife: and were not ashamed.

text: Quod cum vidisset Cham pater Chanaan, verenda scilicet patris sui esse nudata, nuntiavit duobus fratribus suis foras.
translation: And Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father, and told his two brethren without.

text: Maria dicit se posse comparare omnia quibus egemus.
translation: Mary says she can get everything we need.

text: Thomas et Maria inter se adnotationes comparaverunt.
translation: Tom and Mary compared notes.

text: Macbethus exercitum ad hostem oppugnandum comparavit.
translation: Macbeth raised an army to attack his enemy.

text: Tibi exercitus magnus comparandus est.
translation: You need to raise a great army.

text: Birotam novam proxima hebdomade comparabit.
translation: He is going to buy a new bicycle next week.

text: Poeta mortem cum sumno comparavit.
translation: The poet compared death to sleep.

text: Amor meus perpetuus est.
translation: My love is eternal.

text: Qui desiderat potentiam est dux malus.
translation: People who desire power make bad leaders.

text: Thomas Mariam modo pecuniae desiderat.
translation: Tom wants Mary only for the money.

text: Ubi es, Thōmā? Tē dēsīderāmus.
translation: Tom, where are you? We miss you!

text: Quis aliud placentae frustum desiderat?
translation: Who wants another piece of cake?

text: Thomas magnopere Mariam desiderat.
translation: Tom really misses Mary.

text: Thomas valde Mariam desiderat.
translation: Tom really misses Mary.

text: Familiam et patriam meas desidero.
translation: I miss my family and my country.

text: Felices Dies Dedicationis tibi desidero.
translation: Happy Chanukah.

text: Cum abes, te desidero.
translation: I miss you when you're not here.

text: Desidero aliam linguam discere.
translation: I feel like learning another language.

text: Maria primum diem anni apud familiam celebrat.
translation: Mary celebrates New Year's Day with her family.

text: Quomodo primus dies anni in Australia celebratur?
translation: How do people celebrate the new year in Australia?

text: Et celebremus nomen nostrum antequam dividamur in universas terras.
translation: And let us make us a name, lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth.

text: Pervigilium Omnium Sanctorum mense Octobre celebratur.
translation: Halloween's celebrated in October.

text: Quando nox Guy Fawkes celebratur?
translation: When is Bonfire Night celebrated?

text: Nunc tempus est celebrare.
translation: Now, it's time to celebrate.

text: Fessus sum; tamen debeo conficere pensum scholare.
translation: I am tired; nevertheless, I must finish my homework.

text: Thomas tecum veniet si opus confecerit.
translation: Tom will come with you if he finishes his work.

text: Maria mecum veniet si opus confecerit.
translation: Mary will come with me if she finishes her work.

text: Tecum veniam si opus confecerim.
translation: I'll come with you if I finish the job.

text: "Confecistine tuum praescriptum domesticum?" "Confeci."
translation: "Did you finish your homework?" "I did."

text: Iam confeci meum praescriptum domesticum.
translation: I've already finished my homework.

text: Thomas etiam nunc illud facere intendit.
translation: Tom is still planning to do that.

text: Thomas digitum in Mariam intendit.
translation: Tom pointed a finger at Mary.

text: Hercules a puero corpus suum diligenter exercebat; magnam partem diei in palaestra consumebat; didicit etiam arcum intendere et tela conicere.
translation: From childhood, Hercules exercised diligently, spending most of the day at the gymnasium; and he learned to shoot with a bow and arrow.

text: Amici mortem se ulturum esse iuravit.
translation: He vowed to avenge his friend's death.

text: Mortem Thomae se ulturum esse iuravit.
translation: He swore to avenge Tom's death.

text: Mortem Thomae se persecuturum esse iuravit.
translation: He swore to avenge Tom's death.

text: Dixitque Abraham: Ego iurabo.
translation: And Abraham said: I will swear.

text: Civitates iura non habent.
translation: States don't have rights.

text: Posuit ergo servus manum sub femore Abraham domini sui et iuravit illi super hac re.
translation: The servant, therefore, put his hand under the thigh of Abraham, his lord, and swore to him upon his word.

text: Sola erat femina quam semper amaverat.
translation: She was the only woman I ever loved.

text: Domi manere malim, quam sola ire.
translation: I'd rather stay home than go alone.

text: Quam diu sola apud Thoman fuisti?
translation: How long were you alone with Tom?

text: Quomodo sedet sola civitas plena populo!
translation: How the city sits solitary, that was full of people!

text: Lingua Malitensis est sola lingua Semitica quae litteris Latinis utatur.
translation: Maltese is the only Semitic language with a script based on the Latin alphabet.

text: Sōla opus facere coācta sum.
translation: I was compelled to do the work alone.

text: Magistra auctoritatem in discipulos nullam habet.
translation: The teacher has no authority over her students.

text: Punitis ingeniis, gliscit auctoritas.
translation: Genius chastised grows in authority.

text: Thomas aliquam auctoritatem habebat.
translation: Tom had some influence.

text: Cum ianitor pilam tetigit, arbiter alii gregi iactum angularis adiucavit.
translation: When the goalkeeper touched the ball, the referee awarded the other team a corner kick.

text: Ossa in pavimentum iacimus.
translation: We throw the bones onto the floor.

text: Malum in me iecit.
translation: He threw me the apple.

text: Malum ad me iecit.
translation: He threw me the apple.

text: Thomas nocte laborat, de die contra dormit.
translation: Tom works at night and sleeps during day.

text: Praecipuus interpres in praeterito laboravit ut diurnarius.
translation: The main translator worked as a journalist in the past.

text: Scisne ubi Thomas et Maria laborent?
translation: Do you know where Tom and Mary work?

text: Debeo laborare, ergo ire non possum.
translation: I'm busy, so I can't go.

text: Esto laborator, et erit Deus auxiliator.
translation: Work, and God will help you.

text: Qui non laborat, non manducat.
translation: He who does not work, does not eat.

text: Nocte splendet Luna et Stellae micant, scintillant.
translation: In the night the moon shines and the stars glitter and twinkle.

text: Putō hominēs in Lūnā vīvere posse.
translation: I think men can live on the moon.

text: Vita in Luna non est.
translation: There is no life on the moon.

text: Sol maior quam Luna est.
translation: The sun is larger than the moon.

text: Plantae in Luna non sunt.
translation: There are no plants on the Moon.

text: Aer in Luna non est.
translation: There is no air on the moon.

text: Quamquam Lunae dies est, tamen Thomas id faciet.
translation: Even though it's Monday, Tom will do that.

text: Non puto Iovem solum quattuor lunas habere.
translation: I don't think Jupiter only has four moons.

text: Mars duas lunas habet: Phobon et Deimon.
translation: Mars has two moons: Phobos and Deimos.

text: Die lunae Thomas et Maria cenam coxerunt.
translation: Tom and Mary cooked dinner on Monday.

text: Diana est pulchra dea lunæ et silvarum.
translation: Diana is the beautiful goddess of the Moon and the forest.

text: Oportet nos scire quid facturi simus die Lunae .
translation: We need to know what we're supposed to do on Monday.

text: Oportet me protinus domum ire.
translation: I have to go home immediately.

text: Totam cervisiam protinus obsorbuit.
translation: He drank the beer in one gulp.

text: Protinus ad regis imperium eductum de carcere Ioseph totonderunt ac, veste mutata, obtulerunt ei.
translation: Forthwith at the king's command Joseph was brought out of the prison, and they shaved him: and changing his apparel brought him in to him.

text: Protinus aërias Phæacum abscondimus arces, / litoraque Epiri legimus, portuque subimus / Chaonio et celsam Buthroti accedimus urbem.
translation: Phaeacia's heights with the horizon blend; / we skim Epirus, and Chaonia's bay / enter, and to Buthrotum's town ascend.

text: Isto modo id facere nondum conatus sum.
translation: I haven't tried doing it that way.

text: Cur alio modo id facere non conaris?
translation: Why don't you try doing that a different way?

text: Thomas me osculari conatus est, eum autem non sivi.
translation: Tom tried to kiss me, but I didn't let him.

text: Cūr nōn eum vocāre cōnātus es?
translation: Why have you not tried to call him?

text: Noli conari semper vivere. Non succedes.
translation: Do not try to live forever. You will not succeed.

text: Ego numquam clavichordo canere conatus sum.
translation: I never tried playing the piano.

text: Corsica insula est. Corsica et Sicilia insulae sunt.
translation: Corsica is an island. Corsica and Sicily are islands.

text: Haec insula sexies maior est quam Manhata.
translation: This island is six times bigger than Manhattan.

text: Nimis multi in hac insula sunt.
translation: There are way too many people on this island.

text: Insula in mari Caribico est.
translation: This is an island in the Caribbean Sea.

text: Quid novi vidisti in insula?
translation: What did you find new on the island?

text: Finitima Italiæ est insula Sicilia.
translation: The island closest to Italy is Sicily.

text: Caprea una ex pulcherrimis insulis Italiae est.
translation: Capri is one of the most beautiful islands in Italy.

text: Quot īnsulās habet Germānia?
translation: How many islands does Germany have?

text: Quot īnsulās habet Indonēsia?
translation: How many islands does Indonesia have?

text: Mare facit littora, Sinus, promontoria, insulas, peninsulas, isthmos, freta et habet scopulos.
translation: The sea makes shores, bays, capes, islands, peninsulas, necks of land, straights, and has rocks in it.

text: Est Thomae filius, cui nomen est Ioannes.
translation: Tom has a son whose name is John.

text: Caesario filius Cleopatrae et Iulii Caesaris erat.
translation: Caesarion was the son of Cleopatra and Julius Caesar.

text: Nepos meus est filius filii mei.
translation: My grandson is the son of my son.

text: Unum filium et duas filias habet.
translation: He has one son and two daughters.

text: Habet duas filias, quae nuptae sunt.
translation: He has two daughters, who are married.

text: Ea virum et duas filias habet.
translation: She has a husband and two daughters.

text: Descenditque Moyses ad populum et omnia narravit eis.
translation: And Moses went down to the people and told them all.

text: Cur de parentibus tuis mihi non narravisti?
translation: Why didn't you tell me about my parents?

text: Non credidit quae ei de illa narravi.
translation: He didn't believe what I told him about her.

text: estne aliquid quod nos narrare vis?
translation: Is there something you want to tell us?

text: Velim mihi narres de itinere tuo.
translation: I want you to tell me about your trip.

text: Thōmās nihil dē sē mihi nārrābat.
translation: Tom wouldn't tell me anything about himself.

text: Necessitas non habet legem.
translation: Necessity has no law.

text: Hodie egredimini, mense Abib (id est novarum Frugum).
translation: This day you go forth in the month of new corn.

text: Egressus Tobias invenit juvenem stantem et accinctum ad iter faciendum.
translation: While Tobias was going out, he found a young man standing there, prepared for the journey ahead.

text: Sine pecunia egressus sum.
translation: I went out without money.

text: Si solus intraverit, solus exeat; si habens uxorem, et uxor egredietur simul.
translation: With what raiment he came in, with the like let him go out: if having a wife, his wife also shall go out with him.

text: Si quis vendiderit filiam suam in famulam, non egredietur sicut servi exire consueverunt.
translation: If any man sell his daughter to be a servant, she shall not go out as bondwomen are wont to go out.

text: Egressus est ergo Noe et filii eius, uxor illius et uxores filiorum eius cum eo.
translation: So Noah went out, he and his sons: his wife, and the wives of his sons with him.

text: Carmina Horatii, poetae Romani, imitationes poetarum Graecorum sunt.
translation: The poems of Horace, a Roman poet, are imitations of Greek poets.

text: Multi clari philosophi et poetae veniunt Athenis.
translation: Many famous philosophers and poets come from Athens.

text: Non solum medicus, sed etiam poeta fuit.
translation: He was a doctor; moreover, a poet.

text: Quis ex Anglicis poetis optimus est?
translation: Who is the best of the English poets?

text: Hic poeta numquam oblivione delebitur.
translation: This poet will never be forgotten.

text: Fabulator et poeta est.
translation: He is a storyteller and a poet.

text: Erat annos natus decem, cum in Iaponiam venit.
translation: He came to Japan when he was 10 years old.

text: Brasilia a decem terris et ab Oceano Atlantico circumdatur.
translation: Brazil is surrounded by ten countries and the Atlantic Ocean.

text: Filius meus decem annos natus est.
translation: My son is ten years old.

text: Hic decem annos opus factus sum.
translation: I've worked here for ten years.

text: Hic decem annos opus facta sum.
translation: I've worked here for ten years.

text: Decem annos tantum nata eram cum mater mea mortua est.
translation: I was only ten years old when my mother died.

text: Obscurum vestis contegit ampla genus.
translation: Good clothes open all doors.

text: Nostra aula est ampla.
translation: Our yard is large.

text: Diaeta Thomae ampla est.
translation: Tom's apartment is spacious.

text: Jam Deiphobi dedit ampla ruinam / Vulcano superante domus, jam proximus ardet / Ucalegon, Sigea igni freta lata relucent.
translation: And now, Deiphobus, thy halls of pride, / bowed by the flames, come ruining through the air; / next burn Ucalegon's, and far and wide / the broad Sigean reddens with the glare.

text: Fit strepitus tectis, vocemque per ampla volutant / atria; dependent lychni laquearibus aureis / incensi, et noctem flammis funalia vincunt.
translation: The noise of festival / rings through the spacious courts, and rolls along the hall. / There, blazing from the gilded roof, are seen / bright lamps, and torches turn the night to day.

text: Lacus Magni aquam ad bibendum aptam dant.
translation: The Great Lakes supply drinking water.

text: Aquam ad bibendum aptam non habebamus.
translation: We had no drinking water.

text: Aquam ad bibendum aptam non habemus.
translation: We have no drinking water.

text: Calceos ad saltandum aptos gerit.
translation: She is wearing dancing shoes.

text: Sapientia me consequitur, sed ego celerior sum.
translation: Wisdom follows me, but I am faster.

text: Id magis iustitia quam imperio consecutus est.
translation: He achieved this more by justice than by authority.

text: Canis felem consequitur et feles murem consequitur.
translation: A dog runs after a cat, and the cat after a mouse.

text: Nomades aquam consequuntur ac terram herbidam.
translation: Nomadic peoples follow the water and grazing land.

text: Beati misericordes, quia ipsi misericordiam consequentur.
translation: Blessed are the merciful, for they themselves shall obtain mercy.

text: Canis felem consequitur, feles sciurum.
translation: The dog chases the cat, and the cat chases the squirrel.

text: Post ludum frequenter scaccis ludebamus.
translation: We often played chess after school.

text: Nec non et Tyrii per limina læta frequentes / convenere, toris jussi discumbere pictis.
translation: There, entering too, on broidered seats recline / the Tyrians, crowding through the festive court.

text: Tandem unus arridebat plus caeteris. Ille probat meum judicium, dejerans eum equum ex petitum esse frequenter a multis.
translation: At length one pleased me more than the rest. He approves of my judgment, swearing that that horse had been desired frequently by many.

text: Heri Thomas plus quam trigina nuntios mihi scripsit.
translation: Tom wrote me more than thirty messages yesterday.

text: Tristissima fui quando nuntium audivi.
translation: I felt very sad when I heard the news.

text: Thomas nuntios per telehorasim aspicit.
translation: Tom is watching the news on TV.

text: Quis mihi nuntium mittere vult?
translation: Who wants to send me a message?

text: Quota hora nuntios aspicis?
translation: What time do you watch the news?

text: Fere cotidie nuntios aspicio.
translation: I watch the news almost every day.

text: Hic nuntius ad regem afferri non potest.
translation: This message cannot be delivered to the king.

text: Non saepe nuntius per telehorasim aspicio.
translation: I don't usually watch news on TV.

text: Hic nuntius ad regem afferendus est.
translation: This message is to be delivered to the king.

text: Nuntius ad regem allatus est.
translation: A message was brought to the king.

text: Nuntius affert hostem adesse.
translation: A messenger reports that the enemy is approaching.

text: Mercurius nuntius deorum erat.
translation: Mercury was the messenger of the gods.

text: Thomas nobis dixit condicionem Mariae non mutavisse.
translation: Tom told us Mary's condition hadn't changed.

text: Gratias vobis ago quod in convivium meum venistis.
translation: Thanks for coming to my party.

text: Fecit ergo eis convivium, et comederunt et biberunt.
translation: And he made them a feast, and after they had eaten and drunk.

text: Convivium in magna exedra factum est.
translation: The party took place in a big room.

text: Quot homines ad convivium vestrum venient?
translation: How many people will come to your party?

text: Quot hominēs ad convīvium tuum vēnērunt?
translation: How many came to your party?

text: Cur e convivio pulsa es?
translation: Why were you thrown out of the party?

text: Ut ego quidem sentio, illud aedificium foedum est.
translation: That's an ugly building, in my opinion.

text: Homo foedus fores meas pulsavit.
translation: An ugly man knocked on my door.

text: Capilli mei valde foedi sunt.
translation: My hair is very ugly.

text: Verrucae sunt foedae sed innocuae.
translation: Warts are ugly but harmless.

text: Sensi me foedum esse.
translation: I felt like I was very ugly.

text: Maria putat se foedam.
translation: Mary thinks that she is ugly.

text: Hoc videtur vespero frui felicula cibo. Haud semper fruatur.
translation: The kitten seems to be enjoying her food this evening. She doesn't always seem to enjoy it.

text: Vino rubro plus quam albo fruor.
translation: I like red wine better than white.

text: Qua respondente: “Quid mihi dabis, ut fruaris concubitu meo?”, dixit.
translation: And she answered: What wilt thou give me to enjoy my company?

text: Vita est amor. Eā fruere!
translation: Life is love. Enjoy it!

text: Natamus multum et fruimur.
translation: We swim a lot and enjoy it.

text: Terram autem sacerdotum non emit, qui cibariis a rege statutis fruebantur, et idcirco non sunt compulsi vendere possessiones suas.
translation: Except the land of the priests, which had been given them by the king: to whom also a certain allowance of food was given out of the public stores, and therefore they were not forced to sell their possessions.

text: Recordarisne quando Thomas dixerit, se id fecisse?
translation: Do you remember when Tom said he did that?

text: Recordarisne quando Maria dixerit, se id fecisse?
translation: Do you remember when Mary said she did that?

text: Recordarisne quando Thomas id tibi dederit?
translation: Do you remember when Tom gave you that?

text: Num idem Thōmae et Marīae placet?
translation: Do Tom and Mary have the same opinion?

text: Quid mihi accidit? Num aeger sum?
translation: What happened to me? Am I sick?

text: Num lacrimás in vultú tuó cónspició?
translation: I don’t see tears on your face, do I?

text: Telephonum nigrum maiore pretio quam album constat.
translation: The black telephone costs more than the white.

text: Haec feles mea non est. Mea pedes albos habet.
translation: This is not my cat. Mine has white feet.

text: Tres canes nobis sunt, unus albus et duo nigri.
translation: We have three dogs, one white and two black.

text: Iacobus petasum album in capite gerit.
translation: Jim has a white hat on his head.

text: Utrum vinum bibis: album an rubrum?
translation: What are you drinking, white or red?

text: Dominus Albus ad Indiam ivit.
translation: Mr. White has gone to India.

text: Accepto damno ianuam claudere.
translation: It's too late to shut the stable door after the horse has bolted.

text: Si egressus ignis invenerit spinas et comprehenderit acervos frugum sive stantes segetes sive agrum, reddet damnum, qui ignem succenderit.
translation: If a fire breaking out light upon thorns, and catch stacks of corn, or corn standing in the fields, he that kindled the fire shall make good the loss.

text: Dixi: Ascendam in palmam, et apprehendam fructus eius.
translation: I said, I will go up to the palm tree, I will take hold of the boughs thereof.

text: Non potest arbor bona malos fructus facere.
translation: A good tree can't bear bad fruits.

text: Haec arbor vere multos magnosque fructus edit.
translation: This tree produces a lot of big fruit in spring.

text: Fructus huius arboris dulciores sunt quam illius.
translation: The fruit from this tree is sweeter than the fruit from that one.

text: Haec arbor tam iuvenis est, ut fructus edere non possit.
translation: This tree is too young to bear fruit.

text: Quis fructus maxime tibi placet?
translation: What fruit do you like the best?

text: Veniat dilectus meus in hortum suum, et comedat fructum pomorum suorum.
translation: Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat the fruit of his apple trees.

text: Arbor ex fructu cognoscitur.
translation: A tree is known by its fruit.

text: Terra dedit fructum suum.
translation: The earth hath yielded her increase.

text: Mensa fructibus plena est.
translation: The table is full of fruits.

text: Cui iratus respondit Iacob: Num pro Deo ego sum, qui privavit te fructu ventris?
translation: And Jacob being angry with her, answered: Am I as God, who hath deprived thee of the fruit of thy womb?

text: Factum est autem post aliquot dies ut offerret Cain de fructibus agri munus Domino.
translation: And it came to pass after many days, that Cain offered, of the fruits of the earth, gifts to the Lord.

text: Censui te dixisse aliquem ut id faceres iussisse.
translation: I thought you said that someone told you to do that.

text: Eum sermone suo Osaka censeo ortum esse.
translation: Judging from his accent, he must be from Osaka.

text: Quid id ad me, quid Thomas censeat?
translation: What do I care what Tom thinks?

text: Non censebam id Thomae soli faciendum fuisse.
translation: I didn't think Tom really had to do that by himself.

text: Duobus diebus opus fore nobis censeo ad laborem conficiendum.
translation: I estimate that we'll need two days to finish the work.

text: Thoman censeo quid petat Maria nescire.
translation: I don't think Tom knows what Mary is looking for.

text: Licetne tibi litteratim, sodes, nomen tibi prodere?
translation: Could you spell your name, please?

text: Multi ob pecuniam amicos produnt.
translation: Many betrayed their friends for money.

text: "Bis quinos silet ille dies, tectusque recusat / prodere voce sua quemquam aut opponere morti."
translation: "Ten days the seer, as shrinking to reply / or name a victim, did the doom withhold."

text: Postremo propositum suum consecutus est.
translation: In the end he achieved his goal.

text: Propositum capiunt Tartara, facta Polus.
translation: Hell is paved with good intentions.

text: Homo proponit, sed Deus disponit.
translation: Man proposes, but God disposes.

text: Homo proponit sed Deus disponit.
translation: Man proposes, God disposes.

text: Thomas raedam venalem proposuit.
translation: Tom has put his car up for sale.

text: Thomas domum venalem proposuit.
translation: Tom has put his house up for sale.

text: Puto Thoman item sentire.
translation: I think that Tom feels the same way.

text: Nomen Iudaeorum atque Iudaismi ab Iudaea derivatur, item regnum meridianum, ex quo populus religioque derivantur.
translation: The names of Jews and Judaism derive from Judah, the southern kingdom from which the people and religion derive.

text: Magister non est, sed medicus est.
translation: He is not a teacher but a doctor.

text: Is non est medicus, sed magister.
translation: He is not a doctor but a teacher.

text: Tu magister es, et haec nescis?
translation: You're a teacher and you don't know these things?

text: Magister noster dicit omnes Physica egere.
translation: Our teacher says that everybody needs Physics.

text: Magister parentes meos per telephonum adierunt.
translation: The teacher called my parents.

text: Medicus non est, magister est.
translation: He is not a doctor but a teacher.

text: Melius est tibi imaginem photographicam magistro dare.
translation: You'd better give the photograph to the teacher.

text: Meministine quid esset primo magistro tuo nomen?
translation: Do you still remember what your first teacher was called?

text: Quot magistri in tuo ludo sunt?
translation: How many teachers are there at your school?

text: Tu magistra es, et haec nescis?
translation: You're a teacher and you don't know these things?

text: Mater eius magistra linguae Anglicae est.
translation: His mother is an English teacher.

text: Dic mihi, quaeso, de tua magistra.
translation: Please tell me about your teacher.

text: Stellae parvae videntur. Eae autem magnae sunt.
translation: The stars seem small, but they are large.

text: Multae stellae maiores quam Sol noster sunt.
translation: There exist several stars which are larger than our Sun.

text: Multae sunt stellae sole nostro maiores.
translation: There are many stars larger than our sun.

text: Sunt multae stellae maiores nostro sole.
translation: There are many stars larger than our sun.

text: Pater Thomae eum de stellis docuit.
translation: Tom's father taught him about the stars.

text: Hodie nocte multas stellas videre possumus.
translation: We can see many stars tonight.

text: Terra stella non est, sed planeta est.
translation: The earth is not a star, but a planet.

text: Post Caesaris mortem stella crinita per septem dies fulsit.
translation: After the death of Caesar, a comet shone for seven days.

text: Magna stella aurea supra ianuam erat.
translation: There was a big gold star on the door.

text: Stella Saturni triginta annis cursum conficit.
translation: The planet Saturn completes its orbit within thirty years.

text: Tu es stella, quam contemplo.
translation: You are the star I contemplate.

text: Luna stella non est.
translation: The moon isn't a star.

text: Thōmās in vīculō ēducātus est.
translation: Tom was raised in a small village.

text: Thōmās in Austrāliā ēducātus est.
translation: He was brought up in Australia.

text: Thōmās ā Marīā ēducātus est.
translation: Tom was brought up by Mary.

text: Ab aviā ēducātus sum.
translation: I was brought up by my grandmother.

text: Thōmās Bostoniae ēducātus est.
translation: Tom was brought up in Boston.

text: In Austrāliā ēducātus sum.
translation: I was brought up in Australia.

text: At illi portantes frumenta in asinis suis profecti sunt.
translation: But they having loaded their asses with the corn went their way.

text: Potesne frumentum ex hordeo discernere?
translation: Can you tell wheat from barley?

text: Panis e frumento fit.
translation: Bread is made from wheat.

text: Et Ioseph erat princeps in terra Aegypti, atque ad eius nutum frumenta populis vendebantur.
translation: And Joseph was governor in the land of Egypt, and corn was sold by his direction to the people.

text: Det tibi Deus de rore cæli et de pinguedine terræ et abundantiam frumenti et vini.
translation: God give thee of the dew of heaven, and of the fatness of the earth, abundance of corn and wine.

text: Et, cum compelleret illum, suscepit et ait: Gradiamur simul, eroque socius itineris tui.
translation: He took it with much ado at his brother's earnest pressing him, and said: Let us go together, and I will accompany thee in thy journey.

text: Suscipe, quæso, benedictionem, quæ allata est tibi; quia Deus misertus est mihi, et habeo omnia.
translation: Take the blessing which I have brought thee, and which God hath given me, who gives all things.

text: Nunc igitur maledictus eris procul ab agro, qui aperuit os suum et suscepit sanguinem fratris tui de manu tua!
translation: Now therefore cursed shalt thou be upon the earth, which hath opened her mouth and received the blood of thy brother at thy hand.

text: Sacerdotes quoque, qui accedunt ad Dominum, sanctificentur, ne percutiat eos.
translation: The priests also that come to the Lord, let them be sanctified, lest he strike them.

text: Thomas sacerdos Christianus est.
translation: Tom is a Christian priest.

text: Nati sunt autem Ioseph filii duo, antequam veniret fames, quos ei peperit Aseneth filia Putiphare sacerdotis Heliopoleos.
translation: And before the famine came, Joseph had two sons born: whom Aseneth, the daughter of Putiphare, priest of Heliopolis, bore unto him.

text: Erant autem sacerdoti Madian septem filiæ, quæ venerunt ad hauriendam aquam; et impletis canalibus adaquare cupiebant greges patris sui.
translation: And the priest of Madian had seven daughters, who came to draw water: and when the troughs were filled, desired to water their father's flocks.

text: Moyses autem pascebat oves Iethro soceri sui sacerdotis Madian; cumque minasset gregem ultra desertum, venit ad montem Dei Horeb.
translation: Now Moses fed the sheep of Jethro, his father in law, the priest of Madian: and he drove the flock to the inner parts of the desert, and came to the mountain of God, Horeb.

text: Cui bonus est vicinus, felix illucet dies.
translation: Happy is he who has a good neighbor.

text: Vicini nostri coacti erant vendere domum suam.
translation: Our neighbours were forced to sell their house.

text: Avunculus meus est filius spiritalis vicini nostri.
translation: My uncle is our neighbor's godson.

text: Patruus meus est filius spiritalis vicini nostri.
translation: My uncle is our neighbor's godson.

text: Quamquam Thomas vicinus mihi est, vix tamen eum cognovi.
translation: Even though Tom is my neighbor, I don't know him very well.

text: Vicini dicunt Thoman uxorem verberare.
translation: The neighbors say that Tom beats his wife.

text: Incipias cave quod mox perfecisse negabis.
translation: It is better never to begin than never to make an end.

text: Cave ne quis te videat.
translation: Be careful that no one sees you.

text: Cave lupum in vestimentis ovium.
translation: Beware the wolf in sheep's clothing.

text: Cave! Solum umidum est.
translation: Be careful! The floor is wet.

text: Cavete! Solum umidum est.
translation: Be careful! The floor is wet.

text: Thomas Mariam cavere vult.
translation: Tom wants Mary to be careful.

text: Aliquem colorem tibi placet, licet tibi eligere.
translation: You can choose whichever color you like.

text: Urbs Novum Eboracum primum praefectum Musulmanum elegit.
translation: New York City has elected its first Muslim mayor.

text: Haec est vita quam elegi.
translation: This is the life that I chose.

text: Thomas primarius administer electus est.
translation: Tom was elected prime minister.

text: Ex calamis his elige unum.
translation: Choose any of these pens.

text: Ex his unum elige.
translation: Choose one from among these products.

text: Quot homines in familia tua sunt?
translation: How many people are there in your family?

text: In Australiam cum familia ire volo.
translation: I want to go to Australia with my family.

text: Thomas domi mansit apud familiam suam.
translation: Tom stayed at home with his family.

text: Maria etiam nunc apud familiam habitat.
translation: Mary is still living with her family.

text: Thomas etiam nunc apud familiam habitat.
translation: Tom is still living with his family.

text: Familia mea valde magna non est.
translation: My family is not very large.

text: Tam erat mihi molestum ut paene in oscitandum ducerer.
translation: It was so boring that I almost yawned.

text: Tom paene oblitus est secum ducere umbellam.
translation: Tom almost forgot to take an umbrella with him.

text: Paene omne genus musicae audire possum, atque id mihi saepe placet.
translation: I can listen to just about any genre and like it.

text: Paene cotidie pediludio ludo.
translation: I play football almost every day.

text: Miseret me paene eius.
translation: I almost feel sorry for him.

text: Paene te intellegere possum.
translation: I can almost understand you.

text: Thoman hoc facere animo praecipere non possum.
translation: I can't picture Tom doing that.

text: Fecit ergo Noe omnia, quæ præceperat illi Deus; sic fecit.
translation: And Noah did all things which God commanded him.

text: Quæ respondit: Quidquid præceperis, faciam.
translation: She answered: Whatsoever thou shalt command, I will do.

text: Feceruntque ita, ut præceperat Moyses, et non computruit, neque vermis inventus est in eo.
translation: And they did so as Moses had commanded, and it did not putrify, neither was there worm found in it.

text: Præcepit ergo pharao omni populo suo dicens: Quidquid masculini sexus natum fuerit, in flumen proicite; quidquid feminei, reservate.
translation: Pharaoh therefore charged all his people, saying: Whatsoever shall be born of the male sex, ye shall cast into the river: whatsoever of the female, ye shall save alive.

text: Sed omnes opes, quas tulit Deus patri nostro, nobis abstulit ac filiis nostris; unde omnia, quæ præcepit tibi Deus, fac.
translation: But God hath taken our father's riches, and delivered them to us, and to our children: wherefore, do all that God hath commanded thee.

text: Certo hic vir non sanus est satis.
translation: This man is definitely not in his right mind.

text: Sane quidem litteras Anglico sermone scribam.
translation: Of course I'll write the letter in English.

text: Quicumque aquam bibit, semper sanus est.
translation: A man who drinks water is always healthy.

text: Nonne sunt sani Thomas et Maria?
translation: Tom and Mary are healthy, aren't they?

text: "Vivunt adhuc parentes tui?" "Sane."
translation: "Are your parents still alive?" "Yes."

text: ''Sanun' es?'' ''Pol sanus si sim, non te medicum mihi expetam.''
translation: ''Are you alright?'' ''Heavens, if I were alright, I wouldn't seek you as my doctor.''

text: In principio anni MCMXCIV, Windows 3.1 uti coepimus.
translation: We started to use Windows 3.1 in the beginning of 1994.

text: In principio creavit Thomas Bostoniam et Australiam.
translation: In the beginning, Tom created Boston and Australia.

text: In principio creavit Didymus Bostoniam et Australiam.
translation: In the beginning, Tom created Boston and Australia.

text: In principio mensis Iulii Londinium profectus est.
translation: He left for London in the beginning of July.

text: In principio creavit Deus cælum et terram.
translation: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.

text: In principio creavit Deus caelum et terram.
translation: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.

text: Parentes Thomae filii sepulcrum aperiri iusserunt.
translation: Tom's parents ordered their son's tomb to be opened.

text: Filia Mariae matris sepulcrum aperiri iussit.
translation: Mary's daughter ordered her mother's tomb to be opened.

text: Num sepulcrum Papae unquam apertum est?
translation: Was the Pope’s tomb ever opened?

text: Alexander sepulcrum Cyri aperiri iussit.
translation: Alexander ordered the tomb of Cyrus to be opened.

text: Dedisti satis poenarum, etiamsi occidisses Romanum pontificem, aut si minxisses ad sepulchrum divi Petri.
translation: You have taken enough punishment, as if you had killed the Pope of Rome, or pissed on the sepulchre of St Peter.

text: Erexitque Iacob titulum super sepulcrum eius; hic est titulus monumenti Rachel usque in præsentem diem.
translation: And Jacob erected a pillar over her sepulchre: this is the pillar of Rachel's monument, to this day.

text: Nihil sine labore mortalibus datur.
translation: Nothing is given to mortals without effort.

text: Scīmus omnēs hominēs esse mortālēs.
translation: We know that all men are mortal.

text: Omnes homines mortales sunt. Socrates homo est. Ergo Socrates mortalis est.
translation: All men are mortal. Socrates is a man. Therefore, Socrates is mortal.

text: Sumusne mortales, an immortales?
translation: Are we mortal or immortal?

text: Nos omnes mortales sumus.
translation: We are all mortal.

text: Mille modis morimur mortales, nascimur uno. Sunt hominum morbi, mille, sed una salus.
translation: We mortals die in a thousand ways; we are born in only one. There are a thousand diseases of men, but only one source of health.

text: Hodie Thomas a Maria epistulam accepit.
translation: Tom got a letter from Mary today.

text: Scio a te epistulam legi.
translation: I know I read the letter to you.

text: Legistine epistulam quam Thomas scripsit?
translation: Did you read the letter that Tom wrote?

text: "Is heri epistulam scripsitne?" "Scripsit."
translation: "Did he write a letter yesterday?" "Yes, he did."

text: Num epistulam ab eo accepisti?
translation: Have you received a letter from him?

text: Post tres menses epistulam accepi.
translation: I received a letter three months later.

text: "Vidistine librum meum?" "Quem librum quæris?" "Ciceronis epistolas."
translation: "Have you seen my book?" "What book are you looking for?" "Cicero's letters."

text: Epistolas cremavi omnes, quas ad me scripsisti.
translation: I burned all the letters that you wrote to me.

text: Epistolas laceravi omnes, quas ad me scripsisti.
translation: I tore up all the letters that you wrote to me.

text: Volo te hanc epistolam Anglicam legere.
translation: I want you to read this English letter.

text: Epistula receptaculo purgamentorum dedita est.
translation: The letter was consigned to the wastepaper basket.

text: Thomas flens Mariae epistolam legit.
translation: Tom cried as he read Mary's letter.

text: Is mihi non amicus, sed inimicus est.
translation: He's not my friend, he's my enemy.

text: Thomas me inimicum suum esse putat.
translation: Tom thinks I am his enemy.

text: Nunquam habui inimicos nisi rei publicae.
translation: I have never had any enemies other than those of the state.

text: Non sum inimicus. Amicus sum.
translation: I'm not your enemy. I'm your friend.

text: Putabam Thoman inimicum tuum esse.
translation: I thought Tom was your enemy.

text: Thomas nimis multos inimicos habet.
translation: Tom has too many enemies.

text: Thomas Mariam interrogavit an ipsa Ioannem noverit.
translation: Tom asked Mary if she knew John.

text: Thomas Mariam interrogavit num hoc plus quam semel fecisset.
translation: Tom asked Mary if she had done it more than once.

text: Matrem interrogavi, num ientaculum paratum esset.
translation: I asked my mother if breakfast was ready.

text: Quos interrogans: “Numquid, ait, nostis Laban filium Nachor?” Dixerunt: “Novimus”.
translation: And he asked them, saying: Know you Laban, the son of Nachor? They said: We know him.

text: Interrogavi eum quid fecerit heri.
translation: I asked him about what he did yesterday.

text: Me interrogavit num id invenissem.
translation: He asked me if I had found it.

text: Thomas ex consuetudine caffeam sine saccharo sumit.
translation: Tom usually drinks coffee without sugar.

text: Polyphagia et polyposta, crede mihi, est res consuetudinis, non naturae.
translation: Eating and drinking a lot, is a matter of habit, not nature, believe me.

text: oculi amorem incipiunt, consuetudo perficit.
translation: The eyes begin love, custom perfects it.

text: Consuetudinis vis magna est.
translation: Great is the power of habit.

text: Consuetudinis magna vis est.
translation: Great is the power of habit.

text: Respondit Laban: Non est in loco nostro consuetudinis, ut minorem ante maiorem tradamus ad nuptias.
translation: Laban answered: It is not the custom in this place, to give the younger in marriage first.

text: Si quis conviva accessit, locus dabatur pro dignitate.
translation: If any guest came in, they were given a place according to their worth.

text: Tristia iura necis nulla medela fugat.
translation: No remedy chases away the sad laws of death.

text: Sic ait, et dicto citius tumida æquora placat, / collectasque fugat nubes solemque reducit.
translation: Thus he, / and, ere his speech was ended, smoothed the main, / and chased the clouds and brought the sun again.

text: Opinio finaliter determinatur per affectus, et non ab intellectu.
translation: Opinion is ultimately determined by feelings, and not by the intellect.

text: Amor et odium affectus contrarii sunt.
translation: Love and hate are opposite emotions.

text: Islamus vitam meam affecit.
translation: Islam influenced my life.

text: Amor sola realitas est, neque merus affectus. Est summa veritas quae in corde creationis latet.
translation: Love is the only reality, and it is not a mere sentiment. It is the ultimate truth that lies at the heart of creation.

text: Amo Deum, patrem caelestem, qui creavit me.
translation: I love God, the Heavenly Father, who created me.

text: Coelestis arcus in exiguo tempore evanescet.
translation: The rainbow will disappear in little time.

text: Mulier nupta sum et duo liberi sunt mihi.
translation: I am married and have two children.

text: Mulierem quae cum magistro nostro loquitur non novi.
translation: I don't know the woman who's talking to our teacher.

text: Maria una est ex mulieribus Bostoniae pulcherissimis.
translation: Mary is one of the prettiest women in Boston.

text: Aliquid ineffabile de te me fascinat, mulier.
translation: Something ineffable about you fascinates me, woman.

text: Mulierem cum magistro nostro loquentem non novi.
translation: I don't know the woman talking to our teacher.

text: Mundus melior mulieribus est mundus melior omnibus.
translation: A better world for women is a better world for everyone.

text: Tu es vera diva.
translation: You are a real fairy.

text: Tempus erat quo prima quies mortalibus ægris / incipit, et dono divum gratissima serpit.
translation: 'Twas now the time, when on tired mortals crept / first slumber, sweetest that celestials pour.

text: "Non tibi Tyndaridis facies invisa Lacænæ / culpatusve Paris, divum inclementia, divum, / has evertit opes sternitque a culmine Trojam."
translation: "Not oft-blamed Paris, nor the hateful charms / of Helen; Heaven, unpitying Heaven to-day / hath razed the Trojan towers and reft the Dardan sway."

text: Irruimus ferro, et divos ipsumque vocamus / in partem prædamque Jovem. Tum litore curvo / exstruimusque toros, dapibusque epulamur opimis.
translation: We, sword in hand, make onset, and invite / the gods and Jove himself the spoil to share, / and piling couches, banquet on the fare.

text: Hic Hecuba et natæ nequidquam altaria circum, / præcipites atra ceu tempestate columbæ, / condensæ et divum amplexæ simulacra sedebant.
translation: Here, with her hundred daughters, pale with dread, / poor Hecuba and all her female train, / as doves, that from the low'ring storm have fled, / and cower for shelter from the pelting rain, / crouch round the silent gods, and cling to them in vain.

text: Bostoniae te vivere velle apud Thoman arbitror.
translation: I suppose you want to live in Boston with Tom.

text: Mihi opus esse te iubere non arbitror.
translation: I don't think I need to tell you what to do.

text: Thoman et Mariam hic adfuturos non arbitror.
translation: I don't think Tom and Mary are going to be here.

text: Thoman arbitror se nescire ubi sit.
translation: I don't think Tom knows where he is.

text: Thomam non satis etiam fecisse arbitror.
translation: I think Tom hasn't yet done enough.

text: Quotiēns tē hīc cibum sūmpsisse ārbitrāris?
translation: How many times do you think you've eaten here?

text: Melius est librum primum legere et pelliculicam postea spectare
translation: Don't watch the movie first. Read the book.

text: Postea comperi verum eius nomen Thoman esse.
translation: Later, I found out his real name was Tom.

text: Postea ibimus Mundum, et spectabimus omnia.
translation: Afterwards we will go out into the world, and we will see all things.

text: Ehem, age, quid tum postea?
translation: Aha, go on, what happened next?

text: Quid vis facere postea?
translation: What do you want to do after this?

text: Numquam postea collocuti sumus.
translation: We never talked again after that.

text: Non ego te modo ante aedis vidi astare?
translation: Didn't I see you standing in front of the house just now?

text: Aedis fratris mei in hoc aedificio est.
translation: My brother's apartment is in this building.

text: Plurimum valet gallus in aedibus suis.
translation: A cock is bold on his own dunghill.

text: Thomas filium eius ex aedibus extrusit.
translation: Tom threw his son out of the house.

text: Filium eius ex aedibus extrusit.
translation: She threw her son out of the house.

text: Filium eius ex aedibus exturbavit.
translation: He threw his son out of the house.

text: Tibi fructus lavandi sunt antequam eos edis.
translation: You should wash the fruits before eating them.

text: Vicini nostri coacti erant vendere aedes suas.
translation: Our neighbours were forced to sell their house.

text: Vicini nostri cogebantur vendere aedes suas.
translation: Our neighbours were forced to sell their house.

text: Cur olera tua non edis?
translation: Why aren't you eating your vegetables?

text: Qualem paniculum fartum edis?
translation: What kind of sandwich are you eating?

text: Cur illud non edis?
translation: Why aren't you eating that?

text: Tres fabulas Gallicas in Anglicum sermonem converti.
translation: I've translated three French novels into English.

text: Narra mihi fabulam in una sententia.
translation: Tell me a story in one sentence.

text: Cum essem iuvenis, multas fabulas legi.
translation: When I was young, I read a lot of novels.

text: Cum essem iuvenis, multum fabularum legi.
translation: When I was young, I read a lot of novels.

text: Legistine fabulam quam Thomas scripsit?
translation: Have you read the novel that Tom wrote?

text: Quem scriptorem putas fabulae esse?
translation: Who do you think the author of this novel is?

text: Haec fabula etiam in Gallicum sermonem conversa est.
translation: This novel has also been translated into French.

text: Quid rides? Mutato nomine fabula de te narratur.
translation: What are you laughing at? With the name changed, the story is told about you.

text: Haec fabula in Gallicum sermonem conversa est.
translation: This novel has been translated into French.

text: Fabula eius in Iaponicum sermonem conversa est.
translation: His novel was translated into Japanese.

text: Quando haec fabula in lucem emissa est?
translation: When was this novel published?

text: Fabula in multos sermones conversa est.
translation: The novel has been translated into many languages.

text: Ego celerrime cucurri quantum potui.
translation: I ran as fast as I could.

text: Thomas linguam Gallicam celerrime didicit.
translation: Tom learned French incredibly fast.

text: Equus celerrime currere potest.
translation: A horse can run very fast.

text: Ille canis celerrime currit.
translation: That dog runs very fast.

text: Domina Kanda celerrime currit.
translation: Miss Kanda runs very fast.

text: In epistula, quam accepit Thomas, eum quam celerrime domum revenire debere scriptum erat.
translation: The letter Tom received said that he should return home as soon as possible.

text: Thomas me rogavit num bene quievissem.
translation: Tom asked me if I had slept well.

text: Cum Marcus venit, ego quiescebam.
translation: When Marcus arrived, I was sleeping.
