text: In Deo tantum quiescit anima mea, ab ipso venit salus mea.
translation: My soul rests only in God, my salvation comes from him.

text: Leaena sub umbra quievit.
translation: A lioness was resting in the shade.

text: Domi mansi ut quiescerem.
translation: I stayed home to rest.

text: Quotiēns in mēnse Thōmās illud facit?
translation: How many times a month does Tom do that?

text: Quotiēns in annō Thōmās illud facit?
translation: How many times a year does Tom do that?

text: Quotiēns in diē Thōmās illud facit?
translation: How many times a day does Tom do that?

text: Quotiēns in mēnse Thōmās hūc venit?
translation: How many times a month does Tom come here?

text: Quotiēns vōs hīc cibum sūmpsisse ārbitrāminī?
translation: How many times do you think you've eaten here?

text: Quotiēns in diē cibum sūmitis?
translation: How many times a day do you eat?

text: Scientia non habet inimicum nisi ignorantem.
translation: Knowledge has no enemy except an ignorant person.

text: Thomas rogavit num scientia mihi placeret.
translation: Tom asked if I liked science.

text: Scientia gentis humanae omni momento crescit.
translation: Humanity's knowledge grows with every moment.

text: Machinalis scientia theoriam in praxim adducit.
translation: Engineering puts theory into practice.

text: Scientia naturalis mihi non placet.
translation: I do not like science.

text: Sera sunt barba post vigesimum, scientia post trigesimum, divitiae post quadragesimum.
translation: Beards are late after twenty, knowledge after thirty, riches after forty.

text: Ille nihil dubitat qui nullam scientiam habet.
translation: He who knows nothing doubts nothing.

text: Et scientiae et mathematica mihi placent.
translation: I like both science and math.

text: Eva Adamo scientiae malum dedit.
translation: Eve gave Adam the apple of knowledge.

text: Illius quaestionis scientiam non habeo.
translation: I have no knowledge of that question.

text: Magistra scientiae biologicae Sonia vocatur.
translation: The biology teacher is called Sonia.

text: Et scientias et mathematicam amo.
translation: I like both science and math.

text: Thomas confessus est se fenestram fregisse.
translation: Tom confessed that he had broken the window.

text: Thomas se erravisse modo confessus est.
translation: Tom just admitted he made a mistake.

text: Thomas se id fecisse confessus est, quod facere non debuit.
translation: Tom admitted he did what he wasn't supposed to do.

text: Thomas confessus est se hoc fecisse.
translation: Tom admitted he did that.

text: Thomas se Mariam interfecisse confessus est.
translation: Tom admitted he murdered Mary.

text: Thomas se hoc fecisse confessus est.
translation: Tom admitted he's done that.

text: Miseret me huius qui eum non diligat.
translation: I feel sorry for whoever doesn't like him.

text: Thomas ait te a Maria diligi.
translation: Tom said that Mary likes you.

text: Qui me amat, meos diligit.
translation: The friends of my friends are also my friends.

text: Et feles et canes diligo.
translation: I love both cats and dogs.

text: Musae Sagittarium semper dilexerunt.
translation: The Muses have always loved Sagittarius.

text: Accentum germanicum tuum diligo.
translation: I love your German accent.

text: Latine verbum plerumque in fine sententiae est.
translation: In Latin, the verb is usually at the end of the sentence.

text: In principio plerumque simplex amor. Sed tunc satis implicata est.
translation: In the beginning, love is usually simple. But then it can get pretty complicated.

text: Plerumque umbellam prope ianuam posuit.
translation: Usually he put the umbrella near the door.

text: Post prandium plerumque paululum dormiunt.
translation: After lunch, they usually have a nap.

text: Quid facis plerumque post cenam?
translation: What do you usually do after dinner?

text: Thomas plerumque ocularibus solariis gerit.
translation: Tom almost always wears sunglasses.

text: Pleraque Alpium ab Italia breviora.
translation: The Alps are generally lower on the Italian side.

text: Pleraque sententiarum quae in Galiciano video scriptas esse mihi videntur Lusitanice.
translation: Most of the sentences I see in Galician seem to me to be written in Portuguese.

text: Pleraque liquefacta est nix.
translation: Most of the snow has melted already.

text: Ursi plerique omnivori sunt.
translation: Most bears are omnivores.

text: Plerique dextra manu utuntur.
translation: Most people are right-handed.

text: Steriles arbores sunt abies, alnus, betula, cupressus, fagus, fraximus, salix, tilia et cetera; sed pleraque umbriserae.
translation: Barren trees are the fir, elder, birch, cypress, beech, ivy, sallow, linden and so on, but most of them afford shade.

text: Puella ad ludum it, etiamsi dormire vult.
translation: The girl is going to school, even though she wants to sleep.

text: Thomas sine cervicali dormire non potest.
translation: Tom can't sleep without a pillow.

text: Nunc possum multum melius dormire.
translation: I can sleep a lot better now.

text: Vix dormiveram cum telephonum tinnivit.
translation: I had hardly fallen asleep when the telephone rang.

text: Relinque me solum ut dormiam.
translation: Leave me alone so I can get some sleep.

text: Thomas saepe fenestris apertis dormit.
translation: Tom usually sleeps with his windows open.

text: Descenderuntque volucres super cadavera, et abigebat eas Abram.
translation: And the fowls came down upon the carcasses, and Abram drove them away.

text: Parva volucris non ova magna parit.
translation: Small birds don't lay big eggs.

text: Volucris in caelo est.
translation: The bird is in the sky.

text: Volucres in silva canebant.
translation: Birds were singing in the woods.

text: Quid de ludo illo, quem Thomas creavit, putas?
translation: What do you think of the game that Tom created?

text: Homines moriuntur, sed ea, quae creant, permanent.
translation: People die, but the things they create endure.

text: Quod non potes imaginari, creare non potes.
translation: You can't create something you can't imagine.

text: Didymus anno MMVIII senator creatus est.
translation: Tom was elected to the Senate in 2008.

text: Principio creavit Deus caelum et terram.
translation: In the beginning God created Heaven and Earth.

text: Deus hominem ad suam imaginem creavit.
translation: God created man in his own image.

text: Canis fidelior est quam feles.
translation: A dog is more loyal than a cat.

text: Canis fidelior est quam cattus.
translation: A dog is more loyal than a cat.

text: Fidelior erat quam putari potui.
translation: He was more loyal than I had guessed.

text: Canis meus valde fidelis est.
translation: My dog is very faithful.

text: Canis fidelis est domino.
translation: The dog is faithful to its master.

text: Canis animal fidele est.
translation: The dog is a faithful animal.

text: Potesne mihi viam ad stationem curuum publicorum indicare?
translation: Could you show me the way to the bus stop?

text: E fimbria de texto indicatur.
translation: The half shows what the whole means.

text: Irania Americae Foederatae bellum indixit.
translation: Iran proclaimed war against the US.

text: Et indicavit ei quod frater esset patris eius et filius Rebeccæ.
translation: And he told her that he was her father's brother, and the son of Rebecca:

text: Sagitta viam Tokium indicat.
translation: The arrow indicates the way to Tokyo.

text: Magister menda discipuli indicavit.
translation: The teacher pointed out the pupil's mistakes.

text: Heri in ludum ire non potuit, hodie autem potest.
translation: Yesterday he couldn't go to school, but today he can.

text: Dic Thomae et Mariae hoc hodie eis faciendum esse.
translation: Tell Tom and Mary they have to do that today.

text: Quod hodie non est, cras erit.
translation: That which is not today, will be tomorrow.

text: Didymus et Maria hodie domi sunt.
translation: Tom and Mary are at home today.

text: Hodie Thomas in ludum non iit.
translation: Tom didn't walk to school this morning.

text: Hodie Thomas ad ludum non venit.
translation: Tom didn't come to school today.

text: Lex disciplina est quae mihi non placet.
translation: Law is a subject I don't like.

text: Mathematica est bona disciplina.
translation: Mathematics is a good subject.

text: Audi, fili mi, disciplinam patris tui, et ne dimittas legem matris tuæ.
translation: My son, hear the instruction of thy father, and forsake not the law of thy mother.

text: Dixi Thomae me putare fore ut id facere posset.
translation: I told Tom that I thought he could do that.

text: Spero fore ut Thomas quoque veniat.
translation: I hope Tom comes as well.

text: Spērāmus fore ut pellicula tibi placeat.
translation: We hope you enjoy the movie.

text: Spērāmus fore ut pellicula vōbīs placeat.
translation: We hope you enjoy the movie.

text: Spero fore ut Thomas tibi placeat.
translation: I hope you like Tom.

text: Spero fore ut Thomas vobis placeat.
translation: I hope you like Tom.

text: Negabit, noli igitur eum advertere.
translation: He will deny it, so don't pay him any attention.

text: Didymus in forica erat, cum Maria advenit.
translation: Tom was in the bath when Mary arrived.

text: Certiorem fac patrem tuum de adventu meo.
translation: Inform your father of my arrival.

text: Eum certiorem feci de eius adventu.
translation: I informed him of her arrival.

text: Eam certiorem feci de adventu meo.
translation: I informed her of my arrival.

text: Eam de eius adventu certiorem feci.
translation: I informed her of his arrival.

text: Exoptatus ad Tatoebam advenisti, mi amice.
translation: Welcome to Tatoeba, my friend.

text: Tom et Maria pensum suum iuctim fecerunt.
translation: Tom and Mary did their homework together.

text: Thomas pensus est ob id quod fecit.
translation: Tom was paid thirty dollars for what he did.

text: Quomodo pensum scholare facis dum musicam audis?
translation: How do you do the homework listening to music?

text: Parvus pendetur fur, magnus abire videtur.
translation: Petty thieves are hanged, the great ones go free.

text: Pensum perfecerit suum crastino die.
translation: He will have done his homework by tomorrow.

text: Post scholam pensum scholare facio.
translation: I do my homework after school.

text: Ita fessus sum, ut studere non possim.
translation: I am so tired that I can't study.

text: Ita fessi sunt, ut studere non possint.
translation: They are so tired that they cannot study.

text: Ita fessae sunt, ut studere non possint.
translation: They are so tired that they can't study.

text: Ita fessa sum, ut studere non possim.
translation: I'm so tired that I can't study.

text: Frater meus studet quia medicus esse vult.
translation: My brother studies to become a doctor.

text: Thomas Albanus est qui in Australia studet.
translation: Tom is an Albanian studying in Australia.

text: Feles arbores ascendere possunt, sed canes non possunt.
translation: Cats can climb trees, but dogs can't.

text: Thomas nesciebat in quem raedam ascendere.
translation: Tom didn't know which bus to take.

text: O cochleola, pedetemptim ascende, montem Fujium.
translation: Snail, slowly, slowly, climb Fuji mountain!

text: Didymus et Maria raedam ascenderunt.
translation: Tom and Mary got into their car.

text: Et ascendit ab eo Deus.
translation: And he departed from him.

text: Dixitque ei pharao: Ascende et sepeli patrem tuum, sicut adiuratus es.
translation: And Pharaoh said to him: Go up and bury thy father according as he made thee swear.

text: Custodes Thomam velut vulgaris esset scelestus agebant.
translation: The police treated Tom like a common criminal.

text: Dic Thomae Mariam forte volenti nobis coituram esse.
translation: You should tell Tom that Mary will very likely be there.

text: Non minus fortis sum quam tu.
translation: I'm not a man less stronger than you.

text: Forte Didymo hoc facendum non est.
translation: It's likely that Tom won't have to do that.

text: Amor tuus minus fortis meo est.
translation: Your love is less strong than mine.

text: Accepi pecuniam a patre hodie, si forte tibi est opus.
translation: I got money from my father today if you happen to need any.

text: Puella tantum erat, sed fortis.
translation: She was a child, but she was brave.

text: E probatione feliciter evadere poteram.
translation: I was able to pass the test.

text: Beatitudo natorum est nostra felicitas.
translation: Our children's happiness is our happiness.

text: Cometes Halleyanus anno MMLXI revertetur.
translation: Halley's Comet will come back in 2061.

text: Citius venit malum quam revertitur.
translation: Evil comes faster than it recedes.

text: Laurentius ad sanitatem reversus est.
translation: Lorenzo came back to his senses.

text: Avertitque se parumper et flevit; et reversus locutus est ad eos.
translation: And he turned himself away a little while, and wept: and returning, he spoke to them.

text: Oritur sol et occidit, et ad locum suum revertitur; ibique renascitur.
translation: The sun also rises, and the sun goes down, and hurries to its place where it rises.

text: Paucis diebus domum revertetur.
translation: He will come home in a few days.

text: Istud non edicas; scio quid opineris.
translation: You do not have to say it; I know what you think.

text: Cur contra meum edictum fecisti?
translation: Why did you disobey my order?

text: Sociis tunc arma capessant / edico, et dira bellum cum gente gerendum.
translation: To arms I call my comrades, and defy / the loathsome brood to battle.

text: Herculem igitur corripuit et in vincula coniecit. Tum nuntios dimisit et diem sacrificio edixit.
translation: He arrested Hercules and threw him in prison. He then fixed the day of the sacrifice and had the news spread.

text: Mea tua sunt; tua quoque tua sunt.
translation: What's mine is yours, and what's yours is yours.

text: Mea mea sunt; tua quoque mea sunt.
translation: What's mine is mine, and what's yours is mine.

text: Illa adversaria non Thomae, sed mea sunt.
translation: That isn't Tom's notebook. It's mine.

text: Raeda tua carior quam mea est.
translation: Your car is more expensive than mine.

text: Terra mea procul ab Iaponia est.
translation: My country is far away from Japan.

text: Raeda tua carior est quam mea.
translation: Your car is more expensive than mine.

text: Puto te hoc valde amaturum esse.
translation: I think you're really going to like it.

text: Glossarium hoc tibi valde utile erit.
translation: This dictionary will be of great help to you.

text: Haec potio Sinensis valde bona est.
translation: This is a very good tea.

text: Haec domus valde magna non est.
translation: This house is not very large.

text: Illa exedra valde magna non est.
translation: That room is not very large.

text: Eheu, potio Arabica valde fervens est!
translation: Ow, the coffee is very hot!

text: Domi sum quia in ludum non veni.
translation: I'm home because I didn't go to school.

text: Veni et vide me semel aliquandiu.
translation: Come and see me once in a while.

text: Didymus Bostoniam venit ad Mariam invisendam.
translation: Tom came to Boston to visit Mary.

text: Venit, vidit — et nil dixit.
translation: He came, he saw - and didn't say anything.

text: AD LONDONIUM VENIVIT ANTE ANNO DUO
translation: He went to London two years ago.

text: Huc veni ut cum Thoma loquerer.
translation: I came here to talk to Tom.

text: Ego et Thomas etiam nunc in Australia habitamus.
translation: Tom and I still live in Australia.

text: Thomas etiam nunc in Park Street habitat.
translation: Tom is still living on Park Street.

text: Ego et Thomas etiam nunc Bostoniae habitamus.
translation: Tom and I still live in Boston.

text: Thomas et Maria etiam nunc Bostoniae habitant.
translation: Tom and Mary still live in Boston.

text: Thomas non amplius in Park Street habitat.
translation: Tom doesn't live on Park Street anymore.

text: Nemo ex meis condiscipulis hic viciniae habitat.
translation: None of my classmates live near here.

text: Videns Brutum Cæsar dixit: Tu quoque, Brute, fili mi!
translation: Seeing Brutus, Caesar said, "You also, Brutus, my son!"

text: Filia sua ab ea rapta est.
translation: Her child was snatched away from her.

text: Duas filias et unum filium habemus.
translation: We have two daughters and one son.

text: Thomas filium habet, qui medicus est.
translation: Tom has a son who's a doctor.

text: Thomas filium volebat in urbe habitare.
translation: Tom wanted his son to live in the city.

text: Id posset facere etiam filia mea.
translation: Even my daughter could do that.

text: Emas, non quod opus est, sed quod necesse est.
translation: Buy not what you need, but what you can't help buying.

text: Librum emi, et is regulam emit.
translation: I bought a book and he a ruler.

text: Cur hic emis? Omnia cara sunt.
translation: Why are you doing shopping here? Everything is expensive.

text: Cur hic emitis? Omnia cara sunt.
translation: Why are you doing shopping here? Everything is expensive.

text: Idem instrumentum photographicum emi, quod habes.
translation: I have bought the same camera as you have.

text: Legistine librum, quem Thomas tibi emit?
translation: Have you read the book Tom bought for you?

text: Didymus et Mariam et Ioannem e raeda descendentes vidit.
translation: Tom saw both Mary and John getting out of their cars.

text: Domum magnam et duas raedas habet.
translation: She has a big house and two cars.

text: "Quae raeda est tua?" "Ford est."
translation: "What make is your car?" "It is a Ford."

text: Quot sunt raedae in America Foederata?
translation: How many cars are there in the United States?

text: Raeda tua post hanc argentariam est.
translation: Your car is behind this bank.

text: Didymus raedam gubernare non potest.
translation: Tom is not able to drive a car.

text: Natare potes, sed ego non possum.
translation: You can swim, but I can't swim.

text: Proximo mense sedecim annos nata ero.
translation: I'll be sixteen years old next month.

text: Thomas potest natare melius quam Maria.
translation: Tom can swim better than Mary.

text: Quot annos sororcula tua nata est?
translation: How old is your little sister?

text: Dic mihi, quot annos nata es?
translation: Tell me, how old are you?

text: Mense Septembri sedecim annos nata ero.
translation: I'll be sixteen in September.

text: Thomas et Maria domus suas incenderunt.
translation: Tom and Mary set fire to their houses.

text: Thomas et Maria domum suam incenderunt.
translation: Tom and Mary set fire to their house.

text: Cum exore de suis liberis litigabat.
translation: He quarreled with his wife about their children.

text: Cum exore de suis liberis litigavit.
translation: He quarreled with his wife about their children.

text: Narravitne tibi Thomas de parentibus suis?
translation: Did Tom tell you about his parents?

text: Sues intellegentiores sunt quam canes felesque.
translation: Pigs are smarter than dogs and cats.

text: Si verum dicerem medico, accuratior diagnosis fuisset.
translation: If I'd told the doctor the truth, then the diagnosis would've been more accurate.

text: Nunc scīmus hoc vērum nōn esse.
translation: Today, we know that this isn't true.

text: Vera eius proposita nobis incognita sunt.
translation: His true intentions are unknown to us.

text: Thomas re vera optimus pater est.
translation: Tom is actually a really good father.

text: Id quod dicit verum non est.
translation: What he says is not true.

text: Censeo quod Thomas dixit verum esse.
translation: I think that what Tom told you is the truth.

text: Nón potuit pictor réctius déscríbere eius fórmam.
translation: A painter could not better describe his likeness.

text: Quod non potes imaginari, exsequi non potes.
translation: You can’t do it unless you can imagine it.

text: Thomas ea quae dicebantur audire non potuit.
translation: Tom couldn't hear what was being said.

text: Sine dictionario bono, nihil facere potes.
translation: Without a good dictionary, you can't do anything.

text: Abeo, sed sine me operari potes.
translation: I am leaving, but you can continue working without me.

text: Toki Pona in uno vel altero die discere non potes.
translation: You can't learn Toki Pona in a day or two.

text: Nonne tu es qui mihi hoc dixisti?
translation: You're the one who told me that, aren't you?

text: Nonne quoque mense Thomas Bostoniam it?
translation: Doesn't Tom go to Boston every month?

text: Nōnne mē id factūrum esse sciēbās?
translation: You knew I'd do that, didn't you?

text: Nonne tibi est quicum loqui possis?
translation: You have someone you can talk to, don't you?

text: Nonne fuisti praeterito anno in Australia?
translation: Weren't you in Australia last year?

text: Nonne amicus tuus in urbe est?
translation: Isn't your friend in town?

text: Qui ludus hiemalis tibi est praeferitus omnium?
translation: What's your favorite winter sport?

text: Unus pro omnibus, omnes pro uno.
translation: One for all, all for one.

text: Sunt hic libri multi, satis omnibus.
translation: There are a lot of books here, enough for everyone.

text: Peniludium est omnium ludorum popularissimus.
translation: Soccer is the most popular of all sports.

text: Procerissimus est ex omnibus pueris.
translation: He is the tallest of all boys.

text: Belgae omnium Gallorum fortissimi fuerunt.
translation: The Belgians were the strongest of all the Gauls.

text: Multae blattae in culina sunt.
translation: There are many cockroaches in the kitchen.

text: Thomas multis modis me adiuvit.
translation: Tom has helped me in many ways.

text: Multae linguae sunt in mundo.
translation: There are many languages in the world.

text: De multis pulchribus rebus cogito.
translation: I imagine a lot of beautiful things.

text: In Graecia multae insulae sunt.
translation: There are many islands in Greece.

text: Multae urbs bombis deletae sunt.
translation: Many cities were destroyed by bombs.

text: Omnes sciunt Thoman Gallice bene loqui.
translation: Everyone knows that Tom's French is good.

text: Didymus Gallice melius loquitur, quam putas.
translation: Tom can speak French better than you think he does.

text: Didymus cum Maria Gallice locutus est.
translation: Tom spoke with Mary in French.

text: Gallice et loqui et scribere potest.
translation: He both speaks and writes French.

text: Huc veni ut linguam Gallicam disceret.
translation: I came here to study French.

text: Marīa amīcōs suōs linguam Gallicam docuit.
translation: Mary taught French to her friends.

text: Proximō annō Thōmās Bostoniae opus faciet.
translation: Tom will work in Boston next year.

text: Proximo anno hunc librum legere poteris.
translation: You will be able to read this book next year.

text: Ludus noster anno MCMXC conditus est.
translation: Our school was founded in 1990.

text: Hic ludus anno MCMLXX conditus est.
translation: This school was founded in 1970.

text: Proximo anno septemdecim annos natus ero.
translation: I'll be seventeen next year.

text: Et Didymus et Maria eiusdem scholae erant.
translation: Tom and Mary both went to the same school.

text: Ego et Thomas eandem scholam frequentamus.
translation: Tom and I go to the same school.

text: Thomas et Maria eandem scholam frequentant.
translation: Tom and Mary go to the same school.

text: Tatoeba enim mihi schola linguarum est.
translation: I think of Tatoeba as a language school.

text: Solis diebus ad scholam non eo.
translation: I don't go to school on Sunday.

text: Cur heri ad scholam non venisti?
translation: Why didn't you go to school yesterday?

text: Nemo amicorum meorum potionem Arabicam bibit.
translation: None of my friends drink coffee.

text: Sublustres radii solis super palpebris meis, tinctura languida cubiculum colorat.
translation: Dim sunbeams on my eyelids, a faint tinge dyes the room.

text: Telehorasis in cubiculo meo est.
translation: There is a television in my room.

text: Horologium tuum carius est meo.
translation: Your watch is more expensive than mine.

text: Horologium eius carius est meo.
translation: His clock is more expensive than mine.

text: Unum ex fratribus meis quaero.
translation: I'm looking for one of my brothers.

text: Anglice multos annos bene locutus est.
translation: He has spoken English well for many years.

text: Soror tua Anglice loqui non potest.
translation: Your sister can not speak English.

text: Lingua Anglica etiam in Sinis discitur.
translation: English is studied in China, too.

text: Lingua Iaponica difficilior est quam Anglica.
translation: Japanese is harder than English.

text: Estne lingua Anglica difficilior quam Iaponica?
translation: Is English harder than Japanese?

text: Ellen linguam Anglicam loqui non potest.
translation: Ellen does not speak English.

text: Antequam opus facit, potionem Arabicam bibit.
translation: He drinks coffee before work.

text: Puer et vir aquam bibunt.
translation: The boy and the man are drinking water.

text: Aqua oceani bibi non potest.
translation: The water of the ocean is undrinkable.

text: Thomas solus in culina bibebat.
translation: Tom was in the kitchen drinking alone.

text: Thomas ex aquae lagena bibebat.
translation: Tom was drinking from a water bottle.

text: Quotiēns in diē aquam bibis?
translation: How many times a day do you drink water?

text: Didymus Mariae librum de Australia dedit.
translation: Tom gave Mary a book about Australia.

text: Avunculus meus hoc horologium mihi dedit.
translation: My uncle gave me this watch.

text: Thomas Mariae dedit omnia quae volebat.
translation: Tom gave Mary everything she wanted.

text: Frater mihi hoc utendum dedit.
translation: My brother gave it to me to use.

text: Mihi librum dono pater dedit.
translation: My father gave me the book as a gift.

text: Mihi computatorium dono pater dedit.
translation: My father gave me a computer as a gift.

text: Non est mala paenula, mihi placet.
translation: The coat is not bad, I like it.

text: Musae mihi magis quam mala placent.
translation: I like bananas more than apples.

text: Ego potionem Arabicam quam Sinensem malo.
translation: Me, I prefer coffee to tea.

text: Bona vis an mala primo dici?
translation: Do you want the good news or the bad news first?

text: Raedas Anglicas quam externas malo.
translation: I prefer English cars to foreign ones.

text: Thomas terna mala pueris dedit.
translation: Tom has given each child three apples.

text: Velisne potionem Sinensem an potionem Arabicam?
translation: Would you like some tea or coffee?

text: Haec potio Sinensis valde fervens est.
translation: This tea is very hot.

text: Potionem Sinensem cum citreo velim, quaeso.
translation: A tea with lemon, please.

text: Visne me potionem Arabicam parare?
translation: Do you want me to make coffee?

text: Didymus poculum potionis Sinensis parat.
translation: Tom is making a cup of tea.

text: Potionem Arabicam libenter non bibo.
translation: I don't like to drink coffee.

text: Thomas mihi dicit te esse adiutorem suum.
translation: Tom tells me you're his assistant.

text: Thomas corpum suum cremari non vult.
translation: Tom doesn't want to be cremated.

text: Thomas ubi esset autocinetum suum scivit.
translation: Tom knew where his car was.

text: Scitne filium suum profectum esse?
translation: Does he know that his son has gone?

text: Thomas canem suum esse dixit.
translation: Tom said that that dog was his.

text: Mater maesta filium suum sepelivit.
translation: The mother sorrowfully buried her son.

text: Quot feles sunt in hoc domo?
translation: How many cats are there in this house?

text: Canes mihi magis quam feles placent.
translation: I like dogs more than cats.

text: Et feles et canes mihi placent.
translation: I like both cats and dogs.

text: Didymus et Maria duas feles habent.
translation: Tom and Mary have two cats.

text: Didymo et Mariae duae feles sunt.
translation: Tom and Mary have two cats.

text: Et canes et feles mihi placent.
translation: I like both dogs and cats.

text: Robertus multos libros in cubiculo habet.
translation: Bob has a lot of books in his room.

text: Maria nunc in cubiculo suo discit.
translation: Mary is now studying in her room.

text: Audivi eam canentem in cubiculo eius.
translation: I heard her singing in her room.

text: Pater meus in cubiculo suo est.
translation: My father is in his room.

text: Sami solus in cubiculo suo erat.
translation: Sami was alone in his room.

text: Telehorasim in cubiculo suo aspicit.
translation: He is watching TV in his room.

text: Licetne mihi domum Thomae ire ut ludam?
translation: Is it OK if I go over to Tom's house to play?

text: Licetne mihi domum Thomae ire ut ludamus?
translation: Is it OK if I go over to Tom's house to play?

text: Quis ludo follis transvolantis ludere vult?
translation: Who wants to play volleyball?

text: Velisne teniludio Solis diebus ludere?
translation: Would you like to play tennis on Sundays?

text: Pueri in hortis publicis ludebant.
translation: The children were playing in the park.

text: In hortis publicis illis ludebam.
translation: I used to play in that park.

text: Heri Didymus et Maria Bostoniam volaverunt.
translation: Tom and Mary flew to Boston yesterday.

text: Cūr herī in lūdum nōn vēnistī?
translation: Why didn't you go to school today?

text: Cur heri ad scholam non venistis?
translation: Why didn't you go to school yesterday?

text: Heri vesperi cum illis locutus sum.
translation: I spoke to them last night.

text: Heri vesperi cum eo locutus sum.
translation: I spoke to him last night.

text: Heri vesperi cum ea locutus sum.
translation: I spoke to her last night.

text: Eccum cuius liberi tam boni sunt.
translation: That's the man whose kids are so nice.

text: Ego quoque bona artifex esse volo.
translation: I want to be a good artist, too.

text: Didymus et Ioannes amici boni sunt.
translation: Tom and John are good friends.

text: Didymus et Maria amici boni sunt.
translation: Tom and Mary are good friends.

text: Bona artifex quoque esse volo.
translation: I want to be a good artist, too.

text: Boni homines in mundo sunt.
translation: There are good people in the world.

text: In suo municipio quisque plurimum potest.
translation: A cock is bold on his dunghill.

text: Ego te plus amo quam Maria.
translation: I love you more than Mary does.

text: Marcus habet plus pecuniae quam tu.
translation: Mark has more money than you.

text: Marcus plus pecuniae habet quam tu.
translation: Mark has more money than you.

text: Thomas plus pecuniae habet quam Maria.
translation: Tom has more money than Mary.

text: Lingua illa plus iucunda esset si tot limitationes non haberet.
translation: That language would be more interesting if it didn't have so many limitations.

text: Romani victis populis inter alia linguam suam inculcaverunt.
translation: The Romans forced onto the people they defeated, among other things, their language.

text: Fessus ego eram, sic quoque omnes alii.
translation: I was tired and so was everybody else.

text: Bonum est tu ipsa esse. Quis alia esse potes?
translation: It is good to be yourself. Who else could you be?

text: Ferunt vulpem callidiorem esse quam alia animalia.
translation: People say that the fox is more cunning than other animals.

text: Si alios suspectemus, nos alii tantumdem suspectent.
translation: If we suspect others, others will suspect us just as much.

text: Elephantus maior est quam alia animalia.
translation: The elephant is bigger than all the other animals.

text: Quis ludus popularissimus in America est?
translation: What is the most popular sport in America?

text: Thomas ludos in capsulam reponebat suos.
translation: Tom put his toys back in the box.

text: Hodie in ludum ire non possum.
translation: I can't go to school today.

text: Thomae et Maria placet ludus suus.
translation: Tom and Mary like their school.

text: Thomas linguam Gallicam in ludo didicit.
translation: Tom learned French in school.

text: Ludum cum sorore mea ludo.
translation: I am playing a game with my sister.

text: Proximo mense sedecim annos natus ero.
translation: I'll be sixteen years old next month.

text: Mense Februario septemdecim annos natus erit.
translation: He'll be seventeen in February.

text: Mense Septembri sedecim annos natus ero.
translation: I'll be sixteen in September.

text: Mensibus aestatis, hortus Didymo mane irrigandus est ad plantas conservandas.
translation: In the summer months Tom has to water his garden early in the morning to keep the plants alive.

text: Amicum ad duos menses videbo.
translation: I will see my friend for two months.

text: Matri semel in mense scribo.
translation: I write to my mother once a month.

text: Didymus dicit se non multa de Bostonia novisse.
translation: Tom says he doesn't know much about Boston.

text: Pater amicus meus est, quia multa paegnia mihi dat.
translation: My father is my friend because he gives me a lot of toys.

text: Sunt multa verba quae non intellego.
translation: There are many words that I don't understand.

text: Multa de Thoma a Maria didici.
translation: I learned a lot about Tom from Mary.

text: Filia eius multa carmina recitare potest.
translation: Her daughter can recite many poems.

text: Thomas multa de Indonesia non scit.
translation: Tom doesn't know much about Indonesia.

text: Quid Thomas se cras facturum esse dixit?
translation: What did Tom say he was going to do tomorrow?

text: Thomas Mariae dixit sese id cras facturum.
translation: Tom said that Mary was going to do that tomorrow.

text: Frater meus cras domi non erit.
translation: My brother won't be at home tomorrow.

text: Licetne mihi cras ad cinemateum ire?
translation: Can I go to the movies tomorrow?

text: Etiam ego cras hic non ero.
translation: I won't be here tomorrow, either.

text: Thomas dixit cras dies lunae esse.
translation: Tom said tomorrow is Monday.

text: Hic est liber de quo tibi locutus sum.
translation: This is the book I told you about.

text: Cum Thoma de illo non locutus sum.
translation: I didn't talk to Tom about that.

text: Consolatusque est eos et blande ac leniter est locutus.
translation: And he comforted them, and spoke gently and mildly.

text: Qui dixerunt: Fac ut locutus es.
translation: And they said: Do as thou hast spoken.

text: Sami paulum de hoc locutus est.
translation: Sami talked a little bit about this.

text: Hodie mane cum illis locutus sum.
translation: I spoke to them this morning.

text: Canes vident in albo et nigro.
translation: Dogs see in black and white.

text: Quis tē tībiīs canere docuit?
translation: Who taught you how to play the flute?

text: Quis vōs tībiīs canere docuit?
translation: Who taught you how to play the flute?

text: Feles et canes Thoman timent.
translation: Cats and dogs are afraid of Tom.

text: Pauci canes in urbe sunt.
translation: There are few dogs in the city.

text: Negat sē bene canere posse.
translation: He says that he can't sing well.

text: Cur hunc librum emere vis?
translation: Why do you want to buy this book?

text: Magnum armarium frigidarium emere volo.
translation: I want to buy a large sized refrigerator.

text: Didymus domum Bostoniae emere vult.
translation: Tom wants to buy a house in Boston.

text: Cur hunc librum emere vultis?
translation: Why do you want to buy this book?

text: Ubi possum ampullam aquae emere?
translation: Where can I buy a bottle of water?

text: Novum instrumentum photographicum emere volo.
translation: I want to buy a new camera.

text: Sami linguam Arabicam in Cairo didicit.
translation: Sami learned Arabic in Cairo.

text: Duo pocula potionis Arabicae bibi.
translation: I drank two cups of coffee.

text: Eheu, potio Arabica ferventissima est!
translation: Ow, the coffee is very hot!

text: Thomas potionem Arabicam Mariae paravit.
translation: Tom made some tea for Mary.

text: Sciō tē pōtiōnem Arabicam amāre.
translation: I know that you like coffee.

text: Dominus Smith potionem Arabicam bibit.
translation: Mr Smith is drinking coffee.

text: Jim advocatus non est, sed medicus est.
translation: Jim is not a lawyer but a doctor.

text: Visne me medicum per telephonum adire?
translation: Do you want me to call a doctor?

text: Jim advocatus non est. Medicus est.
translation: Jim isn't a lawyer, but a doctor.

text: Jim non advocatus sed medicus est.
translation: Jim isn't a lawyer, but a doctor.

text: Medicum vocare necesse non est.
translation: There's no need to call a doctor.

text: Sit medicus senex, tonsor iuvenis.
translation: Let the doctor be old, and the barber young.

text: Multi homines in hortis publicis sunt.
translation: There are many people in the park.

text: Ad hortos publicos ivimus ut luderemus.
translation: We went to the park to play.

text: Multi pueri in hortis publicis sunt.
translation: There are many children in the park.

text: Hortus circum domum meam pulcher est.
translation: The garden around my house is beautiful.

text: Domus eius prope hortos publicos est.
translation: Her house is near the park.

text: Quam magni sunt hi horti publici?
translation: How big is this park?

text: Discipulus meus erat. Nunc filios meos docet.
translation: He was my student. Now he teaches my children.

text: Et Didymus et Maria discipuli boni sunt.
translation: Tom and Mary are both good students.

text: Magister non est, sed discipulus est.
translation: He is not a teacher but a student.

text: Mihi sunt pauciores discipuli quam Petro.
translation: I have fewer students than Pedro does.

text: Quot discipulī in lūdō tuō sunt?
translation: How many students are in the school?

text: Et Didymus et Maria discipuli sunt.
translation: Tom and Mary are both students.

text: Pulchra gemma ornamenti est in arca rubra.
translation: The beautiful piece of jewelry is in the red box.

text: Malum, quod Ioanni dedi, rubrum est.
translation: The apple I gave John is red.

text: Autocinetum, quod Thomas emit, rubrum est.
translation: The car Tom bought is red.

text: Puella magnum petasum rubrum habēbat.
translation: The girl had a big red hat.

text: Tegmentum meae domi ruber est.
translation: The roof of my house is red.

text: Thomas etiam autocinetum rubrum habet.
translation: Tom has a red car as well.

text: Thomas et Maria possunt facere quicquid voluerint.
translation: Tom and Mary can do what they like.

text: Et Thōmās et Marīa id facere volēbant.
translation: Tom and Mary both wanted to do that.

text: Tantum dicere volebam me tibi non credere.
translation: I just wanted to say I don't believe you.

text: Salas et Skura neque advocati neque medici esse voluerunt.
translation: Salas and Skura didn't want to be lawyers or doctors.

text: Thomas Mariam ad saltationem ducere volebat.
translation: Tom wanted to take Mary to the dance.

text: Hoc ipsum est quod emere volui.
translation: That is exactly what I wanted to buy.

text: Multi flores in hoc horto sunt.
translation: There are a lot of flowers in this garden.

text: Quando rosae horti tui florebunt?
translation: When will the roses in your garden bloom?

text: Suntne multi flores in horto?
translation: Are there many flowers in the garden?

text: Venduntne flores in hac taberna?
translation: Do they sell flowers at this store?

text: Flores in horto pulchri sunt.
translation: The flowers in the garden are beautiful.

text: Pulchros flores in horto habemus.
translation: We have beautiful flowers in the garden.

text: Thomas cum matre per telephonum loquitur.
translation: Tom is talking on the phone with his mother.

text: Nunc cum eo per telephonum loquor.
translation: I'm on the phone with him now.

text: Visne me Thoman per telephonum adire?
translation: Do you want me to call Tom?

text: Visne nos te per telephonum adire?
translation: Do you want us to call you?

text: Visne me eos per telephonum adire?
translation: Do you want me to call them?

text: Visne me eas per telephonum adire?
translation: Do you want me to call them?

text: Thomas mihi dixit se in Australia peregrinatum esse.
translation: Tom told me he visited Australia.

text: Esne ex Austria an Australia oriundus?
translation: Do you come from Austria or Australia?

text: Esne ex Austria an Australia oriunda?
translation: Do you come from Austria or Australia?

text: Frater meus nunc in Australia est.
translation: My brother is now in Australia.

text: Habitatne Thomas etiam nunc in Australia?
translation: Is Tom still living in Australia?

text: Scio Thoman in Australia non esse.
translation: I know Tom isn't in Australia.

text: Non possum credere Thomam Mariamque mortuos esse.
translation: I can't believe Tom and Mary are dead.

text: Si Latinitas mortua est, quomodo ea loquor?
translation: If Latin is dead, how do I speak it?

text: Haec arbor mortua est atque secanda.
translation: This tree is dead and should be cut down.

text: Pater mihi et mater mortui sunt.
translation: My father and mother are dead.

text: Decem annos tantum natus eram cum mater mea mortua est.
translation: I was only ten years old when my mother died.

text: De mortuis nil nisi bene.
translation: Say nothing but good things about the dead.

text: Neminem rogavi umquam ut me adiuvaret nisi te.
translation: You're the only person I've ever asked to help me.

text: Thomas et Maria multis modis nos adiuverunt.
translation: Tom and Mary helped us in many ways.

text: Non dubito quin Thomas me adiuturus sit.
translation: I don't doubt Tom will help me.

text: Thomas nos adiuvare non iam vult.
translation: Tom isn't willing to help us anymore.

text: Nonne te putas Thoman adiuvare debere?
translation: Don't you think you should help Tom?

text: Me paenitet, te adiuvare non possum.
translation: I'm sorry, I can't help you.

text: Tom minus pecuniae habet quam frater eius.
translation: Tom has less money than his brother does.

text: Raeda Ford minus constat quam Mercedes Benz.
translation: A Ford car costs less than a Mercedes Benz.

text: « Intellēxistī? » « Plūs minus. »
translation: "Did you understand?" "More or less."

text: Horologium meum minus carum est tuo.
translation: My watch is less expensive than yours.

text: Minus severus est quam magister noster.
translation: He is less strict than our teacher.

text: Minus pulchra est quam mater.
translation: She is less beautiful than her mother is.

text: Nōn crēdō Thōman scīre quid sibi faciendum sit.
translation: I don't think that Tom knows what he needs to do.

text: Thomas illud Mariae esse faciendum se scire dicebat.
translation: Tom said that he knew that was what Mary was going to do.

text: Estne nobis satis benzoinae ad iter faciendum?
translation: Do we have enough gas for the trip?

text: Nōnne omnēs sciunt quid sibi faciendum sit?
translation: Everyone knows what they have to do, right?

text: Quid de ea re faciendum esse putas?
translation: What do you think should be done about it?

text: Maria iam scit quid ei faciendum sit.
translation: Mary already knows what she should do.

text: Thōmās mihi dīxit sē libenter mihi auxilium lātūrum esse.
translation: Tom told me he'd be glad to help me.

text: Natare scio, sed id non libenter facio.
translation: I know how to swim, but I don't like to.

text: Aquam cum glacie libenter non bibo.
translation: I don't like to drink water with ice.

text: Mater mea telehorasim libenter non aspicit.
translation: My mother doesn't like watching TV.

text: Puella pediludio libenter non ludit.
translation: The girl doesn't like to play soccer.

text: Didymus per telephonum libenter loquitur.
translation: Tom likes to talk on the phone.

text: Stultum est timere quod vitare non potes.
translation: It is foolish to fear what you cannot avoid.

text: Quis tam stultus fuit qui hoc faceret?
translation: Who's the idiot who did that?

text: Omnes qui hoc legunt, stulti sunt.
translation: All that read this are foolish.

text: Scio te me stultum esse putare.
translation: I know you think I'm stupid.

text: Stulti sunt homines in hac terra.
translation: People in this country are dumb.

text: Unus saepe facit complures vivere stultus.
translation: One fool makes a hundred.

text: Pater amici mei est amicus patris mei.
translation: My friend's father is friends with my father.

text: Hoc est cur mihi amici non sint.
translation: This is why I don't have any friends.

text: Si amici mei estis, venite mecum.
translation: If you are my friends, come with me.

text: Volo scire qui sint amici tui.
translation: I want to know who your friends are.

text: Amici matris meae amici mei sunt.
translation: My mother's friends are my friends.

text: Ego et Didymus boni amici sumus.
translation: Tom and I are good friends.

text: Si in loco tuo essem, non istud facerem.
translation: I wouldn't do that if I were you.

text: Si in loco tuo essem, non id facerem.
translation: If I were you, I wouldn't do it.

text: Thomas scit quo in loco pecunia abdita sit.
translation: Tom knows where the money is hidden.

text: Nonne Thomas hoc loco etiam nunc laborat?
translation: Tom is still working here, isn't he?

text: Si in tuo loco essem, eum adiuvarem.
translation: If I were in your shoes, I would help him.

text: Spero fore ut hic locus tibi placeat.
translation: I hope you like this place.

text: Felem parvam tigrem vocare potes, tigrem felem magnam.
translation: You can call a cat a small tiger, and a tiger a big cat.

text: Ea felem habet. Feles alba est.
translation: She has a cat. The cat is white.

text: Feli meae Esperantice loqui mihi placet.
translation: I like to speak Esperanto to my cat.

text: Felis inter me et te est.
translation: The cat is between me and you.

text: Sine fele mea vivere non possum.
translation: I can't live without my cat.

text: Didymus imagines felium libenter aspicit.
translation: Tom likes to look at pictures of cats.

text: Mihi ad pedes proicite, quia vester sum dominus!
translation: Bow before me, for I am your master!

text: Masako normaliter ad scholam it per pedes.
translation: Masako usually walks to school.

text: Ea ad scholam it per pedes.
translation: She goes to school on foot.

text: Saepe ad scholam it per pedes.
translation: He often walks to school.

text: Itisne ad scholam per pedes?
translation: Do you go to school on foot?

text: Maria sinistro pede clauda est.
translation: Mary is lame in her left foot.

text: Cur pater meus in culina est?
translation: Why is my father in the kitchen?

text: Thomas cum Maria in culina est.
translation: Tom is in the kitchen with Mary.

text: Thomas et Maria in culina sunt.
translation: Tom and Mary are in the kitchen.

text: Thomas Mariam in culina canentem audivit.
translation: Tom heard Mary singing in the kitchen.

text: Aliquis cum Thoma in culina est.
translation: Someone's in the kitchen with Tom.

text: Matrem meam in culina adiuvi.
translation: I helped my mother in the kitchen.

text: Potio Sinensis mihi magis quam potio Arabica placet.
translation: I like the tea more than the coffee.

text: Estne aqua satis fervens ad potionem Sinensem parandam?
translation: Is the water hot enough to make the tea?

text: Bibuntne homines potionem Sinensem in terra tua?
translation: Do people drink tea in your country?

text: Linguam Sinensem non intellego, sed discere volo.
translation: I don't understand Chinese, but I want to learn.

text: Spero fore ut cibus Sinensis tibi placeat.
translation: I hope you like Chinese food.

text: Spero fore ut cibus Sinensis vobis placeat.
translation: I hope you like Chinese food.

text: Is optimum advocatum urbis huius esse putatur.
translation: He is reputed the best lawyer in this city.

text: Quid est tempus optimum ad pascendum canem?
translation: When is the best time to feed your dog?

text: Quaeramus ergo, quid optimum factu sit, non quid usitatissimum.
translation: Let's find out what is best to do, not what is most commonly done.

text: Hodie dies optima meae vitae est.
translation: Today is the best day of my life.

text: Putabam Thoman amicum tuum optimum esse.
translation: I thought Tom was your best friend.

text: Putabam eam optimam amicam meam esse.
translation: I thought she was my best friend.

text: Esne ex America Foederata oriundus?
translation: Are you from the United States?

text: Esne ex America Foederata oriunda?
translation: Are you from the United States?

text: Esne recordatus Thomae gratias agere?
translation: Did you remember to thank Tom?

text: Esne recordatus iis gratias agere?
translation: Did you remember to thank them?

text: Esne recordatus ei gratias agere?
translation: Did you remember to thank him?

text: Esne heri cum eis locutus?
translation: Did you speak to them yesterday?

text: Cum quinque annos natus essem, legere non poteram.
translation: When I was five years old I could not read.

text: Cum quinque annos nata essem, legere non poteram.
translation: When I was five years old I could not read.

text: Amicum habeo in Hispania qui quinque linguas scit.
translation: I have a friend in Spain who speaks five languages.

text: Avus meus puer quinque linguas didicit.
translation: My grandfather learned five languages as a child.

text: In Brasilia tantum quinque dies habitaverunt.
translation: They have lived in Brazil for only five days.

text: Tantum quinque dies in Brasilia habitaverunt.
translation: They have lived in Brazil for only five days.

text: Nihil est ad quae ab ea facta sunt.
translation: It's nothing compared to what she did.

text: Nescio quando haec imago photographica facta sit.
translation: I don't know when this photo was taken.

text: In principio erat Verbum. Omnia per ipsum facta sunt.
translation: In the beginning, was the Divine Word. All things were made by It.

text: Omnia in Terra atomis facta sunt.
translation: All things on the Earth are made of atoms.

text: Haec imago photographica Narae facta est.
translation: This photo was taken in Nara.

text: Domus mea e ligno facta est.
translation: My house is built of wood.

text: Non homines habitare mecum hic mihi videntur, sed sues.
translation: It seems to me that it's pigs, not people, living here with me.

text: Cur Thomas mecum iam non loquitur?
translation: Why doesn't Tom talk to me anymore?

text: Visne mecum ad hoc concentum venire?
translation: Do you want to come with me to this concert?

text: Thomas de te mecum locutus est.
translation: Tom spoke with me about you.

text: Vultisne mecum ad hoc concentum venire?
translation: Do you want to come with me to this concert?

text: Num mecum ad concentum ibis?
translation: Won't you go to the concert with me?

text: Thomas ita fessus erat, ut ambulare non posset.
translation: Tom was so tired that he couldn't walk.

text: Noctu ambulabat Thomas, quod somnum capere non posset.
translation: Tom used to walk at night because he could not sleep.

text: Ita fessus erat, ut ambulare non posset.
translation: He was so tired that he couldn't walk.

text: Ita fessa erat, ut ambulare non posset.
translation: She was so tired that she couldn't walk.

text: Avus sine baculo ambulare non potest.
translation: My grandfather cannot walk without a walking stick.

text: Cur in hortos publicos ambulare vis?
translation: Why do you want to walk in the park?

text: Dīcit sē parātum esse ad id faciendum.
translation: He says that he's ready to do that.

text: Dīcit sē parātam esse ad id faciendum.
translation: She says that she's ready to do that.

text: Thomas et Maria se paratos esse dixerunt.
translation: Tom and Mary said they were ready.

text: Thomas et Maria parati ad adiuvandum sunt.
translation: Tom and Mary are ready to help.

text: Thomas et Maria parati ad eundum sunt.
translation: Tom and Mary are ready to go.

text: Maria dixit se paratam esse ad adiuvandum.
translation: Mary said she was ready to help.

text: Didymus est aeque procerus ac pater.
translation: Tom is as tall as his father.

text: Didymus est aeque procerus atque pater.
translation: Tom is as tall as his father.

text: Didymus est tam procerus quam pater.
translation: Tom is as tall as his father.

text: Tam procerus est quam frater meus.
translation: He is as tall as my brother.

text: Pariter procerus est ac frater meus.
translation: He is as tall as my brother.

text: Aeque procerus est ac frater meus.
translation: He is as tall as my brother.

text: Cum de bello loquamur, vere loquimur de pace.
translation: When we talk about war, we're really talking about peace.

text: Si vis pacem para bellum.
translation: If you wish peace, prepare for war.

text: Hic in pace vivere volumus.
translation: We want to live in peace here.

text: Thomas cum Maria pacem fecit.
translation: Tom made peace with Mary.

text: Maria cum Thoma pacem fecit.
translation: Mary made peace with Tom.

text: Pulsate Nazios pro pace mundiali.
translation: Punch Nazis for world peace.

text: Haec domus nimis parva est familiae nostrae.
translation: This house is too small for our family.

text: Domus mea nec magna nec parva est.
translation: My house is neither big nor small.

text: Frater meus in parvo vico habitat.
translation: My brother lives in a small village.

text: Omnia in cubiculo eius parva sunt.
translation: Everything in her room is small.

text: Certiorem me fac de parvis rebus.
translation: Inform me of the details.

text: Hic parva crate uti non licet.
translation: Grilling prohibited here.

text: Insectum non caeruleum, sed purpureum est.
translation: The insect is not blue, it is purple.

text: Oceanus est valde magnus et caeruleus.
translation: The ocean is very big and blue.

text: Uxor mea stolam caeruleam gerit.
translation: My wife is wearing a blue dress.

text: Calamum meum caeruleum vere amo.
translation: I really love my blue pen.

text: Oculi illius puellae caerulei sunt.
translation: That girl's eyes are blue.

text: Oculi huius puellae caerulei sunt.
translation: This girl's eyes are blue.

text: Quid sibi vult, quod abfueris hac tota hebdomade?
translation: What do you mean by being absent the whole week?

text: Is mihi semel in hebdomade scribit.
translation: He writes me once a week.

text: Milton hebdomadem bene non dormivit.
translation: Milton hasn't slept well for a week.

text: Georgius ibi sex hebdomades habitavit.
translation: George has lived there for six weeks.

text: Eam semel in hebdomade convenio.
translation: I meet her once a week.

text: Praeterita hebdomade epistulam eius accepi.
translation: I received her letter last week.

text: Cubiculum meum duplo maius est quam eius.
translation: My room is twice as big as his.

text: Oculi tui maiores quam stomachus tuus est.
translation: Your eyes are bigger than your stomach.

text: Sinae multo maiores sunt quam Iaponia.
translation: China is much bigger than Japan.

text: Scimus solem maiorem esse quam terram.
translation: We know that the Sun is bigger than the Earth.

text: Scīmus Sōlem maiōrem esse quam Terram.
translation: We know that the Sun is bigger than the Earth.

text: Hoc maiore pretio quam illud constat.
translation: This costs more than that.

text: Thomas ad fenestram advolavit et ex ea prospexit.
translation: Tom rushed over to the window and looked out.

text: Thomas ex fenestra prospexit ut videret quid accideret.
translation: Tom looked out the window to see what was happening.

text: Sine fenestra domus non est bona.
translation: Without a window, a house is no good.

text: Thomas et Maria fenestris apertis dormiunt.
translation: Tom and Mary sleep with their windows open.

text: Sella prope fenestram non est.
translation: The chair is not near the window.

text: Maria fenestram adivit velumque retraxit.
translation: Maria went to the window and opened the curtains.

text: Oppidum, in quo natus sum, pulcherrimum est.
translation: The city in which I was born is very beautiful.

text: Oppidum, in quo nata sum, pulcherrimum est.
translation: The city in which I was born is very beautiful.

text: Haec res pulcherrima est quam umquam vidi.
translation: This is the most beautiful thing I have ever seen.

text: Urbs in qua natus sum pulcherrima est.
translation: My hometown is very pretty.

text: Urbs in qua nata sum pulcherrima est.
translation: My hometown is very pretty.

text: Urbs in qua natus es pulcherrima est.
translation: Your hometown is very pretty.

text: Facere non potuimus ut eum mortuum non putaremus.
translation: We couldn't help but think that he was dead.

text: Teneri non potuimus quin eum mortuum putaremus.
translation: We couldn't help but think that he was dead.

text: Facere non potuimus quin eum mortuum putaremus.
translation: We couldn't help but think that he was dead.

text: Quis tibi dixit eum mortuum esse?
translation: Who told you that he is dead?

text: Non potuimus quin eum mortuum putaremus.
translation: We couldn't help but think that he was dead.

text: Thomas paratus ad moriendum non est.
translation: Tom isn't ready to die.

text: Methodus eius multo praesentior est quam tua.
translation: His method is much more effective than ours.

text: Cubiculum meum multo minus est quam tuum.
translation: My room is much smaller than yours.

text: Hoc facere scit multo melius quam ego.
translation: He can do it far better than I can.

text: Televisiones plasmaticae percarae erant sed iam multo sunt viliores.
translation: Plasma TVs used to be very expensive, but now they're much cheaper.

text: Sol multo maior est quam terra.
translation: The sun is much bigger than the earth.

text: Sol multo maior est quam Terra.
translation: The sun is much bigger than the earth.

text: Uxor mea ex Algeria oriunda est. Algeriana est.
translation: My wife is from Algeria. She is Algerian.

text: Ex Israël oriunda sum. Druza sum. Arabice loquor.
translation: I'm from Israel. I'm Druze. I speak Arabic.

text: E Turcia oriunda sum. Sephardita sum. Iudaeo-Hispanice loquor.
translation: I'm from Turkey. I'm Sephardi. I speak Ladino.

text: E Nigritania oriunda sum. Haussana sum. Lingua Haussana loquor.
translation: I'm from Niger. I'm Hausa. I speak Hausa.

text: E Syria oriunda sum. Curda sum. Lingua Aramaica loquor.
translation: I'm from Syria. I'm Kurdish. I speak Aramaic.

text: Catalina ex Argentina oriunda est. Argentina est.
translation: Catalina is from Argentina. She is Argentinian.

text: Multa pecunia eges ut in hac schola discas.
translation: You need a lot of money so that you may learn in that school.

text: Si pecunia egetis, pecuniam vobis dabo.
translation: I'll give you money if you need some.

text: Si pecunia eges, pecuniam tibi dabo.
translation: I'll give you money if you need some.

text: Meo quidem animo hoc non egemus.
translation: I really don't think we need this.

text: Thomas dixit se plus temporis eguisse.
translation: Tom said he needed more time.

text: "Quo eges?" "Nihil, gratias tibi ago."
translation: "What do you need?" "Nothing, thanks."

text: Didymus proximo anno triginta annos natus erit.
translation: Tom is going to be thirty next year.

text: Mense Martio Didymus triginta annos natus erit.
translation: Tom will be thirty in March.

text: Thomas triginta annos natus est, sed multo senior videtur.
translation: Tom is thirty years old, but he looks much older.

text: Februarius mensis triginta dies non habet.
translation: February does not have thirty days.

text: Thomas violino plus triginta annos cecinit.
translation: Tom has been playing the violin for more than thirty years.

text: December unum et triginta dies habet.
translation: December has thirty-one days.

text: Nihil est, quod dei non facere possunt.
translation: There is nothing that the gods may not do.

text: In Biblia dicitur nos imaginem Dei esse.
translation: In the Bible, it says that we are the image of God.

text: Non est deus praeter Deum et Iesus est Filius Dei.
translation: There is no god but God, and Jesus is the Son of God.

text: Reddite quae sunt Caesaris, Caesari et, quae sunt Dei, Deo.
translation: Render that which is Caesar's to Caesar, and that which is God's to God.

text: Cui respondit Moyses: Venit ad me populus quærens sententiam Dei.
translation: And Moses answered him: The people come to me to seek the judgment of God.

text: Se filium Dei esse dixit.
translation: He said he was the son of God.

text: Noli rogare ut faciam quod fieri non potest.
translation: Don’t ask me to do something that's impossible.

text: Sede quaeso, et potionem Sinensem faciam.
translation: Please sit down, and I will make tea.

text: Quid tu vis ut ego faciam?
translation: What do you want me to do?

text: Nescio quo eam nec quid faciam.
translation: I don't know where to go or what to do.

text: Saccharo egeo ut libum faciam.
translation: I need some sugar to make a cake.

text: Bostoniam iter Thomam visitatum faciam.
translation: I'm going to go to Boston to see Tom.

text: Ianua se aperuit atque introiit homo.
translation: The door opened, and in came a man.

text: Sella procul a ianua est.
translation: The chair is far from the door.

text: Sella mea prope ianuam est.
translation: My seat is near the door.

text: Ianua e ligno facta est.
translation: The door is made of wood.

text: Thomas ianuam aperire non potuit.
translation: Tom couldn't open the door.

text: Sella ante ianuam est.
translation: The chair is in front of the door.

text: Mihimet credebam Thomam adiuvare posse, minime tamen poteram.
translation: I thought I could help Tom, but I couldn't.

text: Minime, modam intellegere non possum, quia telehorasim non aspicio.
translation: No, I can't understand the fashion because I don't watch TV.

text: "Num grammatica Esperantica difficilis est?" "Minime, difficilis non est."
translation: “The grammar of Esperanto isn’t difficult is it?” “No, it is not difficult.”

text: "Germanicene loqueris?" "Minime. Galla sum."
translation: "Do you speak German?" "No, I'm French."

text: Sāmī cibus Sīnārum minimē placet.
translation: Sami doesn't like Chinese food at all.

text: "Adhucne in Bostonia habitas?" "Minime."
translation: "Do you still live in Boston?" "No."

text: Gratias tibi ago, quod me osculatus es.
translation: Thanks for the kiss.

text: "Quotiēns tē ōsculātus est?" "Semel tantum."
translation: "How many times did he kiss you?" "Just once."

text: "Quotiēns eum ōsculātus es?" "Semel tantum."
translation: "How many times did you kiss him?" "Just once."

text: Quotiēns in diē Thōmās Marīam ōsculātur?
translation: How many times a day does Tom kiss Mary?

text: Meministine quando te primum osculatus sum?
translation: Do you remember the first time I kissed you?

text: Didymus et Maria inter se osculantur.
translation: Tom and Mary are kissing.

text: Maria dicit se septem linguis loqui posse.
translation: Mary says that she can speak seven languages.

text: Haec sententia e septem verbis constat.
translation: This sentence is composed of seven words.

text: Unum, duo, tria, quattuor, quinque, sex, septem, octo, novem, decem.
translation: One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten.

text: Lutetiae septem dies mansura sum.
translation: I'll stay in Paris for seven days.

text: Septem dies in hebdomade sunt.
translation: A week has seven days.

text: Quantum est quinquies septem?
translation: How much is five times seven?

text: Multae magnaeque urbes in hac terra sunt.
translation: There are many big cities in this country.

text: Urbes in ruinas commovit tremor terrester.
translation: An earthquake has rattled the cities to rubble.

text: Puer ad urbem cum puella it.
translation: The boy goes to the city with the girl.

text: Puer cum puella ad urbem it.
translation: The boy goes to the city with the girl.

text: In Sinis sunt multae urbes magnae.
translation: In China, there are a lot of big cities.

text: Currus publicus hic ad urbem vehit.
translation: This bus goes to the city.

text: Didymus aegrum suum vendere non vult.
translation: Tom doesn't want to sell his farm.

text: Praeterito Iovis die domum meam vendidi.
translation: I sold my house last Thursday.

text: Pro hoc pretio non possum vendere.
translation: I can't sell at this price.

text: Carotas in taberna condimentaria vendunt.
translation: They sell carrots at the grocery store.

text: Vende domi, emi in nundinis.
translation: Sell at home, buy at the market.

text: Puer in servitutem venditus est.
translation: The boy was sold into slavery.

text: Velim mihi dicas quid hoc aestivo tempore egeris.
translation: I would like to know what you have done this summer.

text: Ne me dicas te quidem credere has res ineptas.
translation: Don't tell me you actually believe this nonsense.

text: Nihil habeo amplius quod tibi dicam.
translation: I have nothing more to say to you.

text: Magistra, quid dicas ego non intellego.
translation: Teacher, I don't understand what you are saying.

text: Non video cur tibi quicquam dicam.
translation: I see no reason to tell you anything.

text: Id quod dicis verum non est.
translation: What you say is not true.

text: Caesare pontifice maximo, Romani fastos novos obtitnuerunt.
translation: With Caesar as the greatest pontiff, the Romans obtained a new calendar.

text: Malum maximum si id palam provenit.
translation: It would be terrible if this got out.

text: Parentes Mariae in maxima domo habitant.
translation: Mary's parents live in a monster house.

text: Culina huius domus maxima est.
translation: The kitchen of this house is very large.

text: Miami est urbs maxima Floridae.
translation: Miami is the largest city in Florida.

text: Haec exedra maxima non est.
translation: This room is not very large.

text: Licetne imagines photographicas in illo aedificio facere?
translation: Is taking photographs permitted in that building?

text: Hoc est in urbe procerissimum aedificium.
translation: This is the tallest building in the city.

text: Domus aedificium est in quo habitamus.
translation: A house is a building that people live in.

text: Multa aedificia ad solum exusta sunt.
translation: Many buildings burned to the ground.

text: Oppidum nostrum multa pulchraque aedificia habet.
translation: Our city has many beautiful buildings.

text: Licetne photographare in illo aedificio?
translation: Can you take pictures in this building?

text: Iuvenibus linguam Anglicam discere magni momenti est.
translation: To study English is important for young people.

text: Oxygenium magni valde momenti est ad vitam in terris.
translation: Oxygen is very important for life on Earth.

text: Hoc momento nominis eius non memini.
translation: I can't recall her name at the moment.

text: Linguam Anglicam discimus, et eam discere hodie magni momenti est.
translation: We study English, and that subject is important today.

text: Hi nuntii nobis magni momenti sunt.
translation: This news is important to us.

text: Hoc non tam magni momenti est.
translation: This isn't that important.

text: Verumne est Mariam a Thoma non amari?
translation: Is it true that Tom doesn't like Mary?

text: Credo Didymum Mariamque inter se amare.
translation: I think Tom and Mary like each other.

text: Verumne est Thoman Mariam non amare?
translation: Is it true that Tom doesn't like Mary?

text: Cattus meus scit me eum amare.
translation: My cat knows I love him.

text: "Thomas ab omnibus amatur." "Quid dixisti?" "Thoman ab omnibus amari."
translation: "Tom is loved by everyone." "What did you say?" "Tom is loved by everyone."

text: Omnia praetereunt praeter amare Deum.
translation: All things pass away except to love God.

text: Ea te raedam eius lavare vult.
translation: She wants you to wash her car.

text: Quis post cenam vasa lavabit?
translation: Who will wash the dishes after dinner?

text: Tē raedam suam lavāre vult.
translation: She wants you to wash her car.

text: Noli hac in aqua lavari.
translation: Don't bathe in this water.

text: Potesne hodie vespere catillos lavare?
translation: Can you wash dishes tonight?

text: Lava patellam tuam, amabo te.
translation: Wash your plate, please.

text: Cūr nōn mihi dīxistī Thōman id facere velle?
translation: Why didn't you tell me that Tom wanted to do that?

text: Enuntia omnibus nos quoque hoc facere velle.
translation: Tell everyone we want to do that, too.

text: Thōmās dīcit se linguam Gallicam discere velle.
translation: Tom says he wants to study French.

text: Dic Thomae te velle Bostoniam ire.
translation: Tell Tom you want to go to Boston.

text: Putasne eam tamen velle me videre?
translation: Do you think she still wants to see me?

text: Thomas dicit se velle tecum congredi.
translation: Tom says he wants to meet you.

text: Dixistine Thomae quae capsae sint ponendae in autocineto?
translation: Have you told Tom which boxes need to be put in the car?

text: Thomas Mariam opperiens in autocineto suo est.
translation: Tom is in his car waiting for Mary.

text: Autocineto nobis opus est ut domum redeamus.
translation: We need the car to go back home.

text: Autocinetum tuum minoris pretii est quam meum.
translation: Your car is cheaper than mine.

text: Thomas in autocineto suo Mariam opperitur.
translation: Tom is in his car waiting for Mary.

text: Puto fore ut autocinetum novum emam.
translation: I think I'll buy a new car.

text: Vespertiliones a multis hominibus aves esse putantur.
translation: A lot of people think that bats are birds.

text: Multae aves in hortis publicis sunt.
translation: There are a lot of birds in the park.

text: Multi homines vespertiliones aves esse putant.
translation: A lot of people think that bats are birds.

text: Aves animalia sunt quae volare possunt.
translation: Birds are animals which can fly.

text: Magus aves parentes disparentesque agebat.
translation: The magician made birds appear and disappear.

text: Nōn omnēs avēs canere possunt.
translation: Not every bird can sing.

text: Omne mane potionem Arabicam cum lacte bibo.
translation: Every morning I drink coffee with milk.

text: Lac mihi magis quam sucus placet.
translation: I like milk more than juice.

text: Potionem Sinensem cum lacte nunquam bibo.
translation: I never drink tea with milk.

text: Feles lac sub mensa bibebat.
translation: The kitten was drinking milk under the table.

text: Da mihi poculum lactis, quaeso.
translation: Please give me a cup of milk.

text: Aliquid lactis in poculo est.
translation: There is little milk in the glass.

text: Illae rosae non tam pulchrae sunt quam hae.

text: "Eratne aliquis in exedra?" "Minime, nemo illic erat."

translation: She went to Paris to see her aunt.

translation: My aunt brought me flowers.

translation: Reading is prohibited in this library.

text: Femina librum in bibliotheca legit.
translation: A woman is reading a book in the library.

text: Quando ad bibliothecam ire vis?
translation: When do you want to go to the library?

translation: Felipe has two cars and one bike.

text: Si viceris, birotam meam tibi dabo.
translation: If you win, I'll give you my bicycle.

translation: What's the difference between a bicycle and a motorcycle?

translation: He plans to buy a new bicycle.

text: Birotam tibi emere non possum.
translation: I can't buy the bicycle for you.

text: Pater mihi novam birotam emit.
translation: Father bought me a new bicycle.

text: Unus tantum ex viginti discipulis librum legit.
translation: Out of twenty students, only one has read the book.

text: Et ego et tu discipulae sumus.
translation: Both you and I are students.

text: Soror mea discipula universitatis facta est.
translation: My sister became a college student.

text: Bonum iuxta docendum magna erat discipula.
translation: In addition to being a good teacher, she was a great scholar.

text: Ludus discipulos et discipulas habet.
translation: A school has male and female students.

text: Magister cum discipulis prandium sumpsit.

text: Pater meus acta diurna legit dum ientaculum sumit.
translation: My husband reads the newspaper while eating breakfast.

text: Thomas edit dum uxor eius acta diurna legebat.
translation: Tom ate breakfast while his wife read the newspaper.

text: Vir acta diurna legens pater eius est.
translation: The man reading a newspaper is his father.

text: Puer viro acta diurna vendidit.
translation: The boy sold the man a newspaper.

text: Liber prope acta diurna est.
translation: The book is next to the newspaper.

text: Oculos conjeci ad acta diurna.
translation: I took a look at the newspaper.

text: Mater mea Iudaea est et pater meus Polonicus.

translation: Jews are also known as Hebrews and Israelites.

translation: Jesus was born in Bethlehem in Judea.

text: Pater meus Iudaeus est ex Francia.
translation: My father is a French Jew.

text: Thomas Mariae dixit se nihil ante ientaculum edisse.
translation: Tom told Mary he hadn't eaten anything since breakfast.

text: Mane est. Pueri et puellae ientaculum sumunt.

text: Thomas ientaculum solus in culina sumit.
translation: Tom is eating breakfast alone in the kitchen.

text: Saepe telehorasim aspicimus, dum ientaculum sumimus.
translation: We often watch TV while we're eating breakfast.

text: Cras hoc tempore, Athenis ientaculum habebimus.
translation: This time tomorrow, we will be having breakfast in Athens.

text: Thomas ientaculum cum familia sumit.
translation: Tom is eating breakfast with his family.

text: Praeterito Veneris die cum amicis pediludio lusi.
translation: Last Friday I played soccer with friends.

text: Puellae de pueris loquebantur, et pueri de pediludio loquebantur.
translation: The girls talked about boys, and the boys talked about football.

text: In Brasilia pediludium est ludorum popularissimus.
translation: Football is the most popular sport in Brazil.

text: Mihi placet natare et pediludio ludere.
translation: I like swimming and playing football.

text: Pediludium in Hispania valde populare est.
translation: Soccer is very popular in Spain.

text: Viri sine pediludio vivere non possunt.
translation: Men can't live without football.

text: Vas, quod ab illo fractum, amitae meae est.
translation: The vase broken by him is my aunt's.

text: Vas, quod ab illo fractum, materterae meae est.
translation: The vase broken by him is my aunt's.

text: Hoc vas ex ferro factum est.
translation: This vase is made of iron.

text: Confessus est se vas fregisse.
translation: He confessed that he had broken the vase.

text: Primum vasa tum flores eme.
translation: First, buy a vase, and then the flowers.

text: Flores pulchriores videbuntur in vase.
translation: The flowers will look more beautiful in the vase.

translation: We like your clothes, except for your boots.

translation: You are a wolf in sheep's clothing.

text: Thomas vestimenta in ignem eiecit.
translation: Tom threw the clothes in the fire.

text: Maria vestimenta in ignem eiecit.
translation: Mary threw the clothes in the fire.

text: Domina earum est Aemilia: ea multas ancillas habet.

translation: Zelpha also bore another.

translation: Delia and Syra are two slave girls.

translation: I have to cook dinner today.

text: Sexta hora pomeridiana cenare soleo.
translation: I usually eat dinner at six.

text: Cena vestra vere gustabilis est.
translation: Your dinner is delicious.

text: Si aliquid dicere habes, dic coram me.
translation: If you have something to say, say it to my face.

text: Noe vero invenit gratiam coram Domino.
translation: But Noah found grace before the Lord.

text: Corrupta est autem terra coram Deo et repleta est iniquitate.
translation: And the earth was corrupted before God, and was filled with iniquity.

text: Homines autem Sodomitæ pessimi erant et pecatores coram Domino nimis.
translation: And the men of Sodom were very wicked, and sinners before the face of the Lord beyond measure.

text: Cumque introieritis terram, quam Dominus daturus est vobis, ut pollicitus est, observabitis cæremonias istas.
translation: And when you have entered into the land which the Lord will give you, as he hath promised, you shall observe these ceremonies.

translation: And as they watched him ascend into heaven, behold, two men dressed in white appeared beside them.

text: Cumque evigilasset Iacob de somno, ait: Vere Dominus est in loco isto, et ego nesciebam.
translation: And when Jacob awaked out of sleep, he said: Indeed the Lord is in this place, and I knew it not.

text: Cumque adiurasset eos atque dixisset: “Deus visitabit vos; asportate ossa mea vobiscum de loco isto”.
translation: And he made them swear to him, saying: God will visit you, carry my bones with you out of this place.

text: Cumque mones aliquem, nec se velit ille moneri, si tibi sit carus, noli desistere coeptis.
translation: Whenever you warn someone, and he does not wish to be warned, do not stop once you have begun if he is dear to you.

text: Cumque amplexatus recidisset in collum Beniamin fratris sui, flevit, illo quoque similiter flente, super collum eius.

text: Scipio, cum Carthaginem delevisset, in Italiam rediit.

translation: If God really existed, it would be necessary to abolish him.

translation: He came to Rome to study Italian.

translation: I learned more through experience than through instruction.

text: Praeterita hebdomade Thomas cum Maria Bostoniae prandium sumpsit.

translation: I wrote a letter to my mother last night.

translation: I'm going to a concert next week.

text: Proxima hebdomade Naram invisam.

text: Cum ver venit, effodiunt agros et semina ponunt.
translation: When spring comes, they dig up the fields and plant seeds.

text: E parvo semine magna arbor facta est.
translation: The small seed became a large tree.

text: Huius fructus semina nigra parvaque sunt.
translation: The seeds of this fruit are small and black.

text: Omnem terram, quam conspicis, tibi dabo et semini tuo usque in sempiternum.

text: Thōmās dīxit sē scīre ubi corpus sepultum sit.

text: Dīxit sē scīre ubi corpus sepultum sit.
translation: He said he knew where the body was buried.

text: "Habeo præceptoris dictata describenda." "Quæ dictata?" "In Ciceronis epistolas."

translation: My father is a teacher of the English language.

text: Video amicos atque eos saluto.

translation: Hail, Caesar, those who are about to die salute you.

text: Ave, Cæsar, morituri te salutant!
translation: Hail, Caesar, those who are about to die salute you!

text: Nimis iuvenis Thomas est ut secum habitet.
translation: Tom is too young to live by himself.

text: Non plus habuit secum triginta de suis.
translation: He had no more than thirty of his men with him.

text: Thomas Mariam matrimonio secum coniunxit.

text: Consobrinus meus, cum ebrius esset, dicebat Iesum secum cotidie locutum fuisse.

text: Pauca vestimenta secum fert.
translation: He is taking a few clothes with him.

text: Paucum cibi secum fert.

text: Stola rubra mihi magis quam stola alba placet.
translation: I like the red dress more than the white.

text: Mater praeterito Solis die mihi pulchram stolam emit.
translation: My mother bought me a nice dress last Sunday.
