text: Consobrinus meus ex Aegypto oriundus est. Aegyptius est.
translation: My cousin is from Egypt. He is Egyptian.

text: Consobrinus eius in America Foederata habitat.
translation: His cousin lives in America.

text: Consobrinus eius in Europa habitat.
translation: Her cousin lives in Europe.

text: Thomas consobrinam suam osculatus est.
translation: Tom kissed his cousin.

text: Thomas consobrinam meam osculatus est.
translation: Tom kissed my cousin.

text: Maria consobrinam suam osculata est.
translation: Mary kissed her cousin.

text: Plus foras minusque intro temporis tibi terendum est.
translation: You should spend more time outside and less time inside.

text: Si vis fumare, oportet te foras ire.
translation: You have to go outside if you want to smoke.

text: Thomas nobis dixit foras non exire.
translation: Tom told us not to go outside.

text: Et benedicto rege, egressus est foras.
translation: And Jacob blessed Pharaoh, and went out from before Pharaoh.

text: Velum retraham ut foras spectes.
translation: I'll open the curtain for you to look out.

text: Non licet mihi foras ire.
translation: I'm not allowed to go outside.

text: Formosa facies muta est commendatio.
translation: Beauty carries its dower in its face.

text: Domus parvus est sed formosus.
translation: The house is small but beautiful.

text: Lutetia valde formosa est.
translation: Paris is very beautiful.

text: Me formosum esse dicit.
translation: She says I'm handsome.

text: Oculi eius formosi fuerunt.
translation: She had pretty eyes.

text: Gallina ovum in armario meo peperit.
translation: A hen laid an egg in my closet.

text: Gallina fere cotidie unum ovum parit.
translation: This hen lays an egg almost every day.

text: Etiam gallina alba ova nigra parit.
translation: Even a black hen lays white eggs.

text: Meleagres valde maiores sunt quam gallinae.
translation: Turkeys are much larger than chickens.

text: Utrum prius, gallina an ovum?
translation: What came first? The egg or the hen?

text: Scio te gallinam non amare.
translation: I know you don't like chicken.

text: Tokium est longe omnium Iaponensium urbium maxima.
translation: Tokyo is by far the largest city in Japan.

text: Spero fore ut cibus Iaponensis tibi placeat.
translation: I hope you like Japanese food.

text: Spero fore ut cibus Iaponensis vobis placeat.
translation: I hope you like Japanese food.

text: Didymus raedam Iaponensem emere vult.
translation: Tom wants to buy a Japanese car.

text: Multae cauponae Iaponenses Bostoniae sunt.
translation: There are many Japanese restaurants in Boston.

text: Habesne acta diurna Iaponensia?
translation: Do you have a Japanese journal?

text: Leones multo fortiores quam cervi sunt.
translation: The lions are much stronger than the deer.

text: Melior est canis vivus leone mortuo.
translation: Better a living dog than a dead lion.

text: Quid interest inter leones et pardos?
translation: What's the difference between lions and leopards?

text: In Africa sunt multi leones.
translation: In Africa there are many lions.

text: Possuntne leones elephantos venari?
translation: Can lions hunt elephants?

text: Haec machina plus quam viginti annos habet.
translation: This machine is more than twenty years old.

text: Si machinam temporis haberes, quem annum inviseres?
translation: If you had a time machine, which year would you visit?

text: Ego numquam machina serratoria usus sum.
translation: I've never used a chainsaw.

text: Ego numquam machina serratoria usa sum.
translation: I've never used a chainsaw.

text: Nulla est in machinis mens.
translation: There's no such thing as Artificial Intelligence.

text: Aliquae partes machinae desunt.
translation: The machine has some of its parts missing.

text: Cum e Luna videtur, Terra pilae similis est.
translation: Seen from the Moon, Earth resembles a ball.

text: Teniludium et ludus pilae Caledonicae mihi placent.
translation: I like tennis and golf.

text: Me rogavit ut pilam reicerem.
translation: He asked me to throw the ball back.

text: Puerum rogavi ut pilam reiceret.
translation: I asked the boy to throw the ball back.

text: Placetne tibi ludus pilae Caledonicae?
translation: Are you fond of golf?

text: Da mihi hanc pilam lusoriam.
translation: Give me that soccer ball.

text: Qui sapientiam vult, patientiam habeat primam.
translation: He who wants wisdom should first have patience.

text: Spero me primam impressionem bonam facere.
translation: I hope I make a good first impression.

text: Virtutem primam esse puto compescere linguam.
translation: I think the greatest virtue is holding your tongue.

text: Inter bona animi, sapientia tenet primas.
translation: Among the good things of the mind, wisdom holds the first place.

text: Primae litterae patris mei sunt.
translation: That is my father's first letter.

text: Thoman in primis diligebat.
translation: She loved Tom especially.

text: Hispania usque ad annum MCMLXXV a tyranno recta est.
translation: Spain was ruled by a dictator until 1975.

text: Recta haec translatio, sed nimis litteralis est.
translation: This translation is correct, but it is too literal.

text: "Quonam abis nunc?" "Recta domum, vale." "Vale tu quoque."
translation: "Where are you going now?" "Straight home: farewell." "Farewell to you too."

text: Cur sententiam quae recta est mutes?
translation: Why change a sentence that's correct?

text: Thomas loco temporeque recto fuit.
translation: Tom was at the right place at the right time.

text: Non est recta via dolendi.
translation: There's no right way to grieve.

text: Non est bonum serpentem dormientem e somno excitare.
translation: It's not good to wake a sleeping snake.

text: Serpens a maiore serpente devorata est.
translation: The snake was devoured by a bigger snake.

text: Multae serpentes hac in silva sunt.
translation: There are many snakes in this forest.

text: Multi serpentes in hac silva habitant.
translation: There are a lot of snakes in this forest.

text: Thomas putat Mariam timere serpentes.
translation: Tom thinks that Mary is afraid of snakes.

text: Nesciebam tibi serpentem esse.
translation: I didn't know you had a snake.

text: Sitio. Poculum potionis Arabicae habere velim.
translation: I am thirsty. I would like to have a cup of coffee.

text: Canis tuus sitire videtur.
translation: It looks like your dog is thirsty.

text: Aquam bibo, quia sitio.
translation: I'm drinking water because I'm thirsty.

text: Thomas se sitire dixit.
translation: Tom said that he was thirsty.

text: Aquam bibo, cum sitio.
translation: I drink water when I'm thirsty.

text: Utrum esuris an sitis?
translation: Are you hungry or thirsty?

text: Thomas et Maria in via Tertia domicilium habent.
translation: Tom and Mary live on Third Street.

text: Tertia pars silvarum pluvialium mundi in Brasilia invenitur.
translation: A third of the world's rainforests are found in Brazil.

text: "Jamne tenes quæ sunt reddenda tertia hora?" "Teneo."
translation: "Have you memorised the things which have to be recited at three o'clock?" "I have."

text: Thomas et Maria in via Tertia habitant.
translation: Tom and Mary live on Third Street.

text: Tertia hora te in exedra conveniam.
translation: I'll meet you in the lobby at three.

text: Aeroplanum hora tertia adveniet.
translation: The plane will arrive at three.

text: Conivere potes in veritate, sed non in memoriis.
translation: You can close your eyes to reality but not to memories.

text: Et cognoscetis veritatem, et veritas liberabit vos.
translation: And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.

text: Necessarius est methodus ad veritatem investigandam.
translation: Method is indispensable for investigating the truth.

text: Sapientia nisi in veritate non invenitur
translation: Wisdom is only found in truth.

text: Nos ei veritatem dicere oportebat.
translation: We should have told him the truth.

text: Thomas nihil ad veritatem loquitur.
translation: Tom never tells the truth.

text: Anulus debilissimus catenae quoque fortissimus est. Is catenam frangere potest.
translation: The weakest link in the chain is also the strongest. It can break the chain.

text: Hic anulus nimis carus est.
translation: This ring is far too expensive.

text: Mater filiae anulum donavit.
translation: The mother gave the girl a ring.

text: Fures anulum tuum concupiscunt.
translation: The thieves are greedy for your ring.

text: Amici tui anulum video.
translation: I see your friend's ring.

text: Hic anulus carissimus est.
translation: This ring is very expensive.

text: Anus, quam nuper vidisti, avia mea est.
translation: The old woman you just saw is my grandmother.

text: Avia nostra multos annos mortua est.
translation: Our grandmother died many years ago.

text: Avia capsam malorum nobis misit.
translation: Grandmother sent us a box of apples.

text: Avia mea in hortō labōrat.
translation: My grandmother is working in the garden.

text: Avia tua domina lepida est.
translation: Your grandmother is a charming lady.

text: Avus carmina de avia scribit.
translation: Grandfather likes writing poems about grandmother.

text: Equus, leo, canis et ovis bestiae sunt.
translation: The horse, the lion, the dog and the sheep are animals.

text: Aquilae et columbae bēstiae pulcherrimae sunt.
translation: Eagles and doves are very beautiful animals.

text: Multas bestias in silva vidimus.
translation: We saw many animals in the forest.

text: In silva vivunt bestiae feroces.
translation: Wild animals live in the forest.

text: Squali rubri bestiae periculosae sunt.
translation: Purple sharks are dangerous animals.

text: Non omnia animalia bestiae sunt.
translation: Not all animals are wild.

text: In caupona prope officium cum Thoma prandium sumpsi.
translation: I had lunch with Tom at a restaurant near the office.

text: Thōmās Bostoniae in caupōnā opus facit.
translation: Tom is working in a restaurant in Boston.

text: Thōmās Bostoniae in caupōnā labōrat.
translation: Tom is working in a restaurant in Boston.

text: Potionem Arabicam in caupona bibo.
translation: I am drinking coffee at a cafe.

text: Caupona in pedeplanis sita est.
translation: The restaurant is on the ground floor.

text: Editne Marica in cauponis Iaponensibus?
translation: Does Marika eat at Japanese restaurants?

text: Omnes dicunt huius cauponae cibum optimum esse.
translation: Everyone says that the food at this restaurant is very good.

text: Multae cauponae Iaponenses Novi Eboraci sunt.
translation: There are many Japanese restaurants in New York.

text: Thomas et Maria ad cauponam ierunt.
translation: Tom and Mary went to a restaurant.

text: Thomas Mariam ad cauponam Italicam adduxit.
translation: Tom took Mary to an Italian restaurant.

text: Thoman ad cauponam cafeariam conveni.
translation: I met Tom at the coffee shop.

text: Thomas Mariaque ad cauponam ierunt.
translation: Tom and Mary went to a restaurant.

text: Oculi tui columbarum, absque eo quod intrinsecus latet.
translation: Through your veil we see your dove-like eyes.

text: Columbae albae avēs pulchrae sunt.
translation: White doves are pretty birds.

text: Exspectatis autem ultra septem diebus aliis, rursum dimisit columbam ex arca.
translation: And having waited yet seven other days, he again sent forth the dove out of the ark.

text: Columbarum pennae albae sunt.
translation: The pigeons' feathers are white.

text: Columbas alere non licet.
translation: Feeding pigeons is prohibited.

text: Ecce tu pulchra es, amica mea!, ecce tu pulchra es! Oculi tui columbarum.
translation: How beautiful you are, my beloved, how beautiful you are! Your eyes are doves.

text: Quis Thoman tibi dixit crus fregisse?
translation: Who told you Tom broke his leg?

text: Cur phoenicopterī in ūnā crūrī stant?
translation: Why do flamingos stand on one leg?

text: Scisne quomodo Thomas crus fregerit?
translation: Do you know how Tom broke his leg?

text: Thomas cecidit et crus fregit.
translation: Tom fell and broke his leg.

text: Thomas crura movere non potuit.
translation: Tom couldn't move his legs.

text: Cecidit et crus fregit.
translation: He fell and broke his leg.

text: Thomas imagines photographicas amicae in ignem eiecit.
translation: Tom threw the photos of his girlfriend in the fire.

text: Maria imagines photographicas amici in ignem eiecit.
translation: Mary threw the photos of her boyfriend in the fire.

text: Thomas amicae vestimenta in ignem eiecit.
translation: Tom threw his girlfriend's clothes in the fire.

text: Thomas uxoris vestimenta in ignem eiecit.
translation: Tom threw his wife's clothes in the fire.

text: Maria amici vestimenta in ignem eiecit.
translation: Mary threw her boyfriend's clothes in the fire.

text: Thomas imagines photographicas in ignem eiecit.
translation: Tom threw the photos in the fire.

text: Fumat et hoc incipit ad sanitatem eius afficere.
translation: Smoking began to tell on his health.

text: In hac caupona fumare non licet.
translation: Smoking is prohibited in this restaurant.

text: Ei medicus fumare decidere inebriareque dixit.
translation: The doctor told him to give up smoking and drinking.

text: Quot sigarella per diem fumas?
translation: How many cigarettes do you smoke per day?

text: In hamaxosticho fumare non licet.
translation: Smoking is not permitted on the train.

text: In anabathro fumare non licet.
translation: Smoking is prohibited inside the elevator.

text: Fumum tabaci ducere non licet.
translation: Smoking is prohibited.

text: Spiraculum emittere fumum coepit.
translation: The chimney began to give out smoke.

text: Quid est fumus griseus?
translation: Why is the smoke dark grey?

text: Neque fumo neque bibo.
translation: I neither smoke nor drink.

text: Neque bibo neque fumo.
translation: I don't drink or smoke.

text: Sicut sigarellae fumus olfacis.
translation: You reek of cigarette smoke.

text: Cave ne moveas pedem hinc antequam redeam.
translation: Do not dare move a foot from here until I return.

text: Quae loquatur exaudire hinc non queo.
translation: I can't hear what he's talking about from here.

text: Quae loquatur exaudire hinc non possum.
translation: I can't hear what he's talking about from here.

text: Procul hinc vivere non potest.
translation: She can't live far from here.

text: Quo hinc te agis?
translation: Where are you going?

text: Iam nunc experimentum vestri capiam: per salutem pharaonis, non egrediemini hinc, donec veniat frater vester minimus!
translation: I shall now presently try what you are: by the health of Pharaoh, you shall not depart hence, until your youngest brother come.

text: Vestiarium pone a dextris et lectum a sinistris.
translation: Put the wardrobe on the right and the bed on the left.

text: Mariae litteris lectis Thomas flere coepit.
translation: After reading Mary's letter, Tom burst out crying.

text: Ego cenatus continuo lectum petivi.
translation: I ate supper and immediately went to bed.

text: Nemo super lectum illum dormiverat.
translation: No one had slept on that bed.

text: Pensis confectis continuo lectum petivit.
translation: Having done the lessons, he immediately went to bed.

text: Duo linteamina super lectum erant.
translation: Two sheets were on the bed.

text: Liberi nostri eiusdem ludi litterarii erant.
translation: Our children were at the same elementary school.

text: Quot ludi sunt in urbe tua?
translation: How many schools are there in your city?

text: In vīcō nostrō duo lūdī sunt.
translation: There are two schools in our village.

text: Et musica et ludi ei placent.
translation: He likes both music and sports.

text: Pueri ludi mei stulti sunt.
translation: The boys at my school are stupid.

text: Num es discipulus huius ludi?
translation: You're not a student here, are you?

text: Thomas picturas ad domum suam afferendas curavit.
translation: Tom had the paintings brought to his house.

text: Eramus pictores et pingabamus picturas pulchras.
translation: We were painters and we painted beautiful pictures.

text: Vasya patruus mihi picturam dono dedit.
translation: Uncle Vasya gave me a painting as a gift.

text: Vasya avunculus mihi picturam dono dedit.
translation: Uncle Vasya gave me a painting as a gift.

text: Monstravimus ei picturas quasdam Alpium.
translation: We showed him some pictures of the Alps.

text: Thomas mihi picturam dono dedit.
translation: Tom gave me a painting as a gift.

text: Noli hoc in flumine piscare. Non licet.
translation: Don't fish in this river. It is not allowed.

text: Cur hoc in fluvio piscare non licet?
translation: Why is fishing in this river forbidden?

text: Nolite hoc in flumine piscare. Non licet.
translation: Do not fish in this river. It is not allowed.

text: Hoc in lacu piscare non licet.
translation: Fishing is not permitted in this lake.

text: Hoc in fluvio piscare non licet.
translation: Fishing is not permitted in this river.

text: Hoc in flumine piscare non licet.
translation: Fishing is not permitted in this river.

text: Mihi dixisti hodie non plueret, ita umbellam non adduxi.
translation: You told me it wouldn't rain today, so I didn't bring an umbrella.

text: Si cras pluet, domi manebo.
translation: If it rains tomorrow, I will stay at home.

text: Si pluet, quid facturus es?
translation: What are you going to do if it rains?

text: Si cras pluet, manebisne domi?
translation: If it rains tomorrow, will you stay at home?

text: Si perendie pluet, domi manebo.
translation: If it rains the day after tomorrow, I will stay at home.

text: Nobis Roma profecturis, pluere coepit.
translation: When we were about to depart from Rome, it started to rain.

text: Cum me videret, se dormire simulabat.
translation: When he saw me, he pretended to be asleep.

text: Maria non vere aegrotat; modo simulat.
translation: Mary isn't really sick; she's just pretending.

text: Ille discipulus non numquam aegrum simulat.
translation: That student sometimes pretends to be sick.

text: Thomas apud nos non esse simulavit.
translation: Tom pretended he wasn't with us.

text: Qui curios simulant, et bacchanalia vivunt.
translation: Those who pretend to be like the common Curii, and live like wild Bacchanalians.

text: Cur te Thoman esse simulas?
translation: Why are you pretending to be Tom?

text: Multī mīlitēs in proeliō vulnerātī sunt.
translation: Many soldiers were wounded in the battle.

text: Et Thōmās et Marīa vulnerātī sunt.
translation: Tom and Mary were both wounded.

text: Thomas mihi dixit se vulneratum esse.
translation: Tom told me he was wounded.

text: Maria mihi dixit se vulneratam esse.
translation: Mary told me she was wounded.

text: Aliī mortuī, aliī vulnerātī sunt.
translation: Some died, others were wounded.

text: Nullum vitale viscus vulneratum est.
translation: No vital organs were damaged.

text: Thomas libum in tres partes aequales secuit.
translation: Tom divided the pie into three equal parts.

text: In oculis Dei, omnes homines aequales sunt.
translation: In the sight of God, all men are equal.

text: Actioni contrariam semper et æqualem esse reactionem.
translation: For every action there is always an equal and opposite reaction.

text: Omnibus linguis aequalis, Anglica est omnium aequalissima.
translation: All languages being equal, English is the most equal of all.

text: Omnes aequales sumus in facie mortis.
translation: We are all equal in the face of death.

text: Studiorum agitatio vitæ æqualis fuit.
translation: The activity of studies lasted as long as life itself.

text: Dixitque: Benedictus Dominus Deus Sem! Sitque Chanaan servus eius.
translation: And he said: Blessed be the Lord God of Shem, be Canaan his servant.

text: Oves vestras et armenta assumite, ut petieratis, et abeuntes benedicite mihi.
translation: Your sheep and herds take along with you, as you demanded, and departing bless me.

text: Benedictus est maritus Jacobi.
translation: Borech is Yankev's husband.

text: Erat autem Abraham senex dierumque multorum; et Dominus in cunctis benedixerat ei.
translation: Now Abraham was old, and advanced in age; and the Lord had blessed him in all things.

text: Dixitque: “Dimitte me, iam enim ascendit aurora”. Respondit: “Non dimittam te, nisi benedixeris mihi”.
translation: And he said to him: Let me go, for it is break of day. He answered: I will not let thee go, except thou bless me.

text: Faciamque te in gentem magnam et benedicam tibi et magnificabo nomen tuum, erisque in benedictionem.
translation: And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and magnify thy name, and thou shalt be blessed.

text: Quid Tom cum Maria colloqui non vult?
translation: Why doesn't Tom want to talk with Mary?

text: Magister dixit haec colloquia nobis recordanda esse.
translation: The teacher said that we must memorize these idioms.

text: Maria cum nemine colloqui volebat nisi Thoma.
translation: Tom was the only person Mary wanted to talk to.

text: Thomas dicit se velle tecum colloqui.
translation: Tom says he wants to talk to you.

text: Thomas dicit se tecum colloqui velle.
translation: Tom says he wants to talk with you.

text: Memento cum thoma de eo colloqui.
translation: Remember to talk to Tom about that tomorrow.

text: Commentarius per telephonum gestabile mihi scribendus est.
translation: I have to write an SMS.

text: Commentarium per telephonum gestabile scripturus sum.
translation: I have to write an SMS.

text: Commentarium per telephonum gestabile scriptura sum.
translation: I have to write an SMS.

text: Thomas commentarios diurnos arcanos Mariae invenit.
translation: Tom found Mary's secret diary.

text: Thomas commentarios diurnos arcanos Mariae legit.
translation: Tom read Mary's secret diary.

text: Habesne commentarios periodicos Iaponenses?
translation: Do you have a Japanese magazine?

text: Non omnes, qui mane micant, sub vespere lucent.
translation: Not everyone who shines in the morning shines in the afternoon.

text: Prima luce Thomas e somno experrectus est.
translation: Tom awoke at daybreak.

text: Nox erat. Sed luna plena lucebat.
translation: It was night. But a full moon was shining.

text: Requiem aeternam dona eis, Domine: et lux perpetua luceat eis.
translation: Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon them.

text: Sol lucebat, sed frigidus erat.
translation: The sun was shining, yet it was cold.

text: Prima luce prope silvam conveniamus.
translation: Let's meet by the forest at dawn.

text: Thomas fuscinula, Maria autem manibus placentam Neapolitanam edit.
translation: Tom eats pizza with a fork, but Mary eats it with her hands.

text: Thomas clavem mechanicam in manibus tenens intravit.
translation: Tom came in with a wrench in his hand.

text: Parva puella pupam in manibus tenet.
translation: The little girl has a doll in her hands.

text: Manibus tuis et mente tua egeo.
translation: I need your hands and your brain.

text: Vita tua in manibus meis est.
translation: Your life is in my hands.

text: Vita sua in manibus meis est.
translation: His life is in my hands.

text: Femina cum saccharo vel melle Potionem Sinensem bibit.
translation: The woman drinks the tea with sugar or with honey.

text: Mel et lac sub lingua tua.
translation: Honey and milk are under thy tongue.

text: Apis insectum est et mel comedit.
translation: The bee is an insect and it eats honey.

text: Ubi mel, ibi apes.
translation: Where there is honey, there are bees.

text: Apes nobis mel dant.
translation: Bees give us honey.

text: Te diligo, mel meum.
translation: I love you, sweetheart.

text: Oppidum situm est duodecim milia passuum a mari.
translation: The town is located twelve miles from the sea.

text: Hoc flumen quingenta milia passuum in longitudinem est.
translation: This river is 500 miles in length.

text: Mercurii latera modo tribus milibus passuum distant.
translation: Mercury is just 3000 miles across.

text: Hodie sex milia passuum ambulavi.
translation: Today I walked 10 kilometers.

text: Hodie octo milia passuum ambulavi.
translation: Today I walked eight miles.

text: Ibam circa mille passuum.
translation: I walked about 1 mile.

text: Pater pila Caledonica ludit, sed non bene.
translation: My father does play golf, but not well.

text: Solis die mane pater pila Caledonica lusit.
translation: My father played golf on the Sunday morning.

text: Teniludio et pila Caledonica libenter ludo.
translation: I like playing tennis and golf.

text: Proximo Solis die pila Caledonica ludet.
translation: He will play golf next Sunday.

text: Pater eius pila Caledonica non ludit.
translation: His father doesn't play golf.

text: Praeterito Solis die pila Caledonica lusit.
translation: He played golf last Sunday.

text: Ne sollicitatus sis, id iam refeci.
translation: Don't worry, I have already fixed it.

text: Ne sollicitata sis, id iam refeci.
translation: Don't worry, I have already fixed it.

text: Malleo egeo, ut mensam reficiam.
translation: I need a hammer to repair the table.

text: Thomas birotam Mariae refecturus est.
translation: Tom is going to fix Mary's bicycle.

text: Quotiēns hoc reficere cōnātus es?
translation: How many times have you tried to fix this?

text: Quotiēns hoc reficere cōnātae estis?
translation: How many times have you tried to fix this?

text: Spero fore ut turma nostra vincat.
translation: I hope our team will win.

text: Turma tua fortior est quam mea.
translation: Your team is stronger than ours.

text: Spero fore ut turma mea vincat.
translation: I hope my team wins.

text: Quot in turmā tuā sunt?
translation: How many are on your team?

text: Quae turma verisimiliter vincet?
translation: Which team is likely to win?

text: Turma mea certamen vicit.
translation: My team won the match.

text: Qui satur est, pleno laudat ieiunia ventre.
translation: The fat man knows not what the lean thinks.

text: Noli semina deglutire, alioquin arbor in ventre tuo crescet!
translation: Don't swallow seeds, or a tree's gonna grow in your belly!

text: Omnem escam manducabit venter; et est cibus cibo melior.
translation: The stomach accepts all kinds of food, but some foods are better than others.

text: Venter eius eburneus, distinctus sapphiris.
translation: His belly is as bright ivory overlaid with sapphires.

text: Dein paulum carnium de ventre veteris vaccae apponitur, sed elixum ante quindecim dies.
translation: Then a little flesh from the tripe of an old cow is served up, but boiled fifteen days before.

text: Virginei volucrum vultus, fœdissima ventris / proluvies, uncæque manus, et pallida semper / ora fame.
translation: Birds maiden-faced, but trailing filth obscene, / with taloned hands and looks for ever pale and lean.

text: Ea in armaria culinae ponimus.
translation: We put them in the kitchen cupboards.

text: Lac in armario frigidario est.
translation: There is milk in the refrigerator.

text: Pone ova in armario frigidario.
translation: Put the eggs in the refrigerator.

text: Quid est in armario frigidario?
translation: What is there in the fridge?

text: Cerevisia in armario frigidario est.
translation: There's beer in the fridge.

text: Hoc in armario nihil est.
translation: There's nothing in this closet.

text: Non habet anguillam, per caudam qui tenet illam.
translation: Getting a hold of this world is like holding a wet eel by the tail.

text: Angelis duae alae; daemonio una cauda.
translation: Angels have two wings; the Devil has a tail.

text: Canis meus caudam valde longam habet.
translation: My dog has a very long tail.

text: Canis meus caudam longam habet.
translation: My dog has a long tail.

text: Canis mea caudam longam habet.
translation: My dog has a long tail.

text: Elephanti cauda brevis est.
translation: The elephant has a short tail.

text: In Religione Christiana Iesus filius Dei esse putatur.
translation: In Christianity, Jesus is believed to be the son of God.

text: Inde ab anno 1950 Thomas christianus est.
translation: Tom has been a Christian since the year 1950.

text: Musulmani, Christiani et Iudaei in Deum credunt.
translation: Muslims, Christians, and Jews believe in God.

text: Christiani credunt Deum mundi creatorem esse.
translation: Christians believe that God is the creator of the world.

text: Thomas se bonum Christianum esse dicit.
translation: Tom says he's a good Christian.

text: Uxor mea Christiana est, sed in Deum ego non credo.
translation: My wife is Christian but I do not believe in God myself.

text: Volo ne mea cithara hispanica canatis.
translation: I don't want anyone to play my guitar.

text: Meam citharam hispanicam volo ne citharizetur.
translation: I don't want anyone to play my guitar.

text: Cithara vetus in fundamento recondita est.
translation: The old harp was stored in the basement.

text: Cithara crinitus Iopas / personat aurata, docuit quem maximus Atlas.
translation: His golden lyre long-haired Iopas tunes, / and sings what Atlas taught in loftiest strain.

text: "Potesne cithara canere?" "Ita, possum."
translation: "Can you play the guitar?" "Yes, I can."

text: Ioannes cithara canere non potest.
translation: John cannot play the guitar.

text: Infernus et Caelum nihil aliud sunt quam cogitationes.
translation: Heaven and hell are only mirages.

text: Si lingua non esset, nulla cogitatio.
translation: But for language, there would be no thought.

text: Incoloratae virides cogitationes dormiunt saeviter.
translation: Colorless green ideas sleep furiously.

text: Papilio: cogitatio quae volat.
translation: A butterfly: a thought that flies.

text: Hoc sine cogitatione dixi.
translation: I said this without thinking.

text: Libertatem loquendi libertatemque cogitationis habemus, sed prima multo plus quam secunda exercetur.
translation: We have freedom of speech and freedom of thought, but the former is exercised much more than the latter.

text: Audi dominum Inoue in illo deversorio mansisse.
translation: I heard that Mr. Inoue has stayed at that hotel.

text: Hoc a deversorio non longe abest.
translation: It is not far away from the hotel.

text: Cubicula vacua nulla sunt in deversorio.
translation: No, there is no room in the hotel.

text: In hoc deversorio duas noctes mansi.
translation: I spent two nights in this hotel.

text: Multa deversoria in media urbe sunt.
translation: There are many hotels downtown.

text: Procul a deversorio non est.
translation: It is not far away from the hotel.

text: Ubi pileus et digitabula mea sunt?
translation: Where are my hat and my gloves?

text: Digitabula tua in raeda mea inveni.
translation: I found your gloves in my car.

text: Ecce digitabula, quae Thomas mihi attulit.
translation: These are the gloves Tom bought me.

text: Digitabula mea in bibliotheca amisi.
translation: I left my gloves in the library.

text: "Cuius digitabula sunt?" "Lisae sunt."
translation: "Whose gloves are these?" "They are Lisa's."

text: Thomas nigra scorteaque digitabula gerebat.
translation: Tom was wearing black leather gloves.

text: Id reficere non potes. Novum tibi emendum est.
translation: You can't fix it. You should buy a new one.

text: Semel Maria per hebdomadem ad emendum it.
translation: Marie goes shopping once a week.

text: Pecuniam ad domum emendam non habet.
translation: He has no money to buy a house.

text: Novum computatorium mihi emendum est.
translation: I have to get a new computer.

text: Quid putas mihi emendum esse?
translation: What do you think I should buy?

text: Aliquid cibi Didymo emendum est.
translation: Tom has to buy some food.

text: Deus non mortuus est; immo vero vivit.
translation: God is not dead, He is surely alive.

text: Etsi non verum est, immo tamen callide factum est.
translation: Even if it isn't true, it's still rather clever.

text: Eum fallere non modo credo; immo scio.
translation: I don't believe he's lying; I know he is.

text: Gratias tibi ago ex imo corde.
translation: Thank you from the bottom of my heart.

text: Imo citius extudisses dentem ab eo quam nummum in honesta re.
translation: Nay you would sooner have got a tooth from him than a piece of money in an honest matter.

text: "Sine illum venire; videbis quid respondeat." "Imo, videat quid respondeat præceptori."
translation: "Let him come; you will see what he answers." "No, let him see what he should answer to the teacher."

text: Omnes aliud agentes, aliud simulantes improbi sunt.
translation: Everyone who does one thing and pretends to do another is dishonest.

text: Odimus duces nostros improbos pravosque!
translation: We hate our wicked and corrupt leaders!

text: Iulius iratus puerum improbum verberat.
translation: Julius angrily beats the rude boy.

text: Thomas discipulus improbus non erat.
translation: Tom wasn't a bad student.

text: Thomas discipulus improbus non est.
translation: Tom isn't a bad student.

text: Didymus puer improbus est.
translation: Tom is a bad boy.

text: Ex Italia oriundus sum et Italice loquor.
translation: I come from Italy and I speak Italian.

text: Ex Italia oriunda sum et Italice loquor.
translation: I come from Italy and I speak Italian.

text: Spero fore ut cibus Italicus tibi placeat.
translation: I hope you like Italian food.

text: Spero fore ut cibus Italicus vobis placeat.
translation: I hope you like Italian food.

text: Verba Italica in tres coniugationes dividuntur.
translation: Italian verbs are grouped into three conjugations.

text: Cur autocinetum Italicum emisti?
translation: Why did you buy an Italian car?

text: Puto hunc pullum de nido cecidisse.
translation: I think this little bird fell from the nest.

text: Aves semper in nidum reveniunt.
translation: The birds always return to the nest.

text: Aves nidos in arboribus construunt.
translation: Birds make their nests in trees.

text: Omni volucri placet suus nidus.
translation: Every bird likes its nest.

text: Nidus de arbore cecidit.
translation: The nest fell from the tree.

text: Nidus ad terram cecidit.
translation: The nest fell on the ground.

text: Hamaxostichus noster triginta minutis post octavam horam proficiscetur.
translation: Our train leaves at eight-thirty.

text: "Quando expectas reditum patris?" "Ad octavum diem hinc."
translation: "When do you expect your father to return?" "Eight days from now."

text: Scholae triginta minuta post octavam horam incipiunt.
translation: School begins at eight-thirty.

text: Et circumcidit eum octavo die, sicut præceperat ei Deus.
translation: And he circumcised him the eighth day, as God had commanded him.

text: Te vocabo circa horam octavam vesperi.
translation: I'll call you up around eight this evening.

text: Octava hora ad scholam eo.
translation: I go to school at eight o'clock.

text: Haec femina plus quam octoginta annos nata est.
translation: This woman is more than eighty years old.

text: "Quot annos habes?" "Octoginta et novem annos natus sum."
translation: "How old are you?" "I am eighty-nine years old."

text: Decem, viginti, triginta, quadraginta, quinquaginta, sexaginta, septuaginta, octoginta, nonaginta, centum.
translation: Ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety, hundred.

text: Tribus ab hinc annis, octoginta lei solvebam; nunc ducentos solvo.
translation: Three years ago, I was paying eighty lei; now I pay two hundred.

text: Octoginta et sex annorum erat Abram quando peperit ei Agar Ismaelem.
translation: Abram was four score and six years old when Agar brought him forth Ismael.

text: Pondo octoginta chiliogrammata pendit.
translation: It weighs eighty kilograms.

text: Talibus Ilioneus; cuncti simul ore fremebant / Dardanidae.
translation: He spake; the Dardans answered with a cheer.

text: Digitum in ore ne ponas quia bacteria plenum est.
translation: Do not put the finger in the mouth because it is full of bacteria.

text: Vicitque Iosue Amalec et populum eius in ore gladii.
translation: And Josue put Amalec and his people to flight, by the edge of the sword.

text: Non est bonum ore pleno loqui.
translation: It is not good to talk with your mouth full.

text: Quid habes in ore tuo?
translation: What do you have in your mouth?

text: Noli cum pleno ore loqui!
translation: Don't speak with your mouth full!

text: Mulier magnae pulchritudinis est.
translation: She is a woman of great beauty.

text: Pulchritudo causa vitae est.
translation: Beauty is the reason of life.

text: Honestum tale est ut, vel si ignorarent id homines, sua tamen pulchritudine laudabile esset.
translation: Virtue is such a thing that even if men were ignorant of it, it would still be worthy of praise for its loveliness.

text: Cum limen transgressus esset princeps, puellam magnae pulchritudinis oculis cum fuscis crispoque crine formoso conspiciebat.
translation: When the prince stepped over the threshold he caught sight of a maiden of wonderful beauty, with brown eyes and fair curly hair.

text: Pater meus quindecim annos tantum natus est.
translation: My father is only fifteen years old.

text: Quindecim minutis post septimam horam cenam sumo.
translation: I have my supper at a quarter past seven.

text: Proximo anno Canicus quindecim annos natus erit.
translation: Ken will be fifteen next year.

text: Canicus proximo anno quindecim annos natus erit.
translation: Ken will be 15 next year.

text: Cum quindecim annos natus essem, quinque linguis loqui poteram.
translation: When I was fifteen years old, I could speak five languages.

text: Cum quindecim annos nata essem, quinque linguis loqui poteram.
translation: When I was fifteen years old, I could speak five languages.

text: Certo haec mulier non sana est satis.
translation: This woman is definitely not in her right mind.

text: Num corpus aegro corde sanari potest?
translation: Can a body heal with a sick heart?

text: Mens sana in corpore sano.
translation: A sound mind dwells in a sound body.

text: Hoc medicamentum eum sanare potest.
translation: This medicine may cure him.

text: Medici multos aegrotos sanant.
translation: The doctors heal many sick people.

text: Medici multos aegros sanant.
translation: The doctors heal many sick people.

text: Paucissimi sciunt quid coetus sanguinis eorum sit.
translation: Very few people know what their blood group is.

text: Qui color est sanguinis?
translation: What is the color of the blood?

text: "Sunt et Siculis regionibus urbes / arvaque, Trojanoque a sanguine clarus Acestes".
translation: "Towns yet for us in Sicily remain, / and arms, and, sprung from Trojan sires of yore, / our kinsman there, Acestes, holds his reign."

text: Dixitque ad eum: Quid fecisti? Vox sanguinis fratris tui clamat ad me de agro.
translation: And he said to him: What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother's blood crieth to me from the earth.

text: Squalentem barbam et concretos sanguine crines, / vulneraque illa gerens, quæ circum plurima muros / accepit patrios.
translation: Foul is his beard, his hair is stiff with gore, / and fresh the wounds, those many wounds, remain, / which erst around his native walls he bore.

text: Fabulam audire totam volo, et noli transilire singulas res.
translation: I want to hear the whole story, and don't skip any details.

text: Thomas singularum rerum notitiam non habet.
translation: Tom doesn't know the details.

text: Pueri singulas birotas habent.
translation: Each boy has a bike.

text: Tanta vero Graeco vino gratia erat ut singulae potiones in convictu darentur.
translation: But Greek wine was so highly prized that only one cup was given to each guest at a banquet.

text: Omnes hi in tribubus Israel duodecim. Hæc locutus est eis pater suus benedixitque singulis benedictionibus propriis.
translation: All these are the twelve tribes of Israel: these things their father spoke to them, and he blessed every one with their proper blessings.

text: Osculatusque est Ioseph omnes fratres suos et ploravit super singulos. Post quæ ausi sunt loqui ad eum.
translation: And Joseph kissed all his brethren, and wept upon every one of them: after which they were emboldened to speak to him.

text: Thomas etiam nunc bona valetudine utitur.
translation: Tom is still in good health.

text: Thomas bona valetudine uti videtur.
translation: Tom seems to be in good health.

text: Oceani non bona valetudine utuntur.
translation: The oceans are not in good health.

text: Nonne Thomas bona valetudine utitur?
translation: Tom is in good health, isn't he?

text: Nonne Maria bona valetudine utitur?
translation: Mary is in good health, isn't she?

text: Pater meus bona valetudine utitur.
translation: My father is in good health.

text: Si ad me non veneris, veniam ad te.
translation: If you don't come to me, I'll come to you.

text: Si tu essem, veniam ab ea peterem.
translation: If I were you, I would beg for her forgiveness.

text: Cras veniam ad domum tuam.
translation: I will come tomorrow to your house.

text: Tu velim quam primum venias.
translation: Come as soon as possible.

text: Da mihi veniam, quid dixisti?
translation: Excuse me?

text: Post paucos dies veniam.
translation: I will come in a few days.

text: In ludo hodie in ludibrium versus sum.
translation: I got laughed at at school today.

text: In schola hodie in ludibrium versus sum.
translation: I got laughed at at school today.

text: Aut insanit homo, aut versus facit.
translation: Either the man is crazy or he's writing poetry.

text: Filiae meae est cubiculum verrere.
translation: Sweeping the room is my daughter's job.

text: In versūs magicōs nōn crēdō.
translation: I do not believe in magic spells.

text: Ad solem versus cucurri.
translation: I ran in the direction of the sun.

text: Vilis capsa lignea super sellam erat.
translation: A cheap wooden box was set on a chair.

text: Parva raeda vilior quam magna est.
translation: A small car is cheaper than a big one.

text: Raeda tua vilior quam mea est.
translation: Your car is cheaper than mine.

text: Haec stola vilior quam tua est.
translation: This dress is cheaper than yours.

text: Diaetae huius regionis valde viles sunt.
translation: Apartments here are really cheap.

text: Et bonus et vilis est.
translation: It is both good and cheap.

text: Elephantes in Asia et in Africa habitant.
translation: Elephants live in Asia and Africa.

text: Nilus fluvius maximus in Africa est.
translation: The Nile is the largest river in Africa.

text: Quot elephantes in Africa relicti sunt?
translation: How many elephants are left in Africa?

text: Multi in Africa Gallice loquuntur.
translation: Many people in Africa speak French.

text: Quot terrae in Āfricā sunt?
translation: How many countries are in Africa?

text: Physici poloni in Africa laborant.
translation: Polish scientists work in Africa.

text: Formicae et apes exemplaria industriae et concordiae sunt.
translation: Ants and bees are examples of industry and harmony.

text: Thomas et Maria ab apibus puncti sunt.
translation: Tom and Mary were stung by bees.

text: Cur apes servare magni momenti est?
translation: Why is it important to preserve the bees?

text: Pollen apes ex floribus colligunt.
translation: The bees collect the pollen from the flowers.

text: Omnes sciunt apes mel bibere.
translation: Everyone knows bees drink honey.

text: Non omnes apes eusociales sunt.
translation: Not all bees are eusocial.

text: Arcus sine sagittis nihil est.
translation: A bow is nothing without arrows.

text: Et confractus est arcus eorum, et dissoluti sunt nervi brachiorum eorum per manus Potentis Iacob, per nomen Pastoris, Lapidis Israel.
translation: His bow rested upon the strong, and the bands of his arms and his hands were loosed, by the hands of the mighty one of Jacob: thence he came forth a pastor, the stone of Israel.

text: Namque humeris de more habilem suspenderat arcum / venatrix dederatque comam diffundere ventis, / nuda genu nodoque sinus collecta fluentes.
translation: Bare were her knees, and from her shoulders hung / the wonted bow, kept handy for the prey / her flowing raiment in a knot she strung, / and loosed her tresses with the winds to play.

text: Utra magis tibi placent, mala an aurantia?
translation: Which do you like best—apples or oranges?

text: Mala mihi magis quam aurantia placent.
translation: I like apples more than oranges.

text: Aurantia mihi magis quam mala placent.
translation: I like oranges better than apples.

text: Aurantia super mensam non sunt.
translation: There are no oranges on the table.

text: Extrahe aurantia ex armario frigidario.
translation: Take the oranges out of the fridge.

text: Terra caerulea est ut aurantium.
translation: The Earth is blue like an orange.

text: Thomas et Maria ambo in carcere mortui sunt.
translation: Tom and Mary both died in prison.

text: Scisne cur Thomas in carcere sit?
translation: Do you know why Tom is in jail?

text: Nōlō Thōman in carcerem addūcī.
translation: I don't want Tom to go to jail.

text: Nolo te in carcerem duci.
translation: I don't want you to go to jail.

text: Numquam Thomam exspectabam carcere dimitti.
translation: I never expected Tom to get out of prison.

text: In carcere plurimos libros legi.
translation: I read a lot when I was in prison.

text: Nemo opus facit. Omnes Certamen Mundanum Pedilusorium aspiciunt.
translation: No one is working. Everyone's watching the World Cup.

text: Thōmās putat Brasiliam certāmen mundānum pedilūsōrium victūram esse.
translation: Tom thinks that Brazil will win the World Cup.

text: Certamen tenilusorium per telehorasim aspexi.
translation: I watched a tennis match on TV.

text: Certamen secunda hora pomeridiana incipit.
translation: The play begins at 2 p.m.

text: Nauticus exoritur vario certamine clamor, / hortantur socii: "Cretam proavosque petamus!"
translation: Loud rise the shouts of sailors to the sky; / "Crete and our fathers", rings for all to hear / the cry of oarsmen.

text: Duo lusores certamen reliquerunt.
translation: Two of the players left the match.

text: America a Columbo anno MCDXCII reperta est.
translation: America was discovered by Columbus in 1492.

text: America a Columbo anno millesimo quadringentesimo nonagesimo secundo reperta est.
translation: America was discovered by Columbus in 1492.

text: Rosa est flos, columba est avis.
translation: The rose is a flower and the dove is a bird.

text: Columba pacis est symbolum.
translation: The dove is a symbol of peace.

text: Illa columba sauciata est.
translation: That dove is wounded.

text: Ista columba sauciata est.
translation: That dove is wounded.

text: Die decimo mensis Octobris, anni MCMLXXII nata sum.
translation: I was born on October 10, 1972.

text: Die decimo mensis Octobris, anni MCMLXXII natus sum.
translation: I was born on October 10, 1972.

text: Thomas anno bis millesimo tertio decimo natus est.
translation: Tom was born in 2013.

text: Lintea in cubiculo quinto decimo non sunt.
translation: There are no towels in room 15.

text: Anno bis millesimo tertio decimo natus sum.
translation: I was born in 2013.

text: Mater Teresa in Iugoslavia anno millesimo nongentesimo decimo nata est.
translation: Mother Teresa was born in Yugoslavia in 1910.

text: Deinde eum ad nosocomium adduximus.
translation: After that, we took him to the hospital.

text: "Tu audi me igitur dum pronuncio prælectionem, ego audiam te deinde." "Age, pronuncia."
translation: "You listen to me then while I recite the lesson, and I will listen to you afterwards." "Go on, recite it."

text: Da mi basia mille, deinde centum, dein mille altera, dein secunda centum, deinde usque altera mille, deinde centum.
translation: Give me a thousand kisses, then a hundred, then another thousand, then a second hundred, then yet another thousand, then a hundred.

text: Deinde sepelivit Abraham Saram uxorem suam in spelunca agri Machpela, qui respiciebat Mambre hæc est Hebron­ in terra Chanaan.
translation: And so Abraham buried Sara, his wife, in the double cave of the field, that looked towards Mambre, this is Hebron in the land of Canaan.

text: Vina bonus quæ deinde cadis onerarat Acestes / litore Trinacrio dederatque abeuntibus heros, / dividit, et dictis mærentia pectora mulcet:
translation: Then opes the casks, which good Acestes, fain / at parting, filled on the Trinacrian beach, / and shares the wine, and soothes their drooping hearts with speech.

text: Quot animalia omnium generum in arca Moysi erant?
translation: How many animals of each species were there on Moses' ark?

text: Hoc flumen huic generi lintris altum satis.
translation: This river isn't deep enough for this kind of boat.

text: Silva plena avium animaliumque omnium generum est.
translation: The forest is full of birds and animals of all kinds.

text: Pecunia deus generis hominum est.
translation: Money is the god of the human race.

text: Pecunia deus humani generis.
translation: Money is the god of the human race.

text: Libros omnis generis legi.
translation: I read all kinds of books.

text: Die secundo mensis Ianuarii, anni MCMLXVIII natus sum.
translation: I was born on January 2 in 1968.

text: Die secundo mensis Ianuarii, anni MCMLXVIII nata sum.
translation: I was born on January 2 in 1968.

text: In Russia Christi Natalis VII mensis Ianuarii est.
translation: In Russia, Christmas is on the seventh of January.

text: In bibliotheca e mense Ianuario opus facio.
translation: I've been working at the library since January.

text: Ita, ianuario calet. Aestas in Brasilia est.
translation: Yes, in January it is hot. It's summer in Brazil.

text: Die secundo mensis Ianuarii, anni millesimi nongentesimi sexagesimi octavi natus sum.
translation: I was born on January 2 in 1968.

text: Incendium altum aedificium delevit.
translation: The fire destroyed the tall building.

text: Incendium tres domos delevit.
translation: The fire destroyed three houses.

text: Quis deus, o Musae, tam saeva incendia Teucris avertit? Tantos ratibus quis depulit ignes?
translation: What god, O Muses, kept such a cruel fire from the Trojans? Who prevented those terrible flames from devouring their ships?

text: Interdum domum eo ut prandium edam.
translation: I sometimes go home for lunch.

text: Invenit interdum caeca columba pisum.
translation: A blind man may perchance hit the mark.

text: Solis occasus interdum caelum rubet.
translation: The sunset sometimes turns the sky red.

text: Hæc oculis, hæc pectore toto / hæret et interdum gremio fovet, inscia Dido, / insideat quantus miseræ deus.
translation: She, fixing on the boy / her eyes, her soul, impatient to admire, / now, fondling, folds him to her lap with joy; / weetless, alas! what god is plotting to destroy.

text: Maria Iuliam sororem suam esse credebat.
translation: Mary believed that Julia was her sister.

text: Hic calamus Iuliae est.
translation: This is Julia's pen.

text: "Quousque Romae manebis?" "Usque ad Martis diem."
translation: "How long will you remain in Rome?" "Until Tuesday."

text: Praeterito Martis die Americam Foederatam invisi.
translation: Last Tuesday I visited the United States.

text: Quid interest inter Terram et Martem?
translation: What's the difference between Earth and Mars?

text: Thomas natus est in Marte.
translation: Tom was born on Mars.

text: In Marte mox habitabimus.
translation: Soon, we'll live on Mars.

text: Hodie Martis dies est.
translation: Today is Tuesday.

text: Contra malum mortis non est medicamentum in hortis.
translation: Against the evil of death, there is no remedy in the gardens.

text: Affer medicamentum eius et poculum aquae.
translation: Go get her medicine and a glass of water.

text: Hoc medicamentum ter in die sume.
translation: Take this medicine three times a day.

text: Hoc medicamentum bis in die sume.
translation: Take this medicine twice a day.

text: Medicamento eget, sed non vult.
translation: He needs a medication but doesn’t want it.

text: Medicamentum ter in die sume.
translation: Take the medicine three times a day.

text: Caelum rotatur et ambit terram, stantem in medio.
translation: The heavens rotate and encompass the earth, which stands in the middle.

text: Caelum rotatur, et ambit Terram stantem in medio.
translation: The Heaven is wheeled about and encompasses the Earth, standing in the middle.

text: Theatrum in medio stat vetus, sed omnino non malum.
translation: The theater in the center is old but it is not bad.

text: Vinum est optimum in medio dolio.
translation: Wine is best in the middle of the cask.

text: Dixit quoque Deus: Fiat firmamentum in medio aquarum et dividat aquas ab aquis.
translation: And God said: Let there be a firmament made amidst the waters: and let it divide the waters from the waters.

text: Dixitque Dominus: Si invenero Sodomæ quinquaginta iustos in medio civitas, dimittam omni loco propter eos.
translation: And the Lord said to him: If I find in Sodom fifty just within the city, I will spare the whole place for their sake.

text: In Italiam iit ut arti musicae studeret.
translation: She went to Italy to study music.

text: Nescio nomen compositoris qui hanc musicam scripsit.
translation: I do not know the name of the composer who wrote this music.

text: Tenta musicam effingere in animo tuo.
translation: Try to reproduce the music in your mind.

text: Ea et amici eius musicam amant.
translation: She and her friends love music.

text: Artem musicam et linguam Anglicam amo.
translation: I like music and English.

text: Linguam Anglicam quam artem musicam malo.
translation: I prefer English to music.

text: Cur Deus nobis omnibus nates foetidas dare statuit?
translation: Why did God decide to give us all smelly butts?

text: Thomas et Ioannes Mariae nati sunt.
translation: Tom and John are Mary's sons.

text: Non nobis solis nati sumus.
translation: We were not born only for ourselves.

text: Quā in terrā nātī estis?
translation: In what country were you born?

text: Natus nati est nepos.
translation: The child of a child is a grandchild.

text: Quō mēnse nātī estis?
translation: In what month were you born?

text: In nube pluviosa, soli opposita, apparet iris.
translation: By a rain cloud, the sun against it, appears a rainbow.

text: Umbras e nubibus in terra video.
translation: I see shadows from the clouds on the ground.

text: Aves volant sub nubibus.
translation: Birds fly under the clouds.

text: Aves volant sub Nubibus.
translation: Birds fly under the clouds.

text: Nunquam defuit columna nubis per diem, nec columna ignis per noctem, coram populo.
translation: There never failed the pillar of the cloud by day, nor the pillar of fire by night, before the people.

text: Ex vapore suphureo sit Tonitru, quod, erumpens e nube cum fulgure, tonat et fulminat.
translation: Thunder is made from a sulphurous vapour, breaking out of a cloud with lightning, thundering and striking with lightning.

text: Thomas surrexit ut solem orientem spectaret.
translation: Tom woke up to watch the sunrise.

text: Thomas surrexit ad solem orientem spectandum.
translation: Tom woke up to watch the sunrise.

text: In oriente civitatis magna taberna est.
translation: In the east of the city, there is a big store.

text: Iaponia terra orientis solis est.
translation: Japan is the land of the rising sun.

text: Cotidie solem orientem video.
translation: I see the sun rising every day.

text: Sole oriente, tenebrae fugiunt.
translation: Darkness flees at sunrise.

text: Otia corpus alunt, animus quoque pascitur illis.
translation: Rest nurtures the body and the mind.

text: In hortum publicum ivit ut aves pasceret.
translation: She went to the park to feed the birds.

text: Amabo te, pasce canem cotidie.
translation: Please feed the dog every day.

text: Canis nobis pascendus est.
translation: We need to feed the dog.

text: Mater mea canem pascit.
translation: My mother feeds the dog.

text: Duo ubera tua sicut duo hinnuli, capreae gemelli, qui pascuntur in liliis.
translation: Your two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle, which graze among the lilies.

text: Nemo perfectus est, qui perfectior esse non appetit.
translation: No one is perfect, who does not desire to be more perfect.

text: Igitur perfecti sunt cæli et terra et omnis exercitus eorum.
translation: So the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the furniture of them.

text: Terra non est sphaera perfecta.
translation: The earth is not a perfect globe.

text: In mundo perfecto sum.
translation: I'm in a perfect world.

text: Lingua Latina perfecta est.
translation: Latin is a perfect language.

text: Iudaeismus religio perfecta est.
translation: Judaism is a complete religion.

text: Potionem Arabicam sine saccharo bibere non soleo.
translation: I am not used to drinking coffee without sugar.

text: Potio Arabica cum saccharo Didymo non placet.
translation: Tom doesn't like coffee with sugar.

text: Velisne plus sacchari in coffea tua?
translation: Do you want more sugar in your coffee?

text: Potionem Sinensem sine saccharo mihi dedit.
translation: He gave me tea without sugar.

text: Potionem Arabicam sine saccharo libenter bibit.
translation: He likes drinking coffee without sugar.

text: Saccharo egeo. Habesne aliquid sacchari?
translation: I need some sugar. Do you have any?

text: Cum grano salis cena melius sapit.
translation: Supper tastes better with a pinch of salt.

text: Super piscem sal adieci et piper.
translation: I seasoned the fish with salt and pepper.

text: Minus est quam granus salis.
translation: It's smaller than a grain of salt.

text: Minor est quam granus salis.
translation: It's smaller than a grain of salt.

text: Piper nigrum, sal album est.
translation: The pepper is black and the salt is white.

text: Num sal mihi ponendum est?
translation: Do I need to add salt?

text: Haec mensa scriptoria est tam bona quam illa.
translation: This desk is as good as that one.

text: Haec mensa scriptoria est pariter bona ac illa.
translation: This desk is as good as that one.

text: Haec mensa scriptoria est aeque bona ac illa.
translation: This desk is as good as that one.

text: Haec mensa scriptoria est aeque bona atque illa.
translation: This desk is as good as that one.

text: Ad murum mensa scriptoria duo metra longa erat.
translation: By the wall there was a desk two meters long.

text: Haec mensa scriptoria e ligno facta est.
translation: This desk is made of wood.

text: Usque ad secundam vel tertiam horam mane laboravimus.
translation: We worked until two or three in the morning.

text: Thomas triginta minutis post secundam horam mortuus est.
translation: Tom died at 2:30.

text: Thomas triginta minutis post secundam horam profectus est.
translation: Tom left at 2:30.

text: Triginta minutis post secundam horam domum advenio.
translation: I come home at two thirty.

text: Thomas triginta minutis post secundam horam advenit.
translation: Tom arrived at 2:30.

text: Triginta minutis post secundam horam profecti sumus.
translation: We left at 2:30.

text: Vigiles publici eam usque ad Lutetiam secuti sunt.
translation: The police followed her all the way to Paris.

text: Puto me ab aliquo secutum fuisse.
translation: I think that I was followed by someone.

text: Maria me noctem diemque secuta est.
translation: Mary followed me night and day.

text: Nullum me secutum esse certus sum.
translation: I'm sure I wasn't followed.

text: Te noctem diemque secuti sumus.
translation: We followed you night and day.

text: Te noctem diemque secutae sumus.
translation: We followed you night and day.

text: Thomas oblitus est ubi umbellam suam reliquerit.
translation: Tom forgot where he left his umbrella.

text: Oblitus sum ubi umbellam meam posuerim.
translation: I forgot where I put my umbrella.

text: Oblita sum ubi umbellam meam posuerim.
translation: I forgot where I put my umbrella.

text: Oblitus sum ubi umbellam meam reliquerim.
translation: I forgot where I left my umbrella.

text: Oblita sum ubi umbellam meam reliquerim.
translation: I forgot where I left my umbrella.

text: Umbellae in hieme utilissimae sunt.
translation: Umbrellas are very useful when it's raining.

text: Videsne illum virum? Maritus meus est.
translation: Do you see that man? He's my husband.

text: Videsne illam feminam? Uxor mea est.
translation: Do you see that woman? She's my wife.

text: Videsne illam domum? Mea est.
translation: Do you see that house? That's my house.

text: Videsne viam in charta?
translation: Do you see the road on the map?

text: Videsne istic fumum atrum?
translation: Do you see the black smoke over there?

text: Ecce eum. Videsne eum?
translation: There he is. Do you see him?

text: Aqua viridis ad bibendum apta non est.
translation: Green water is not good for drinking.

text: Thomas aqua ab bibendum apta lagenam replevit.
translation: Tom filled the bottle with drinking water.

text: Haec aqua ad bibendum apta non est.
translation: This isn't drinking water.

text: Liberis, qui sitiunt, aqua bibenda est.
translation: Children who are thirsty should drink water.

text: Estne haec aqua ad bibendum apta?
translation: Is this drinking water?

text: Visne aliquid ad bibendum?
translation: Would you like something to drink?

text: Hoc castellum anno millesimo sescentesimo decimo aedificatum est.
translation: This castle was built in 1610.

text: Hoc castellum anno MDCX aedificatum est.
translation: This castle was built in 1610.

text: Castellum eius e ligno factum erat.
translation: His castle was made of wood.

text: Da mihi clavem huius castelli!
translation: Give me the key to this castle!

text: In castello habitare velim.
translation: I would like to live in a castle.

text: In castello habitare volo.
translation: I want to live in a castle.

text: Haec sella commodior est quam illa.
translation: This chair is more comfortable than that one.

text: Lectus meus commodior est quam tuus.
translation: My bed is more comfortable than yours.

text: Domus mea commodior est quam tua.
translation: My house is more comfortable than yours.

text: Diaeta mea commodior est quam tua.
translation: My apartment is more comfortable than yours.

text: Hae litterae ad commodum publicum pertinent.
translation: This letter concerns the public good.

text: Hae litterae ad tuum commodum pertinent.
translation: This letter is for your benefit.

text: Maria surgere conata est, neque potuit.
translation: Mary tried to stand up, but she couldn't.

text: Cūr nōn eum vocāre cōnāta es?
translation: Why have you not tried to call him?

text: Cūr nōn eum vocāre cōnātī estis?
translation: Why have you not tried to call him?

text: Cūr nōn eum vocāre cōnātae estis?
translation: Why have you not tried to call him?

text: Quotiēns hoc reficere cōnāta es?
translation: How many times have you tried to fix this?

text: Quotiēns hoc reficere cōnātī estis?
translation: How many times have you tried to fix this?

text: Non dubito quin somni cupidus sis.
translation: I'm sure you're sleepy.

text: Non dubito quin somni cupida sis.
translation: I'm sure you're sleepy.

text: Thomas se somni cupidum esse dicit.
translation: Tom says he's sleepy.

text: Maria se somni cupidam esse dicit.
translation: Mary says she's sleepy.

text: Nunc non sum cupidus edendi.
translation: I don't feel like eating anything now.

text: Infans lactis cupidus plorat.
translation: The baby is crying for milk.

text: Vita brevis est, etiamsi supra centum annos duret.
translation: Life is short, even if it lasts more than a hundred years.

text: Vita dura, ego autem durior.
translation: Life is hard, but I am harder.

text: Dura lex sed lex.
translation: The Law is harsh, but it is the Law.

text: Dura lex, sed lex.
translation: The law is harsh, but it is the law.

text: Bellum duos annos duravit.
translation: The war lasted two years.

text: Dura est mensarii vita.
translation: A banker's life is hard.

text: Grex totus in agris unius scabie cadit.
translation: One scabbed sheep infects a whole flock.

text: Grex puerorum in hortis publicis canebat.
translation: A group of children were playing in the park.

text: Dixit: Mittam tibi hædum de gregibus.
translation: He said: I will send thee a kid out of the flock.

text: Praepositus huius gregis sum.
translation: I'm the one in charge of this group.

text: Quis est dux gregis?
translation: Who is the group leader?

text: Estne in hoc grege?
translation: Is he in this group?

text: Hic articulus nimis facilis est interpretatu.
translation: This article is too easy to translate.

text: Mihi non placet longas sententias interpretari.
translation: I don't like to translate long sentences.

text: Sciresne hoc scriptum hieroglyphicum interpretari?
translation: Would you know how to translate these hieroglyphs?

text: Thomas cur acciderit interpretabitur.
translation: Tom will explain why that happened.

text: Has sententias Iaponice interpretare.
translation: Translate the following sentences into Japanese.

text: Interpretari mihi est taediosum!
translation: Translating is tedious to me!

text: Lente locutus sum ut omnes intellegere possent.
translation: I spoke slowly, so everyone could understand.

text: Lente guberno, quia bestias videre volumus.
translation: I'm driving slowly because we want to see the animals.

text: Thomas lente de sella surrexit.
translation: Tom slowly rose from his chair.

text: Lentes inserticias meas quaero.
translation: I'm looking for my contact lens.

text: Invenistine lentes oculares tuas?
translation: Did you find your contact lenses?

text: Lente e sellis surgebant.
translation: They slowly rose from their chairs.

text: Thomas a rege poena liberatus est.
translation: Tom was pardoned by the king.

text: Rex eum poena liberavit.
translation: The king freed him from punishment.

text: Et ait: Benedictus Dominus, qui liberavit vos de manu Aegyptiorum et de manu pharaonis.
translation: And he said: Blessed is the Lord, who hath delivered his people out of the hand of Egypt.

text: Audiens autem hoc Ruben nitebatur liberare eum de manibus eorum et dixit: Non interficiamus animam eius.
translation: And Ruben hearing this, endeavoured to deliver him out of their hands, and said: Do not take away his life.

text: Responderunt: Vir Aegyptius liberavit nos de manu pastorum; insuper et hausit aquam nobis potumque dedit ovibus.
translation: They answered: A man of Egypt delivered us from the hands of the shepherds: and he drew water also with us, and gave the sheep to drink.

text: Cum enim subverteret Deus civitates regionis illius, recordatus Abrahæ liberavit Lot de subversione urbium, in quibus habitaverat.
translation: Now when God destroyed the cities of that country, remembering Abraham, he delivered Lot out of the destruction of the cities wherein he had dwelt.

text: Suntne lingua lusitanica et lingua callaeca eadem lingua?
translation: Are Portuguese and Galician the same language?

text: Lingua Lusitanica e Latina oriunda est.
translation: Portuguese descends from Latin.

text: Linguam Lusitanicam duos menses didici.
translation: I have studied Portuguese for two months.

text: Quamdiu Georgius linguam Lusitanicam didicit?
translation: How long has George studied Portuguese?

text: Potesne me linguam Lusitanicam docere?
translation: Can you teach me Portuguese?

text: Paulus Lusitanice bene non loquitur.
translation: Paul doesn't speak Portuguese well.

text: Nimis multi pueri in piscina erant.
translation: There were too many children in the pool.

text: Noli lapides in piscinam deicere.
translation: Don't throw stones into the swimming pool.

text: Nolite lapides in piscinam deicire.
translation: Don't throw stones into the swimming pool.

text: Canis meus in piscina natat.
translation: My dog is swimming in the pool.

text: Aestate ad piscinam cotidie eo.
translation: In the summer I go to the pool every day.

text: Piscina in medio horto est.
translation: There is a pond in the middle of the park.

text: "Quousque Novi Eboraci manebis?" "Usque ad Saturni diem."
translation: "How long will you remain in New York?" "Until Saturday."

text: "Quousque Londinii manebis?" "Usque ad Lunae diem."
translation: "How long will you remain in London?" "Until Monday."

text: "Quousque Lutetiae manebis?" "Usque ad Mercurii diem."
translation: "How long will you remain in Paris?" "Until Wednesday."

text: "Quousque Bostoniae manebis?" "Usque ad Iovis diem."
translation: "How long will you remain in Boston?" "Until Thursday."

text: "Quousque Tokii manebis?" "Usque ad Veneris diem."
translation: "How long will you remain in Tokyo?" "Until Friday."

text: "Quousque Moscoviae manebis?" "Usque ad Solis diem."
translation: "How long will you remain in Moscow?" "Until Sunday."

text: Pater meus domum heri vesperi serius venit.
translation: My father got home late last night.

text: Sera nimis vita est crastina: vive hodie.
translation: Life doesn't wait. Tomorrow will be too late. Live today.

text: Nulla ætas ad discendum sera.
translation: It is never too late to learn.

text: Hoc in agro hordeum seretur.
translation: Barley will be planted in this field.

text: Hoc in agro oryza seretur.
translation: Rice will be planted in this field.

text: Quid hoc in agro seretur?
translation: What will be planted in this field?

text: Bibuntne homines theam in terra tua?
translation: Do people drink tea in your country?

text: In culīnā sedent et theam bibunt.
translation: They are sitting in the kitchen and drinking tea.

text: In thea mea non est saccharum.
translation: There's no sugar in my tea.

text: Theam cum lacte numquam bibo.
translation: I never drink tea with milk.

text: Ubi est thea cum lacte?
translation: Where is the tea with milk?

text: Da mihi, quaeso, poculum theae.
translation: A cup of tea, please.

text: In ludo hodie in ludibrium versa sum.
translation: I got laughed at at school today.

text: Ille aeger in vitae discrimine versatur.
translation: That sick person's life is in danger.

text: Fere cotidie in athletica versor.
translation: I practice sport almost every day.

text: Esne versatus in re publica?
translation: Are you involved in politics?

text: Etiam nunc in egestate versor.
translation: I'm still living in poverty.

text: Quālī in perīculō versāmur?
translation: What sort of danger are we in?

text: Porrexitque Abram de mansione in mansionem usque ad Nageb.
translation: And Abram went forward, going and proceeding on to the south.

text: Peperitque Agar Abræ filium; qui vocavit nomen filii sui, quem peperat Agar, Ismael.
translation: And Agar brought forth a son to Abram: who called his name Ismael.

text: Flagellavit autem Dominus pharaonem plagis maximis et domum eius propter Sarai uxorem Abram.
translation: But the Lord scourged Pharaoh and his house with most grievous stripes for Sarai, Abram's wife.

text: Addiditque Abram: En mihi non dedisti semen, et ecce vernaculus meus heres meus erit.
translation: And Abram added: But to me thou hast not given seed: and lo my servant born in my house shall be my heir.

text: Pertransivit Abram terram usque ad locum Sichem, usque ad Quercum Moreh. Chananæus autem tunc erat in terra.
translation: Abram passed through the country unto the place of Sichem, as far as the noble vale: now the Canaanite was at that time in the land.

text: Facta est autem fames in terra; descenditque Abram in Aegyptum, ut peregrinaretur ibi; prævaluerat enim fames in terra.
translation: And there came a famine in the country: and Abram went down into Egypt, to sojourn there: for the famine was very grievous in the land.

text: Puer patrem adorabat, sed matrem paulum timebat.
translation: The boy adored his father, but he was a little afraid of his mother.

text: Quod cum audisset puer Abraham, procidens adoravit in terram Dominum.
translation: Which when Abraham's servant heard, falling down to the ground, he adored the Lord.

text: Genibus flexis Sami Deo adorabat.
translation: Sami was on his knees, praying to God.

text: Cumque tulisset eos Ioseph de gremio patris, adoravit pronus in terram.
translation: And when Joseph had taken them from his father's lap, he bowed down with his face to the ground.

text: Thomas adorator felium est.
translation: Tom is a cat worshiper.

text: Et ipse prægrediens adoravit pronus in terram septies, donec appropinquaret ad fratrem suum.
translation: And he went forward and bowed down with his face to the ground seven times, until his brother came near.

text: Vicus est inter flumen et collem.
translation: There is a village between the river and the hill.

text: Ludus noster in colle situs est.
translation: Our school stands on a hill.

text: Aspice aedificium super collem stantem.
translation: Look at that building standing on the hill.

text: Mola venti in colle est.
translation: There is a windmill on the hill.

text: Ludus in colle situs est.
translation: The school is on a hill.

text: Est domus in colle.
translation: There is a house on the hill.

text: Separationes nullae sunt. Unum conscientia omnes et omnia coniungit.
translation: There are no separations. One single Consciousness unites everyone and everything.

text: Ita conscientia omnes timidos facit.
translation: Thus conscience does make cowards of us all.

text: Cur tantum spatium in hoc mundo et in conscientia nostra est? Unde hoc omne spatium infinitum?
translation: Why is there so much room in this universe and within our consciousness? Where did all this infinite space come from?

text: Mihi pergratum feceris si cum consilio meo consenseris.
translation: I would appreciate it if you could agree to my plan.

text: Non possum tecum consentire de hoc loco.
translation: I cannot agree with you on this point.

text: Tecum consentire de ea re non possum.
translation: I cannot agree with you on the matter.

text: Propterea tecum consentire non possum.
translation: That's why I can't agree with you.

text: Dīcit sē cum eā cōnsentīre.
translation: He says that he agrees with her.

text: Dīcit sē cum eō cōnsentīre.
translation: She says that she agrees with him.

text: Num pater tuus est contentus?
translation: Your father isn’t content, is he?

text: Thomas se contentum esse dixit.
translation: Tom said that he was pleased.

text: Perpetuo contendere non valeo.
translation: I don't have the strength to keep trying.

text: Thomas nunquam contentus fuit.
translation: Tom never was contented.

text: Defessi Aeneadæ, quæ proxima litora, cursu / contendunt petere, et Libyæ vertuntur ad oras.
translation: Tired out, the Trojans seek the nearest land / and turn to Libya.

text: Responditque universus populus simul: Cuncta, quæ locutus est Dominus, faciemus.
translation: And all the people answered together: All that the Lord hath spoken, we will do.

text: Vade et vide, si cuncta prospera sint erga fratres tuos et pecora, et renuntia mihi quid agatur.
translation: He said to him: Go, and see if all things be well with thy brethren, and the cattle: and bring me word again what is doing.

text: Nuntiate patri meo universam gloriam meam in Aegypto et cuncta, quæ vidistis. Festinate et adducite eum ad me.
translation: You shall tell my father of all my glory, and all things that you have seen in Egypt: make haste and bring him to me.

text: Non quia cunctas gentes numero vincebatis, vobis junctus est Dominus, et elegit vos, cum omnibus sitis populis pauciores.
translation: The LORD did not set his love upon you, nor choose you, because ye were more in number than any people; for ye were the fewest of all people.

text: Sella quoque genuit Tubalcain, qui fuit malleator et faber in cuncta opera æris et ferri. Soror vero Tubalcain Noema.
translation: Sella also brought forth Tubalcain, who was a hammerer and artificer in every work of brass and iron. And the sister of Tubalcain was Noema.

text: Vir quem amicum esse putaveram me decepit.
translation: The man who I thought was my friend deceived me.

text: Fistula dulce canit, volucrem dum decepit auceps.
translation: To fright a bird is not the way to catch it.

text: Iacob autem decepit cor Laban, non indicans ei quod fugeret.
translation: And Jacob would not confess to his father-in-law that he was flying away.

text: Decipiunt multos favor principis, muliebris amor, aprile serenum, labile folium rosae.
translation: A woman's mind and winter's wind change oft.

text: Et dixit Dominus Deus ad mulierem: “Quid hoc fecisti?” Quæ respondit: “Serpens decepit me, et comedi”.
translation: And the Lord God said to the woman: Why hast thou done this? And she answered: The serpent deceived me, and I did eat.

text: Et dixit ad Iacob: Quare ita egisti et decepisti cor meum, abigens filias meas quasi captivas gladio?
translation: And he said to Jacob: Why hast thou done thus, to carry away, without my knowledge, my daughters as captives taken with the sword?

text: Oculos numquam de illius facie deiecit.
translation: He kept his eyes fixed on her face.

text: Oculos nusquam de illius facie deiecit.
translation: He kept his eyes fixed on her face.

text: Didymus in aquae deiectu lavatus est.
translation: Tom took a shower.

text: Tum in aquae deiectu lavabar.
translation: I was taking a shower then.

text: Nunc in aquae deiectu lavor.
translation: I'm taking a shower right now.

text: Thomas, diu in aquae deiectu lavatus, tota aqua calida usus est.
translation: Tom had a long shower and used all the hot water.

text: Deversorium in quo habitat in media urbe est.
translation: The hotel he's living in is downtown.

text: "Estne deversorium bonum?" "Est, sed valde procul."
translation: "Is it a good hotel?" "Yes, but it is too far away."

text: Ad deversorium una abhinc hora advenimus.
translation: We arrived at the hotel one hour ago.

text: Hoc deversorium praeterito anno aedificatum est.
translation: This hotel was built last year.

text: Deversorium ad solum exustum est.
translation: The hotel was burned to the ground.

text: Deversorium in colle situm est.
translation: The hotel stands on a hill.

text: Devorabat ille igitur suas fabas solus?
translation: Did he eat his beans by himself then?

text: Extendisti manum tuam, devoravit eos terra.
translation: Thou stretchedst forth thy hand, and the earth swallowed them.

text: Piscis ab aquilā dēvorātus est.
translation: The fish was devoured by the eagle.

text: Canis a serpente devoratus est.
translation: The dog was devoured by the snake.

text: Lupus oves etiam numeratas devorat.
translation: Worry about your sheep, and the wolf will worry them.

text: Accipe librum et devora illum.
translation: Take the book and devour it.

text: Illud vocābulum difficillimum est trānslātū.
translation: That word is very difficult to translate.

text: Difficillimum est eam intellegere.

text: Difficillimum est tē intellegere.
translation: It's very difficult to understand you.

text: Difficillimum est vōs intellegere.

translation: The fruit of this tree is not to be eaten.

translation: He brushes his teeth after his meals.

text: Aliquid tibi edendum est.
translation: You have to eat something.

translation: I was what you are, you'll be what I am.

text: Quod tu es, eqo fui, quod ego sum, tu eris.
translation: What you are, I once was; what I am, you will become.

text: Ubi eris, cum mundus decidebit?
translation: Where will you be when the world ends?

text: Quantum habebis, tantus eris.
translation: However much you have, you will want more.

text: donec eris felix, multos numerabis amicos, tempora si fuerint nubila, solus eris
translation: When I was happy, I had many friends. When times were gray, I found myself alone.

text: Tales res tibi obtingere possunt cum festinas.
translation: That sort of thing can happen when you're in a hurry.

text: Hic erat, sed cito discessit quia festinabat.
translation: He was here but left soon because he was in a hurry.

text: Festinemus ut currum publicum praevertamus.
translation: Let's hurry so we can catch the bus.
