text: Hic liber maximi momenti est.
translation: This book is very interesting.

text: Opus meum maximi momenti est.
translation: My work is very important.

text: Nescio cur id tam mirum tibi videatur.
translation: I don't know why you find that so surprising.

text: Mirum est eum hoc non cognovisse.
translation: It is surprising that he should not know this.

text: Quonam modo delphini audiant, mirum.
translation: I wonder how dolphins can hear.

text: Radix mire unguentis expetitur.
translation: This root is highly sought after for perfumes.

text: Liber donum mirum est.
translation: A book is a wonderful gift.

text: Senex scit se mox moriturum esse.
translation: The old man knows that he will die soon.

text: Ubi es, Thoma? Hic moritura sum!
translation: Tom, where are you? I'm dying here.

text: Praeses dixit se pro patriam moriturum.
translation: The president said that he would die for his country.

text: Non credo te hodie moriturum esse.
translation: I don't think you'll die today.

text: Non credo te hodie morituram esse.
translation: I don't think you'll die today.

text: Thomas me moriturum esse dixit.
translation: Tom said that I was going to die.

text: "Potesne dare mutuo mihi aliquantulum pecuniæ?" "Quantum petis?"
translation: "Can you lend me a little money?" "How much are you asking for?"

text: Tatoebae maxima virtus est mutua eius operatio.
translation: Tatoeba's greatest virtue is its interactivity.

text: Erat ibi valde sonus, et non audiebamus nos mutuo.
translation: It was very noisy there, and we did not hear each other.

text: Potesne dare mutuo mihi aliquantulum pecuniae?
translation: Can you lend me a little money?

text: "Quid si forte eguero, dabisne mutuo?" "Dabo mutuo, et libenter quidem." "Ago tibi gratias."
translation: "What if I happen to need something, will you give me a loan?" "I will gladly lend something to you." "Thank you."

text: Surgentesque mane iuraverunt sibi mutuo. Dimisitque eos Isaac, et profecti sunt ab eo cum pace.
translation: Arising in the morning, they swore one to another: and Isaac sent them away peaceably to their own home.

text: Thomas se opinatur fortiorem quam ego esse.
translation: Tom thinks he's stronger than me.

text: Opinor nomen Macci audi tum aliquot vestrum.
translation: I suppose the name of Maccus has been heard by some of you.

text: "Tenesne nunc?" "Opinor sic, faciam periculum, si vis audire me."
translation: "Do you remember it now?" "I think so, I will make an attempt at it, if you will listen to me."

text: Non opinor posse fieri.
translation: I don't think it's possible.

text: Hoc fieri posse opinor.
translation: I guess that's possible.

text: A: Non repetes Neptunum posthac, opinor. B. Non nisi Deus adimat sanam mentem mihi.
translation: A: You will not go again to sea hereafter, I suppose. B: Not unless God take away my wits from me.

text: Cur non dedisti osculum ei?
translation: Why didn't you kiss her?

text: Thomas feli suae osculum dedit.
translation: Tom kissed his cat.

text: Maria feli suae osculum dedit.
translation: Mary kissed her cat.

text: Repentine mihi osculum dedit.
translation: She suddenly kissed me.

text: Plurimis defectibus non obstantibus, omnes eum amant.
translation: Despite all his faults, everybody likes him.

text: Terra Israel plurimis Iudaeis magni momenti est.
translation: The Land of Israel is important to most Jews.

text: Plurima qui tenet, plura tenere cupit.
translation: Those who possess many things desire to possess even more.

text: Plurimi homines credunt me esse delirum.
translation: Most people think I'm crazy.

text: At ille: Habeo, ait, plurima, frater mi; sint tua tibi.
translation: But he said: I have plenty, my brother, keep what is thine for thyself.

text: Itinera nivibus plurimis impedita sunt.
translation: The roads are impassable because of the heavy snow.

text: Tibi pollicitus sum me ad horam perventurum esse.
translation: I promised you that I'd arrive on time.

text: Quid pollicitus es te facturum esse?
translation: What did you promise that you would do?

text: Pollicitus sum me ei litteras missurum.
translation: I promised that I would send him a letter.

text: De illa re tantum habeo polliceri.
translation: On the subject, I can only promise.

text: Id quod pollicitus erat praestitit.
translation: He remained true to what he had promised.

text: Polliceor me hoc facturum esse.
translation: I promise I'll do that.

text: Si Thomas sanus est, problema non est.
translation: If Tom is healthy, there's no problem.

text: Problema meum idem est ac problema eius.
translation: My problem is the same as his.

text: Cupio ut omnia mihi problemata eiciantur.
translation: I wish all my problems would go away.

text: Problema meum idem est ac tuum.
translation: My problem is the same as yours.

text: Nemo hoc problema solvere potest.
translation: Nobody can solve this problem.

text: Thomas non est problema meum.
translation: Tom isn't my problem.

text: Rana quae in puteo habitat nescit mare esse.
translation: A frog in a well doesn't know the ocean.

text: Hic puteus valde altus est.
translation: This well is very deep.

text: Hic puteus altissimus est.
translation: This well is very deep.

text: Et increpavit Abraham Abimelech propter puteum aquæ, quem vi abstulerant servi eius.
translation: And he reproved Abimelech for a well of water, which his servants had taken away by force.

text: Isaac autem venerat a regione putei Lahairoi et habitabat in terra Nageb.
translation: At the same time, Isaac was walking along the way to the well which is called Of the living and the seeing: for he dwelt in the south country.

text: Et post obitum illius benedixit Deus Isaac filio eius, qui habitabat iuxta puteum Lahairoi.
translation: And after his death, God blessed Isaac his son, who dwelt by the well named Of the living and seeing.

text: Sumerica est lingua scripta antiquissima in mundo.
translation: Sumerian is the oldest written language in the world.

text: Scio, vita mea male scripta est.
translation: I know, my life is poorly written.

text: Scripta eius in regem contumeliosa fuerunt.
translation: His writings were insulting to the king.

text: Epistula a Didymo scripta est.
translation: The letter was written by Tom.

text: A Taro Acagava scripta est.
translation: That was written by Taro Akagawa.

text: Epistula a Guilielmo scripta est.
translation: The letter was written by Bill.

text: Quid in summō monte sit, nesciō.
translation: I don't know what's on top of the mountain.

text: Suntne arbores in summo monte?
translation: Are there trees on top of the mountain?

text: Arbores in summo monte sunt.
translation: There are trees on top of the mountain.

text: Estne nix in summo monte?
translation: Is there snow on top of the mountain?

text: Nix in summo monte est.
translation: There's snow on top of the mountain.

text: Poculum a summo plenum est.
translation: The cup is filled to the brim.

text: Primum ad argentariam eo. Tum tesseras emam.
translation: First I'll go to the bank, and then I'll buy the tickets.

text: Tesseram aeream meam invenire non possum.
translation: I can't find my plane ticket.

text: Haec perdunt hominem: vinum, femina, tesserae.
translation: Gaming, women, and wine, while they laugh, they make men pine.

text: Quanti constat tessera currus publici?
translation: How much is the bus fare?

text: Tesseram meam invenire non possum.
translation: I can't find my ticket.

text: Tesseram meam iam ēmī.
translation: I've already bought my ticket.

text: Quis amicorum tuorum veniet?
translation: Who out of your friends will come?

text: Miseret me filiorum tuorum.
translation: I feel sorry for your kids.

text: Miseret me liberorum tuorum.
translation: I feel sorry for your kids.

text: Miseret me parentium tuorum.
translation: I feel sorry for your parents.

text: Vulnerasti cor meum in uno oculorum tuorum, et in uno crine colli tui.
translation: Thou hast ravished my heart with one of thine eyes, with one chain of thy neck.

text: Et dixit Dominus ad Iacob: Revertere in terram patrum tuorum et ad cognationem tuam, eroque tecum.
translation: Especially the Lord saying to him: Return into the land of thy fathers and to thy kindred, and I will be with thee.

text: Vexillum rectum non est. Id muta, quaeso.
translation: The flag is not right. Please change it.

text: Hoc vexillum Civitatium Foederatarum Americae in Sinis factum est.
translation: This American flag is made in China.

text: Vexillum Brasiliae quattuor colores continet: viridis, flavus, caeruleus, albus.
translation: The flag of Brazil has four colors: green, yellow, blue and white.

text: Quinquaginta stellae in vexillo Americano sunt.
translation: There are fifty stars on the American flag.

text: Quindecim sunt stellae in vexillo Americano.
translation: There are fifty stars in the American flag.

text: Vexillum nostrum caeruleum et album est.
translation: Our flag is blue and white.

text: Hodie in ludum ire non possum. Aegroto.
translation: I can't go to school today. I'm sick.

text: In ludum ire non possum, quod aegroto.
translation: I can't go to school today because I'm sick.

text: Aegroto dum anima est, spes est.
translation: To the sick, while there is life, there is hope.

text: Quid mihi accidit? Num aegroto?
translation: What happened to me? Am I sick?

text: Omnes aegroti tandem mortui sunt.
translation: All the patients eventually died.

text: Audi Robertum aegrotum esse.
translation: I heard that Robert is ill.

text: Urbe capta, Aeneas fugit.
translation: When the city had been captured, Aeneas fled.

text: Jam pater Aeneas et jam Trojana juventus / conveniunt, stratoque super discumbitur ostro.
translation: There, flocking in, the Trojans and their King / recline on purple coverlets outspread.

text: Conticuere omnes, intentique ora tenebant. / Inde toro pater Aeneas sic orsus ab alto:
translation: All hushed intent, when from his lofty seat / Troy's sire began:

text: "Tune ille Aeneas quem Dardanio Anchisae / alma Venus Phrygii genuit Simoentis ad undam?"
translation: "Art thou, then, that AEneas, whom of yore / Venus on Simois' banks to old Anchises bore?"

text: "Ecquid in antiquam virtutem animosque viriles / et pater Aeneas et avunculus excitat Hector?"
translation: "Doth the name / of sire or uncle make his young heart glow / for deeds of valour and ancestral fame?"

text: Ubi emas aliena, cave ne vendas tua.
translation: He that buys what he does not want, must often sell what he does want.

text: Nonne quasi alienas reputavit nos et vendidit nos comeditque pretium nostrum?
translation: Hath he not counted us as strangers, and sold us, and eaten up the price of us?

text: Quæ peperit ei filium, quem vocavit Gersam dicens: Advena sum in terra aliena.
translation: And she bore him a son, whom he called Gersam, saying: I have been a stranger in a foreign country.

text: Deus creator est. Et Caelum et Terra et homines omniaque a Deo aliena creata sunt.
translation: God is the creator. Heaven and Earth and people and everything apart from God are created.

text: Anna e Paraquaria oriunda est. Paraquariana est.
translation: Ana is from Paraguay. She is Paraguayan.

text: Nomen eius non Carmen, sed Anna est.
translation: Her name's not Carmen, it's Anna.

text: Anna tribus annis in Germania egit.
translation: Anna spent three years in Germany.

text: Anna hoc mihi dono dedit.
translation: Anna gave this to me as a present.

text: Anna mihi hoc donum dedit.
translation: Ann gave me this present.

text: Anna sorori meae similis est.
translation: Anna looks like my sister.

text: Heu! Ab ape puncta sum!
translation: Ouch! I was stung by a bee.

text: Ubi tē apis pupugit?
translation: Where did the bee sting you?

text: Ab ape punctus sum.
translation: I was stung by a bee.

text: Ab ape puncta sum.
translation: I was stung by a bee.

text: Apis avis non est.
translation: A bee is not a bird.

text: Qualis apis te pupugit?
translation: What bee has stung you?

text: Bibi per eos insigniter bonam cerevisiam.
translation: I drank extraordinarily good beer from them.

text: Duo amici septem cerevisias simul biberunt.
translation: The two friends drank seven beers together.

text: Et cerevisiam et vinum libenter bibo.
translation: I like drinking beer and wine.

text: Convivae cerevisiam et vinum bibunt.
translation: The guests are drinking beer and wine.

text: Cerevisiam in taberna potoria bibunt.
translation: They're at the bar drinking beer.

text: Nolo, gratias. Cerevisiam non bibo.
translation: No, thanks. I don't drink beer.

text: Nocte citius laboraturum, quam ut cum Thoma laborem.
translation: I'd rather work night shift than work with Tom.

text: Si citius locutus essem, num alius eventus fuisset?
translation: If I'd spoken up sooner, would the result have been different?

text: Hoc te oportet quam citissime agere.
translation: You'd better do that in a hurry.

text: Omnes moriemur, alii citius, alii serius.
translation: We all die sooner or later.

text: Omnes moriemur, alii citius alii serius.
translation: We will all die, some quickly, others will take their time.

text: Dicunt Terram se citius circumagere.
translation: They say the Earth is spinning faster.

text: Thomas nesciebat unum hominem in conclavi.
translation: Tom didn't know a single person in the room.

text: In hoc conclavi fumare non licet.
translation: Smoking is prohibited in this room.

text: Thomas reliquas sarcinas in conclave portavit.
translation: Tom carried the rest of his luggage up to his room.

text: Canis in illud conclave est.
translation: There is a dog in this room.

text: Potesne mihi aliud conclave monstrare?
translation: Can you show me another room?

text: Nemo in conclavi scholari est.
translation: There's no one in the classroom.

text: Universalis actio conscientiae absolutae in omni ente pulsat.
translation: The universal activity of absolute consciousness pulsates in every being.

text: Hypothesis alicuius programmatis ad operandum capax conscientiae plene excluditur.
translation: The hypothesis of some software capable of functioning as conscience can be completely ruled out.

text: Conscientiam tuam nemo curat.
translation: No one cares about your conscience.

text: Haec est quaestio conscientiae.
translation: This is a question of conscience.

text: Vita est status conscientiae.
translation: Life is a state of consciousness.

text: Num bestiae conscientiam habent?
translation: Do animals have a conscience?

text: Mala erat sententia mea, sed magister correxit.
translation: My sentence was wrong, but the teacher corrected it.

text: Exercitia tua corrigere possum, si vis.
translation: If you'd like, I can correct your exercises.

text: Thomas animadvertit picturam pendentem in pariete transversam et ita corrigit.
translation: Tom noticed the picture hanging on the wall was crooked, so he straightened it.

text: Error corrigitur ubi deprehenditur.
translation: Errors are corrected where detected.

text: Exercitia tua non corrigam.
translation: I'm not correcting your exercises.

text: Exercitia eorum non corrigo.
translation: I don't correct their exercises.

text: Consilium eius mihi prospere eveniendi facultatem dedit.
translation: Because of his advice, I was able to succeed.

text: Thomae ad id faciendum facultatem concessi.
translation: I gave Tom an opportunity to do that.

text: Finis studii sui foris esse videtur ut facultatem Anglice loquendi emendare possit.
translation: It seems that the purpose of his study abroad was to improve his ability to speak English.

text: Lingua Latina mihi quidem non ignota est, sed loquendi facultate omnino careo.
translation: The Latin language is not entirely unknown to me, but I altogether lack the ability to speak it.

text: Duodecima hora placentam Neapolitanam et gallinaceam edimus.
translation: We've eaten pizza and chicken at noon.

text: Thomas pullum gallinaceum in furno posuit.
translation: Tom put the chicken in the oven.

text: Pullum gallinaceum in furno posuit.
translation: She put the chicken in the oven.

text: Bubula carior est quam gallinacea.
translation: Beef is more expensive than chicken.

text: Pullus gallinaceus in culina est.
translation: The chicken is in the kitchen.

text: Quot pullī gallīnāceī tibi sunt?
translation: How many chickens do you have?

text: Capilli tui sicut greges caprarum quae ascenderunt de monte Galaad.
translation: Your hair is like a herd of goats, spreading over the slopes of Mount Gilead.

text: Greges avium in Africam migrant.
translation: Flocks of birds migrate to Africa.

text: At ille respondit: Fratres meos quæro; indica mihi, ubi pascant greges.
translation: But he answered: I seek my brethren, tell me where they feed the flocks.

text: Sed et Lot, qui erat cum Abram, fuerunt greges ovium et armenta et tabernacula.
translation: But Lot also, who was with Abram, had flocks of sheep, and herds of beasts, and tents.

text: Adhuc loquebatur cum eis, et ecce Rachel veniebat cum ovibus patris sui; nam gregem ipsa pascebat.
translation: They were yet speaking, and behold Rachel came with her father's sheep; for she fed the flock.

text: At ille respondit: Tu nosti quomodo servierim tibi et quanti in manibus meis facti sint greges tui.
translation: But he answered: Thou knowest how I have served thee, and how great thy possession hath been in my hands.

text: Proficiscemur tertio die ante idus Iunias.
translation: We are leaving on the eleventh of June.

text: In calendario romano, hodie ante diem quartum idus Maias erat.
translation: In the Roman calendar, today was the fourth day before the Ides of May.

text: Natalis Mariae idus Ianuarias est.
translation: Mary's birthday is the thirteenth of January.

text: Thomas et Maria cognoscunt se invicem ab die sexto ante idus Maias anno MMVI.
translation: Tom and Mary met each other on May 10th, 2006.

text: Quae te causa impulit ut huc venires?
translation: What brought you here?

text: Quid te in tantum furorem impulit?
translation: What made you so furious?

text: Thomas Mariam in furorem impulit.
translation: Tom made Mary furious.

text: Ea me in furorem impulit.
translation: She made me furious.

text: His rebus impulsus, litteras longas prima nocte ad patrem amici mittit.
translation: Excited by these things, he sends his friend's father a long letter by nightfall.

text: Eum in furorem impulit.
translation: She made him furious.

text: Quid dies ferat incertum est.
translation: What the day may bring is uncertain.

text: Mors certa, hora incerta.
translation: Death is certain, only the time is not certain.

text: Pater semper incertus est.
translation: The father is always uncertain.

text: Thomas adhuc incertus est.
translation: Tom is still uncertain.

text: Multa adhuc incerta sunt.
translation: Much is still uncertain.

text: Futurum nostrum incertum est.
translation: Our future is uncertain.

text: Universum quanto magis videtur intelligi, magis videtur esse vacuum.
translation: The more the universe seems comprehensible, the more it seems meaningless.

text: Sine experimentis et mathematicis nunquam id quod intelligimus intelleximus.
translation: Without experiments and mathematics, we would never have understood what we understand.

text: Intelligere recte, agere recte, et eloqui recte omnia necessaria.
translation: To understand rightly, to do rightly, and to speak out rightly all that are necessary.

text: Nimis celeriter loqueris et non possum omnia quae dicis intelligere.
translation: You talk too fast and I can't understand everything you say.

text: Cum cito loqueris, intelligam.
translation: When you speak fast, I can understand.

text: Se censent feminas intelligere.
translation: They think they understand women.

text: Ioci instar ovium, non instar canum mordere debent.
translation: Good jests bite like lambs, not like dogs.

text: Spero Thoman et Mariam per iocum dixisse.
translation: I hope that Tom and Mary were joking.

text: Haec dixit Thomas per iocum.
translation: Tom said it as a joke.

text: Ut Tannina ridetur facere non possum. Ioci mei ei non placet.
translation: I cannot make Taninna laugh. She doesn't like my jokes.

text: Thōmās iocum Marīae nōn intellēxit.
translation: Tom didn't understand Mary's joke.

text: Paulus semper benefacit iocus.
translation: A little bit of fun is always good.

text: Dydimus laetus erat quod Maria non irata ei.
translation: Tom was happy that Mary was not angry with him.

text: Ita irata erat ut loqui non potuerit.
translation: She was so angry that she could not speak.

text: Thomas et Maria etiamnunc irati sunt.
translation: Tom and Mary are still angry.

text: Thōmās Marīam īrātam esse dīxit.
translation: Tom said that Mary was angry.

text: Uxor mea valde irata est.
translation: My wife is very upset.

text: Thomas dixit Mariam iratam esse.
translation: Tom said Mary was mad.

text: "Graecene loqueris?" "Ita, tantum paululum Graece loquor."
translation: “Do you speak Greek? "Yes, I speak a little Greek, very little."

text: Americanus sum, sed paululum Iaponice loquor.
translation: I'm American, but I can speak Japanese a little.

text: Americana sum, sed paululum Iaponice loquor.
translation: I'm American, but I can speak Japanese a little.

text: Caseum et paululum lactis emi.
translation: I bought some cheese and a little milk.

text: Didymus tantum paululum Gallice loquitur.
translation: Tom can speak just a little French.

text: Is paululum Anglice loqui potest.
translation: He can speak a little English.

text: Semel in hebdomade commentarii periodici eduntur.
translation: The magazine comes out once a week.

text: Hi comentarii periodici huius mensis sunt.
translation: It's this month's magazine.

text: Visne hos commentarios periodicos legere?
translation: Do you want to read this magazine?

text: Mater mea commentarios periodicos legit.
translation: My mother is reading a magazine.

text: Dum edo, commentarios periodicos lego.
translation: I read a newspaper while eating.

text: Ubi commentarios periodicos emere possum?
translation: Where can I buy a magazine?

text: Mihi satis persuasum est me Thomae non placere.
translation: I'm pretty sure that Tom doesn't like me.

text: Mihi persuadeo eum hoc non consulto fecisse.
translation: I'm sure he didn't do that on purpose.

text: Thomas his verbis Mariam tandem persuasit.
translation: Tom finally persuaded Mary with these words.

text: Maria his verbis Thoman tandem persuasit.
translation: Mary finally persuaded Tom with these words.

text: Ei persuasi ut venderet domum suam.
translation: I talked him into selling his house.

text: His verbis me non persuadebis.
translation: You will not persuade me with these words.

text: Is sum qui tabulam hanc pinxi.
translation: It is me that painted this picture.

text: Pictor agricolam in pictura pingit.
translation: The painter paints a farmer in the picture.

text: Scio eum pingere posse.
translation: I know that he can draw.

text: Pictores picturas pulchras pingunt.
translation: The painters paint pretty pictures.

text: Picturas topiarias saepe pingit.
translation: He often paints landscapes.

text: Pinge omnia quae vidisti.
translation: Draw everything you saw.

text: Haec poma rubra sunt alicui.
translation: These red apples belong to someone.

text: Et poma et panem edit.
translation: She's eating fruit and bread.

text: Noli poma fricta mea edere.
translation: Don't eat my french fries.

text: Poma fricta mihi valde placent.
translation: I love French fries.

text: Poma edo, quia esurio.
translation: I'm eating fruits because I'm hungry.

text: Musae genus pomi sunt.
translation: Bananas are a kind of fruit.

text: Die decimo quarto mensis Februarii, anni MCMLX natus sum.
translation: I was born on February 14, 1960.

text: Die decimo quarto mensis Februarii, anni MCMLX nata sum.
translation: I was born on February 14, 1960.

text: Quinquagesimum quartum aetatis annum agens, mortua est.
translation: She died at the age of 54.

text: Quinquagesimum quartum aetatis annum agens, mortuus est.
translation: He died at age 54.

text: Die decimo quarto mensis Februarii, anni millesimi nongentesimi sexagesimi natus sum.
translation: I was born on February 14, 1960.

text: Die decimo quarto mensis Februarii, anni millesimi nongentesimi sexagesimi nata sum.
translation: I was born on February 14, 1960.

text: "Quot annos natus es?" "Sedecim annos natus sum."
translation: "How old are you?" "I'm 16 years old."

text: Cum quadraginta annos nata esset, sedecim linguis loqui poterat.
translation: When she was forty, she could speak sixteen languages.

text: Adultus non est, sedecim annos natus est!
translation: He is not an adult, he is sixteen years old!

text: Cum quadraginta annos natus esset, sedecim linguis loqui poterat.
translation: When he was forty years old, he could speak sixteen languages.

text: Proximo anno sedecim annos natus ero.
translation: I will be sixteen years old next year.

text: Proximo anno sedecim annos nata ero.
translation: I will be sixteen years old next year.

text: Thomas nonagesimum septimum aetatis annum agens, mortuus est.
translation: Tom died at the age of 97.

text: Hoc est septimum operistitium huius anni.
translation: This is the seventh strike of this year.

text: Anno millesimo nongentesimo vicesimo septimo, Arthur Bernardes senator creatus est.
translation: Arthur Bernardes was elected senator in the year nineteen hundred and twenty-seven.

text: Et sabbatizavit populus die septimo.
translation: And the people kept the sabbath on the seventh day.

text: Septem diebus vesceris azymis, et in die septimo erit sollemnitas Domini.
translation: Seven days shalt thou eat unleavened bread: and on the seventh day shall be the solemnity of the Lord.

text: Requievitque arca mense septimo, decima septima die mensis super montes Ararat.
translation: And the ark rested in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, upon the mountains of Armenia.

text: Homini servo suos domitos habere oportet oculos.
translation: It is fitting for a servant to be blindfolded.

text: Si servo nequam palmus datur, accipit ulnam.
translation: Give a clown your finger, and he'll take your whole hand.

text: Thomas rursus eum interrogat: "Ubi est pecunia mea? Responde, serve!"
translation: Tom asked him again: "Where is my money? Answer me, slave!"

text: In familia Iulii magnus numerus servorum, parvus numerus liberorum est.
translation: In the family of Julius there is a large number of slaves, and a small number of children.

text: Dentem quoque si excusserit servo vel ancillæ suæ, dimittet eos liberos pro dente.
translation: Also if he strike out a tooth of his manservant or maidservant, he shall in like manner make them free.

text: Apud quemcumque fuerit inventum servorum tuorum, quod quæris, moriatur; et nos erimus servi domini nostri.
translation: With whomsoever of thy servants shall be found that which thou seekest, let him die, and we will be the bondmen of my lord.

text: Didymus valde somniculosus est, quia praeterita nocte bene non dormivit.
translation: Tom is very sleepy, because he didn't sleep well last night.

text: Thomas se somniculosum esse dixit.
translation: Tom said that he was sleepy.

text: Nos duo valde somniculosi eramus.
translation: We were both very sleepy.

text: Utrum es somniculosus an fessus?
translation: Are you sleepy or tired?

text: Utrum estis somniculosi an fessi?
translation: Are you sleepy or tired?

text: Utrum es somniculosa an fessa?
translation: Are you sleepy or tired?

text: Statio curruum publicorum in eodem loco ut prius.
translation: The bus stop is at the same place as before.

text: Statio ferriviaria in media urbe sita est.
translation: The train station is located downtown.

text: Scisne ubi statio vigilum publicorum sit?
translation: Do you know where the police station is?

text: Statio in media urbe est.
translation: The station is the middle of the city.

text: Ubi statio curruum publicorum est?
translation: Where's the bus stop?

text: Ubi statio ferriviaria est?
translation: Where is the train station?

text: Me non solum paenitet stultitiae meae, sed etiam pudet.
translation: My foolishness not only causes me regret but also shames me.

text: Nihil tristius quam stultitia et languor.
translation: Nothing is more sad than stupidity and apathy.

text: Non omnis error stultitia est dicenda.
translation: Not every error is to be called folly.

text: Omnem pecuniam meam in stultitiis consumpsi.
translation: I spent all my money on stupid stuff.

text: Stultitia est morte alterius sperare salutem.
translation: He that waits for dead men's shoes may go long enough barefoot.

text: Thomas se eam pecuniam surripuisse confessus est.
translation: Tom admitted he stole the money.

text: "Quid Thomas iis surripuit?" "Aliquam pecuniam."
translation: "What did Tom steal from them?" "Some money."

text: Thomas se birotam surripuisse confessus est.
translation: Tom admitted he had stolen the bike.

text: Quis me pecuniam surripuere dicit?
translation: Who says that I steal money?

text: Thomas a Maria aliquid surripuit.
translation: Tom stole something from Mary.

text: Vir pecuniam viatoris surripuit.
translation: The man robbed the traveler of his money.

text: In tabernaculo dormire non soleo.
translation: I'm not used to sleeping in a tent.

text: Egressus inde Israel, fixit tabernaculum trans Magdaleder (id est Turris gregis).
translation: Departing thence, he pitched his tent beyond the Flock tower.

text: Tabernaculum in litore posuerunt.
translation: They pitched their tent on the beach.

text: Dilatet Deus Iapheth, et habitet in tabernaculis Sem, sitque Chanaan servus eius.
translation: May God enlarge Japheth, and may he dwell in the tents of Shem, and Canaan be his servant.

text: Dixeruntque ad eum: "Ubi est Sara uxor tua?" Ille respondit: "Ecce in tabernaculo est".
translation: And when they had eaten, they said to him: Where is Sara thy wife? He answered: Lo she is in the tent.

text: Cœpitque Noe agricola plantare vineam; bibensque vinum inebriatus est et nudatus in tabernaculo suo.
translation: And Noah a husbandman began to till the ground, and planted a vineyard. And drinking of the wine was made drunk, and was uncovered in his tent.

text: Avunculus meus tabernam florum prope stationem habet.
translation: My uncle has a flower shop near the station.

text: Ego ad tabernam ibo vinumque tibi emam.
translation: I shall go to the shop and buy you wine.

text: Multae tabernae in media urbe sunt.
translation: There are many shops downtown.

text: Vidi eum in tabernam intrare.
translation: I saw him enter the store.

text: Diebus profestis tabernae tranquillae sunt.
translation: Shops are quiet on weekdays.

text: In mediam tabernam eo.
translation: I go into the middle of the inn.

text: Magnus thesaurus in navi mersa inventus est.
translation: A great treasure was discovered in a sunken ship.

text: Nullus thesaurus pretiosior est quam filius.
translation: There is no treasure more precious than a child.

text: Nullus thesaurus pretiosior est filio.
translation: There is no treasure more precious than a child.

text: Verus amicus magnus thesaurus est.
translation: A true friend is a great treasure.

text: Thesaurum hic non sepelivimus.
translation: We didn't bury the treasure here.

text: Thomas dixit se Mariam timidam esse putare.
translation: Tom said he thought that Mary was nervous.

text: Dixerunt omnibus se non timidos esse.
translation: They told everyone they were unafraid.

text: Qui timide rogat, docet negare.
translation: He who asks timidly invites a refusal.

text: Non puto Thoman timidum esse.
translation: I don't think Tom is timid.

text: Necessitudo etiam timidos fortes facit.
translation: Necessity even emboldens the timid.

text: Timidi nunquam statuerunt trophaeum.
translation: Faint heart never won fair lady.

text: Ventus vehementer perflat et ignis pontem antiquum delet.
translation: The wind violently blows through and the fire destroys the ancient bridge.

text: Pater mihi vehementer iratus est.
translation: My father is very angry with me.

text: Thomas vehementer mihi iratus est.
translation: Tom is very angry with me.

text: Thomas vehementer mihi iratus erat.
translation: Tom was very angry with me.

text: Ea illi vehementer irascitur.
translation: She is very angry with him.

text: Vehementer mihi irata est.
translation: She is very angry with me.

text: Asinus meus est velocior quam raeda tua.
translation: My donkey is faster than your car.

text: Potesne currere tam velociter, quam Thomas?
translation: Can you run as fast as Tom can?

text: Cervus magis velox est quam fortis.
translation: The deer is more rapid than strong.

text: Sonus minus est velox quam lux.
translation: Sound is less quick than light.

text: Cervus velocior est quam fortior.
translation: The deer is faster than it is strong.

text: Sonus minus velox est luce.
translation: Sound is less quick than light.

text: Sanguis est liquor rubicundus qui per arterias et venas fluit.
translation: Blood is a red liquid that flows through arteries and veins.

text: Dic mihi, quotiens Romam venis?
translation: Tell me, how often do you come to Rome?

text: Dic mihi, quoties Romam venis?
translation: Tell me, how often do you come to Rome?

text: Quotiēns in mēnse hūc venīs?
translation: How many times a month do you come here?

text: Unde venis et quo vadis?
translation: Where do you come from and where are you going?

text: Cur ad me venis?
translation: Why do you come to me?

text: Avus meus anno millesimo nongentesimo vicesimo natus est.
translation: My grandfather was born in 1920.

text: Die vicesimo secundo mensis Martii, anni MCMLXII natus sum.
translation: I was born on March 22, 1962.

text: Die vicesimo secundo mensis Martii, anni MCMLXII nata sum.
translation: I was born on March 22, 1962.

text: Die vicesimo secundo mensis Novembris, anni MCMXLVIII natus sum.
translation: I was born on the 22 of November 1948.

text: Die vicesimo secundo mensis Novembris, anni MCMXLVIII nata sum.
translation: I was born on the 22 of November 1948.

text: Thomas die vicesimo octobris mortuus est.
translation: Tom died on October 20th.

text: Thomas est tribus digitis altior quam uxor eius.
translation: Tom is three inches taller than his wife is.

text: Quo quisque est altior, eo est periculo proximior.
translation: The higher a person is, the closer they are to danger.

text: Thomas est tribus digitis altior quam ego.
translation: Tom is three inches taller than I am.

text: Thomas est tribus digitis altior quam Maria.
translation: Tom is three inches taller than Mary.

text: Thomas est duobus digitis altior quam Maria.
translation: Tom is a couple of inches taller than Mary.

text: Est duobus digitis altior quam ego.
translation: He is two inches taller than I am.

text: Mater mea conata est amantes in gratiam reducere.
translation: My mother tried to reconcile the couple.

text: Amantis iusiurandum poenam non habet.
translation: The vow of a lover is not taken seriously.

text: Amantes inter se osculati sunt.
translation: The lovers kissed.

text: Cum amante meo sum.
translation: I'm with my boyfriend.

text: Cum amante mea sum.
translation: I'm with my girlfriend.

text: Mulier cupido quod dicit amanti, in vento et rapida scribere oportet aqua.
translation: What a woman says to her passionate lover must be written in the wind and in the swift waters.

text: Calamus, quem heri amisi, novus erat.
translation: The pen I lost yesterday was new.

text: Horologium quod pater mihi dedit amisi.
translation: I lost the watch that my father gave me.

text: Telephonum gestabile amisi nec invenire possum.
translation: I lost my cell phone and I can't find it.

text: Fiducia pecuniam amisi, diffidentia vero servavi.
translation: Sudden trust brings sudden repentance.

text: Claves amisi nec invenire possum.
translation: I lost my keys and I can't find them.

text: Horologium amisi nec invenire possum.
translation: I've lost my watch and I can't find it.

text: Mensa scriptoria ferrea in angulo erat.
translation: There was an iron desk in the corner.

text: Aditus ad stationem est circa angulum.
translation: The entrance to the station is around the corner.

text: Loqueris optime, secedamus aliquo in angulum, ne quis impediat nos.
translation: You speak very well, let us find somewhere quiet in case anyone should disturb us.

text: Domus in angulo nostra est.
translation: The house on the corner is ours.

text: Hoc caput est creationis anguli.
translation: This is the cornerstone of creation.

text: Officium nostrum circa angulum est.
translation: Our office is around the corner.

text: Triginta minutis post sextam horam antemeridianam expergiscor.
translation: I wake up at half past six in the morning.

text: Octava hora antemeridiana est.
translation: It's eight o'clock in the morning.

text: Secunda hora antemeridiana est.
translation: It's two o'clock in the morning.

text: Cras viginti quinque minutis post sextam horam antemeridianam hamaxostichus meus Dusseldorpium adveniet.
translation: My train to Düsseldorf will arrive tomorrow at 06:25 AM.

text: Titanic submersa est viginti minutis post secundam horam antemeridianam Lunae diei, die quinto decimo mensis Aprilis.
translation: The Titanic sank at 02:20 on Monday, April 15th.

text: Historia Sinarum antiquor est quam Iaponiae.
translation: The history of China is older than that of Japan.

text: Multa aedificia ibi sunt antiqua.
translation: There are a lot of old buildings there.

text: Nara urbs valde antiqua est.
translation: Nara is a very old city.

text: Nonne antiquas pelliculas cinematographicas aspicis?
translation: Don't you watch old movies?

text: Mihi placet linguas antiquas discere.
translation: I like learning ancient languages.

text: Roma urbs antiqua est.
translation: Rome is an ancient city.

text: Potesne pilam una manu captare?
translation: Can you catch a ball with one hand?

text: Falco, Nisus, et Accipitur, captant aviculas; Astur, columbas, et aves majores.
translation: The falcon, the hobby, and the hawk, catch small birds; the Gerfalcon, pigeons and larger birds.

text: Mustela murem pinguem captat.
translation: A weasel tries to grab the fat mouse.

text: Mures captare canes nolunt.
translation: Dogs don't try to catch mice.

text: Capta eum! Capta eum!
translation: Catch him! Catch him!

text: Aquilae muscās nōn captant.
translation: Eagles don't hunt flies.

text: Thomas et Maria de caeli temperie colloquebantur.
translation: Tom and Mary were talking about the weather.

text: Pater vix cum filio moroso suo colloquitur.
translation: The father had trouble communicating with his wayward son.

text: Ut antiqui amici inter se colloquebantur.
translation: They were talking together like old pals.

text: Cum ea per litteras crebro colloquor.
translation: I frequently correspond with her.

text: Thomas Mariaque se nescire de quo inter se colloquerentur videbantur.
translation: Tom and Mary didn't seem to know what they were talking about.

text: Inter se per litteras crebro colloquuntur.
translation: They correspond regularly.

text: Omnes libros, quos mihi commodavisti, perlegi.
translation: I've finished reading all the books you lent me.

text: Bibliotheca urbana hos libros mihi commodat.
translation: I borrow them from the city library.

text: Librum, quem mihi commodavisti, perlegi.
translation: I've finished reading the book you lent me.

text: Haec sella valde commoda est.
translation: This chair is very comfortable.

text: Amico meo pecuniam commodavi.
translation: I lent my friend some money.

text: Thomas mihi pecuniam commodavit.
translation: Tom lent me some money.

text: Coquus eorum peregrinus est sed nescio unde sit.
translation: Their cook is a foreigner but I do not know where he is from.

text: Didymus est tam bonus coquus quam Maria.
translation: Tom is as good a cook as Mary is.

text: Didymus est pariter bonus coquus ac Maria.
translation: Tom is as good a cook as Mary is.

text: Didymus est aeque bonus coquus ac Maria.
translation: Tom is as good a cook as Mary is.

text: Didymus est aeque bonus coquus atque Maria.
translation: Tom is as good a cook as Mary is.

text: Non coquus semper, cui longus culter adhaeret.
translation: The cook is not always the one with a long knife.

text: Tam ebrius est ut sui compos non sit.
translation: He's shit-faced drunk.

text: Te dixi me non ebrium esse.
translation: I told you I'm not drunk.

text: Fessus et ebrius domum rediit.
translation: He went back home tired and drunk.

text: Thōmās dīxit Marīam ēbriam vidērī.
translation: Tom said that Mary seemed drunk.

text: Thomas et Maria ebrii sunt.
translation: Tom and Mary are drunk.

text: I domum, Thoma. Ebrius es.
translation: Go home, Tom. You're drunk.

text: Una abhinc hora magnam placentam Neapolitanam cum amico edi.
translation: I ate a large pizza with a friend an hour ago.

text: Satis edi. Stomachus meus plenus est.
translation: I've had enough, so my stomach is full.

text: Heri nimis multum cibi edi.
translation: I ate too much food yesterday.

text: Hodie nimis multum acetariorum edi.
translation: They've eaten too much salad today.

text: Quartam partem libi edi.
translation: I ate a quarter of the cake.

text: Nolo, gratias. Satis edi.
translation: No, thank you. I've had enough.

text: Saepe dat una dies quod non evenit in anno.
translation: Not infrequently, more happens in a day than in a year.

text: Alienum est omne, quicquid optando evenit.
translation: What we obtain by asking is not really ours.

text: Nemo eventum tale possibile esse credebat.
translation: No one believed that such a thing could happen.

text: Propter consilium eius prospere evenire potui.
translation: Because of his advice, I was able to succeed.

text: Nihil mali tibi eveniet.
translation: Nothing bad's going to happen to you.

text: Nihil tibi evenire potest.
translation: Nothing can happen to you.

text: Ferias duorum mensium acturus sum.
translation: I'm going out on vacation for two months.

text: Ferias duorum mensium actura sum.
translation: I'm going out on vacation for two months.

text: Consilia de feriis nostris facimus.
translation: We're making plans for our vacation.

text: Ubi ferias acturus es?
translation: Where are you going to spend the vacation?

text: Ubi ferias actura es?
translation: Where are you going to spend the vacation?

text: Quem fecisti dum feriae?
translation: What did you do during the holidays?

text: Multi pueri et puellae in foro erant.
translation: There were many children in the square.

text: Scripturam de monumentis in foro composui.
translation: I wrote a composition about the monuments in the forum.

text: Balnea in foro non sunt.
translation: The baths are not in the forum.

text: "Ubi es?" "In forō sum."
translation: "Where are you?" "I'm in the square."

text: Vinum est in foro.
translation: The wine is in the market.

text: Ecce autem venerunt in ipso die servi Isaac annuntiantes ei de puteo, quem foderant, atque dicentes: Invenimus aquam.
translation: And behold, the same day the servants of Isaac came, telling him of a well which they had digged, and saying: We have found water.

text: Sapiens nunquam dubitabit, quin immortalis sit animus.
translation: A wise person will never doubt that the soul is immortal.

text: Hominis corpus moriturum, animus autem immortalis.
translation: A man's body dies, but his soul is immortal.

text: Corpus est mortale, animus autem immortalis.
translation: The body is mortal, but the soul is immortal.

text: Credo animum esse immortalem.
translation: I believe in the immortality of the soul.

text: Credunt animum esse immortalem.
translation: They believe that the soul is immortal.

text: Nemo nostrum immortalis est.
translation: None of us are immortal.

text: Intelligentia artificialis res faciliores facit.
translation: Artificial intelligence makes things easier.

text: Heu nihil invitis fas quemquam fidere divis!
translation: Ah! vain to boast, if Heaven refuse to aid!

text: Invitis canibus venari haud facile est.
translation: It's not easy to hunt against the will of the hounds.

text: Hoc denuo facere invitus sum.
translation: I'm reluctant to do that again.

text: Soli ire inviti erant.
translation: They were reluctant to go by themselves.

text: Thomas abire invitus videtur.
translation: Tom seems reluctant to go.

text: Thomas adiuvare invitus videtur.
translation: Tom seems reluctant to help.

text: Interest non quid legas, sed quo modo.
translation: It doesn't matter what you read, but how.

text: Placetne tibi id quod legis?
translation: Do you like what you are reading?

text: Quis librum quem legis scripsit?
translation: Who wrote the book that you're reading?

text: Thoma, quid est quod legis?
translation: Tom, what are you reading?

text: Ignorantia legis non excusat.
translation: Ignorance of the law does not exempt punishment.

text: Ne talem librum legas.
translation: Don't read that kind of book.

text: Et plumba et libellos et glossaria et cetera emit.
translation: He bought pencils, notebooks, dictionaries and so on.

text: "Ubi libellus meus est?" "Super sellam est."
translation: "Where is my notebook?" "It is on the chair."

text: Accipe libellum et devora illum.
translation: Take the little book, and eat it up.

text: Quid in libello tuo scribis?
translation: What are you writing in your notebook?

text: Magister discipulis libellos distribuit.
translation: The teacher distributed the handouts to the students.

text: Sepone libros et libellos.
translation: Put away your books and notebooks.

text: Quot nautās vidēre poterās?
translation: How many sailors could you see?

text: Thomas nauta factus est.
translation: Tom became a sailor.

text: Maria nautam quemdam amat.
translation: Mary loves a sailor.

text: Mox et Leucatæ nimbosa cacumina montis, / et formidatus nautis aperitur Apollo.
translation: Soon, where Leucate lifts her cloud-capt head, / looms forth Apollo's fane, the seaman's name of dread.

text: Erat sublustris nox, et quidam e nautis stabat in galea; nam sic vocant, opinor; circumspectans, si videret quam terram.
translation: It was a moonlit night, and one of the sailors stood upon the round top; as I think they call it; he looked around to see if he could see any land.

text: Avus vetus nepotibus suis historiam legit.
translation: The old grandfather read his grandchildren a story.

text: Parentes mei vere nepotes suos amant.
translation: My parents really love their grandchildren.

text: Senex nepotibus suis historiam legit.
translation: The old grandfather read his grandchildren a story.

text: Laetissimus cum nepotibus est.
translation: He is happiest when he is with his grandchildren.

text: Maneat ea cura nepotes.
translation: Let us leave these concerns to posterity.

text: Quot nepōtēs tibi sunt?
translation: How many grandchildren do you have?

text: Mori me malim quam tibi nubam!
translation: I'd rather die than marry you!

text: Num vīs illō mufriō nūbere?
translation: You want to marry that swindler?

text: Anna parentibus insciis nupsit.
translation: Anna married without the knowledge of her parents.

text: Filiam iurisconsulto nuptum dedit.
translation: He married his daughter to a lawyer.

text: Anna inscientibus parentibus nupsit.
translation: Anna got married without her parents' knowledge.

text: Nuptus sum. Uxorem habeo.
translation: I am married. I have a wife.

text: Utrum malo? Venerem an scacchorum ludum? Ex positione pendet.
translation: Which do I prefer? Sex or chess? It depends on the position.

text: Speculum magnum est in muro pendens.
translation: There is a large mirror hanging on the wall.

text: Cerasum pendet longo pediolo; prunum et persicium breviori. Morum brevissimo.
translation: The cherry hangs by a long stalk, the plum and peach's are shorter. The mulberry’s stalk is very short.

text: Speculum in muro pende.
translation: Hang the mirror on the wall.

text: Nubes pendent in aere.
translation: Clouds hang in the air.

text: Pondo duodesexaginta chiliogrammata pendeo.
translation: He weighs 80 kilos.

text: Ego sum Iesus, quem tu persequeris.
translation: I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.

text: Feles nostra mures persequi non amat.
translation: Our cat doesn't like to chase mice.

text: Thomas mortem fratris persequi vult.
translation: Tom wants to avenge his brother's death.

text: Thomas mortem Mariae persecutus est.
translation: Tom avenged Mary's death.

text: Quis mortem Caroli persequetur?
translation: Who will avenge the death of Karl?

text: Patris mortem persecutus est.
translation: He avenged his father's death.

text: Hodie pluit. Ubi umbella mea est?
translation: It's raining today. Where is my umbrella?

text: Quamquam pluit, tamen pila Caledonica ludam.
translation: Even though it is raining, he will play golf.

text: Ex die ultima Iovis pluit.
translation: It has been raining since last Thursday.

text: Cum graviter pluit, ecquid egredieris?
translation: When it rains cats and dogs, do you go out?

text: De die Martis pluit.
translation: It has been raining since Tuesday.

text: Ventosum est et pluit.
translation: It's windy and it's raining.

text: Utrum mecum prandere vis, an domum ire?
translation: Do you want to eat lunch with me, or go home?

text: Caupona in qua prandimus frequentissima erat.
translation: The restaurant where we ate lunch was very crowded.

text: Thomas cum Maria in triclinio prandet.
translation: Tom is eating lunch with Mary in the dining room.

text: Meridies est. Viri prandent.
translation: It is midday. The men are eating lunch.

text: Visne apud me prandere?
translation: Do you want to have lunch with me?

text: Vultisne apud me prandere?
translation: Do you want to have lunch with me?

text: Petroleum tibi pretiosius est quam vita humana, nonne?
translation: Oil is more precious than human life to you, right?

text: Petroleum tibi pretiosius est vita humana, nonne?
translation: Oil is more precious than human life to you, right?

text: Nihil pretiosius quam bona valetudo.
translation: Nothing is more valuable than good health.

text: Aurum pretiosius est quam ferrum.
translation: Gold is more precious than iron.

text: Nihil pretiosius bona valetudine.
translation: Nothing is more valuable than good health.

text: Aurum pretiosius est ferro.
translation: Gold is more precious than iron.

text: Non loqueris contra proximum tuum falsum testimonium.
translation: Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.

text: Dixitque alter ad proximum suum : Venite, faciamus lateres, et coquamus eos igni.
translation: And they said one to another, Go to, let us make brick, and burn them thoroughly.

text: Si quis de industria occiderit proximum suum et per insidias, ab altari meo evelles eum, ut moriatur.
translation: If a man kill his neighbour on set purpose, and by lying in wait for him: thou shalt take him away from my altar that he may die.

text: Dixitque alter ad proximum suum: Venite, faciamus lateres et coquamus eos igni. Habueruntque lateres pro saxis et bitumen pro cæmento.
translation: And each one said to his neighbour: Come, let us make brick, and bake them with fire. And they had brick instead of stones, and slime instead of mortar.

text: Caecus oculum requirit unum sed gaudeat duos acceptus.
translation: A blind man asks only for one eye, but would rejoice if he got two.

text: Voca me, si auxilium meum requiris.
translation: Call me if you need my help.

text: Si linguam discere vis, patientiam habere oportet. Exitus tempus requirit.
translation: If you want to learn a language, you must be patient. Success requires some time.

text: Alii novemve decem horas requirunt.
translation: Other people need nine or ten hours of sleep.

text: Omne Thomas requisitum habet.
translation: Tom has everything that he needs.

text: Odi et amo. Quare id faciam, fortasse requiris. Nescio, sed fieri sentio et excrucior.
translation: I hate and I love. Why would I do this, maybe you're asking? I don't know, but I feel it happening and am tortured.

text: Saccharum salemque in illa taberna vendunt.
translation: They sell sugar and salt at that store.

text: Saccharum in potione Arabica non pono.
translation: I don't put sugar in my coffee.

text: Puto me pinguem esse quod saccharum et gelatum multum edo.
translation: I think I am fat because I eat a lot of sugar and ice cream.

text: Saccharo egeo. Estne tibi saccharum?
translation: I need some sugar. Do you have any?

text: Saccharo egeo. Habesne saccharum?
translation: I need some sugar. Do you have any?

text: Visne saccharum vel lac?
translation: Do you want sugar or milk?

text: Oceanus Atlanticus Americam ab Europa secernit.
translation: The Atlantic Ocean separates America from Europe.

text: Agricolae poma bona e malis secernunt.
translation: Farmers separate good apples from bad ones.

text: Oceanus Britannicus Galliam a Britannia secernit.
translation: The English Channel separates France from England.

text: Dominus pugnabit pro vobis, et vos silebitis.
translation: The Lord will fight for you, and you shall hold your peace.

text: Thoman quereri oportebat, sed modo siluit.
translation: Tom should've complained, but he just kept quiet.

text: Inter arma enim silent leges.
translation: In times of war, the law falls silent.

text: Cum fantur theologi, silet Deus.
translation: While the theologians speak, God has nothing to say.

text: Praestat silere, quam stulte loqui.
translation: It is better to keep quiet than to talk nonsense.

text: Manu significabat ut silerem.
translation: He gave me a sign to keep quiet.

text: Oblitus sum ubi schola mea sita sit.
translation: I forgot where my school is.

text: Oblita sum ubi schola mea sita sit.
translation: I forgot where my school is.

text: Scisne ubi sita sit haec insula?
translation: Do you know where this island is located?

text: Domus mea in colle sita est.
translation: My house stands on a hill.

text: Corēa Septentriōnālis prope Iapōniam sita est.
translation: North Korea​ is located near Japan.

text: Iaponia in Asia orientali sita est.
translation: Japan is in eastern Asia.

text: Struthiocameli volare non possunt, quia alas brevissimas habent.
translation: Ostriches don't fly because they have very short wings.

text: Struthiocameli ovum quater et vicies gravius est quam galliae.
translation: An ostrich egg weighs as much as twenty-four chicken eggs.

text: Feles mea struthiocamelum edere vult.
translation: My cat wants to eat an ostrich.

text: Cur struthiocamelus volare non potest?
translation: Why can't an ostrich fly?

text: Struthiocamelum in therotrophio vidi.
translation: I have seen an ostrich at the zoo.

text: Struthiocamelus volare non potest.
translation: An ostrich can't fly.

text: Scisne qua de cause Thomas surdus factus sit?
translation: Do you know how Tom lost his hearing?

text: Thomas et Maria surdi facti sunt.
translation: Tom and Mary have lost their hearing.

text: Thomas dextra aure surdus est.
translation: Tom is deaf in his right ear.

text: Maria sinistra aure surda est.
translation: Mary is deaf in her left ear.

text: Esne surdus aut stultus?
translation: Are you deaf or stupid?

text: Uterque puer surdus est.
translation: Both children are deaf.

text: Tata in culina est, quia coquit.
translation: Dad is in the kitchen because he's cooking.

text: Id autem Tatae non placebit.
translation: But Dad won't like it.

text: Carolus Marx tatam meum interfecit.
translation: Karl Marx killed my dad.

text: Quo te agis, tata?
translation: Where are you going, Dad?

text: Tata instrumentum photographicum emit.
translation: Dad bought a camera.

text: Venisti ut testimonium perhibeas de Filio Dei?
translation: Have you come to bear witness to the Son of God?

text: Sicut præcepit Dominus Moysi, posuit illud Aaron coram testimonio reservandum.
translation: As the Lord commanded Moses. And Aaron put it in the tabernacle to be kept.

text: Tum Ioannes testimonium suum dedit.
translation: Then John gave this testimony.

text: Veni ut testimonium perhibeam.
translation: I have come to bear witness.

text: Veni ergo, et ineamus fœdus ego et tu, ut sit in testimonium inter me et te.
translation: Come, therefore, let us enter into a league; that it may be for a testimony between me and thee.

text: Quem vocavit Laban Iegarsahadutha (id est Tumulus testimonii), et Iacob Galed (uterque iuxta proprietatem linguæ suæ).
translation: And Laban called it 'The witness heap'; and Jacob, 'The hillock of testimony': each of them according to the propriety of his language.

text: Mundus super dorsum immanis testudinis jacet.
translation: The world rests on the back of a great turtle.

text: Testudinibus aquatilibus dentes non sunt.
translation: Sea turtles don't have teeth.

text: Testudines aquatiles dentes non habent.
translation: Sea turtles don't have teeth.

text: Testudines dentes non habent.
translation: Turtles don't have teeth.

text: Thomas duas testudines habet.
translation: Tom has two turtles.

text: Tum foribus divae, media testudine templi, / septa armis, solioque alte subnixa, resedit.
translation: Then, girt with guards, within the temple's gate / beneath the centre of the dome she sate.

text: Quod cibus est aliis, aliis est venenum.
translation: One man's meat is another man's poison.

text: Quali veneno usus es?
translation: What kind of poison did you use?

text: Quali veneno usa es?
translation: What kind of poison did you use?

text: Aliquis Thomae venenum dedit.
translation: Somebody poisoned Tom.

text: Non aegritudo fuit quae fecerat ut Sami per dolorem pateretur sed venenum.
translation: It wasn't a natural illness that made Sami suffer in agony. It was poisoning.

text: Semel hedomade Maria amicam suam visit.
translation: Once a week, Mary meets up with her friend.

text: Semel hedomade Maria amicum suum visit.
translation: Once a week, Mary meets up with her friend.

text: Multi Italiae pulchra oppida visunt.
translation: Many people visit the beautiful towns of Italy.

text: Jam pridem cupio te visere.
translation: I have long been desiring to visit you.

text: Mihi est pergratum vos visere.
translation: I'm happy to see you guys.

text: Licetne te visere hodie vesperi?
translation: Can I see you tonight?

text: Ecce agnus Dei, ecce qui tollit peccatum mundi.
translation: Look, the Lamb of God; look at him who carries the sin of the world.

text: Pastor putat agnos a lupis occisos fuisse.
translation: The shepherd thinks that the lambs were killed by wolves.

text: Agnus balat 'b a a a'.
translation: The lamb bleats 'baa'.

text: Agni a lupo occisi sunt.
translation: The lambs were killed by a wolf.

text: Agnus a lupo interfectus est.
translation: The lamb was killed by the wolf.

text: Lupus in agnum impetum fecit.
translation: The wolf attacked the lamb.

text: Via quae ad vīcum dūcit angusta est.
translation: The road to the village is narrow.

text: Via quae ad deversorium ducit angusta est.
translation: The road which leads to the hotel is narrow.

text: Via angusta ad vīcum dūcit.
translation: There's narrow road to the village.

text: Haec via valde angusta est.
translation: This road is very narrow.

text: Via valde angusta est.
translation: The street is very narrow.

text: Haec angusta est via.
translation: This is a narrow street.

text: Hoc horologium multo carius est quam illud.
translation: This clock is far more expensive than that.

text: Hoc horologium multo carius est illo.
translation: This clock is far more expensive than that.

text: Hoc brachiale carius est quam illud.
translation: This bracelet is more expensive than that one.

text: Horologium tuum carius est quam meum.
translation: Your watch is more expensive than mine.

text: Horologium eius carius est quam meum.
translation: His clock is more expensive than mine.

text: Hoc brachiale carius est illo.
translation: This bracelet is more expensive than that one.

text: Cumque cessasset loqui cum eo, ascendit Deus ab Abraham.
translation: And when he had left off speaking with him, God went up from Abraham.

text: Anni non cessant, quantumvis homines cessant.
translation: Years do not wait, no matter how much men may wait.

text: Hic hamaxosticus hic non cessat.
translation: This train does not stop here.

text: Ubi maior minor cessat.
translation: Where there is the major, the minor becomes neglected.

text: Cur Thomas non cessavit?
translation: Why didn't Tom stop?

text: Abiit Dominus, postquam cessavit loqui ad Abraham; et ille reversus est in locum suum.
translation: And the Lord departed, after he had left speaking to Abraham: and Abraham returned to his place.

text: Hanc ianuam claudere non possum. Fracta est.
translation: I can't close this door. It's broken.

text: Nunc claude librum et dic quid sit de textu.
translation: Now, close the book and say what the text is about.

text: Nonne tibi dixi ut clauderes ianuam?
translation: Didn't I tell you to close the door?

text: Ostium claudere non possum. Clavem perdidi.
translation: I cannot lock the door. I have lost the key.

text: Esne recordatus fenestras claudere?
translation: Did you remember to close the windows?

text: Esne recordata fenestras claudere?
translation: Did you remember to close the windows?

text: Thomas Mariae suasit ut emeret computatrum novum.
translation: Tom advised Mary to buy a new computer.

text: Thomas Mariam suasit emere computatrum novum.
translation: Tom advised Mary to buy a new computer.

text: Hoc computatrum nimis antiquum est.
translation: This computer is obsolete.

text: Cum mē ignōrēs, multās tamen imāginēs tuās habeō in computātrō meō.
translation: Although you don't know me, I do have many pictures of you on my computer.

text: Uti computatro tempus conservet.
translation: Using a computer can save you time.

text: Novum computatrum heri emi.
translation: Yesterday I bought a new computer.

text: Conceperunt ergo duæ filiæ Lot de patre suo.
translation: So the two daughters of Lot were with child by their father.

text: María alterum ínfantem concipere cupívit.
translation: Mary wished to conceive a second child.

text: Qui ingressus est ad eam. At illa concepisse se videns despexit dominam suam.
translation: And he went in to her. But she perceiving that she was with child, despised her mistress.

text: Adam vero cognovit Evam uxorem suam, quæ concepit et peperit Cain dicens: Acquisivi virum per Dominum.
translation: And Adam knew Eve his wife; who conceived and brought forth Cain, saying: I have gotten a man through God.

text: Deditque illi Bilham famulam suam in coniugium. Quæ, ingresso ad se Iacob, concepit et peperit filium.
translation: And she gave him Bala in marriage: who, when her husband had gone in unto her, conceived and bore a son.

text: Quarto concepit et peperit filium et ait: “Modo confitebor Domino”; et ob hoc vocavit eum Iudam. Cessavitque parere.
translation: The fourth time she conceived and bore a son, and said: Now will I praise the Lord: and for this she called him Juda. And she left bearing.

text: Thomas et Maria tres annos matrimonio coniuncti sunt.
translation: Tom and Mary have been married three years.

text: Parentes mei triginta annos matrimonio coniuncti sunt.
translation: My parents have been married for thirty years.

text: Omnia viventia nexu essendi coniuncta sunt.
translation: All living things are connected in one chain of being.

text: Canis felesque coniuncti in canistro dormiunt.
translation: The dog and the cat are sleeping together in a basket.

text: Tres annos matrimonio coniuncti sumus.
translation: We have been married for three years.

text: Decem annos matrimonio coniuncti sunt.
translation: They have been married for ten years.

text: Ita, sunt plena Habitatoribus suis, quatuor Elementa, Mundi maxima Corpora.
translation: Thus, the greatest bodies of the world, the four elements, are full of their own inhabitants.

text: Corpora lente augescent cito extinguuntur.
translation: Bodies grow slowly and die quickly.

text: Corpora reptilium squamosa sunt.
translation: The bodies of reptiles are covered by scales.

text: Avete, omnes animae fideles, quarum corpora hic et ubique requiescunt in pulvere.
translation: Hail all faithful souls, whose bodies here and everywhere do rest in the dust.

text: "Incute vim ventis submersasque obrue puppes, / aut age diversos et disjice corpora ponto."
translation: "Strike force to the winds, sink and overwhelm the ships; or drive them apart and scatter their bodies on the sea."

text: Sternimur optatæ gremio telluris ad undam, / sortiti remos, passimque in litore sicco / corpora curamus; fessos sopor irrigat artus.
translation: Close by the water, in a sheltered bay, / a few guardians of the oars we choose, / then stretched at random on the beach we lay / our limbs to rest, and on the toil-worn crews / sleep steals in silence down, and sheds her kindly dews.

text: Thomas putat omnes aequales creatos fuisse.
translation: Tom believes that all men are created equal.

text: Homines ad divinam imaginem creati sunt.
translation: Human beings were created in God's image.

text: nunc paradīsum, ā nōbīs creātum, timēmus.
translation: Now we are afraid of the paradise we created.

text: Lingua Esperantica a Zamenhof creata est.
translation: Esperanto was created by Zamenhof.

text: Ad divinam imaginem creati sumus.
translation: We were created in God's image.

text: Sapientia non ex libris creata est, libri autem ex ipsa creati sunt.
translation: Wisdom was not created from books, but books were created from wisdom.

text: Qui potest transferre amorem, potest deponere.
translation: Whoever can transfer love, can also remove it.

text: Difficile est longum subito deponere amorem.
translation: It is difficult to give up a long love suddenly.

text: difficile est longum subito deponere amorem.
translation: It is difficult to suddenly put aside a long-standing love.

text: Ocularia depone et oculos claude.
translation: Take your glasses off and close your eyes.

text: Numquam Thomas depositus sit.
translation: Tom should never have been fired.

text: Thomas nondum spem deposuit.
translation: Tom still hasn't abandoned hope.

text: Noli Thoma tuae sorori tantum displicere.
translation: Don't be so unpleasant with your sister, Tom.

text: Thomae displicuit sēparārī ab uxōre līberīsque.
translation: Tom didn't like being separated from his wife and children.

text: Hoc est cur mihi displiceant feles.
translation: This is why I dislike cats.

text: Numquam dixi Thoman mihi displicere.
translation: I never said that I didn't like Tom.

text: Ei displicet in scholam ire.
translation: She dislikes going to school.

text: Tibi displicebunt quae dicam.
translation: You won't like what I'm going to say.

text: Nemo umquam ex eo carcere effugit nisi Thomas.
translation: Tom was the only person to ever escape from that prison.

text: Vix effugit ne in accidente interiret.
translation: He barely missed being killed in the accident.

text: Modo a vitalibus problematibus effugis.
translation: You're just running away from life's problems.

text: Plus quattuor milia hominum effugerunt.
translation: More than four thousand people escaped.

text: At Tobias cum uxore et filio delituit, sicque regis iram effugit.
translation: But Tobias hid himself with his wife and son, and thus escaped the wrath of the King.

text: Effugit obtutum oculorum animus.
translation: The soul cannot be seen by the eyes of the body.

text: Haud equidem nobis hoc opus esse arbitror.
translation: I really don't think we need this.

text: Equidem, plurimum gaudeo, tuā causā et eius, quod rediērit peregrē salvus.
translation: I am truly very glad, for your sake and his, that he has returned from abroad safely.

text: Equidem, quota hora est?
translation: By the way, what time is it?

text: Equidem nihil omnino curo.
translation: I don't care at all.

text: "Vivo equidem, vitamque extrema per omnia duco. / Ne dubita, nam vera vides."
translation: "Yea, alive, indeed, / alive through all extremities of woe. / Doubt not, thou see'st the truth, no shape of empty show."

text: "Credo equidem, et custodiet eum adhuc. Sed quando est reversurus?" "Nescio, expectamus in horas."
translation: "I believe it indeed, and will guard him still. But when is he returning?" "I don't know, we expect him every hour."

text: Omnes sciunt Lunam e caseo factam esse.
translation: Everybody knows the moon is made of cheese.

text: Et die tertia nuptiae factae sunt in Cana Galilaeae.
translation: On the third day, a wedding took place at Cana in Galilee.

text: Horologii acus ex auro factae sunt.
translation: The hands of the clock are made of gold.

text: Et gustavit architriclinus aquam vinum factam.
translation: And the master of the banquet tasted the water that had been turned into wine.

text: Architriclinus gustavit aquam vinum factam.
translation: The butler tasted the water turned into wine.

text: Sellae e ligno factae sunt.
translation: The chairs are made of wood.

text: Thomas Mariae dixit quid eam facturam esse vellet.
translation: Tom told Mary what he needs her to do.

text: Maria se hoc non facturam dixit.
translation: Mary said that she wouldn't do that.

text: Dīcit sē hodiē id factūram esse.
translation: She says that she'll do that today.

text: Dīcit sē id factūram esse.
translation: She says that she plans to do that.

text: Dixit se id tibi facturam.
translation: She said that she'll do that for you.

text: Dīcit sē hodiē id factūram.
translation: She says that she'll do that today.

text: Quot genera avium in horto tuo sunt?
translation: How many kinds of birds are in your garden?

text: Quae genera ciborum tibi placent?
translation: What kind of food do you like?

text: Thomas multa florum genera emit.
translation: Tom bought many kinds of flowers.

text: Non enim materia est quae cogitationem generat, sed cogitatio quod materiam generat.
translation: It is not matter that generates thought, but thought that generates matter.

text: Hercules leonem clava interfecit.
translation: Hercules killed the lion with a club.

text: Hercules filius Iovis est.
translation: Hercules is a son of Jupiter.

text: Hercules ambas serpentes necavit.
translation: Hercules killed both serpents.

text: Iphicles, frater Herculis, magna voce exclamavit; sed Hercules ipse, fortissimus puer, haudquaquam territus est.
translation: Iphicles, Hercules' brother, gave a loud cry; but Hercules himself, a stout boy, was not afraid at all.

text: Misit igitur duas serpentes saevissimas; hae media nocte in cubiculum Alcmenae venerunt, ubi Hercules cum fratre suo dormiebat.
translation: She then dispatched two very fierce serpents, which came in the middle of the night to the room of Alcmena, where Hercules and his brother were sleeping.

text: Nōbīs imperātum est ut id facerēmus.
translation: We were ordered to do that.

text: Mihi imperātum est ut id facerem.
translation: I was ordered to do that.

text: Thōmae imperātum est ut id faceret.
translation: Tom was ordered to do that.

text: Mihi imperātum est ut tē interficiam.
translation: I've been ordered to kill you.

text: Mihi imperātum est ut hoc faciam.
translation: I've been ordered to do this.

text: Eī imperātum est ut taceat.
translation: He was ordered to shut up.

text: Scisne quam terram in praesentia incolat?
translation: Do you know in which country she lives now?

text: Māter Thōmae in hōc vīco incolit.
translation: Tom's mother lives in this village.

text: Frater meus in vīculō incolit.
translation: My brother lives in a small village.

text: Māter Thōmae hunc vīcum incolit.
translation: Tom's mother lives in this village.

text: Quālī in oppidō incolitis?
translation: In what kind of city do you live?

text: Quālī in urbe incolitis?
translation: In what kind of city do you live?

text: Dícó nimiam lúxuriam iamnunc cívitátí inesse.
translation: I say that the city now has too much extravagance.

text: Inest mendum in hac sententia.
translation: There's an error in this sentence.

text: Multum vitaminorum in fructibus inest.
translation: Fruit is rich in vitamins.

text: Corpus meum mihi inest.
translation: My body belongs to me.

text: Res age, quae prosunt, rursus vitare memento in quibus error inest, nec spes est certa laboris.
translation: Do those things which are profitable, and remember to avoid again those in which there is error, and there is no hope of certain employment.

text: Nemo enim fere saltat sobrius, nisi forte insanit.
translation: No one dances sober, unless he is insane.

text: Postquam uxor sua eum reliquit, Haroldus insanivit.
translation: After his wife left him, Harold went nuts.

text: Pugillares mei satis insani sunt.
translation: My schedule is pretty crazy.

text: Vincet ratio insanire nepotes.
translation: Reason will prove that prodigals are crazy.

text: Omnes Thoman arbitrabantur insanire.
translation: They all thought Tom was crazy.

text: Omnes praeter me insaniunt.
translation: Everyone is insane except me.

text: Si quis non invidetur, qualitates non habent invidiosas.
translation: If someone is not envied, they don't have enviable qualities.

text: Didymus dixit Bostoniam bonam esse invisu.
translation: Tom said Boston is a nice place to visit.

text: Invidebant igitur ei fratres sui; pater vero rem tacitus considerabat.
translation: His brethren therefore envied him: but his father considered the thing with himself.

text: Omnibus rebus invidet. Ea est femina zelotypissima quam umquam novi.
translation: She is jealous of everything. She is the most jealous woman I have ever known.

text: Praesidens Trump valde invisus est.
translation: President Trump is very unpopular.

text: Thomas omnibus invisus est.
translation: Tom is hated by everyone.

text: Dixit se ituram esse ad Lutetiam in Augusto.
translation: She said she will go to Paris in August.

text: Thoman proximo mense in Australiam iturum esse non credo.
translation: I don't think Tom will go to Australia next month.

text: Thomas mihi dixit se cras in ludum non iturum esse.
translation: Tom told me that he won't come to school tomorrow.

text: Thomas se ad ecclesiam iturum dixit.
translation: Tom said he'd go to church.

text: Thōmās respondit sē libenter itūrum.
translation: Tom replied that he'd be glad to go.

text: Marīa respondit sē libenter itūram.
translation: Mary replied that she'd be glad to go.

text: Raeda Didymo lavanda non est. Maria eam iam lavit.
translation: Tom doesn't have to wash the car. Mary's already washed it.

text: Raeda mea mihi lavanda est.
translation: I need to wash my car.

text: Raeda mea lavanda est.
translation: I need to get my car washed.

text: Dentes mihi lavandi sunt.
translation: I have to brush my teeth.

text: Manus mihi lavandae sunt.
translation: I have to wash my hands.

text: Corpus tibi lavandum est.
translation: You must wash your body.

text: Leva manum ad caelum.
translation: Raise your hand to the sky.

text: Adjuva me hoc levare.
translation: Help me lift this.

text: "Ipse viro primus manicas atque arta levari / vincla jubet Priamus, dictisque ita fatur amicis:"
translation: "Priam bids the cords unbind, / and thus with friendly words the captive cheers:"

text: Levavit Abraham oculos suos viditque arietem unum inter vepres hærentem cornibus; quem assumens obtulit holocaustum pro filo.
translation: Abraham lifted up his eyes, and saw behind his back a ram, amongst the briers, sticking fast by the horns, which he took and offered for a holocaust instead of his son.

text: Quod si altare lapideum feceris mihi, non ædificabis illud de sectis lapidibus; si enim levaveris cultrum super eo, polluetur.
translation: And if thou make an altar of stone unto me, thou shalt not build it of hewn stones; for if thou lift up a tool upon it, it shall be defiled.

text: Mihi etiam cum Thoma de hoc loquendum est.
translation: I still have to talk to Tom about that.

text: Estne lingua Anglica difficilis ad loquendum?
translation: Is speaking in English hard?

text: Ei sunt quibuscum tibi loquendum.
translation: Those are the people you have to talk to.

text: Anglice ei loquendum est.
translation: He needs to speak English.

text: Non est tibi loquendum.
translation: You're not supposed to talk.

text: Pater meus linguam Anglicam in lyceo docet.
translation: My father teaches English at a high school.

text: Cum in lyceo eram, linguam Gallicam didici.
translation: I studied French when I was in high school.

text: Didymus nesciebat Mariam discipulam lycei esse.
translation: Tom didn't know that Mary was a high school student.

text: Soror discipula lycei non est.
translation: My sister is not a high school student.

text: In lyceo teniludio ludebam.
translation: I used to play tennis in high school.

text: Frater discipulus lycei est.
translation: My brother is a high school student.

text: Semel in hebdomade ad macellum it.
translation: She goes to the market once a week.

text: Habitamus in domo quinquagesima, iuxta macellum.
translation: We live in house number fifty, next to the market.

text: Alicia ad macellum non ambulavit.
translation: Alice didn't walk to the market.

text: Scisne ubi macellum sit?
translation: Do you know where the supermarket is?

text: Ad macellum cotidie venit.
translation: She goes to market every day.

text: Mamma ad macellum iit.
translation: Mom went to the supermarket.

text: Magis hic mansuri quam illuc venturi videmur.
translation: It seems that we are more likely to stay here than to go there.

text: Novi Eboraci quinque dies mansura sum.
translation: I'll remain in New York for five days.

text: Dixit se mansurum esse dum revenerim.
translation: He said he'd wait for me to come back.

text: Berolini decem dies mansura sum.
translation: I'll stay in Berlin for ten days.

text: Romae tres dies mansura sum.
translation: I'll remain in Rome for three days.

text: Pekini quattuor dies mansura sum.
translation: I'll remain in Beijing for four days.

text: Sunt mihi nonnulli amici qui bene anglice loquuntur.
translation: I have several friends who speak English well.

text: Mea sententia sunt nonnulla requisita fundamentalia ad felicitatem.
translation: In my opinion, happiness has a few fundamental requirements.

text: Videtis nonnulli arbores ante scholam.
translation: You see some trees in front of the school.

text: Nonnulla ossa brachii manusque fregit.
translation: He broke some bones in his arm and hand.

text: Nonnullae feles caudas non habent.
translation: Some cats don't have tails.

text: Nonnulli discipuli relicti sunt.
translation: A few students were left behind.

text: Thomas nonagesimum nonum aetatis annum agens, mortuus est.
translation: Tom died at the age of ninety-nine.

text: Iapones oculos fuscos habent.
