text: Ubi possum invenire bonum oecum homosexualium?
translation: Where can I find a good gay club?

text: Noli nominare viros homosexuales "cinaedos".
translation: Don't ever call gays "fags".

text: Thomas non clam est homosexualis.
translation: Tom is openly gay.

text: Sami non clam erat homosexualis.
translation: Sami was openly gay.

text: Michael Angelus Bonarotius homosexualis fuit.
translation: Michelangelo was gay.

text: Bonum est homosexualis esse.
translation: It's good to be gay.

text: Apage, haud me id deceat, furem imitari.
translation: Oh come on, I'm not the sort of man to behave like a thief.

text: Psittacus humanas voces imitare potest.
translation: A parrot can imitate human speech.

text: Id se imitari posse confidebant.
translation: They believed they could imitate it.

text: Psittacus humanas voces saepe imitatur.
translation: Parrots often imitate human speech.

text: Psittaci humanas voces imitantur.
translation: Parrots imitate human speech.

text: Thomas Mariam imitatus est.
translation: Tom imitated Mary.

text: Mīlitibus imperātum est ut impetum faciant.
translation: The soldiers were ordered to make an attack.

text: Mīlitibus imperātum est ut impetum facerent.
translation: The soldiers were ordered to make an attack.

text: Nōbīs imperātum est ut impetum faciāmus.
translation: We've been ordered to attack.

text: Nōbīs imperātum est ut impetum facerēmus.
translation: We've been ordered to attack.

text: Cainus in Abelem impetum fecit.
translation: Cain attacked Abel.

text: Maria in Thoman impetum fecit.
translation: Mary attacked Tom.

text: Civis Britanniae est, sed in India habitat.
translation: He is a British citizen, but lives in India.

text: Anglus est, sed in India habitat.
translation: He's English, but lives in India.

text: Ex India oriundus non sum.
translation: I am not from India.

text: Ex India oriunda non sum.
translation: I am not from India.

text: India molibus ferarum mirabilis.
translation: India is famous for the corpulence of its beasts.

text: Fuistine umquam in India?
translation: Have you ever been to India?

text: Scissisque vestibus, indutus est cilicio lugens filium suum multo tempore.
translation: And tearing his garments, he put on sackcloth, mourning for his son a long time.

text: Fecit quoque Dominus Deus Adæ et uxori eius tunicas pelliceas et induit eos.
translation: And the Lord God made for Adam and his wife garments of skins, and clothed them.

text: Expoliavi me tunica mea, quomodo induar illa? Lavi pedes meos, quomodo inquinabo illos?
translation: I have already taken off my robe, and shall I put it on again? I have already washed my feet, and shall I dirty them again?

text: Lavare igitur, ungere et induere pallio tuo ac descende in aream; non te videat homo, donec esum potumque finierit.
translation: Wash thyself therefore and anoint thee, and put on thy best garments, and go down to the barnfloor: but let not the man see thee, till he shall have done eating and drinking.

text: Et vestibus Esau valde bonis, quas apud se habebat domi, induit eum pelliculasque hædorum circumdedit manibus et colli nuda protexit.
translation: And she put on him very good garments of Esau, which she had at home with her: and the little skins of the kids she put about his hands, and covered the bare of his neck.

text: Maria se Thoman infelicem putare dixit.
translation: Mary said she thought Tom was unhappy.

text: Infeliciter, mater mea domi non est.
translation: Unfortunately, my mother isn't at home.

text: Thomas se infelicem esse dicit.
translation: Tom says he's unhappy.

text: Maria se infelicem esse dicit.
translation: Mary says she's unhappy.

text: Hodie Thomas infelicior videbatur.
translation: Tom didn't look very happy today.

text: Miser et infelix eram.
translation: I was miserable and unhappy.

text: Tum litore funem / deripere, excussosque jubet laxare rudentes.
translation: Then bids the crews unbind / the stern-ropes, loose the sheets and spread them to the wind.

text: Inducit in stabulum, jubet ut eligam ex omnibus equis quemcunque vellem.
translation: He leads me into the stable, bids me choose out of all the horses whichsoever I would.

text: Inducit in tabernam, jubet ut eligam ex omnibus raedis quemcunque vellem.
translation: He leads me into the shop, and urges me to choose from all the cars whichever I would like.

text: "Mutandæ sedes: non hæc tibi litora suasit / Delius, aut Cretæ jussit considere, Apollo."
translation: "Not here thy destined seat, / so saith the Delian god, not thine the shores of Crete."

text: Tunc etiam fatis aperit Cassandra futuris / ora, dei jussu non umquam credita Teucris.
translation: E'en then – alas! to Trojan ears in vain – / Cassandra sang, and told in utterance plain / the coming doom.

text: Gad, latrones aggredientur eum, ipse autem aggredietur calcaneum eorum.
translation: Gad, being girded, shall fight before him: and he himself shall be girded backward.

text: Dīvitior est quam ut latrō fīat.
translation: He is too rich to become a thief.

text: Latrones pecuniam inter se diviserunt.
translation: The thieves divided the money among themselves.

text: Latrones se in silva abdiderunt.
translation: The thieves hid in the woods.

text: Latrones ex urbe aufugerunt.
translation: Bandits ran away from the city.

text: Cur canis tuus latrat?
translation: Why is your dog barking?

text: Magister me hortatus est ad legendum, scribendum et loquendum.
translation: The teacher encouraged me to read, write and speak.

text: Magistra me hortata est ad legendum, scribendum et loquendum.
translation: The teacher encouraged me to read, write and speak.

text: Ad bibliothecam ivi ad libros legendos.
translation: I went to the library to read books.

text: Tempus mihi deest ad legendos libros.
translation: I have no time to read books.

text: Tempus mihi deest ad legendum.
translation: I have no time to read.

text: Multum legendum esse non multa.
translation: One should read a lot, not a lot of things.

text: Sicut lilium inter spinas, sic amica mea inter filias.
translation: As the lily among thorns, so is my love among the girls.

text: Iulia multas rosas et multa lilia in horto suo habet.
translation: Julia has many roses and many lilies in her garden.

text: Iulius multas rosas et multa lilia in horto suo habet.
translation: Julius has many roses and many lillies in his garden.

text: Rosae mihi magis quam lilia placent.
translation: I like roses more than lilies.

text: Nec semper lilia florent.
translation: Lilies don't always bloom.

text: Duo ubera tua sicut duo hinnuli, capreæ gemelli, qui pascuntur in liliis.
translation: Thy two breasts are like two young roes that are twins, which feed among the lilies.

text: Quomodo hae duae locutiones Gallice dicuntur?
translation: How do you say these two phrases in French?

text: Placet ista locutio, sed dolendum mihi non licet eam adoptare.
translation: I like that phrase, but unfortunately, I am not allowed to adopt it.

text: Quivis potest locutiones in linguis mortuis, sicut Latinis, vel in linguis artificialibus usurpare, sicut Toki Pona et Esperanto.
translation: Anyone can adopt sentences in dead languages like Latin or artificial languages like Toki Pona and Esperanto.

text: Novi Eboraci quinque dies mansurus sum.
translation: I will stay in New York for five days.

text: Moscoviae sex dies mansurus sum.
translation: I'll remain in Moscow for six days.

text: Berolini decem dies mansurus sum.
translation: I'll stay in Berlin for ten days.

text: Athenis novem dies mansurus sum.
translation: I'll stay in Athens for nine days.

text: Pekini quattuor dies mansurus sum.
translation: I'll stay in Beijing for four days.

text: Romae tres dies mansurus sum.
translation: I'll stay in Rome for three days.

text: Is se mature domum iturum dixit quod fessus esset.
translation: He said that because he was tired, he'd go home early.

text: Senex mature fias, ut maneas diu.
translation: Be old early, that you may live long.

text: Veri simile est Thoman mature isse.
translation: Tom must've left early.

text: Hodie mane mature Nagoiam adveni.
translation: I reached Nagoya early this morning.

text: Thomas domum mature heri advenit.
translation: Tom came home early yesterday.

text: Verisimile est Thomam mature ivisse.
translation: Tom must've left early.

text: Negat sē umquam eī mentītam esse.
translation: She says that she's never lied to him.

text: Scīmus tē nōbīs mentītam esse.
translation: We know that you lied to us.

text: Scīmus tē Thōmae mentītam esse.
translation: We know that you lied to Tom.

text: Thōmās dīxit Marīam mentītam esse.
translation: Tom said that Mary lied.

text: Quotiēns mihi mentīta es?
translation: How many times have you lied to me?

text: Quotiēns mihi mentītī estis?
translation: How many times have you lied to me?

text: Lithium, natrium, kalium, rubidium, caesium, francium metalla alkalica sunt.
translation: Lithium, sodium, potassium, rubidium, caesium and francium are alkali metals.

text: Sub terra nascuntur metalla, lapides, mineralia.
translation: Metals, stones and minerals arise from under the earth.

text: Hydrogenium, carbonium, nitrogenium, phosphorus, oxygenium, sulphur, selenium non sunt metalla.
translation: Hydrogen, carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, oxygen, sulfur and selenium are nonmetals.

text: Beryllium, magnesium, calcium, strontium, barium, radium metalla alkalica terrena sunt.
translation: Beryllium, magnesium, calcium, strontium, barium and radium are alkaline earth metals.

text: Aurum est omnium metallorum pretiosissimum.
translation: Gold is the most precious of all metals.

text: Ferrum valde utile metallum est.
translation: Iron is a very useful metal.

text: Hoc monumentum plus centum annorum est.
translation: This monument is more than one hundred years old.

text: Monumentum est in media urbe.
translation: There is a monument in the center of the city.

text: si monumentum requiris, circumspice.
translation: If you seek his monument, look around.

text: Tum genitor, veterum volvens monumenta virorum, / "Audite, o proceres," ait "et spes discite vestras."
translation: Then spake my sire, revolving in his mind / the ancient legends of the Trojan kind, / "Chieftains, give ear, and learn your hopes and mine."

text: Habebitis autem hanc diem in monumentum et celebrabitis eam sollemnem Domino in generationibus vestris cultu sempiterno.
translation: And this day shall be for a memorial to you; and you shall keep it a feast to the Lord in your generations, with an everlasting observance.

text: Vespertiliones de more in tenebris volant.
translation: Bats usually fly in the dark.

text: De more recentissimo vestis non curo.
translation: I don't care about fashion.

text: "Quid agis?" "Mandrabūli more res succidit."
translation: "How is it going?" "Out of the frying pan, into the fire."

text: Mandrabūli more res succidit.
translation: Out of the frying pan, into the fire.

text: Morum maiorum studiosi sumus.
translation: We are conservative.

text: Morum maiorum studiosae sumus.
translation: We are conservative.

text: Melania errore et imprudenter muscam occidit.
translation: Melanie has accidentally killed a fly.

text: Musca in potione Arabica est.
translation: There is a fly in the coffee.

text: Quot ova parit musca?
translation: How many eggs does a fly lay?

text: Aquila muscas non capit.
translation: The eagle does not catch flies.

text: Aquila non capit muscas.
translation: The eagle does not catch flies.

text: Aquila non captat muscas.
translation: The eagle does not catch flies.

text: Daniel omnes linguas didicit Slavicas omnium nationum Europaearum Orientalium quas invisit.
translation: Dan learned the Slavic languages of all the Eastern European countries he visited.

text: Certe plerique habent Hispanicam scabiem, sive, ut quidam vocant, Gallicam, cum sit communis omnium nationum.
translation: Certainly most have the Spanish pox, or, as some call it, the French, tho it be common to all nations.

text: Somnio ut filii olim quattuor cives sint nationis in qua colore cutis non censebuntur sed qualitate mentali.
translation: I have a dream that my four little children will one day live in a nation where they will not be judged by the color of their skin, but by the content of their character.

text: Dixitque ei: Ego Deus omnipotens. Cresce et multiplicare; gens et congregatio nationum erunt ex te, reges de lumbis tuis egredientur.
translation: And said to him: I am God almighty, increase thou and be multiplied. Nations and peoples of nations shall be from thee, and kings shall come out of thy loins.

text: Thoman non novi, ergo tibi dicere qualis sit nequeo.
translation: I don't know Tom, so I can't tell you what he's like.

text: Thomae mandare nequeo ut hoc faciat.
translation: I can't order Tom to do it.

text: Mutatum saxum nequit ullum ducere muscum.
translation: A rolling stone gathers no moss.

text: Quae loquatur exaudire hinc nequeo.
translation: I can't hear what he's talking about from here.

text: Poetae sine amore vivere nequeunt.
translation: Poets cannot live without love.

text: Nequeo contineri quin loquar.
translation: I can't keep from speaking.

text: Avus et avia horum liberorum nonaginta annorum sunt.
translation: The grandparents of these children are ninety years old.

text: Didymus decessit annos septem et nonaginta natus.
translation: Tom died at the age of 97.

text: Ego nondum nonaginta annos natus sum.
translation: I am not ninety years old yet.

text: Avus noster nonaginta annos natus est.
translation: Our grandfather is ninety years old.

text: Fere nonaginta annos natus sum.
translation: I am almost ninety years old.

text: Vixitque Lamech, postquam genuit Noe, quingentos nonaginta quinque annos et genuit filios et filias.
translation: And Lamech lived after he begot Noah, five hundred and ninety-five years, and begot sons and daughters.

text: Nomen suum notavi ne eius obliviscar.
translation: I wrote down her name so as not to forget it.

text: Haec cantio nobis nota est.
translation: We know this song.

text: Haec cantio mihi nota est.
translation: I know this song.

text: Omnes homines, qui condemnati erant, occisi sunt.
translation: All the people who had been condemned were killed.

text: Filii eius ambo bello occisi sunt.
translation: Both of her sons died in the war.

text: Omnes fratres mei bello occisi sunt.
translation: All of my brothers died in the war.

text: Duae oves a lupo occisae sunt.
translation: Two sheep were killed by a wolf.

text: Feles a cane occisa est.
translation: The cat was killed by the dog.

text: Maria hoc saxo occisa est.
translation: Mary was killed with this rock.

text: Has rosas, quarum odor est suavis, tibi dono.
translation: These sweet-scented roses I give to you.

text: Hic flos odores suaves exspirat.
translation: This flower smells sweet.

text: Dum esset rex in accubitu suo, nardus mea dedit odorem suum.
translation: While the king is on his couch, my spikenard exudes its perfume.

text: Olor, candidus, Anser et Anas, natant; Mergus se mergit. His adde Fulicam, Pelecannum et cetera.
translation: The white swan, the goose and the duck swim; the Cormorant dives. To these can be added the water hen, the pelican and so on.

text: Favus distillans labia tua, sponsa; mel et lac sub lingua tua; et odor vestimentorum tuorum sicut odor thuris.
translation: Thy lips, O my spouse, drop as the honeycomb: honey and milk are under thy tongue, and the smell of thy garments is like the smell of Lebanon.

text: Potesne latinae verba originis in hac sententia cognoscere?
translation: Can you spot words of Latin origin in this sentence?

text: Regum, inquis, origo cum Sole novo coepit.
translation: The origin of Kings, you say, is as ancient as that of the sun.

text: In terminis thermodynamicis, singularitas est vicus qui nullum habet exitum. Originem universi non explicat.
translation: A singularity is a thermodynamic dead end and does not explain the origin of the universe.

text: Oryza omnia edimus, sed fabam reliquimus.
translation: We ate all the rice but left the beans.

text: Panis mihi magis quam oryza placet.
translation: I like bread more than rice.

text: Hoc in agro sata est oryza.
translation: Rice is planted in this field.

text: Eduntne homines terrae tuae oryzam?
translation: Do the people of your country eat rice?

text: Edisne oryzam in terra tua?
translation: Do you eat rice in your country?

text: Editisne oryzam in terra vestra?
translation: Do you eat rice in your country?

text: Didymus multo peritior est quam ego.
translation: Tom is way more experienced than I am.

text: Thōmās multō perītior est quam ego.
translation: Tom is far more experienced than me.

text: Didymus multo peritior est me.
translation: Tom is way more experienced than I am.

text: Thōmās multō perītior est mē.
translation: Tom is much more experienced than me.

text: Marīa perītior est quam ego.
translation: Mary is more experienced than I am.

text: Thōmās perītior est quam ego.
translation: Tom is more experienced than me.

text: Poemata scribo ex amore, non ex officio.
translation: I write poetry out of love, not out of duty.

text: Poemata Homeri Graece scripta sunt.
translation: The poems of Homer were written in Greek.

text: Haicu genus poematis est.
translation: A haiku is one type of poem.

text: Mutum est pictura poema.
translation: A painting is a wordless poem.

text: Hoc poema non intellego.
translation: I don't understand this poem.

text: Poema Thomae non intellego.
translation: I don't understand Tom's poem.

text: Cui dixit Iacob: Vende mihi prius primogenita tua.
translation: And Jacob said to him: Sell me thy first birthright.

text: Ille respondit: En morior; quid mihi proderunt primogenita?
translation: He answered: Lo I die, what will the first birthright avail me?

text: Cum viginti annos nata esset, primogenitum peperit.
translation: She gave birth to her first child at twenty years old.

text: Quatuor sorores omnes mirandae sunt. Filia primogenita est pulcherrima.
translation: The four sisters are wonderful. The eldest is the most beautiful.

text: Dedit autem Iudas uxorem primogenito suo Her nomine Thamar.
translation: And Juda took a wife for Her, his first born, whose name was Thamar.

text: Ait Iacob: “Iura ergo mihi”. Iuravit et vendidit primogenita.
translation: Jacob said: Swear therefore to me. Esau swore to him, and sold his first birthright.

text: Cubiculum meum mihi purgandum est.
translation: I have to clean my room.

text: Cubiculum Didymi ei purgandum est.
translation: Tom needs to clean his room.

text: Culina nobis purganda est.
translation: We must clean up the kitchen.

text: Cubiculum Didymo purgandum est.
translation: Tom needs to clean his room.

text: Cubiculum Lisae purgandum est.
translation: Lisa's room needs to be cleaned.

text: Domus mihi purganda est.
translation: I have to clean the house.

text: Ioannes Thoman cum Maria in gratiam reduxit.
translation: John reconciled Tom and Mary.

text: Dixit Abraham: Cave, ne quando reducas illuc filium meum.
translation: And Abraham said: Beware thou never bring my son back again thither.

text: Reduc me. Domum redire volo.
translation: Take me back. I want to go home.

text: Thomas domum reductus est.
translation: Tom was accompanied back home.

text: Sin autem noluerit mulier sequi te, non teneberis iuramento; filium tantum meum ne reducas illuc.
translation: But if the woman will not follow thee, thou shalt not be bound by the oath: only bring not my son back thither again.

text: Magister eos docuit Terram rotundam esse.
translation: The teacher taught them that the earth is round.

text: Prope villam est magnus lacus rotundus.
translation: There is a large round lake near the village.

text: Magister dixit Terram rotundam esse.
translation: The teacher said that the earth is round.

text: Terram rotundam esse verum est.
translation: It is true that the earth is round.

text: Columbus putabat Terram rotundam esse.
translation: Columbus believed that the earth was round.

text: Columbus dicebat Terram rotundam esse.
translation: Columbus claimed the Earth was round.

text: Sanctus Vincentius urbs prima in Brasilia fuit.
translation: São Vicente was the first city in Brazil.

text: Sanctus Antonius Patavinus est patronus rerum perditarum.
translation: Saint Anthony of Padua is the patron saint of lost things.

text: Post suam mortem sanctus est.
translation: After his death, he was sainted.

text: Exoptatus Sanctum Franciscum advenisti.
translation: Welcome to San Francisco.

text: incarnatus est de spiritu sanctu ex maria virgine et homo factus est.
translation: He was incarnate of the Holy Spirit from the Virgin Mary, and was made man.

text: Dux fuisti in misericordia tua populo, quem redemisti, et portasti eum in fortitudine tua ad habitaculum sanctum tuum.
translation: In thy mercy thou hast been a leader to the people which thou hast redeemed: and in thy strength thou hast carried them to thy holy habitation.

text: Id quod dixit verum non est, quod sciam.
translation: As far as I know, what he has said is true.

text: Ea quae dixit vera non sunt, quod sciam.
translation: As far as I know, what he has said is true.

text: Sciam cur id mihi non agendum sit.
translation: I'd like to know why I shouldn't do that.

text: Thomas, quod sciam, non maritus est.
translation: As far as I know, Tom isn't married.

text: Ille ipse, quod sciam, hoc dixit.
translation: As far as I know, he said that himself.

text: Quomodo num aliquem delectem sciam?
translation: How can I know if a guy likes me?

text: Hoc animal in solitudine illa invenitur.
translation: This is an animal found in that desert.

text: Nos solitudo vivos facit, alienatio interficit.
translation: Solitude vitalizes; isolation kills.

text: Ubi solitudinem faciunt, pacem appellant.
translation: Where they make a desert, they call it peace.

text: Solitudinem faciunt, pacem apellant.
translation: They make a wilderness, and they call it peace.

text: Et murmuravit omnis congregatio filiorum Israel contra Moysen et Aaron in solitudine.
translation: And all the congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness.

text: Viam trium dierum pergemus in solitudinem et sacrificabimus Domino Deo nostro, sicut præcepit nobis.
translation: We will go three days' journey into the wilderness; and we will sacrifice to the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.

text: Didymus et Maria inter se aspexerunt atque subriserunt.
translation: Tom and Mary looked at each other and smiled.

text: Homines approbationem nutando, plaudendo, subridendo vel ridendo indicant.
translation: People communicate approval by nodding, by clapping their hands, by smiling or laughing.

text: Simul atque me vidit subridens me salutavit.
translation: As soon as she saw me, she greeted me with a smile.

text: Ei salutem dixit et ea subrisit.
translation: I said hello to her and she smiled.

text: Medicus subrisit, ac mitigavit consilium.
translation: The doctor smiled, and qualified his advice.

text: Omnes in imagine photographica subrident.
translation: Everybody in the picture is smiling.

text: Putabam me suffragium habere.
translation: I thought I had the right to vote.

text: Thomae suffragium non tuli.
translation: I didn't vote for Tom.

text: Ei suffragium non tuli.
translation: I didn't vote for him.

text: Tibi suffragium non tuli.
translation: I didn't vote for you.

text: Tempus est suffragium ferre.
translation: It's time to vote.

text: Thomas Mariae suffragium tulit.
translation: Tom voted for Mary.

text: Libri mentionem fecit cuius titulus meam memoriam nunc refugit.
translation: He mentioned a book the title of which I can't remember now.

text: Lēgī librum cui titulus est "Rēgulus".
translation: I have read the book "The little prince".

text: Libri mentionem fecit cuius titulus mihi nunc in mentem non venit
translation: He mentioned a book the title of which I can't remember now.

text: Recordarisne tituli illius libri?
translation: Do you remember the title of that book?

text: Quid hic titulus significat?
translation: What does this mark mean?

text: Titulum nuntii legi solum.
translation: I read only the headline.

text: Soror mea proxima aestate tredecim annos nata erit.
translation: My sister will be thirteen years old next summer.

text: Thomas erat annos natus tredecim, cum Bostoniam venit.
translation: Tom came to Boston when he was thirteen years old.

text: Hic liber habet capita tredecim.
translation: This book has 13 chapters.

text: Decem, undecim, duodecim, tredecim, quattuordecim, quindecim, sedecim, septendecim, duodeviginti, undeviginti, viginti.
translation: Ten, eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen, twenty.

text: Puer sum tredecim annos natus.
translation: I'm a 13-year-old boy.

text: Alexander tredecim annos regnavit.
translation: Alexander ruled for thirteen years.

text: Dic mihi, quaeso, modo quid velis.
translation: Please just tell me what you want.

text: Intellego quid mihi dicere velis.
translation: I understand what you're trying to tell me.

text: Quid bibere velis, bone vir?
translation: What would you like to drink, sir?

text: Quoniam non potest id fieri quod vis, is velis quod possit.
translation: He that may not do as he would must do as he may.

text: Nescio quid dicere velis.
translation: I don't know what you want to say.

text: Adjuvare possum, si velis.
translation: I can help, if you want.

text: Heri nos videndi causa venit.
translation: She came to see us yesterday.

text: Thomas ad te videndum venit.
translation: Tom has come to see you.

text: Oculi ad videndum facti sunt.
translation: Eyes were made for seeing.

text: Thomas venit me videndi causa.
translation: Tom came to see me.

text: Thomas veni Mariam videndi causa.
translation: Tom came to see Mary.

text: Veni causa eam videndi.
translation: I came to see her.

text: Sero ad litteras saepe vigilat scribendas.
translation: He often sits up late writing letters.

text: Thomas dormit, sed Maria vigilat.
translation: Tom is asleep, but Mary is awake.

text: Spero fore ut Thomas vigilet.
translation: I hope Tom is awake.

text: Sero nocte vigilat studio.
translation: He sits up studying till late at night.

text: Nocte solet sero vigilare.

translation: Tom and Mary are ready to leave.

text: Thomae et Mariae mox proficiscendum erit.
translation: Tom and Mary are going to have to leave soon.

text: Thomas paratus ad proficiscendum non est.
translation: Tom isn't ready to leave.

text: Non sum paratus ad proficiscendum.
translation: I'm not ready to go.

text: Mox Thomae proficiscendum erit.
translation: Tom is going to have to leave soon.

text: Quies suburbana regio praebet ambitum perfectum ad familiam excitandam.
translation: The quiet suburban neighborhood provides the perfect milieu for raising a family.

text: Si quietem mavis, duc uxorem parem.
translation: If you prefer a peaceful life, seek a like-minded spouse.

text: Quiete cenabamus cum subito mater mea se in scholam redire nuntiavit.
translation: We were having a quiet supper when out of the blue my mother announced she was going back to school.

text: Postquam prima quies epulis mensæque remotae, / crateras magnos statuunt et vina coronant.
translation: Now, hushed the banquet and the tables all / removed, huge wine-bowls for each guest apart / they wreathe with flowers.

text: Quid liberis tuis nomina tam ridicula dare potes?
translation: How can you give your children such ridiculous names?

text: Parturient montes, nascetur ridiculus mus.
translation: The mountains will labor, and a ridiculous mouse will be born.

text: Hoc ridiculum esse putas?
translation: Do you think that's funny?

text: Calor et silentium in horto erat.
translation: It was warm and quiet in the park.

text: Silentium clamat omni disputatio majus.
translation: The quiet screams louder than any argument.

text: Erat silentium in silva.
translation: There was silence in the woods.

text: Haec spelunca anno bis millesimo tertio decimo reperta est.
translation: This cave was discovered in 2013.

text: Saxum, quod in spelunca invenerunt, pondo fere ducenta chiliogrammata pendit.
translation: The rock they found in the cave weighs almost two hundred kilograms.

text: Marīam in spēluncam dūxit Thōmās.
translation: Tom led Mary into the cave.

text: Speluncae portam obstruit draco.
translation: The entrance to the cave is blocked by a dragon.

text: Cyclopes in speluncis habitabant.
translation: The cyclopes lived in caves.

text: Thomas gladium e vagina eduxit eumque sustulit.
translation: Tom pulled out his sword and raised it.

text: Avis rostro sarmentum sustulit et ad nidum suum advolavit.
translation: The bird picked up the twig with its beak and flew to its nest.

text: Thomas librum sustulit eumque Mariae dedit.
translation: Tom picked the book up and handed it to Mary.

text: Difficultatum mearum se taedet.
translation: He is fed up with my problems.

text: Taedet me verborum tuorum.
translation: I'm bored of your language.

text: Taedebat me sermonis eius.
translation: His speech bored me.

text: Me taedet vitae quotidianae.
translation: Everyday life bores me.

text: Pisces quoque, qui sunt in fluvio, morientur, et computrescent aquæ, et tædebit Aegyptios bibere aquam fluminis.
translation: And the fishes that are in the river shall die, and the waters shall be corrupted, and the Egyptians shall be afflicted when they drink the water of the river.

text: Descendit autem Dominus ut videret civitatem et turrim.
translation: And the Lord came down to see the city and the tower.

text: Multis ab hinc annis ex turri cecidit.
translation: Many years have passed since he fell from the tower.

text: Pallida mors aequo pulsat pede pauperum tabernas regumque turres.
translation: Pale death comes to both the huts of the poor and the castles of kings.

text: Domus mea prope Turrim Tokii est.
translation: My house is near Tokyo Tower.

text: Palatium altam turrim habet.
translation: The palace has a tall tower.

text: Vidistine unquam Turrim Tokii?
translation: Have you ever seen Tokyo Tower?

text: "Visne dare mihi unicam pennam?" "Non dantur mihi."
translation: "Will you lend me a pen?" "I don't have any."

text: Visne dare mihi unicam pennam?
translation: Will you give me one pen?

text: Thomas fuit unicus amicus Mariae.
translation: Tom was Mary's only friend.

text: Tu es unica spes nostra.
translation: You're our only hope.

text: Feles quaeque unica est.
translation: Every cat is unique.

text: Cerebrum tuum est unicum.
translation: Your brain is unique.

text: Non omnibus vehiculo opus est.
translation: Not everybody needs a car.

text: Quali vehiculo usus es?
translation: What form of transportation did you use?

text: Quali vehiculo usa es?
translation: What form of transportation did you use?

text: Quali vehiculo usi estis?
translation: What form of transportation did you use?

text: Quali vehiculo usae estis?
translation: What form of transportation did you use?

text: Lingua vehiculum cogitationis est.
translation: Language is the vehicle of thought.

text: Nōlī eō absente dē hīs rēbus loquī.
translation: Don't talk about that in his absence.

text: Antequam domum adveni numquam perulam annotaveram absentem.
translation: I never even noticed I'd lost my wallet until I got home.

text: Me absente, ille vicarius meus erit.
translation: He will be my deputy while I am away.

text: Puto Thoman et Mariam absentes esse.
translation: I think Tom and Mary are gone.

text: Tua absentia in Australia habitare nequirem.
translation: I couldn't live in Australia without you.

text: Tenebrae sunt lucis absentia.
translation: Darkness is the absence of light.

text: Defendi rem publicam adulescens, non deseram senex.
translation: I defended the republic as a young man, I shall not desert it in my old age.

text: Quem di diligunt adulescens moritur.
translation: He whom the gods love dies young.

text: Adolescentis est maiores natu revereri.
translation: Young people should respect their elders.

text: Maria dixit se Thoman amare atque semper amaturam.
translation: Mary said that she loved Tom and always would love him.

text: Thomas dixit se Mariam amare atque semper amaturum.
translation: Tom said that he loved Mary and always would love her.

text: Maria dixit se Thoman semper amaturam esse.
translation: Mary said that she would always love Tom.

text: Thomas dixit se Mariam semper amaturum esse.
translation: Tom said that he would always love Mary.

text: Dixi me eam non amare neque unquam amaturum esse.
translation: I said that I did not love her nor would I ever love her.

text: Dixi me eum non amare neque unquam amaturam esse.
translation: I said that I did not love him nor would I ever love him.

text: Nam tui Catulli plenus sacculus est aranearum.
translation: For your Catullus' purse is completely covered in cobwebs.

text: Librum de araneis regionis meae scribere volo.
translation: I want to write a book about the spiders of my region.

text: Araneis et scorpionibus octo pedes sunt.
translation: Spiders and scorpions have eight legs.

text: Araneae, scorpiones et ricini arachnida sunt.
translation: Spiders, scorpions, and ticks are arachnids.

text: Araneam videt et concidit animo.
translation: She sees a spider and she faints.

text: Araneis octo pedes sunt.
translation: Spiders have eight legs.

text: Imago venit in mentem una: orbis suspectus et ater.
translation: One image comes to mind: an eerie, pitch-black disk.

text: Ea in habitu atro semper vestita est.
translation: She always wears black.

text: Didymus in atrum intrantem vidi.
translation: I saw Tom going into the cave.

text: Nonne atrum militare habitum geris?
translation: Do you wear a black uniform?

text: Hi semper atras vestes gerunt.
translation: Those men always wear black.

text: Nubes atrae oriri coeperunt.
translation: Black clouds began to come up.

text: Avaritia unum est ex septem peccatis mortalibus.
translation: Greed is one of the seven deadly sins.

text: Inopiae desunt multa, avaritiae omnia.
translation: Poor people lack many things, greedy lack everything.

text: Avaritia una est ex saligiis.
translation: Greed is one of the seven deadly sins.

text: Ira et avaritia sunt periculosæ.
translation: Fury and avarice are dangerous.

text: Ira et avaritia sunt periculosa.
translation: Fury and avarice are dangerous.

text: Ira et avaritia periculosae sunt.
translation: Fury and avarice are dangerous.

text: Butyrum et caseus e lacte parantur.
translation: Butter and cheese are made from milk.

text: Saccharum dulce est, butyrum pingue est.
translation: Sugar is sweet, butter is fat.

text: Et panis et butyrum ei placent.
translation: He likes bread and butter.

text: Butyro egeo. Estne tibi butyrum?
translation: I need some butter. Do you have any?

text: Estne butyrum in armario frigidario?
translation: Is there any butter in the refrigerator?

text: Butyrum e lacte vaccarum paratur.
translation: The butter is made from cows' milk.

text: Hic calix ex auro factus est.
translation: This goblet is made of gold.

text: Num calicem ex auro vides?
translation: You can’t see a golden cup, can you?

text: Num pueri calicem vides?
translation: You don’t see the boy’s cup?

text: Hic calix aureus est.
translation: This goblet is made of gold.

text: Thomas ac Maria censent se cantores esse peritos.
translation: Tom and Mary think they're good singers.

text: Cantrix est tam clara quam Madonna.
translation: The singer is as famous as Madonna.

text: Cantrix est pariter clara ac Madonna.
translation: The singer is as famous as Madonna.

text: Cantrix est aeque clara ac Madonna.
translation: The singer is as famous as Madonna.

text: Cantrix est aeque clara atque Madonna.
translation: The singer is as famous as Madonna.

text: Non cantrix sed actrix est.
translation: She is not a singer, but an actress.

text: Iulia rosas carpit et cum quinque rosis ex horto venit.
translation: Julia picks some roses, and goes from the garden with five roses.

text: Non licet tibi flores carpere.
translation: You may not pick the flowers.

text: Thomas et Maria flores carpunt.
translation: Tom and Mary are picking flowers.

text: Flores in horto carpsimus.
translation: We picked flowers in the garden.

text: Flores in horto carpsit.
translation: She picked flowers in the garden.

text: Thomas Mariae flores carpsit.
translation: Tom picked some flowers for Mary.

text: Ubi est proxima cella telephonica?
translation: Where is the nearest telephone box?

text: Domus mea duas cellas habet.
translation: My house has two pantries.

text: Cella plena hominibus est.
translation: The room is full of people.

text: Domus mea cellam habet.
translation: My house has a pantry.

text: In vita hominis cellae nervorum crescunt, retractant, efficiunt et frangunt nexus cum aliis nervorum cellis.
translation: Throughout a person's life, nerve cells are growing, retracting, creating, and breaking connections with other nerve cells.

text: Sunt in cellis pulmonis sicut fila pectinata, quarum continua pulsus mucum et infectiones e pulmone tuo expellunt.
translation: There are comb-like strands in the lung cells, whose continuous beating drives mucus and infections out of your lungs.

text: E systematis solaris planetis oblongissimus est Mercurii circuitus.
translation: Mercury has the most elliptical orbit of any planet in the Solar System.

text: Et Iesus mirabatur propter incredulitatem eorum, et circuibat castella in circuitu docens.
translation: And Jesus wondered because of their unbelief, and he went through the villages round about teaching.

text: Et nomen fluvio secundo Geon: ipse est, qui circuit omnem terram Aethiopiæ.
translation: And the name of the second river is Gehon: the same is it that compasseth all the land of Ethiopia.

text: Factum est ergo vespere, et ascendens coturnix operuit castra; mane quoque ros iacuit per circuitum castrorum.
translation: So it came to pass in the evening, that quails coming up, covered the camp: and in the morning a dew lay round about the camp.

text: Foderunt autem omnes Aegyptii per circuitum fluminis aquam, ut biberent; non enim poterant bibere de aqua fluminis.
translation: And all the Egyptians dug round about the river for water to drink; for they could not drink of the water of the river.

text: Cumque profecti essent, terror Dei invasit omnes per circuitum civitates, et non sunt ausi persequi filios Iacob.
translation: And when they were departed, the terror of God fell upon all the cities round about, and they durst not pursue after them as they went away.

text: Circulus manens ad fores stabat.
translation: A bunch of people were standing outside waiting.

text: Quadraginta homines in circulo sunt.
translation: There are forty people in the group.

text: Circulus trecentos sexaginta gradus habet.
translation: A circle has three hundred sixty degrees.

text: Nōlī turbāre circulōs meōs!
translation: Do not disturb my circles!

text: Delinea mihi circulum magnum.
translation: Draw me a large circle.

text: Estne in hoc circulo?
translation: Is he in this group?

text: Professor cum Maria coffeam bibit.
translation: The professor drinks coffee with Mary.

text: Thomas theam quam coffeam mavult.
translation: Tom prefers tea to coffee.

text: Didymus theam quam coffeam mavult.
translation: Tom prefers tea to coffee.

text: Dominus Smith coffeam bibit.
translation: Mr Smith is drinking coffee.

text: Da mihi coffeam, quaeso.
translation: Give me a coffee, please.

text: Coffeam sine saccharo, quaeso.
translation: A coffee without sugar, please.

text: Post coitum omne animal triste est præter mulierem gallumque.
translation: Every animal is sad after coitus, except the woman and the rooster.

text: Volo, Thomas, ut amico meo coeas.
translation: I want you to meet my friend, Tom.

text: Thomae persuadere nobis coire conatus sum.
translation: I tried to talk Tom into going with us.

text: Coitus tropaeum non est.
translation: Sex is not a trophy.

text: Declinansque ad eam in via ait: “Veni, coeam tecum”; nesciebat enim quod nurus sua esset.
translation: And going to her, he said: Suffer me to lie with thee: for he knew her not to be his daughter-in-law.

text: Factumque est ut in ipso calore coitus greges intuerentur virgas et parerent striata et varia et maculosa.
translation: And it came to pass, that in the very heat of coition, the sheep beheld the rods, and brought forth ringstraked, speckled, and spotted lambs.

text: Thomas huc venit ut computatorio meo uteretur.
translation: Tom came here to use my computer.

text: Thomas huc venit ut computatorio meo utar.
translation: Tom came here to use my computer.

text: Machina computatoria praesentior est quam abacus.
translation: A calculator is more efficient than an abacus.

text: Machina computatoria praesentior est abaco.
translation: A calculator is more efficient than an abacus.

text: Thomas computatorio scribere desiit.
translation: Tom stopped typing.

text: Ego duo computatoria habeo, sed utrumque fractum est. Nunc computatorio sororis, quae abest, utor.
translation: I have two computers, but they're both broken. So now I'm using my sister's while she's away.

text: Veneruntque simul et congregaverunt cunctos seniores filiorum Israel.
translation: And they came together, and they assembled all the ancients of the children of Israel.

text: Congregamini et audite, filii Iacob, audite Israel patrem vestrum!
translation: Gather yourselves together, and hear, O ye sons of Jacob, hearken to Israel, your father:

text: Vere aquilæ hic congregantur.
translation: Eagles congregate here in the spring.

text: Vocavit autem Iacob filios suos et ait eis: Congregamini, ut annuntiem, quæ ventura sunt vobis in diebus novissimis.
translation: And Jacob called his sons, and said to them: Gather yourselves together, that I may tell you the things that shall befall you in the last days.

text: Dixit vero Deus: “Congregentur aquæ, quæ sub cælo sunt, in locum unum, et appareat arida”. Factumque est ita.
translation: God also said; Let the waters that are under the heaven be gathered together into one place: and let the dry land appear. And it was so done.

text: Dixitque: Adhuc multum diei superest, nec est tempus, ut congregentur greges; date potum ovibus et sic ad pastum eas reducite.
translation: And Jacob said: There is yet much day remaining, neither is it time to bring the flocks into the folds again: first give the sheep drink, and so lead them back to feed.

text: Cum sorore controversiam habui.
translation: I had a quarrel with my sister.

text: Melius est a sapiente corripi, quam stultorum adulatione decipi.
translation: It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a man to hear the song of fools.

text: Illum expirantem transfixo pectore flammas turbine corripuit scopuloque infixit acuto.
translation: She snatched him up in a whirlwind, exhaling flames from his pierced chest, and impaled him on the point of a rock.

text: Quo cursum corripis, parva lepus?
translation: Where are you running, little hare?

text: Quo te corripis, puella?
translation: Where are you going in such a hurry, girl?

text: Thomas morbo correptus est.
translation: Tom got sick.

text: Corripuere viam interea, qua semita monstrat; / jamque ascendebant collem, qui plurimus urbi / imminet adversasque aspectat desuper arces.
translation: They by the path their forward steps pursued, / and climbed a hill, whose fronting summit frowned / steep o'er the town.

text: Thomas tempestive cubitum ibat, quia fatigatus erat.
translation: Tom was tired, so he went to bed early.

text: Cum iam sero esset, cubitum adivi.
translation: Since it was already late, I went to sleep.

text: Surgo, cum cubitum eunt.
translation: I get up when they go to sleep.

text: Thomas laetus cubitum abivit.
translation: Tom went to sleep happy.

text: Maria laeta cubitum abivit.
translation: Mary went to sleep happy.

text: Prius autem quam irent cubitum, viri civitatis, viri Sodomæ, vallaverunt domum a iuvene usque ad senem, omnis populus simul.
translation: But before they went to bed, the men of the city beset the house, both young and old, all the people together.

text: Spernens omne datum non se facit esse ligatum.
translation: Spurning every gift, he does not let himself be bound.

text: Quia fortasse devoratis uno convictu quod datum fuerat in tres.
translation: Because you devour in one meal what was given for three.

text: Date ei gladium ne interficiatur.
translation: Give him a sword so he won't be killed.

text: Date mihi operam, quaeso.
translation: Please give me your attention.

text: "Nempe, quia novit vos esse gulosos." "Quomodo sumus gulosi?" "Quia fortasse devoratis uno convictu, quod datum fuerat in tres."
translation: "Sure, because she knows you're gluttons." "How are we gluttons?" "Maybe because you devour at one meal what had been meant for three."

text: Thomas rogari vult ut hoc denuo faciat.
translation: Tom wants to be asked to do that again.

text: Et si patis, mea lux, denuo moriar.
translation: And if you suffer, my love, I will die again.

text: Medici tibi dicunt fratrem tuum numquam denuo experrecturum esse.
translation: The doctors tell you that your brother will never wake up again.

text: Nisi quis renatus fuerit denuo, non potest videre regnum Dei.
translation: No one can see the kingdom of God unless he is born again.

text: Illam peliculam denuo videre volo.
translation: I want to watch that movie again.

text: Esne pecuniae tuae denuo oblitus?
translation: Did you forget your money again?

text: Nemo audivit Thoman dicentem Mariae nomen.
translation: No one has heard Tom say Mary's name.

text: Urgebantque Aegyptii populum de terra exire velociter dicentes: Omnes moriemur.
translation: And the Egyptians pressed the people to go forth out of the land speedily, saying: We shall all die.

text: Rursum illa dicente: Si dederis mihi arrabonem, donec mittas illum.
translation: And when she said again: I will suffer what thou wilt, if thou give me a pledge, till thou send what thou promisest.

text: Veneruntque præfecti filiorum Israel et vociferati sunt ad pharaonem dicentes: Cur ita agis contra servos tuos?
translation: And the officers of the children of Israel came, and cried out to Pharaoh, saying: Why dealest thou so with thy servants?

text: Ecce autem post tres menses nuntiaverunt Iudæ dicentes: Fornicata est Thamar nurus tua et gravida est ex fornicatione.
translation: And behold, after three months, they told Juda, saying: Thamar, thy daughter-in-law, hath played the harlot, and she appeareth to have a big belly.

text: Da mihi, quaeso, orthographiam huius dicti?
translation: Could you spell it, please?

text: Omnibus dictis gestisque evasit mendax.
translation: He turned out to be a liar when all was said and done.

text: His dictis profecta est.
translation: After she said these things, she departed.

text: Mihi dicto audiens est.
translation: He obeys my orders.

text: Pater meus saepe vascula eluit.
translation: My father often washes the dishes.

text: Gratias ago, quod vascula eluisti.
translation: Thanks for washing the dishes.

text: Cena absoluta vascula elui.
translation: After eating dinner, I washed the dishes.

text: Post cenam vascula elui.
translation: After eating dinner, I washed the dishes.

text: Vascula post cenam elui.
translation: I washed the dishes after supper.

text: Non etiam vascula elui.
translation: I haven't yet washed the dishes.

text: Mihi opus est iurem coquere ac escaria lavare.
translation: I need to cook the soup and wash the dishes.

text: Thomae vasa escaria lavare non placet.
translation: Tom doesn't like washing dishes.

text: Vasa escaria post cenam lavi.
translation: I washed the dishes after supper.

text: Ego vasa escaria lavi.
translation: I was the one who washed the dishes.

text: Tum vasa escaria lavabat.
translation: She was washing the dishes then.

text: Puella vasa escaria lavat.
translation: The girl is doing the dishes.

text: Una abhinc hora e somno experrecta sum.
translation: I got up an hour ago.

text: Septima hora e somno experrecta sum.
translation: I got up at seven.

text: Caelo albente e somno experrecta sum.
translation: I woke up at sunrise.

text: Quandō ē somnō experrēcta es?
translation: When did you wake up?

text: Sero e somno experrecta est.
translation: She got up late.

text: Maria saltat ut exprimat affectus.
translation: Mary dances to express her feelings.

text: Thomas Mariam paniculum fartum sub arbore edentem vidit.
translation: Tom saw Mary eating a sandwich under the tree.

text: "Esurisne?" "Non esurio. Cum in schola eram, paniculum fartum edi."
translation: "Are you hungry?" "I'm not hungry. When I was at school, I ate a sandwich."

text: Eum paniculum fartum edentem vidit.
translation: She saw him eating a sandwich.

text: Noli paniculum fartum meum tangere!
translation: Don't touch my sandwich!

text: Panis est fartus caseo.
translation: The bread is stuffed with cheese.

text: Ii paniculum fartum edunt.
translation: They are eating a sandwich.

text: Acta diurna hodierna iam legi.
translation: I have already read today's paper.

text: Ubi acta diurna hodierna sunt?
translation: Where is today's paper?

text: Haec acta diurna hodierna sunt.
translation: This is today's newspaper.

text: Vídistíne acta díurna hodierna?
translation: Have you seen today's paper?

text: Ambulavi totum diem hodiernum.
translation: I've been walking all day.

text: Non sum ignarus multos studiose contra meam sententiam esse dicturos.
translation: I am well aware that many will eagerly argue against my view.

text: Ignarus erat oppidum eversum fuisse.
translation: He was ignorant of the fact that the town had been destroyed.

text: "Sed tibi qui cursum venti, quæ fata dedere, / aut quisnam ignarum nostris deus appulit oris?"
translation: "But thou – what chance, or god, or stormy squalls / have driven thee here unweeting?"

text: "O socii (neque enim ignari sumus ante malorum), / o passi graviora, dabit deus his quoque finem".
translation: "Comrades! of ills not ignorant; far more / than these ye suffered, and to these as well / will Jove give ending, as he gave before."

text: "Ignari hominumque locorumque / erramus, vento huc vastis et fluctibus acti. / Multa tibi ante aras nostra cadet hostia dextra".
translation: "Say, who the people, what the clime and place, / and many a victim's blood thy hallowed shrine shall grace."

text: Domi manere malim quam in calorem inire.
translation: I would rather stay at home than go out in this hot weather.

text: Num absque me inisti?
translation: You didn't begin without me, did you?

text: Abiturus eram cum inisti.
translation: I was about to leave when you came in.

text: Cur absque me inisti?
translation: Why did you begin without me?

text: Eum vidi domum inire.
translation: I saw him enter the house.

text: Noli absque me inire.
translation: Don't begin without me.

text: Inopi beneficium bis dat qui dat celeriter.
translation: He gives twice who gives quickly.

text: Accipere humanum est, inopi donare deorum.
translation: To accept gifts is human, to give to the poor is of gods.

text: Somnis inopia caput dolet suum.
translation: She had a headache from lack of sleep.

text: Latina lingua non inops.
translation: The Latin language is not poor.

text: Translationes nihil aliud sunt quam interpretationes originalis.
translation: Translations are nothing more than interpretations of the original.

text: Verbum "gentilis" interpretatio est verbi Hebraici "goi".
translation: The word "gentile" is derived from a Latin translation of the Hebrew word "goy."

text: Videruntque ambo somnium nocte una iuxta interpretationem congruam sibi.
translation: And they both dreamed a dream the same night, according to the interpretation agreeing to themselves.

text: Omnis translatio aliquo modo est interpretatio.
translation: Every translation is in some ways an interpretation.

text: Bona interpretatio non interpretationi similis apparet.
translation: A good translation does not look like a translation.

text: Credidit Deo, et reputatum est ei ad iustitiam.
translation: Abram believed God, and it was reputed to him unto justice.

text: Beati, qui esuriunt et sitiunt iustitiam, quoniam ipsi saturabuntur.
translation: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness: for they will be filled.

text: Beati, qui persecutionem patiuntur propter iustitiam, quoniam ipsorum est regnum caelorum.
translation: Blessed are those who are persecuted for righteousness sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

text: Fiat justitia ruat cælum.
translation: Let justice be done though the heavens fall.

text: Populus iustitiam socialem postulat.
translation: The people demand social justice.

text: Vir minus libi habet quam filius eius.
translation: The man has less cake than his son.

text: Maria primam libi partem Thomae dedit.

translation: I will bless them that bless thee, and curse them that curse thee, and in thee shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed.

text: Non maledices surdo, nec coram caeco pones offendiculum: sed timebis Dominum Deum tuum, quia ego sum Dominus.
translation: You shall not curse the deaf, nor put a stumbling block before the blind, but you shall fear your God. I am the Lord.

text: Qui est sine peccato, primus lapidem mittat.

translation: "How much do you want?" "Five pence, if it is convenient." "I don't have that many." "How many then?" "Just four."

translation: "How much money do you have?" "A penny and a half; how much do you have?" "Not as much." "How much then?" "One penny."

text: Comitia generalia dicuntur fore ut proximo autumno habeantur.

translation: "Here Scylla, gaping from her gloomy lair, / the passing vessels on the rocks doth hale."

translation: "Enough and more, to live when Ilion fell, / and once to see Troy captured."

translation: But meanwhile it flees: time flees irretrievably, while we wander around, prisoners of our love of detail.

translation: The Cock (which crows in the morning) has a comb and spurs; when castrated, is called a capon and is crammed in a Coop.

text: Quos cum vidisset, ait: "Castra Dei sunt hæc”; et appellavit nomen loci illius Mahanaim (id est Castra).
translation: And when he saw them, he said: These are the camps of God, and called the name of that place Mahanaim, that is, Camps.

text: Iamque advenerat vigilia matutina, et ecce respiciens Dominus super castra Aegyptiorum per columnam ignis et nubis perturbavit exercitum eorum.
translation: And now the morning watch was come, and behold the Lord looking upon the Egyptian army through the pillar of fire and of the cloud, slew their host.

text: Lingua Anglica optimum communicationis medium in mundo est.
translation: English is a better means of communication than any other in the world.

text: Exactores quoque instabant dicentes: Complete opus vestrum cotidie, ut prius facere solebatis, quando dabantur vobis paleæ.
translation: And the overseers of the works pressed them, saying: Fulfil your work every day, as before ye were wont to do, when straw was given you.

text: "Huc delecta virum sortiti corpora furtim / includunt cæco lateri, penitusque cavernas / ingentes uterumque armato milite complent."
translation: "And deep within the sides of pine / and caverns of the womb by stealth enclose / armed men, a chosen band, drawn as the lots dispose."

text: Dixitque Noemi: Exspecta, filia, donec videamus quem res exitum habeat; neque enim cessabit homo, nisi compleverit hodie, quod locutus est.
translation: Then she said, "Wait, my daughter, until you know what will happen; for the man will not rest until he has settled this today."

text: Quod ergo Deus coniunxit, homo non separet.
translation: What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.

text: Thomas et Maria mox matrimonio coniungentur.

text: Ego et Thomas mox matrimonio coniungemini.
translation: Tom and I are getting married.

text: Decem annos matrimonio coniunctus sum.
translation: I have been married for ten years.

translation: He's without a doubt a lot better than you.

translation: Tom told me my life's in danger.

translation: Next week I will write an e-mail to my parents.

translation: God is my leader, and my sword is my companion.

text: Haud secus ac jussi faciunt, tectosque per herbam / disponunt enses et scuta latentia condunt.
translation: They obey, / and swords and bucklers hide amid the grass away.

text: Sic fatus, deinde comantem / Androgei galeam clipeique insigne decorum / induitur, laterique Argivum accommodat ensem.
translation: Then he takes the crest, / the shield and dagger of Androgeus.

text: Ocularia solaria viginti nummis Europaeis constant.

text: Eurō est ratiō ærāria Eurōpæa.
translation: The Euro is the European currency.

text: Tessera centum nummis Europaeis constat.
translation: The ticket costs 100 euros.

text: Circa triginta nummis Europaeis constat.
translation: It costs around thirty Euros.

text: Mox umbra in nebulam densam evanuit.
translation: Before long, the ghost disappeared into a thick fog.

translation: His daughter disappeared seven years ago.

text: Filia eorum abhinc septem annos evanuit.
translation: Their daughter disappeared seven years ago.

translation: The rainbow will disappear in little time.

translation: The train disappeared from view.

text: Grandia cum minimis mors ferit ense pari.
translation: Death is sure to all.

text: Qui gladio ferit, gladio perit.
translation: He who wounds by the sword, dies by the sword.

text: Talia jactanti stridens Aquilone procella / velum adversa ferit, fluctusque ad sidera tollit.
translation: E'en as he cried, the hurricane from the North / struck with a roar against the sail. Up leap / the waves to heaven.

text: Da mihi tabulam geographicam urbis, quaeso.
translation: Please give me a map of the town.

translation: There is a map on the desk.

translation: Maps were distributed to all the soldiers.

translation: Do you have a subway map?

translation: There is a map on the wall.

translation: This is a map of Australia.

text: Quinque mala citrea eme et unum gratis posside.
translation: Buy five lemons and get one more for free.

text: Gratis significat quod non opus est reddere pro eo.
translation: "Free" means that you don't need to pay for it.

translation: What is asserted without evidence may be dismissed without evidence.

text: Theatrum cinematographicum gratis intravimus.
translation: We entered the cinema for free.

translation: Mice are looking for free cheese.

text: Nesciebam hoc verbum ex Hebraica lingua oriundum esse.

translation: Hebrew and Phoenician are Canaanite languages.

translation: Phoenician is very similar to Hebrew.

translation: Phoenician was very similar to Hebrew.

translation: Yiddish is not Hebrew.

text: Una hirundo non efficit ver.
translation: One swallow does not make a spring.

translation: The Swallow, the Sparrow, the Jay, the Jackdaw and the Bat (Flittermouse) fly around the house.

text: Hirundines appropinquante hieme abvolant.
translation: Swallows fly away at the approach of winter.

text: Idcirco vocatus est locus ille Bersabee, quia uterque iuraverunt.
translation: Therefore that place was called Bersabee; because there both of them did swear.

text: Et idcirco occidit et eum Dominus, quod rem detestabilem fecerat.
translation: And therefore the Lord slew him, because he did a detestable thing.

text: Qui ait: Vacatis otio et idcirco dicitis: "Eamus et sacrificemus Domino".
translation: And he said: You are idle, and therefore you say: Let us go and sacrifice to the Lord.

translation: Immediately the other coming forth, held his brother's foot in his hand: and therefore he was called Jacob.

text: Sex diebus colligite; in die autem septimo sabbatum est Domino, idcirco non invenietur in eo.
translation: Gather it six days; but on the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord, therefore it shall not be found.

text: Ponamque buccellam panis, et confortate cor vestrum, postea transibitis; idcirco enim declinastis ad servum vestrum.
translation: And I will set a morsel of bread, and strengthen ye your heart, afterwards you shall pass on: for therefore are you come aside to your servant.

text: Hic fungus idoneus ad edendum non est.
translation: This mushroom is not good to eat.

translation: If you're the smartest person in the room, you're in the wrong room.

translation: He's not fit to be a teacher.

text: Haec planta idonea ad edendum est.
translation: This plant is good to eat.

translation: These oranges are good to eat.

text: Tu non idoneus es qui videaris.
translation: You're not fit to be seen.

text: Imber est aqua quae de nubibus cadit.
translation: Rain is water falling from clouds.

text: Et imber et nix mihi placent.
translation: I like the rain and the snow.

text: Imber est aqua de nubibus cadens.
translation: Rain is water falling from clouds.

text: Imber bonum in segetes effectum habuit.
translation: The rain had a good effect on the farm's crops.

text: Filius meus in imbri ludit.
translation: My son is playing in the rain.

text: Imber hanc arborem vivificabit.
translation: The rain will revive this tree.

text: Nisi me fallit animus, impossibile est.
translation: If I'm not mistaken, that is not possible.

translation: Nothing is impossible for God.

text: Hoc mihi impossibile est.
translation: This is impossible for me.

text: Multi ex huius regionis incolis piscatores sunt.
translation: Many of the inhabitants of this region are fishermen.

text: Multi ex huius regionis incolis agricolae sunt.
translation: Many of the inhabitants of this region are farmers.

text: Multi ex huius regionis incolis nautae sunt.
translation: Many of the inhabitants of this region are sailors.

translation: He had little experience with international issues.

translation: The international language Ido was born in 1907 in Paris, France.

text: Hodie internationalis amicitiae dies est.
translation: Today is the International Day of Friendship.

text: Lingua Anglica est lingua internationalis.
translation: English is an international language.

text: Invadunt socii et nova prœlia tentant, / obscenas pelagi ferro fœdare volucres.
translation: All to the strange encounter, sword in hand, / rush forth, these miscreants of the deep to slay.

text: Si servum vel ancillam invaserit, triginta siclos argenti dabit domino; bos vero lapidibus opprimetur.
translation: If he assault a bondman or bondwoman, he shall give thirty sicles of silver to their master, and the ox shall be stoned.

text: Cumque sol occumberet, sopor irruit super Abram, et ecce horror magnus et tenebrosus invasit eum.
translation: And when the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell upon Abram; and, lo, an horror of great darkness fell upon him.

text: Aqua in mortui pulmonibus inventa est.
translation: Water was found in the dead man's lungs.

text: Radiophonia a Marconi inventa est.
translation: The radio was invented by Marconi.

text: Charta a Sinensibus inventa est.
translation: Paper was invented by the Chinese.

text: Quō annō America inventa est?
translation: In what year was America discovered?

text: Rursumque locutus est ad eum: "Si forte inventi fuerint ibi quadraginta?" Ait: "Non percutiam propter quadraginta".
translation: And again he said to him: But if forty be found there, what wilt thou do? He said: I will not destroy it for the sake of forty.

text: Basipila iucundior est quam pila Caledonica.
translation: Baseball is a lot more fun than golf.

translation: It makes me very happy to hear that.

text: Est mihi istud auditu perquam iucundum.
translation: I'm delighted to hear that.

text: Basipila iucundior est pila Caledonica.
translation: Baseball is a lot more fun than golf.

text: Cenavistine iucunde cum Thoma?
translation: Did you have a nice dinner with Tom?

translation: The weather's rather jolly today.

text: Tunicas laneas et chirothecas coriaceas nostras gerimus.
translation: We wear our wool coats and our leather gloves.

text: Thorax laneus cinereus mihi magis quam thorax laneus purpureus placet.
translation: The gray sweater I like more than the purple.

text: Thorax laneus caeruleus valde pulcher est.
translation: This blue sweater is very pretty.

translation: What color is his sweater?

text: Thoracem laneum gero, quia algeo.
translation: I'm wearing a sweater because I'm cold.

text: Thorax laneus caeruleus pulcherrimus est.
translation: This blue sweater is very pretty.

translation: Chess books were something irreplaceable for him.

translation: Magnus Carlsen won third world chess title.

translation: Do you play checkers with your grandmother?

translation: Chess is not an easy game.

translation: Tom and Mary played checkers.

text: Ego et Thomas latrunculis lusimus.
translation: Tom and I played checkers.

text: Avus meus in lectulo sedens obdormivit.
translation: My grandfather fell asleep sitting on the couch.

text: In lectulo meo, per noctes, quæsivi quem diligit anima mea.
translation: In my bed by night I sought him whom my soul loveth.

text: Lucernam super lectuli mensam posuerunt.
translation: They put the lamp on the nightstand.

text: Tres magnos lectulos emi.
translation: I bought three large couches.

text: Vado in lectulum meum.
translation: I go to my bed.

text: In lectulo meo, per noctes, quaesivi quem diligit anima mea, quaesivi illum, et non inveni.
translation: By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loved: I sought him, but I found him not.

text: Literae celebrari debent, quae tanquam naves sulcantes oceanum temporis.
translation: Books are ships which pass through the vast sea of time.

text: "Quid legebas?" "Aliquid ex sacris literis."
translation: "What were you reading?" "Something from the sacred scriptures."

translation: I'm going to have to write some letters.

text: Mihi scribendum fuit literas.
translation: I had to write some letters.

text: Sic ore effata, recepit / ad sese et sacra longævum in sede locavit.
translation: She said, / and to his hallowed seat the aged monarch led.

text: Cum venit, aulæis jam se regina superbis / aurea composuit sponda mediamque locavit.
translation: There, under gorgeous curtains, at the head / sate Dido, throned upon a golden bed.

text: Scis quanta impostura fit apud nostros in bis qui vendunt aut locant raedās.
translation: You know how much cheating there is around here from those who sell or rent out cars.

text: Scis quanta impostura fit apud nostros in bis qui vendunt aut locant equos.
translation: You know what abundance of cheating there is with our countrymen among those who sell or let out horses.

text: Talia flammato secum dea corde volutans, / nimborum in patriam, loca feta furentibus Austris, / Aeoliam venit.
translation: Turning over such things in her inflamed heart, the goddess came to the country of storm-clouds, Aeolia, breeding place of the raging winds.

text: Matura igitur, ne in commodes meo studio.
translation: Hurry then, don't get in the way of my studies.

text: Haec mala nondum matura sunt.

translation: Those apples aren't ripe yet.

text: Haec nondum matura sunt.
translation: These aren't ripe yet.

text: "Sed quando reddes?" "Quum descripsero contextum in tres quattuor praelectiones." "Matura igitur, ne incommodes meo studio." "Maturabo."
translation: "But when will you return?" "When I have written out my notes for three or four lessons." "Hurry, then so you don't get in the way of my studies." "I will hurry."

text: Praeterita hebdomade maximus terrae motus in America Meridiana accidit.
translation: Last week a very powerful earthquake occurred in South America.

translation: Layla is a mother of six, living in the south west of England.

translation: Australia is smaller than South America.

translation: Tomorrow it will rain in the south of England.

text: Africa Meridiana procul abest.
translation: South Africa is far away.

text: Numeri magni momenti in Toki Pona non sunt.
translation: Numbers are not important in Toki Pona.

translation: Two, four, six and eight are even numbers.

translation: 2, 4, 6 etc. are even numbers.

text: Numeri telephonici eius oblitus sum.

text: Numeri telephonici eius oblita sum.
translation: I forgot his phone number.

text: Unus, duo, tres, quattuor, quinque, sex, septem, octo, novem, et decem sunt numeri.
translation: One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, and ten are numbers.

text: Thomas hoc faciendi occasionem nanctus est.
translation: Tom got the chance to do that.

text: Deliberando saepe perit occasio.
translation: The opportunity is often lost in deliberating.

text: Te occasionem amplexurum arbitrabar.
translation: I thought you'd jump at the chance.

text: Te occasionem amplexuram arbitrabar.
translation: I thought you'd jump at the chance.

text: Hanc oblatam occasionem teneo.
translation: I can't pass up this chance.

text: Abyssi operuerunt eos, descenderunt in profundum quasi lapis.
translation: The depths have covered them, they are sunk to the bottom like a stone.

text: Quindecim cubitis altior fuit aqua super montes, quos operuerat.
translation: The water was fifteen cubits higher than the mountains which it covered.

text: Quam cum vidisset Iudas, suspicatus est esse meretricem; operuerat enim vultum suum.
translation: When Juda saw her, he thought she was a harlot: for she had covered her face, lest she should be known.

text: Cumque operuisset superficiem deserti, apparuit minutum et squamatum in similitudinem pruinæ super terram.
translation: And when it had covered the face of the earth, it appeared in the wilderness small, and as it were beaten with a pestle, like unto the hoar frost on the ground.

text: Flavit spiritus tuus, et operuit eos mare; submersi sunt quasi plumbum in aquis vehementibus.
translation: Thy wind blew and the sea covered them: they sunk as lead in the mighty waters.

text: Talis erat Dido, talem se laeta ferebat / per medios, instans operi regnisque futuris.
translation: E'en such was Dido; so with joyous mien, / urging the business of her rising state, / among the concourse passed the Tyrian queen.

text: Quantoque opprimebant eos, tanto magis multiplicabantur et crescebant.
translation: But the more they oppressed them, the more they were multiplied and increased.

text: Opprimantur operibus et expleant ea, ut non acquiescant verbis mendacibus.
translation: Let them be oppressed with works, and let them fulfil them; that they may not regard lying words.

text: Omne malum nascens facile opprimitur.
translation: Every evil is easily crushed at birth.

text: Clamor ergo filiorum Israel venit ad me, vidique afflictionem eorum, qua ab Aegyptiis opprimuntur.
translation: For the cry of the children of Israel is come unto me: and I have seen their affliction, wherewith they are oppressed by the Egyptians.

text: In tota terra panis deerat, et oppresserat fames terram valde, defecitque terra Aegypti et terra Chanaan præ fame.
translation: And there was no bread in all the land; for the famine was very sore, so that the land of Egypt and all the land of Canaan fainted by reason of the famine.

text: Et invaluit fames in omni terra Aegypti; aperuitque Ioseph universa horrea et vendebat Aegyptiis; nam et illos oppresserat fames.
translation: And the famine increased daily in all the land: and Joseph opened all the barns, and sold to the Egyptians: for the famine had oppressed them also.

text: Barba non facit philosophum, neque vile gerere pallium.
translation: A beard doesn't make a philosopher, nor does wearing a cheap coat.

translation: I must buy a new winter coat.

text: Pallium habeo, sed petasum non habeo.
translation: I have a coat, but I don't have a hat.

text: Barbam et pallium, philosophum nondum video.
translation: I see a beard and a cloak, but I have yet to see a philosopher.

text: Pallium tuum valde pulchrum est.
translation: Your coat is very beautiful.

text: Habesne pallium et petasum?
translation: Do you have a coat and a hat?

text: Thōmās scīre volēbat quōmodo Marīa tam pecūniōsa facta esset.
translation: Tom wanted to know how Mary had become so rich.

translation: Tom's parents have a lot of money.

translation: There is no less confusion there of tongues and persons, than formerly in the tower of Babel.

translation: Vera lives on the same street as you.
