translation: And they said: No, but we will abide in the street.

text: In hac platea duae sunt ecclesiae.
translation: There are two churches on this street.

text: Urbana nostra regio tres habet plateas.
translation: Our neighborhood has three avenues.

text: Surgam, et circuibo civitatem; per vicos et plateas quaeram quem diligit anima mea, quaesivi illum, et non inveni.
translation: I will rise now, and go about the city in the streets, and in the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loves: I sought him, but I found him not.

text: Beati mites : quoniam ipsi possidebunt terram.
translation: Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth.

text: Thomas Jefferson Alcoranum possedit.
translation: Thomas Jefferson owned a Qur'an.

text: Et ille ait: Domine Deus, unde scire possum quod possessurus sim eam?
translation: But he said: Lord God, whereby may I know that I shall possess it?

text: Et habitate nobiscum; terra in potestate vestra est: manete, perambulate et possidete eam.
translation: And dwell with us: the land is at your command, till, trade, and possess it.

text: Et reliquit omnia, quæ possidebat, in manu Ioseph nec cum eo quidquam aliud noverat nisi panem, quo vescebatur.
translation: Neither knew he any other thing, but the bread which he ate.

text: Habitavit ergo Israel in Aegypto, id est in terra Gessen, et possedit eam; auctusque est et multiplicatus nimis.
translation: And Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt, in the country of Goshen; and they had possessions therein, and grew, and multiplied exceedingly.

text: Domi maneam potius quam in calorem ineam.
translation: I would rather stay at home than go out in this hot weather.

text: Cur aliquid potius est quam nihil?
translation: Why is there something instead of nothing?

text: Potius diabolus cognitus quam incognitus angelus.
translation: Better the devil you know than the angel you don't.

text: Praeceptorem potius quam machinatorem esse velim.
translation: I would like to be a teacher rather than an engineer.

text: Cur potius aliquid quam nihil?
translation: Why is there something rather than nothing?

text: Moriar potius quam me dedam.
translation: I'd rather die than surrender.

text: Ziri chirographum protulit, et illud daturus erat Rimae.
translation: Ziri took out a note and was about to hand it to Rima.

text: Ficus protulit grossos suos; vineæ florentes dederunt odorem suum.
translation: The fig tree hath put forth her green figs: the vines in flower yield their sweet smell.

text: Fratrem Mariae non protulit Thomas.
translation: Tom didn't mention Mary's brother.

text: “Retrahe, ait, manum tuam in sinum tuum!” Retraxit et protulit iterum, et erat similis carni reliquæ.
translation: And he said: Put back thy hand into thy bosom. He put it back, and brought it out again, and it was like the other flesh.

text: Dixitque Dominus rursum: “Mitte manum tuam in sinum tuum!” Quam cum misisset in sinum, protulit leprosam instar nivis.
translation: And the Lord said again: Put thy hand into thy bosom. And when he had put it into his bosom, he brought it forth leprous as snow.

text: Thomas plorat, quia ab ape punctus est.
translation: Tom is crying because he got stung by a bee.

text: Non nisi tangentem crudelis apicula pungit.
translation: Bees only sting if they are touched.

text: Mel dulce est, sed apis pungit.
translation: Honey is sweet, but the bee stings.

text: Si nos pungitis, nonne sanguinamus?
translation: If you prick us, do we not bleed?

text: Heu! Ab ape punctus sum!
translation: Ouch! I was stung by a bee.

text: Thomas ab ape punctus est.
translation: Tom was stung by a bee.

text: Thomas nuntios per radiophoniam auscultavit.
translation: Tom listened to the news on the radio.

text: Thomas nuntios per radiophoniam auscultat.
translation: Tom is listening to the news on the radio.

text: Nuntios per radiophoniam auscultavi.
translation: I listened to the news on the radio.

text: Nuntios per radiophoniam audivi.
translation: I heard the news on the radio.

text: Nuntios per radiophoniam auscultat.
translation: He is listening to the news on the radio.

text: Potesne radiophoniam fractam reficere?
translation: Can you fix the broken radio?

text: Pecunia est omnium malorum radix.
translation: Money is the root of all evil.

text: Binarius est radix quadrata quaternarii.
translation: The square root of four is two.

text: E semine procrescis planta, planta abit in fruticem. Frutex in arborem. Arborem sustentat radix.
translation: A shoot grows from a seed. A shoot transforms to a sapling, a sapling to a tree. The root sustains the tree.

text: E radice surgit stirps (stemma). Stirps se dividit in ramos et frondes, factas ex foliis.
translation: From the root rises the stem. The stem divides itself into boughs and green branches made from leaves.

text: Trunc adhaeret radicibus. Caudex est dejectus stipes, sine ramis: habens corticem et librum, pulpam et medullam.
translation: The trunk is attached to the root. A log is the body of the tree cut down, without boughs: having bark and rind, pith and heart.

text: Nam quæ prima solo ruptis radicibus arbos / vellitur, huic atro liquuntur sanguine guttæ, / et terram tabo maculant.
translation: Scarce the first stem uprooted, from the wood / black drops distilled, and stained the earth with gore.

text: Num Thomas hanc ranam edet?
translation: Tom isn't really going to eat that frog, is he?

text: Ranae et aves insecta edunt.
translation: Frogs and birds eat insects.

text: Ubi illam ranam captavisti?
translation: Where did you catch that frog?

text: Fecerunt autem et malefici per incantationes suas similiter eduxeruntque ranas super terram Aegypti.
translation: And the magicians also, by their enchantments, did in like manner, and they brought forth frogs upon the land of Egypt.

text: Et extendit Aaron manum super aquas Aegypti, et ascenderunt ranæ operueruntque terram Aegypti.
translation: And Aaron stretched forth his hand upon the waters of Egypt, and the frogs came up, and covered the land of Egypt.

text: Egressique sunt Moyses et Aaron a pharaone; et clamavit Moyses ad Dominum pro sponsione ranarum, quam condixerat pharaoni.
translation: And Moses and Aaron went forth from Pharaoh: and Moses cried to the Lord for the promise, which he had made to Pharaoh concerning the frogs.

text: Esne recordata ad bibliothecam ire?
translation: Did you remember to go to the library?

text: Esne recordata Mariae flores emere?
translation: Did you remember to buy flowers for Mary?

text: Esne recordata cibum caninum emere?
translation: Did you remember to buy dog food?

text: Esne recordata Thomae gratias agere?
translation: Did you remember to thank Tom?

text: Esne recordata iis gratias agere?
translation: Did you remember to thank them?

text: Esne recordata ei gratias agere?
translation: Did you remember to thank him?

text: Computatorium meum reficiendum est.
translation: I have to get my computer repaired.

text: Haec birota reficienda est.
translation: This bike needs to be repaired.

text: Horologium meum reficiendum est.
translation: I must get my watch repaired.

text: Illud mihi reficiendum est.
translation: I need to repair that.

text: Hoc mihi reficiendum est.
translation: I have to fix this.

text: Calcei tui reficiendi sunt.
translation: Your shoes want mending.

text: Inquietum es cor nostrum donec requiescat in te.
translation: Stressed is our heart till it rests in you.

text: Afferatur pauxillum aquæ, et lavate pedes vestros et requiescite sub arbore.
translation: But I will fetch a little water, and wash ye your feet, and rest ye under the tree.

text: Thomas requiescere non potuit.
translation: Tom couldn't rest.

text: Maria requiescere non potuit.
translation: Mary couldn't rest.

text: Vidua verba habuit "Requiesce in pace – donec iterum conveniamus" lapidi inscripta.
translation: The widow had the gravestone inscribed with the words "Rest in Peace – till we meet again."

text: Cunctis diebus terræ, sementis et messis, frigus et æstus, æstas et hiems, dies et nox non requiescent.
translation: All the days of the earth, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, night and day, shall not cease.

text: Cur sapo est in mensa?
translation: Why is the soap on the table?

text: Os tuum sapone lavabo!
translation: I'll wash your mouth out with soap!

text: Os tuum sapone eluam!
translation: I'll rinse your mouth out with soap!

text: Ubi istud sāpōnem ēmistī?
translation: Where did you buy that soap?

text: Ubi istud sāpōnem ēmistis?
translation: Where did you buy that soap?

text: Sapo oculos meos vulneravit.
translation: The soap hurt my eyes.

text: Corea Septentrionalis multo pulchrior est quam Meridionalis.
translation: South Korea is much more beautiful than North Korea.

text: Hae aves hieme in Africam Septentrionalem migrant.
translation: These birds migrate to North Africa in the winter.

text: "Ubi Algerium situm est?" "In Africa Septentrionali."
translation: "Where is Algeria located?" "In North Africa."

text: Mexicum terra in America Septentrionali est.
translation: Mexico is a country in North America.

text: Corea Septentrionalis multo pulchrior est Meridionali.
translation: South Korea is much more beautiful than North Korea.

text: Quot terrae in America Septentrionali sunt?
translation: How many countries are in North America?

text: Num mater tua est severa?
translation: Your mother isn’t severe, is she?

text: Pater meus severissimus est.
translation: My dad is very strict.

text: Magister noster severissimus erat.
translation: Our teacher was so strict.

text: Lege antequam signabitur quod scripsisti.
translation: Read your statement before you sign it.

text: Tria signa in horto erant.
translation: There were three statues in the garden.

text: Cur signa meatus deseruere suos?
translation: Why did the flags leave their path?

text: Virgam quoque hanc sume in manu tua, in qua facturus es signa.
translation: And take this rod in thy hand, wherewith thou shalt do the signs.

text: Narravitque Moyses Aaron omnia verba Domini, quibus miserat eum, et signa, quæ mandaverat.
translation: And Moses told Aaron all the words of the Lord, by which he had sent him, and the signs that he had commanded.

text: Locutusque est Aaron omnia verba, quæ dixerat Dominus ad Moysen, et fecit signa coram populo.
translation: And Aaron spoke all the words which the Lord had said to Moses: and he wrought the signs before the people.

text: Mercurius e systematis solaris planetis craterosissimus planeta est.
translation: Mercury is the planet with the most craters in the Solar System.

text: Mercurius solus systematis solaris planeta sine satellitibus est.
translation: Mercury is the only planet in the Solar System that doesn't have moons of its own.

text: Mercurius e systematis solaris planetis rapidissime Soli se circumvolvit.
translation: Mercury is the fastest rotating planet around the Sun.

text: Mercurius minor est paucis systematis solaris satellitibus.
translation: Mercury is smaller than some moons in the Solar System.

text: Intimus e systematis solaris planetis Mercurius est.
translation: Mercury is the innermost of the planets of the Solar System.

text: Virtus solaris est fons energiae purae.
translation: Solar power is a clean source of energy.

text: Non semper praestant homines, quae plurima spondent.
translation: A long tongue is a sign of a short hand.

text: Et dimisit eum, postquam dixerat: “Sponsus sanguinum”, ob circumcisionem.
translation: And he let him go after she had said: A bloody spouse art thou to me, because of the circumcision.

text: Sodales atque sponsus certatim celebrant sponsam.
translation: The companions and the groom compete in praising the bride.

text: Colloquentibus sponsis, fratres sponsae apparent.
translation: The bride and groom are talking when the bride's brothers appear.

text: Tulit ilico Sephora acutissimam petram et circumcidit præputium filii sui; tetigitque pedes eius et ait: Sponsus sanguinum tu mihi es.
translation: Immediately Sephora took a very sharp stone, and circumcised the foreskin of her son, and touched his feet, and said: A bloody spouse art thou to me.

text: Sponsa, sodalibus comitata, sponsum exspectat, eoque adventante, uterque mutuum amorem declarat, adeo ut sponsa, extra se rapta, in exstasim incidat.
translation: The bride, accompanied by her companions, waits for the groom and, upon his arrival, both declare their love for each other, so much so that the bride, overcome with passion, goes into ecstasy.

text: Ego poscerem statuam mihi, si designassem aliquid tale.
translation: I would demand a statue for myself, if I had contrived any such thing.

text: Statua Libertatis Novi Eboraci sita est.
translation: The Statue of Liberty is located in New York.

text: Respiciensque uxor eius post se versa est in statuam salis.
translation: And his wife looking behind her, was turned into a statue of salt.

text: Qui Corinthum veniunt, statuas inspiciunt.
translation: Those who come to Corinth look at the statues.

text: Magistri statua ante scholam est.
translation: There is a statue of the teacher in front of the school.

text: Pactum vero meum statuam ad Isaac, quem pariet tibi Sara tempore isto in anno altero.
translation: But my covenant I will establish with Isaac, whom Sara shall bring forth to thee at this time in the next year.

text: Cathedram emi, sed adhuc nescio ubi eam sistam.
translation: I bought an armchair, but I don't know where I am going to put it on yet.

text: Status eius praeterita nocte deterioravit.
translation: Her condition got worse last night.

text: Statum volo gubernacularem appetere.
translation: I want to run for governor.

text: Russia est status saecularis.
translation: Russia is a secular state.

text: Status valde malus est.
translation: Things are very bad.

text: Instamus tamen immemores cæcique furore, / et monstrum infelix sacrata sistimus arce.
translation: But heedless, blind with frenzy, one and all / up to the sacred citadel we strain, / and there the ill-omened prodigy install.

text: Aspice imaginem in summam paginam sitam.
translation: Look at the picture at the top of the page.

text: Summam paginam tantum legi.
translation: I only read the top of the page.

text: "Jam summas arces Tritonia, respice, Pallas / insedit, nimbo effulgens et Gorgone sæva."
translation: "See, on the citadel, all grim with gore, / red-robed, and with the Gorgon shield aglow, / Tritonian Pallas bids the conflict roar."

text: In somnis quaerit sponsa dilectum. Per desertum advenientem sponsum prospicit sponsa, sponsusque sponsae pulchritudinem summis laudibus effert.
translation: In dreams, the bride searches for her beloved. She sees him arriving through the desert, and the groom highly praises her beauty.

text: Summum est quod simul sumus.
translation: The important thing is that we are together.

text: Ad summum arboris ramum scandit.
translation: She climbs to the highest branch of the tree.

text: Aristoteles eudaimonian summum bonum dixit.
translation: Aristotle considered eudaimonia to be the highest human good.

text: Dicit eis Iesus: Implete hydrias aqua. Et impleverunt eas usque ad summum.
translation: Jesus said to the servants, "Fill the jars with water"; so they filled them to the brim.

text: Homines quinque sensus habent: visum, auditum, tactum, gustum, olfactum.
translation: Humans have five senses: sight, hearing, touch, taste and smell.

text: Talia non iam facio.
translation: I don't do things like that anymore.

text: Talia voce refert curisque ingentibus æger / spem vultu simulat, premit altum corde dolorem.
translation: He spake, and heart-sick with a load of care, / suppressed his grief, and feigned a cheerful air.

text: "Quis talia fando / Myrmidonum Dolopumve aut duri miles Ulixi / temperet a lacrimis?"
translation: "What Myrmidon, or who / of stern Ulysses' warriors can withhold / his tears, to tell such things, as thou would'st have re-told?"

text: Olli subridens hominum sator atque deorum, / vultu, quo cœlum tempestatesque serenat, / oscula libavit natæ, dehinc talia fatur:
translation: Then Jove, soft-smiling with the look that clears / the storms, and gently kissing her, replies.

text: Deus ubique esse non potest, itaque matres creavit.
translation: God could not be everywhere, therefore he created mothers.

text: Ubique hieme dies breviores et calores inferiores sunt.
translation: Everywhere, the days are shorter and the temperatures are lower in winter.

text: Quisquis Deum quaerit, ubique inveniet.
translation: Anyone who wants to look for God will find him everywhere.

text: Nemo ubique esse potest.
translation: No one can be everywhere.

text: Ubique medius caelus est.
translation: The sun shines on everybody.

text: Ubique esse non possum.
translation: I can't be everywhere.

text: Sapientia abscondita et thesaurus invisus, quae utilitas in utrisque?
translation: Hidden wisdom and invisible treasure, what use can both be?

text: hoc lexicon nūllam omnīnō ūtilitātem affert.
translation: This dictionary is not useful at all.

text: Anglia amicos non habet, sed utilitates.
translation: England doesn't have friends, only interests.

text: Hoc nihil utilitatis habet.
translation: There's no benefit to this.

text: Suae quisque tutelae ius habet morum rationis utilitatis quae ex suis studiis scientiae litterarum artium efficiantur.
translation: Everyone has the right to the protection of the moral and material interests resulting from any scientific, literary or artistic production of which he is the author.

text: Ferrum multo utilius est quam aurum.
translation: Iron is much more useful than gold.

text: Ferrum utilius est quam pulchrius.
translation: Iron is more useful than it is beautiful.

text: Telephonum utilius est quam monile.
translation: A telephone is more useful than a necklace.

text: Ferrum multo utilius est auro.
translation: Iron is much more useful than gold.

text: Ferrum utilius est quam aurum.
translation: Iron is more useful than gold.

text: Telephonum utilius est monili.
translation: A telephone is more useful than a necklace.

text: Aquila trāns vallem sub sōle volat.
translation: The eagle flies through the sunny valley.

text: Thomas in Valle Silicii opus facit.
translation: Tom works in Silicon Valley.

text: "Nondum Ilium et arces / Pergameæ steterant; habitabant vallibus imis."
translation: "Nor yet proud Ilion nor her towers had stood; / in lowly vales sequestered they abode."

text: Quomodo profunditatem vallis metiri possumus?
translation: How can we measure the depth of a valley?

text: Aquila per apricum vallem volat.
translation: The eagle flies through the sunny valley.

text: Ascanium Anchisenque patrem Teucrosque Penates / commendo sociis, et curva valle recondo.
translation: Troy's gods commending to my comrades' care, / with old Anchises and my infant heir, / I hide them in a winding vale from view.

text: Vanitas, superbia, et egotismus sunt essentiae patriotismi.
translation: Conceit, arrogance and egotism are the essentials of patriotism.

text: Vanitas vanitatum, dixit Ecclesiastes; vanitas vanitatum, et omnia vanitas.
translation: Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher, vanity of vanities; all is vanity.

text: Vanitas vanitatum et omnia vanitas.
translation: Vanity of vanities; all is vanity.

text: Vanitas vanitatum, et omnia vanitas.
translation: Vanity of vanities, all is vanity.

text: Carotae et rapae stirpes accommodae ad vescendum sunt.
translation: Carrots and turnips are edible roots.

text: Etiam radix taraxaci ad vescendum accommoda est.
translation: The root of a dandelion is edible, too.

text: Haec planta ad vescendum accommoda est.
translation: This plant is good to eat.

text: Multae vespae pollen e flore in florem ferunt.
translation: Many wasps are pollinators.

text: Apes et formicae de vespis descendunt.
translation: Bees and ants are descended from wasps.

text: Thomas a vespa punctus est.
translation: Tom got stung by a wasp.

text: Proximo anno in Scotia me visuri estis.
translation: Next year, you'll come to see me in Scotland.

text: haud crēdere possum mē umquam iterum autobirotam surreptam vīsūrum.
translation: I think it's highly unlikely that I'll ever see my stolen motorcycle again.

text: Quando putas te illam visuram esse?
translation: When do you think that you'll see her?

text: Spero me cras eum visurum esse.
translation: I hope that I will see him tomorrow.

text: Quando putas te illum visurum esse?
translation: When do you think you'll see him?

text: Spero me te visurum esse.
translation: I hope to see you again.

text: Multi enim sunt vocati, pauci vero electi.
translation: For many are called, but few are chosen.

text: Prima magistra mea Iracema vocata erat. Iracema etiam nomen est unius sororum mearum.
translation: My first teacher was called Iracema. Iracema is also the name of one of my sisters.

text: "Ad eorum nuptias vocatus sum." "Quid dixisti?" "Me ad eorum nuptias vocatum fuisse."
translation: "I have been invited to their wedding." "What did you say?" "That I have been invited to their wedding."

text: At ille: “Ubi est?”, inquit. “Quare dimisistis hominem? Vocate eum, ut comedat panem”.
translation: But he said: Where is he? why have you let the man go? call him that he may eat bread.

text: Cumque vocata venisset, sciscitati sunt: “Vis ire cum homine isto?” Quæ ait: "Vadam".
translation: And they called her, and when she was come, they asked: Wilt thou go with this man? She said: I will go.

text: "Festina et salvare ibi, quia non potero facere quidquam, donec ingrediaris illuc". Idcirco vocatum est nomen urbis illius Segor.
translation: Make haste, and be saved there: because I cannot do any thing till thou go in thither. Therefore the name of that city was called Segor.

text: Capite nobis vulpes parvulas quae demoliuntur vineas; nam vinea nostra floruit.
translation: Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vines: for our vines have tender grapes.

text: Vulpes est animal ferox.
translation: A fox is a wild animal.

text: Vulpes bestiae ferae sunt.
translation: Foxes are wild animals.

text: Vulpes, quae nunquam leonem viderat, quum ei forte occurrisset leo, ita est perterrita, ut paene moreretur formidine.
translation: A fox, that had never seen a lion, when one happened to meet her, was so thoroughly terrified that she almost died from fright.

text: Quem in locum clavem abdiderint nescio.
translation: I don't know where they hid the key.

text: Puellula se in armario abdidit.
translation: The little girl hid in the closet.

text: Thomas se in armario abdidit.
translation: Tom hid in the closet.

text: Se in cellario subterraneo abdiderunt.
translation: They hid in the cellar.

text: Thomas se in cenaculo abdidit.
translation: Tom hid in the attic.

text: Haec facile abdi possunt.
translation: These can be hidden easily.

text: Responderunt: Numquid ut scorto abuti debuere sorore nostra?
translation: They answered: Should they abuse our sister as a strumpet?

text: Accipe, utere ut libet, modo ne abutere.
translation: Take it, use it as you like, but do not abuse it.

text: Quousque tandem abutere, Catilina, patientia nostra?
translation: How long, O Catiline, will you abuse our patience?

text: "Credo equidem; age, non peto dono, visne commodare? reddam tibi cras." "Non recuso, modo ne abutaris." "Non abutar."
translation: "I do think so; come, I'm not asking for you to give it to me, will you lend it me? I will give it you tomorrow." "I am not refusing, but don't abuse it." "I won't."

text: Thomas scit quid Maria actura sit.
translation: Tom knows what Mary is going to do.

text: Dicunt Thomam hoc non acturum esse.
translation: They say that Tom won't do that.

text: Perbene existimo te acturum esse.
translation: I know you'll do a wonderful job.

text: Scio quid acturi sint.
translation: I know what they're going to do.

text: Scio quid acturae sint.
translation: I know what they're going to do.

text: Ille pollicetur se acturum mecum sic, ut ageret cum suo charissimo fratre.
translation: He promises me that he would deal with me so, as he would deal with his most dear brother.

text: Deum agnoscimus ex operibus ejus.
translation: We know God by his works.

text: Agnovit prolem ambiguam geminosque parentes, / seque novo veterum deceptum errore locorum.
translation: The two-fold race Anchises understands, / the double sires, and owns himself misled / by modern error 'twixt two ancient lands.

text: Quam cum agnovisset pater, ait: Tunica filii mei est; fera pessima comedit eum, bestia devoravit Ioseph.
translation: And the father acknowledging it, said: It is my son's coat, an evil wild beast hath eaten him, a beast hath devoured Joseph.

text: Procedo, et parvam Trojam simulataque magnis / Pergama et arentem Xanthi cognomine rivum / agnosco, Scææque amplector limina portæ.
translation: I see another but a tinier Troy, / a seeming Pergama recalls the great. / A dried-up Xanthus I salute with joy, / and clasp the portals of a Scaean gate.

text: Thomas aperte adesse non vult.
translation: It's quite clear that Tom doesn't want to be here.

text: Mihi aperte inclementer dixit.
translation: He publicly insulted me.

text: Mihi aperte contumeliam dixit.
translation: He publicly insulted me.

text: Utrum horum duorum miraculorum magis admiratur: pulchritudo stupenda caudae pavonis apertae, an oculus humanus eam percipere et interpretari capax?
translation: Which of these two wonders is more impressive: the stunning beauty of a peacock's open tail, or the human eye capable of perceiving and interpreting it?

text: Anuli argentei mihi magis quam aurei placent.
translation: I prefer silver rings to gold ones.

text: Non facietis præter me deos argenteos nec deos aureos facietis vobis.
translation: You shall not make gods of silver, nor shall you make to yourselves gods of gold.

text: Hic nummus argenteus est.
translation: This is a silver coin.

text: Emitque partem agri, in qua fixerat tabernaculum suum, a filiis Hemmor patris Sichem centum argenteis.
translation: And he bought that part of the field, in which he pitched his tents, of the children of Hemor, the father of Sichem, for a hundred lambs.

text: Feceruntque filii Israel, sicut præceperat Moyses, et petierunt ab Aegyptiis vasa argentea et aurea vestemque plurimam.
translation: And the children of Israel did as Moses had commanded: and they asked of the Egyptians vessels of silver and gold, and very much raiment.

text: Prolatisque vasis argenteis et aureis ac vestibus, dedit ea Rebeccæ; res pretiosas dedit fratri eius et matri.
translation: And bringing forth vessels of silver and gold, and garments, he gave them to Rebecca, for a present. He offered gifts also to her brothers, and to her mother.

text: Scio id nihil ad me attinere.
translation: I know that this is none of my business.

text: Quid illud attinet ad hoc?
translation: What does that have to do with this?

text: Quid id ad me attinet?
translation: What does this have to do with me?

text: Quid id ad nos attinet?
translation: What does this have to do with us?

text: Quid id ad eum attinet?
translation: What does that have to do with him?

text: Nihil attinet te quicquam dicere.
translation: It's no use your saying anything.

text: Pons "Porta Aurea" e ferro factus est.
translation: The Golden Gate Bridge is made of iron.

text: Simia semper simia etiamsi aurea gestet insignia.
translation: An ape's an ape, a varlet's a varlet, though they be clad in silk or scarlet.

text: Reginae corona aurea erat.
translation: The Queen's crown was made of gold.

text: Verba mea aurea sunt.
translation: My words are golden.

text: Dices ergo omni plebi, ut postulet vir ab amico suo et mulier a vicina sua vasa argentea et aurea.
translation: Therefore thou shalt tell all the people, that every man ask of his friend, and every woman of her neighbour, vessels of silver and of gold.

text: Pons Aureae Portae ex ferro factus est.
translation: The Golden Gate Bridge is made of iron.

text: Crura illius columnæ marmoreæ quæ fundatæ sunt super bases aureas.
translation: His legs are as pillars of marble, set upon sockets of fine gold.

text: Pons Aureae Portae ferreus est.
translation: The Golden Gate Bridge is made of iron.

text: Horologii acus aureae sunt.
translation: The hands of the clock are made of gold.

text: Pulchrae sunt genae tuae sicut turturis; collum tuum sicut monilia. Murenulas aureas faciemus tibi, vermiculatas argento.
translation: How beautiful are your cheeks between earrings, your neck with necklaces! We will make you gold earrings with silver filigrees.

text: Tulitque anulum de manu sua et dedit eum in manu eius; vestivitque eum stola byssina et collo torquem auream circumposuit.
translation: And he took his ring from his own hand, and gave it into his hand: and he put upon him a robe of silk, and put a chain of gold about his neck.

text: Vērus est, is dīves est, sed avārus est.
translation: It is true he is rich, but he is a miser.

text: Nemo avarus adhuc inventus est, cui, quod haberet, esset satis.
translation: No miser has yet been found who was satisfied with what he had.

text: Didymus valde avarus est.
translation: Tom is very stingy.

text: Thomas avarus non est.
translation: Tom isn't greedy.

text: Noli infantem cum aqua balnei proicere.
translation: Don't throw the baby out with the bathwater.

text: In balneo sum, quia manus lavo.
translation: I'm in the bathroom because I'm washing my hands.

text: Puerorum ludi in balneo sunt.
translation: The boy's toys are in the bathroom.

text: In balneo libenter cantat.
translation: He likes to sing in the bathtub.

text: Cur in balneo es?
translation: Why are you in the bathroom?

text: Linteum in balneo est.
translation: The towel is in the bathroom.

text: Capillos promissos habet et bracas Genuenses gerit.
translation: He has long hair and wears jeans.

text: Bracae caeruleae maiore pretio quam virides constant.
translation: The blue pants cost more than the green ones.

text: Germani et Celtae bracas habebant, Romani illas non habebant.
translation: The Germans and Celts had pants, but the Romans didn't.

text: Illae bracae meae sunt.
translation: Those are my trousers.

text: Robert brasiliensis est. Pater eius canadensis est.
translation: Robert is Brazilian. His father is Canadian.

text: Guillelmus e Brasilia oriundus est. Brasiliensis est.
translation: Guilherme is from Brazil. He is Brazilian.

text: Laura e Brasilia oriunda est. Brasiliensis est.
translation: Laura is from Brazil. She is Brazilian.

text: Brasiliensis non sum. Lusitanus sum.
translation: I am not a Brazilian. I am Portuguese.

text: Mihi, ut Brasiliensis, est vere delectabile et captans linguam Galicianam studere.
translation: For me, as a Brazilian, studying the Galician language is something truly delicious and captivating.

text: Cibus Brasiliensis Mariae placet.
translation: Mary likes Brazilian food.
